CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which ONE of the options is the only time that the fight, flight or freeze response is triggered by a real danger instead of a perceived danger?
options: You see a fire in the accommodation.
You are shouted at by your supervisor.
You feel anxious about an upcoming work task.
You are overwhelmed by your current workload.
Yes, that’s correct! An angry supervisor, anxiety and feeling overwhelmed are all perceived dangers, whereas a fire on board is a real danger.
No, that is incorrect. An angry supervisor, anxiety and feeling overwhelmed are all perceived dangers, whereas a fire on board is a real danger.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: You see a fire in the accommodation.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Why does the Fight, Flight or Freeze response happen when there is no real danger present?
options: The perceived danger activates the survival response quicker than the rational mind can process.
People consciously want to experience their body going into survival mode.
The human brain cannot differentiate between real and perceived danger, and so it goes into survival mode at the first sign of anything unusual.
The Fight, Flight or Freeze responses release addictive chemicals that increase the desire to experience danger, whether it is real or perceived.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: The perceived danger activates the survival response quicker than the rational mind can process.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the options BEST describes Fight, Flight or Freeze responses to danger?
options: They are survival responses that your brain uses to keep you safe.
They are survival responses taught as part of safety awareness training.
They are survival responses that you consciously choose when you perceive danger.
They are natural reactions to pleasure that you cannot change.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: They are survival responses that your brain uses to keep you safe.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘People suffering from depression or anxiety are more likely to trigger the Fight, Flight or Freeze response.’
options: True.
False.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Adequate resilience requires a person to have immense physical strength to be able to deal with situations and challenges.’
options: False.
True.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the options is incorrect when describing the reason to adopt a positive outlook on board a vessel?
options: Most people are inherently negative, and so a positive outlook shows them that you are better than they are.
A positive outlook can lift others and create a strong sense of unity between team members.
There are fewer people on board vessels today, increasing the need for positive interactions on board.
A positive outlook increases belief in a person’s ability to overcome a setback.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: Most people are inherently negative, and so a positive outlook shows them that you are better than they are.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Why is confidence such an important part of resilient behaviour?
options: It helps you cope correctly with stressful situations.
It allows you to ignore procedures when you can finish a task quicker.
It makes you feel as though you cannot make a mistake.
It increases self-belief so that you can attempt tasks you are not competent at without supervision.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: It helps you cope correctly with stressful situations.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: According to this module, which of the following is NOT one of the main components of resilience?
options: Ambition.
Social support.
Confidence.
Purposefulness.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: How does inadequate resilience affect safety on board a vessel?
options: People with inadequate resilience may struggle to make safety based decisions when facing everyday problems.
People with inadequate resilience are not competent at completing work tasks.
People with inadequate resilience will never be able to improve their resilience, endangering the crew, cargo and ship.
People with inadequate resilience are incapable of recognising hazards.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: People with inadequate resilience may struggle to make safety based decisions when facing everyday problems.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘A positive outlook is a behaviour that can be learned.’
options: True.
False.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Why is it important to reframe some situations?
options: It allows you to have a wider view of a situation.
It allows you to ignore all the negatives.
It allows you to create positives that don’t exist to make you feel better.
It allows you to create a separation between reality and what you want reality to be.
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: It allows you to have a wider view of a situation.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘Perspectives are…’
options: ‘…the way you view things in your life.’
‘…learned at an early age and cannot be changed.’
‘…always correct as they are created by human feelings.’
‘…limited to how you view interactions with other people.’
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: ‘…the way you view things in your life.’

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following statement? ‘Resilience is defined as a person’s ability to…’
options: ‘…recover from or deal with difficult situations.’
‘…avoid and ignore difficult situations.’
‘…complete every task they begin, regardless of setbacks.’
‘…foresee any potential setback and navigate away from it.’
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: ‘…recover from or deal with difficult situations.’

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical physical symptom of the Fight, Flight or Freeze response?
options: Temporary blindness.
Raised heartache.
Chest pain.
Shortening of breath.

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘When making safety based decisions, resilient people…’
options: ‘…need to have a strong sense of self-belief to maintain their mental, emotional and physical wellbeing.’
‘…always double check their decisions with a superior, regardless of how simple the task may be.’
‘…choose the fastest way to resolve the issue because they are confident that they are always right.’
‘…always pass responsibility to someone else if they have made the wrong decision in the past.’
CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.answer: ‘…need to have a strong sense of self-belief to maintain their mental, emotional and physical wellbeing.’

CD0570 — Resilience, Positivity, perspec.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Creating a positive perspective can improve your overall wellbeing.’
options: True.
False.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: According to this module, what is the key to effective crisis management?
options: Preparation – having a plan to deal with a situation gives you the best opportunity to overcome it effectively.
Reactivity – responding in line with your emotions often leads to the best result.
Teamwork – all crisis management situations involve people and so it is essential that they work together.
Discipline – anyone found responsible for creating a crisis must be disciplined severely to stop them from making the same mistake again.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: Preparation – having a plan to deal with a situation gives you the best opportunity to overcome it effectively.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following statement? ‘People with inadequate resilience…’
options: ‘…often feel they have no control over a situation, often feeling like a victim of circumstance.’
‘…take full responsibility for their actions and learn from their mistakes.’
‘…are more likely to view new work tasks as an opportunity to build their resilience.’
‘…only struggle with more difficult tasks and will always complete simple tasks successfully.’
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: ‘…often feel they have no control over a situation, often feeling like a victim of circumstance.’

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘By accepting change with a positive mindset…’
options: ‘…you can improve both personally and professionally.’
‘…you reduce the amount of change that will occur around you.’
‘…you can avoid negative change altogether.’
‘…you risk making more mistakes on a daily basis.’
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: ‘…you can improve both personally and professionally.’

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of taking deep breaths when managing a crisis?
options: It increases the flow of adrenaline around the body.
It helps calm you down.
It helps you gain an understanding of the situation.
It gives you time to view the situation objectively.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: It increases the flow of adrenaline around the body.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘People with inadequate resilience tend to make decisions emotionally, rather than logically.’
options: True.
False.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Acceptance is a skill that can be developed.’
options: True.
False.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: According to this module, what is the first step to accepting change?
options: Recognising that change is a normal part of life.
Setting time aside for trying new things.
Only engaging with changes that you believe to be positive.
Being the driving force behind all changes in your life.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: Recognising that change is a normal part of life.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: How does having people with inadequate resilience affect the safety of a vessel?
options: People with inadequate resilience make choices based on what is easiest or will avoid making a superior angry rather than choosing the correct course of action.
People with inadequate resilience actively make choices that endanger their colleagues.
People with inadequate resilience improve the safety of a vessel because they always follow procedures.
People with inadequate resilience do not affect the safety of the vessel because other more resilient people will always make up for their mistakes.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: People with inadequate resilience make choices based on what is easiest or will avoid making a superior angry rather than choosing the correct course of action.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘It is usually best to have a team approach when resolving a difficult crisis.’
options: True.
False.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: What is the likely consequence of people working under too much pressure for too long a period?
options: They can burn out and lose their ability to deal with challenges.
Their abiltiy to deal with challenges will continuously increase for as long as needed.
They will quickly adapt to the increased pressure and view it as normal.
They will only struggle to cope with work tasks that are unfamiliar to them.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: They can burn out and lose their ability to deal with challenges.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: Why is adaptability such an important part of resilience?
options: It helps people cope with change, recover from setbacks and maintain resilience.
Procedures rarely work in crisis situations and so people must make new plans in the moment.
It is impossible to predict setbacks and so people must adapt at the first sign of trouble.
People will only understand what is required of them after the setback has occured.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: It helps people cope with change, recover from setbacks and maintain resilience.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: What would a resilient person do in a challenging situation?
options: Develop an objective view of a situation.
Develop tunnel vision.
Fail to note important details.
Lack confidence in ability to overcome a setback.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: Develop an objective view of a situation.

CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.question: What is the likely consequence of people with inadequate resilience undertaking routine or boring work for a prolonged period?
options: They lose motivation and become complacent.
Their confidence increases because they cannot fail at the task.
They gain motivation and their focus increases.
They will continuously improve for as long as they continue with the work.
CD0571 — Resilience, Adapting to change.answer: They lose motivation and become complacent.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Which of the following statements is true with regards to people with adequate resilience?
options: Though some factors are outside of their personal control, they believe their actions will have a direct and positive effect on the outcome.
They believe everything is in their personal control, and therefore nothing can go wrong.
They believe their actions will have no effect on the outcome.
They believe the outcome is ultimately out of their control.
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: Though some factors are outside of their personal control, they believe their actions will have a direct and positive effect on the outcome.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Connections made through social media remove the need to have physical connections with others.’
options: False.
True.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘By building a habit of letting people know that you are grateful for their help...’
options: ‘...you encourage them to be grateful for the help you give.’
‘...you encourage them to take advantage of your kind nature.’
‘...you risk losing respect from others on board who think you are a soft touch.’
‘...they are less likely to want to help you again.’
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: ‘...you encourage them to be grateful for the help you give.’

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Making connections to build social support is a key component of resilience.’
options: True.
False.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: What is the likely consequence of having good connections with other people on board?
options: Increased resilience.
Feelings of loneliness and isolation.
Feeling depressed.
Increased misunderstandings.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Gratitude is a skill that can be learned and developed.’
options: True.
False.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: According to this module, the best connections are built on which of the following?
options: Mutual support.
Mutual indifference.
Singlemindedness.
Selfishness.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: What does a person with poor resilience do when faced with a work task?
options: They focus on the amount of work that needs to be done.
They devote their time to resolving challenges.
They focus on the progress they have made.
They don’t waste time looking for someone or something to blame.
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: They focus on the amount of work that needs to be done.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘People should always try to cope with problems on their own, otherwise they will never learn how to deal with them.’
options: False.
True

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘The most resilient people do not need a support network.’
options: False.
True.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘If a colleague seems to be suffering…’
options: ‘…offer support – they may not accept it, but at least they know they are not alone.’
‘…leave them alone – they will figure out how to overcome their problems in their own time.’
‘…make jokes about their low mood – they will feel better about their problems when someone else mocks them.
‘…give them extra work – they will not be able to think about their problems if they have too much work to do.’
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: ‘…offer support – they may not accept it, but at least they know they are not alone.’

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: In today’s diverse shipping industry, why is it important to be open to learning about other people whilst respecting their need for space?
options: Connecting with and learning about others breaks down cultural barriers and creates a strong sense of community.
Learning about other people helps you identify their weaknesses so that you can progress your career at their expense.
Work on board ships is tedious and people need to learn about each other to make the time pass quicker.
Learning about other people helps you limit your interactions with people who come from a different background than  you.
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: Connecting with and learning about others breaks down cultural barriers and creates a strong sense of community.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Which of the following is likely to be decreased by being grateful?
options: Isolation.
Self-worth.
Resilience.
Perspective.

CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘When a challenge emerges, people with adequate resilience…’
options: ‘…calmly analyse the situation and work towards a successful solution that will lead to a safe outcome.’
‘…know instinctively how to respond and will be able to overcome any issues without conscious thought.’
‘…pass responsibility onto someone else so that their resilience is not lessened.’
‘…react in line with their emotional response, trusting that it will lead to the best outcome.’
CD0572 — Resilience, Connecting with oth.answer: ‘…calmly analyse the situation and work towards a successful solution that will lead to a safe outcome.’

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to improve decisiveness?
options: Consider work tasks in their entirety at all times.
Consider contingency plans and ways to resolve issues before they happen.
Retain a clear vision of your purpose.
Build confidence in being able to make the right decision at the right time.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: Consider work tasks in their entirety at all times.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Why is purposefulness such an important component of resilience?
options: It helps individuals achieve their goals.
It helps individuals understand their role in society as a whole.
It helps individuals develop tunnel vision.
It helps individuals focus solely on their own needs.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: It helps individuals achieve their goals.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Which of the following is the BEST course of action when a resilient person is confronted with a challenge?
options: Think of possible solutions, decide on the best one and then break it down into manageable steps before implementing them.
React in the way that seems best for the moment.
Don’t take any action at all until you have spoken with a senior officer to identify the best course of action.
Focus on how much work there is left to do before you overcome the challenge and ignore the progress you have made so far.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: Think of possible solutions, decide on the best one and then break it down into manageable steps before implementing them.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘In many situations, indecision…’
options: ‘…can be as damaging as, or worse than, making the wrong decisions.’
‘…is preferable to making the wrong decision.’
‘…is better than decisiveness because it leaves you with more flexibility.’
‘…is the best course of action because it doesn’t commit you to any one decision.’
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: ‘…can be as damaging as, or worse than, making the wrong decisions.’

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Only inexperienced people have moments where their resilience is tested.’
options: False.
True.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to improve resilience?
options: Identify who is to blame for a situation.
Learn how to be flexible and adaptable to change.
Take positive lessons from negative situations.
Take care of your physical health.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: Identify who is to blame for a situation.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: According to this module, how is wellbeing defined?
options: Being healthy, contented and successful.
The absence of illness.
The ability to work when suffering from ill health.
Having good physical health.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Putting off tasks or ignoring situations can lead to serious consequences, causing unnecessary stress that makes setbacks more difficult to overcome.’
options: True.
False.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Resilience is a natural talent that cannot be improved with practice.’
options: False.
True.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: How is wellbeing affected by having a sense of belonging?
options: It improves – strong connections with those around you provide support in times of need and heighten your enjoyment of everyday successes.
It improves – when you belong to a group, you don’t need to work as hard and your wellbeing gets better.
It gets worse – having a sense of belonging reduces your work ethic and your wellbeing suffers.
It gets worse – being part of a group increases the chances of suffering from anxiety and depression.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: It improves – strong connections with those around you provide support in times of need and heighten your enjoyment of everyday successes.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Finding pleasure in your work and feeling as though you are making daily progress is beneficial to your wellbeing.’
options: True.
False.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the steps in the process for effective decision making?
options: Implement the easiest solution.
Discover a problem.
Think of possible solutions.
Monitor solution for correctness.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: According to this module, what is decisiveness?
options: The ability to make decisions quickly and effectively.
The ability to make decisions after several hours of deep consideration.
The ability to make decisions as quickly as possible, regardless of how successful they are.
The ability to follow instructions regardless of the obstacles that arise.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: The ability to make decisions quickly and effectively.

CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.question: Why is it important to initially step back from difficult situations?
options: To limit your emotional response and gain more control over the situation.
It is best to let other people handle difficult situations.
The physical act of stepping back reduces the impact the situation may have.
In the hope that the situation resolves itself.
CD0573 — Resilience, Wellbeing and purpo.answer: To limit your emotional response and gain more control over the situation.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Is the following statement true or false? ^M‘All Safety Data Sheets must be stored either as a hard copy or electronically in a place that is known and accessible to everyone on board.’
options: True.
False.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Is the following statement true or false?^M‘MARPOL requires Safety Data Sheets for cargos carried and fuel oil supplied.’
options: False.
True.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: When should you read a Safety Data Sheet? Select the BEST answer.
options: Before using any chemical to remind ourselves of the dangers and make ourselves aware of the first aid actions.
Only when using a chemical you haven’t used before.
Only when your supervisor is watching.
Before using any flammable substances that could damage the ship.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: Before using any chemical to remind ourselves of the dangers and make ourselves aware of the first aid actions.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Section 7 of the safety data sheet is titled “Handling and Storage” What information might be found here?
options: Possible reactions of the substance with other chemicals and required segregation.
The length of time the substance can be kept on board.
The number of times the substance can be handled before it causes harm.
Transport information.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: Possible reactions of the substance with other chemicals and required segregation.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Which of the following is the BEST way to familiarise crewmembers with new or different chemicals delivered on board?
options: Brief all the staff who may come into contact with the chemicals.
Ensure all staff read the Safety Data Sheets prior to using new or different chemicals.
Hold a briefing with ALL crewmembers about ALL chemicals used on board.
Make crewmembers read all Safety Data Sheets prior to starting work on board the vessel.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: Brief all the staff who may come into contact with the chemicals.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ^M‘If the information provided in the Safety Data Sheet is not satisfactory…’
options: ‘…do not accept the chemicals on board until the supplier can be contacted and an updated version of the Safety Data Sheet is provided.’
‘…accept the chemicals on board and contact the supplier for an updated version.’
‘…do not accept the chemicals on board and refuse to accept any chemicals from the supplier.’
‘…dispose of the chemicals to avoid any potential accidents caused by incorrect information.’
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: ‘…do not accept the chemicals on board until the supplier can be contacted and an updated version of the Safety Data Sheet is provided.’

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Section 4 of the safety data sheet is titled “First aid measures”, What information might be found here?
options: The action to take if a person is harmed by the substance.
The action to take if a fire is caused by the substance.
The action to take if there is an accidental release of the substance.
The action to take that will best aid recovery of any spilled substance.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: The action to take if a person is harmed by the substance.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Section 8 of the safety data sheet is titled “Exposure controls and personal protection”. What information might be found here?
options: The ventilation required in a space before the substance may be used there.
The action to take if there is an accidental release of the substance.
The physical and chemical properties of the substance.
Stability and reactivity .
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: The ventilation required in a space before the substance may be used there.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ^M‘Safety Data Sheets must be made available to…’
options: ‘…all employees so that they can manage the risks to avoid unwanted incidents.’
‘…all officers so that they can explain the contents of the Safety Data Sheets to the ship’s crew.’
‘…the master of the vessel so that they can create the necessary procedures for officers and crewmembers.’
‘…all new employees only, as more experienced crewmembers will know the hazards involved.’
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: ‘…all employees so that they can manage the risks to avoid unwanted incidents.’

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ^M‘If there is an Exposure Scenario annexed to the Safety Data Sheet…’
options: ‘…the crew must ensure the relevant risk management measures are in place.’
‘…the crew must only use the chemical under supervision from senior management.’
‘…the crew must acquire a permit to work prior to using the chemical.’
‘…the crew must not use the chemical in the engine room.’
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: ‘…the crew must ensure the relevant risk management measures are in place.’

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Who out of the following need to know where the Safety Data Sheets are stored? Select the BEST answer.
options: All crewmembers.
Deck department staff.
Engine room staff.
Catering department staff.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: What will the management team do upon receipt of a new or different Safety Data Sheet on board?
options: They will prepare chemical risk assessments, often during Safety Meetings.
They will ensure the information is correct and instruct crewmembers to use the chemicals immediately.
They will filter out non-essential Safety Data Sheets.
They will file the Safety Data Sheet and trust crew to use the chemicals safely.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: They will prepare chemical risk assessments, often during Safety Meetings.

CD0574 — Safety data sheets.question: Section 2 of the safety data sheet is titled “Hazards Identification”. What information might be found here?
options: That the substance can cause human health problems.
The name of the substance.
The composition/information on ingredients.
The action to take in case of a spill.
CD0574 — Safety data sheets.answer: That the substance can cause human health problems.

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘When the correct PPE isn’t worn, chemicals can get through your skin and into your body.’
options: The statement is true.
The statement is false.

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: 下面的陈述是真是假？ “如果不佩戴正确的 PPE，化学品会穿过皮肤，进入您的体内。”
options: 此陈述为真。
此陈述为假。

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Synthetic vinyl boots should also have steel toecap protection.’
options: The statement is true.
The statement is false.

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: 下面的陈述是真是假？ “合成乙烯基安全靴也应有钢脚趾套保护。”
options: 此陈述为真。
此陈述为假。

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: After finishing a task wearing chemical suits, what should you do with the PPE?
options: Clean it, inspect it, and hang it in a safe place to dry.
Give it a wipe and put it back where you found it.
Hang it straight back up in case someone wants to use it.
Leave it by the work area for the next person.
CD0576 — Use of PPE.answer: Clean it, inspect it, and hang it in a safe place to dry.

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: 佩戴防化服装完成一项任务之后，应如何处理 PPE？
options: 对其进行清洁，检查，然后挂在安全位置进行干燥。
擦拭一遍，放回原地。
直接放回，以供其他人使用。
将其留在工作区，给下一个人用。
CD0576 — Use of PPE.answer: 对其进行清洁，检查，然后挂在安全位置进行干燥。

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: Which of the following is BEST suited to protecting your head in a confined space?
options: A bump hat.
A helmet with a chin strap.
A climber’s hat.
A barrier.

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: 以下哪种最适合在有限空间内保护您的头部？
options: 凸顶帽。
带绑带的安全帽。
攀爬帽。
挡板。

CD0576 — Use of PPE.question: Which of the options best completes the following sentence? ‘Before putting on any PPE...’
options: ‘...it should be visually inspected to ensure it is in good condition.’
‘…you should always read the company procedures.’

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the options best completes the following sentence? ‘When planning the route of an inspection, it is always better…’

Yes, that’s correct! It is always better to start furthest away and work back to the point of entry.
No, that is not correct. It is always better to start furthest away and work back to the point of entry.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: ‘…to start furthest away and work back to the point of entry.’

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Where in a ballast tank is general corrosion most extensive?
options: At the top of the ballast tank.
At the bottom of the ballast tank.
In the area around the suction bell-mouth.
On transverse bulkheads.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which document will illustrate the means of access in each ballast tank on tankers and bulk carriers built after 2005?

SMS.
Cargo Operating Procedures.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Ship Structure Access Manual.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: When taking photographs of defects, which of the following is NOT correct?

Ensure the photo gives an idea of size and severity.
Ensure the photo is in focus.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Only take one photo of each defect.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What sort of damage might be found after a vessel has grounded?

Cracks at connection between vertical stiffeners and bottom longitudinal frames.
Extensive paint detachment on the tank bottom.
Extensive corrosion on the tank bottom.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Deformed bottom or side shell plating and the associated stiffeners.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following is NOT commonly used to measure defects during a ballast tank inspection?

Tape measure.
Digital camera.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Chipping hammer.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What is indicated if a shiny pit filled with grey sludge is found in steelwork?
options: The pit is active and must be filled or repaired as soon as possible.

As long as the sludge is present there will be no further corrosion.
The grey sludge needs to be moved and the pit cleaned and painted.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: The pit is active and must be filled or repaired as soon as possible.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: According to this module, which of the following is a slipping hazard?
options: The presence of mud or silt.
Pure epoxy tank coatings.
Pools of standing water.
High humidity in the ballast tank.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: The presence of mud or silt.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: How is pitting measured?

Discolouration and depth.
Dye penetrant.
Diameter and discolouration.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Diameter and depth.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which term describes a type of paint coating damage described in this module?
options: Blistering.
Bubbling.
Peeling.
Corroding.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Blistering.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What type of paint coating failure is indicated in the photograph?
options: Flaking.
Blistering.
Cracking.
Bubbling.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Flaking.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: How is structural deformity measured?
options: Deflection measured with depth gauge and ruler.
Diameter measured with a tape measure.
There is no need to measure it, a photo will be enough.
Dye penetrant.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Deflection measured with depth gauge and ruler.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What needs to be recorded when inspecting sacrificial anodes?
options: Percentage wasted and condition of securing bracket.
Degree of oxidation and condition of securing bracket.
The weight of the anodes as compared with when they were new.
The electrical current between the steel structure and the anode (Battery effect).
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Percentage wasted and condition of securing bracket.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following describes where fatigue cracks are normally found?
options: End of brackets, especially when they come to an abrupt end.
They are only ever found along welded seams.
Side shell near to the waterline.
Where bottom longitudinal connects to transverse frames.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: End of brackets, especially when they come to an abrupt end.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: How is a fatigue crack assessed?
options: Marked with dye penetrant and length measured.
With a depth gauge and ruler for width.
Diameter and depth.
There is no need to measure it, a photo will be enough.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Marked with dye penetrant and length measured.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: According to this module, what is the best way to inspect a ballast tank systematically?
options: Start furthest away and work back to the point of entry.
Start nearest the point of entry and finish as far away from the point of entry as possible.
Start at the highest point in the tank and work downwards.
Start at the suction bell-mouth and work from there in a logical manner.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Start furthest away and work back to the point of entry.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following options describes the characteristics of a fatigue crack?
options: They are hairline cracks, often difficult to find.
They are wide cracks, which are easy to find.
They are narrow fissures that often have branches.
They are narrow cracks that are apparent zigzag rust patterns on the tank structure.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: They are hairline cracks, often difficult to find.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following is required to ensure the safety of all prior to entering a ballast tank for inspection?
options: A valid enclosed space entry permit.
A risk assessment checklist.
A work order from the Chief Officer.
Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: A valid enclosed space entry permit.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Where in a ballast tank is pitting most commonly found?
options: On the tank bottom.
On the underside of stringers.
On transverse bulkheads.
Close to the welded seams.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: On the tank bottom.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: According to this module, how is the condition of tank fittings assessed?
options: With a rating of good, satisfactory or poor.
With a rating of good, fair or poor.
A photograph to be viewed after the inspection.
They are assumed to be in good condition.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: With a rating of good, satisfactory or poor.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Why might dye penetrant be initially used in a ballast tank inspection?
options: To highlight a suspected crack.
To highlight a crack so that its exact length can be measured.
As an adhesive to prevent a crack from extending further.
To determine the width of a crack.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: To highlight a suspected crack.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What might be an indication of slight leaking hydraulic pipes during a ballast tank inspection?
options: Smell of hydraulic oil.
Hydraulic couplings corroded.
Hydraulic valves can’t be opened.
All surfaces oily to the touch.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Smell of hydraulic oil.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following is NOT a classification of tank coating based on IACS charts?
options: Acceptable.
Good.
Fair.
Poor.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Acceptable.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What needs to be worn in order to detect an oxygen deficiency in the cargo tank?
options: Personal gas monitoring device.
An EEBD.
SCBA.
An explosimeter.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Personal gas monitoring device.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: When inspecting a deformation, crack or isolated pitting, what information should be included in the report?
options: Dimensions, location and defect type.
Dimensions and defect type.
Location and defect type.
Dimensions, location, defect type and course of action to fix the defect.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Dimensions, location and defect type.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What types of ships built after 2005 need to carry a Ship Structure Access Manual?
options: Tankers and bulk carriers.
Only bulk carriers.
Only oil tankers.
All ships greater than 1600 gross tons.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Tankers and bulk carriers.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: Which of the following best describes the information that should be recorded for deformations?
options: The length and width of the damage and amount of deflection.
The area of the damage.
The amount of deflection.
A photograph of the deformation with details of its location.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: The length and width of the damage and amount of deflection.

CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.question: What has caused the crack found in the tank structure illustrated in the drawing?
options: Stress concentration.
Electrochemical action.
Welding failure.
Corrosion following coating failure.
CD0584 — Tank inspection, Ballast compar.answer: Stress concentration.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which of the following indicates that boundary cooling is effective?
options: Steel surfaces stay wet for longer each time cooling is stopped to make a check.
Paint on the bulkhead blisters and becomes detached.
The bulkhead begins to warp, buckle or distort.
Water spray turns to steam without wetting the surface at all.
Yes, that’s correct! If surfaces stay wet for longer, it indicates that the temperature is dropping and cooling is being effective.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Steel surfaces stay wet for longer each time cooling is stopped to make a check.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which one of the following statements is correct in respect of boundary cooling?
options: When compared, the vaporisation technique is six times more thermally effective in drawing heat from a compartment than the defensive technique.
When compared, the defensive technique is six times more thermally effective in drawing heat from a compartment than the vaporisation technique.
When compared, the defensive technique is ten times more thermally effective in drawing heat from a compartment than the vaporisation technique.
When compared, the vaporisation technique is ten times more thermally effective in drawing heat from a compartment than the defensive technique.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: When compared, the vaporisation technique is six times more thermally effective in drawing heat from a compartment than the defensive technique.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: What does boundary cooling do when applied to bulkheads?
options: It increases their resistance to the transmission of heat, flame and smoke.
It increases their resistance to the transmission of heat and flames, but has no effect on the smoke.
It increases their resistance to the transmission of heat and sound.
It decreases their resistance to the transmission of heat, flame and smoke.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: It increases their resistance to the transmission of heat, flame and smoke.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which of these indicators tells you that boundary cooling is working?
options: Steel surfaces stay wet for longer each time cooling is stopped to make a check.
Paint on the bulkhead blisters and becomes detached.
The bulkhead begins to warp, buckle or distort.
Water spray turns to steam without wetting the surface at all.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Steel surfaces stay wet for longer each time cooling is stopped to make a check.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: On what type of surface is boundary cooling most effective?

Boundary cooling is most effective on epoxy coated steel or metal structures.
Boundary cooling is most effective on fireproof composite panels or structures.
Boundary cooling is most effective on decorative panels covering painted steel or other metal structures.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Boundary cooling is most effective on bare steel or metal structures.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: When applying water to vertical surfaces, where should it be mainly directed?
options: At the upper part.
At the lower part.
At the central part.
At the whole area equally.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: At the upper part.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which of the following would provide the easiest route for fire to spread from one compartment to another?

Transmission of heat through fire rated steel bulkheads.
Transmission of heat or flames through closed doors.
Transmission of heat or flames through cable ducts.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Transmission of heat or flames through air conditioning and ventilation systems.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which of these is the most important way of slowing the spread of a developed fire?
options: Fire boundary cooling.
Fire boundary penetration and removal.
Rapid deployment of a fire extinguishing team.
Closing doors to adjacent spaces.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Fire boundary cooling.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: What is the likely maximum number of boundaries that could be considered to be adjacent to a compartment fire?
options: Six.
Four.
Two.
Eight.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Six.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: At what stage is fire easiest to extinguish?
options: Ignition.
Growth.
Fully developed.
Decay.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Ignition.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: For boundary cooling team members, which of these correctly identifies two of the possible dangers associated with using the vaporisation technique?
