Increased risk of burns on exposed skin and asphyxiation of team members.
Increased risk of heat stroke and failure of the SCBA.
Increased risk of backdraft and burns on exposed skin.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Increased risk of burns on exposed skin and decreased team endurance.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which tactic is preferred when the aim is to contain a compartment fire and prevent its spread, allowing it to be extinguished by deprivation of air or fuel, or by other fixed systems?
options: Defensive boundary cooling.
Vaporisation boundary cooling.
Aggressive boundary cooling.
Steam boundary cooling.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Defensive boundary cooling.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: At high temperatures, fuel in a compartment continues to burn even if it is deprived of air. If an additional supply of oxygen is introduced by opening a door or vent, explosive combustion will result. What is this known as?
options: Backdraft.
Flashover.
Flashout.
Backflash.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Backdraft.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: When boundary cooling, why should water be mainly directed at the upper part of vertical structures?
options: This is likely to be the hottest part.
Gravity will make the water run downward, so it will get maximum coverage with least effort from the team.
So that the team can stay beneath the protective curtain of water generated.
If the water turns to steam it will remain high up in the compartment and be less of a danger to the team.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: This is likely to be the hottest part.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: What is it known as when fuel sources in the room ignite almost simultaneously during the fully developed stage of a fire?
options: Flashover.
Backdraft.
Flashout.
Backflash.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Flashover.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: When using the vaporisation technique for boundary cooling, which of the following is correct?
options: Spray or mist nozzles are used to wet the bulkheads, deckheads and decks around the fire.
The steel structures are cooled by conduction when water jets are directed onto the surfaces.
The volume of water used should be sufficient to absorb a large quantity of heat, but not enough to produce steam.
Any type of nozzle or water pattern can be used.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Spray or mist nozzles are used to wet the bulkheads, deckheads and decks around the fire.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which boundary cooling tactic is preferred when the fire must be extinguished through direct attack by the ship’s fire teams?
options: Vaporisation boundary cooling.
Defensive boundary cooling.
Aggressive boundary cooling.
Steam boundary cooling.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Vaporisation boundary cooling.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: Which of the following will best ensure that boundary cooling is as effective as possible?
options: Trained, competent personnel in the boundary cooling teams.
Any randomly chosen ship’s staff in the boundary cooling teams.
Only the ship’s junior officers in the boundary cooling teams.
Only the ship’s senior officers in the boundary cooling teams.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Trained, competent personnel in the boundary cooling teams.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: In which boundary cooling technique is the water on the compartment surfaces allowed to heat up and turn to steam, or boil off?
options: Vaporisation boundary cooling.
Defensive boundary cooling.
Aggressive boundary cooling.
Steam boundary cooling.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: Vaporisation boundary cooling.

CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.question: When boundary cooling, where should teams position themselves?
options: They should get as close to the surfaces to be cooled as possible, and stay low.
They should get as far away from the surfaces to be cooled as possible, and stay low.
They should get as close to the surfaces to be cooled as possible, and stay upright.
They should get as far from the surfaces to be cooled as possible, and stay upright.
CD0586 — Fire-fighting, Effective bounda.answer: They should get as close to the surfaces to be cooled as possible, and stay low.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Who is responsible for the information that is entered on an SCBA identification tag?
options: The tags should be completed by the SCBA set wearer and the information confirmed by the Control Board Officer.
The tags should be completed by the SCBA set wearer and the information confirmed by the other SCBA team member.
The tags should be completed by the SCBA set wearer.
The tags should be completed by the Control Board Officer and the information confirmed by the SCBA set wearer.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The tags should be completed by the SCBA set wearer and the information confirmed by the Control Board Officer.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: When is it permitted for team members to break the seal on their face mask?
options: When all team members are out and tags have been removed from the SCBA control board.
As soon as any team member is out.
When all team members are out and clear of the incident entry point.
When all team members are out and permission is given by the SCBA Control Board Officer.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: When all team members are out and tags have been removed from the SCBA control board.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: An SCBA set is fitted with a 9 litre cylinder which is charged to 300 bar. What volume of breathable air does this set contain?
options: 2700 litres.
3600 litres.
900 litres.
180 litres.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: 2700 litres.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: What is the status of an SCBA control board in respect of any incident investigation that may be required by the authorities?
options: It is regarded as an official documentary record of events.
It is regarded as an unofficial documentary record of events.
It is regarded as an unreliable documentary record of events.
It is regarded as a second hand documentary record of events.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: It is regarded as an official documentary record of events.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: What minimum information should be recorded on the SCBA control board as an SCBA team member is about to leave the control board location?
options: The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, the time of entry to the incident and expected exit.
The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, the time of entry to the incident, expected exit and records of communications.
The identity of the wearer and the cylinder pressure when entering.
The cylinder pressure when entering and the time of entry to the incident.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, the time of entry to the incident and expected exit.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Where should the SCBA Control Board Officer and control board be sited in relation to any fire or emergency incident?
options: As close as practicable but clear of any hazards.
As close as possible so long as hazards are only smoke.
At least 30 metres from the entry point to the incident.
Never more than 5 metres from the entry point to the incident.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: As close as practicable but clear of any hazards.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: An SCBA set is fitted with a 9 litre cylinder that is charged to 300 bar. The wearer is breathing at 60 litres per minute. How long will this set supply air?
options: 30 minutes.
20 minutes.
40 minutes.
10 minutes.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: 30 minutes.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: What are SCBA set identification tags?
options: SCBA set identification tags are a detachable part of each SCBA set and are numbered or otherwise marked to correspond to the identification on the set itself.
SCBA set identification tags are a secured part of each SCBA set and are numbered or otherwise permanently marked to identify the set in itself in case of fire damage.
SCBA set identification tags are a secure part of each SCBA set used by the manufacturer for quality control of parts manufacture.
SCBA set identification tags are a detachable part of each SCBA set and are marked with the user’s name so that each emergency team member can identify their own set.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: SCBA set identification tags are a detachable part of each SCBA set and are numbered or otherwise marked to correspond to the identification on the set itself.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: An SCBA wearer is using a set equipped with a 9 litre cylinder charged to 300 bar pressure. Which of these factors is likely to cause the greatest variation from the calculated/expected duration of this set during use?
options: The breathing rate of the wearer.
The temperature of the environment in which it is being used.
The temperature of the air in the cylinder.
The distance from the control point to the incident.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The breathing rate of the wearer.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: An SCBA team leaves the SCBA control point with pressure gauges reading 280 bar. When they arrive at the scene of the fire, the lowest gauge reading is 240 bar. If the safety margin is set at 50 bar, at what pressure gauge reading should the team begin to return to the control point?
options: 90 bar.
150 bar.
120 bar.
50 bar.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: 90 bar.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: What minimum information should be recorded on an SCBA identification tag before it is inserted in the SCBA control board?
options: The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, and the time of entry to the incident.
The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, the time of entry to the incident and expected exit.
The identity of the wearer and the cylinder pressure when entering.
The cylinder pressure when entering, and the time of entry to the incident.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The identity of the wearer, the cylinder pressure when entering, and the time of entry to the incident.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: When should breathing apparatus control boards be used?
options: Every time SCBA sets are being used.
Only when they are used in search and rescue operations.
Only when they are used to fight fires in enclosed spaces.
Only when they are used by inexperienced SCBA wearers.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: Every time SCBA sets are being used.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Which of these statements is correct in respect of the amount of air an SCBA set wearer will use during drills or emergencies?
options: Specific individual consumption varies depending on physical condition, workload and psychological state.
Consumption does not vary significantly from individual to individual.
Specific individual consumption varies depending on the type of SCBA used, manufacturer and age of the version in use.
Specific individual consumption varies depending on height, nationality and physical genotype.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: Specific individual consumption varies depending on physical condition, workload and psychological state.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: There is a cabin fire in the accommodation block of a small bulk carrier. What number of SCBA entry/exit control points would expect to be set up to fight this fire?
options: One.
Two.
Three.
None.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: One.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Once the “time to the alarm” has been calculated for an SCBA set, what minimum safety margin should be applied?
options: 10 minutes.
5 minutes.
20 minutes.
It depends on the distance from the control point to entry into the incident area.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: 10 minutes.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: How is the breathable air in an SCBA cylinder usually calculated?
options: Multiply the volume of the cylinder by the charge pressure.
Divide the charge pressure by the volume of the cylinder.
Multiply the volume of the cylinder by the charge pressure and subtract 50 litres.
Divide the charge pressure by the volume of the cylinder and add 100 litres.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: Multiply the volume of the cylinder by the charge pressure.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Which of these is a principal aim of the messaging protocol that is used between SCBA team members and the SCBA Control Board Officer?
options: To limit air consumption.
To limit communication.
To maximise radio battery life.
To limit radio interference.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: To limit air consumption.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Which of the following is correct with respect to the duration calculator or table that forms part of an SCBA control board?
options: It must be calibrated for the volumes and pressures of the specific SCBA set cylinders in use.
It must be calibrated for the breathing rates of the specific SCBA set wearers in the team.
It must be calibrated to a standard volume and pressure setting as required by IMO’s fire safety code.
The calibration must be re-validated at least once every year by the manufacturer.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: It must be calibrated for the volumes and pressures of the specific SCBA set cylinders in use.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: A ship’s four man SCBA team has been split into two parties to conduct accommodation searches through two entry doors. How many SCBA control boards should be used in this instance?
options: Two – one at each entry/exit point.
One – the number of SCBA teams is the controlling factor for the number of SCBA control boards.
Three – one at each entry/exit location and one master control board.
Four – one for each SCBA wearer.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: Two – one at each entry/exit point.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: To whom should the SCBA Control Board Officer directly report?
options: The on scene commander.
The bridge or command team.
The Master.
The support team leader.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The on scene commander.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Typically, which of the ship’s emergency teams will directly control the operations of the SCBA Control Board Officer and the SCBA team?
options: The emergency team.
The bridge or command team.
The support team.
The engine room team.
Yes, that’s correct! Typically, the SCBA team and Control Board Officer will be part of the ship’s emergency team.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The emergency team.

CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.question: Typically, which of the ship’s emergency teams will directly control the operations of the SCBA Control Board Officer and the SCBA team?
options: The emergency team.
The bridge or command team.
The support team.
The engine room team.
Yes, that’s correct! Typically, the SCBA team and Control Board Officer will be part of the ship’s emergency team.
Yes, that’s correct! Typically, the SCBA team and Control Board Officer will be part of the ship’s emergency team.
CD0587 — SCBA, Effective control in an e.answer: The emergency team.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ^M‘In respect to fire drills, SOLAS requires that seafarers…’
options: ‘…are familiar with the location and operation of all firefighting systems and appliances.’
‘…are familiar with the regulations of SOLAS.’
‘…receive instructions on fire safety from the ship’s master.’
‘…are trained to operate firefighting equipment in specialised shore-based firefighting schools.’
CD0591 — Effective fire drills.answer: ‘…are familiar with the location and operation of all firefighting systems and appliances.’

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the following should be completed during preparations to conduct a fire drill?
options: Development of performance standards.
Testing of hoses and equipment to be used.
Testing of communication equipment.
Timing of mustering procedure.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Who should be involved in the debrief following every fire drill?
options: Everyone who has been involved.
Senior officers only.
Fire team leaders only.
The master, ship’s safety officer and fire team leaders only.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the following helps to create more effective fire drills?
options: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.
Mustering at the correct muster stations.
Use of Fireman’s outfits and rescue equipment during the drill.
Testing of communications between fire teams and team members.
CD0591 — Effective fire drills.answer: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the following BEST describes the state in which it is important for personnel to practice taking effective action during fire drills?
options: Stressed.
Happy.
Agitated.
Nervous.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the options describes the three sections of a drill?
options: Drill initiation – Firefighting activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Firefighting activity.
Pre drill preparations – Firefighting activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Post drill activity.
CD0591 — Effective fire drills.answer: Drill initiation – Firefighting activity – Post drill activity.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Why is it important that the debrief includes everyone who took part in the drill?
options: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.
Because it is required by SOLAS regulations.
So that bad judgements about procedures are not made.
Team members must be guided by team leaders at all times.
CD0591 — Effective fire drills.answer: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘Plans for fire drills should…’
options: ‘…be as specific as possible.’
‘…be as flexible as possible.’
‘…not take equipment into account.’
‘…not consider the personnel involved.’

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the options below should be considered when planning a fire drill?
options: The location of the drill.
The cost of the equipment to be used or tested.
The working time lost.
The volume of the fire alarm.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the following describes the four elements that all effective training and drills will include?
options: Planning, Preparation, Execution and Evaluation.
Approval, Preparation, Execution and Observation.
Planning, Approval, Execution and Evaluation.
Planning, Preparation, Observation and Execution.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the following must be tested as part of a fire drill?
options: Watertight doors.
Ventilation fans.
Personal gas monitoring equipment.
GMDSS.

CD0591 — Effective fire drills.question: Which of the methods below is a tactic deployed during a drill to control the possible spread of a fire?
options: Boundary cooling.
Opening fire dampers.
Electrical isolation of the area.
Deploying extra personnel to each hose team.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the options describes the three sections of a drill?
options: Drill initiation – Abandon ship activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Abandon ship activity.
Pre drill preparations – Abandon ship activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Post drill activity.
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: Drill initiation – Abandon ship activity – Post drill activity.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following helps to create more effective abandon ship drills?
options: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.
Mustering at the correct muster stations.
Use of equipment during the drill.
Testing of communications between boat teams and team members.
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the options below should be considered first when planning an abandon ship drill?
options: The type of drill and associated risks.
The cost of the equipment to be used or tested.
The working time lost.
The type of lifeboats and time since the last drill.
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: The type of drill and associated risks.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘In respect to abandon ship drills, SOLAS requires that seafarers…’
options: ‘…are familiar with their assigned emergency duties.’
‘…are familiar with the regulations of SOLAS.’
‘…receive instructions on abandon ship drill safety from the ship’s Master.’
‘…are trained to operate survival craft in specialised shore-based training schools.’
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: ‘…are familiar with their assigned emergency duties.’

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following describes the four elements that all effective training and drills will include?
options: Planning, Preparation, Execution and Evaluation.
Approval, Preparation, Execution and Observation.
Planning, Approval, Execution and Evaluation.
Planning, Preparation, Observation and Execution.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following must be tested as part of an abandon ship drill?
options: Lifeboats and their launching apparatus.
Lifebuoys and their attachments.
Line throwing appliances.
GMDSS.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘Plans for abandon ship drills should…’
options: ‘…be as specific as possible.’
‘…be as flexible as possible.’
‘…not take equipment into account.’
‘…not consider the personnel involved.’

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the methods below is a tactic deployed during a drill to calm proceedings?
options: Methodical mustering and checking each other’s lifejackets.
Personnel checking their own lifejackets and standing in orderly rows.
Setting fast targets for the preparation of the survival craft.
Deploying extra personnel to each survival craft preparation team.
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: Methodical mustering and checking each other’s lifejackets.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Why is it important that the debrief includes everyone who took part in the drill?
options: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.
Because it is required by SOLAS regulations.
So that bad judgements about procedures are not made.
Team members must be guided by team leaders at all times.
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Who should be involved in the debrief following every abandon ship drill?
options: Everyone who has been involved.
Senior officers only.
The coxswain or boat team leaders only.
The master, ship’s safety officer and boat team leaders only.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following best completes the following sentence? ‘The debrief should take place…’
options: ‘…as soon as possible after the drill.’
‘…the day after the drill has taken place.’
‘…only if there has been an incident during the drill.’
‘…in the Master’s office with only the senior officers.’
CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.answer: ‘…as soon as possible after the drill.’

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following should be completed during preparations to conduct an abandon ship drill?
options: Development of performance standards.
Testing of hoses and equipment to be used.
Testing of communication equipment.
Timing of mustering procedure.

CD0592 — Effective lifeboat drills.question: Which of the following BEST describes the state in which it is important for personnel to practice taking effective action during abandon ship drills?
options: Stressed.
Happy.
Agitated.
Nervous.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the following must be tested as part of a security drill?
options: Controlling access to the vessel.
Preparing to launch the rescue boat.
Ship evacuation at sea.
Monitoring cargo operations.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the options describes the three sections of a drill?
options: Drill initiation – Security drill activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Security drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Security drill activity – Post drill activity.
Pre drill preparations – Drill initiation – Post drill activity.
CD0593 — Effective security drills.answer: Drill initiation – Security drill activity – Post drill activity.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘In respect to security drills, ISPS requires that all seafarers…’
options: ‘…are familiar with their assigned security duties.’
‘…are familiar with the regulations of SOLAS.’
‘…receive instruction on security drill safety from the ship’s master.’
‘…are trained to operate security equipment in specialised shore-based training schools.’
CD0593 — Effective security drills.answer: ‘…are familiar with their assigned security duties.’

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the following BEST describes the state in which it is important for personnel to practice taking effective action during security drills?
options: Stressed.
Happy.
Agitated.
Nervous.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the methods below is a tactic deployed during a drill to control the possible panic of crew members?
options: Methodical mustering.
Setting fast targets for the preparation of the security equipment.
Shouting criticism at underperforming team members.
Deploying extra personnel to each security team.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the following helps to create more effective security drills?
options: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.
Mustering at the correct muster stations.
Use of equipment during the drill.
Testing of communications between security teams and the command team.
CD0593 — Effective security drills.answer: Unexpected elements, such as unplanned equipment failures.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the options below should be completed during preparations to conduct a security drill?
options: Development of performance standards.
Testing of security equipment to be used.
Testing of communication equipment.
Timing of mustering procedure.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Why is it important that the debrief includes everyone who took part in the drill?
options: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.
Because it is required by SOLAS regulations.
So that bad judgements about procedures are not made.
Team members must be guided by team leaders at all times.
CD0593 — Effective security drills.answer: Team leaders do not see everything that happens, so it is important that other viewpoints are included.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Who should be involved in the debrief following every security drill?
options: Everyone involved.
Senior officers only.
Security team leaders only.
The master, ship’s security officer and team leaders only.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the options below should be considered when planning a security drill?
options: The dangers and risks inherent to the drill.
The cost of the equipment to be used or tested.
The working time lost.
The number of visitors expected.
CD0593 — Effective security drills.answer: The dangers and risks inherent to the drill.

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the options BEST completes the following sentence? ‘Plans for security drills should…’
options: ‘…be as specific as possible.’
‘…be as flexible as possible.’
‘…not take equipment into account.’
‘…not consider the personnel involved.’

CD0593 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the following describes the four elements that all effective training and drills will include?
options: Planning, Preparation, Execution and Evaluation.
Approval, Preparation, Execution and Observation.
Planning, Approval, Execution and Evaluation.
Planning, Preparation, Observation and Execution.

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the options BEST COMPLETES the following sentence? ‘If there is a defect or deficiency on any equipment under your care…’
options: ‘…it is always best to prepare your honest answer before the inspection.’
‘…it is always best to pretend that it doesn’t exist.’
‘…it is always best to hide the defect or deficiency from the inspector.’
‘…it is always best to pass the deficient or defective equipment to someone more experienced.’
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: ‘…it is always best to prepare your honest answer before the inspection.’

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: How should someone claiming to be an inspector be welcomed on board?
options: Confirm their identity and then welcome them on board in a friendly manner
Welcome on board anyone claiming to be an inspector in a friendly manner, without checking their ID
Adopt a forceful attitude to show that security is taken seriously on board the vessel
Refuse entry to anyone claiming to be an inspector until the Chief Officer has had sufficient time to prepare the vessel
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: Confirm their identity and then welcome them on board in a friendly manner

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the options BEST COMPLETES the following sentence? ‘PSCO nspections check that…’
options: ‘…the ship and its equipment are in a safe working condition and that the officers and crew can safely operate it.’
‘…the ship and its equipment appear to be in good condition at first glance.’
‘…crewmembers know what to say to pass the inspection.’
‘…crewmembers follow all orders given to them by the officers on board.’
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: ‘…the ship and its equipment are in a safe working condition and that the officers and crew can safely operate it.’

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: What should be done with the inspector once they have cleared security?
options: They should be escorted to the Master or an appointed deputy
They should be left to inspect the ship by themselves
They should be directed to the Master’s office and left to find their own way
You should escort them directly to the Master, leaving the gangway temporarily unguarded if necessary
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: They should be escorted to the Master or an appointed deputy

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: What is the MOST LIKELY consequence of a Port State inspector forming a negative impression of a vessel prior to and after boarding?
options: A more detailed inspection
The vessel being detained
A fine
The inspector will not form an impression until they are on board

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why the inspector may ask you to operate machinery or equipment?
options: To try to make you make a mistake in a high pressure environment
To see if the equipment works and is not defective
To see if you are familiar with the equipment or system
To see if you know and follow the procedure relating to it
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: To try to make you make a mistake in a high pressure environment

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: What is the worst case scenario if your vessel is found to have many or serious deficiencies that cannot be resolved immediately?
options: The vessel is detained
The vessel is prevented from sailing at the planned time
The charterer would receive a negative report on the vessel prior to it being allowed to depart
The owner would have to pay a fine before the vessel is allowed to sail

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the following would result in the inspector forming the most favourable impression on the gangway?
options: Gangway properly rigged with a safety net and a lifebuoy and light available
Gangway properly rigged
Gangway properly rigged with a safety net
Gangway guarded by four crewmembers
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: Gangway properly rigged with a safety net and a lifebuoy and light available

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: When will the inspector start to form an impression of the vessel?
options: Before boarding
As they board the vessel
Upon meeting the Master
Once the inspector meets the Chief Officer

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the following may make the inspector think that you are not competent at operating a piece of machinery?
options: You have to read the instructions
You check that you have permission to operate it
You speak slowly, clearly and confidently, maintaining eye contact
You explain what is happening and what you might expect to happen next
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: You have to read the instructions

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the following is NOT a common deficiency on deck?
options: A replacement lifebuoy
Wrongly rigged lifeboat painter securing arrangement
Lifeboat release mechanism is in poor condition
Air vent flaps are in poor condition

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Who out of the following may be required to speak with the inspector?
options: Everyone
The Master
All senior officers
All officers

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: The inspector will speak with officers and crew to check that they speak in a common language. Which of the following is NOT a reason why the inspector will speak to officers and crew?
options: To trick crewmembers into admitting a deficiency
To gain an understanding of conditions on board
To understand how the ship is managed
To see how well the officers and crew are able to perform their duties
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: To trick crewmembers into admitting a deficiency

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: During an inspection, the inspector asks you to operate a piece of machinery and you find that it is defective. Which of the following actions is likely to impress the inspector?
options: Advising the appropriate senior officer as soon as possible
Explaining slowly and confidently why the defect is not your fault
Guessing what caused the defect
Demonstrating how the defective equipment would work and then continuing with the inspection
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: Advising the appropriate senior officer as soon as possible

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: During an inspection, if you are unsure of an answer to a question, what should you do?
options: Tell the inspector that you don’t know and then seek information from a more senior person
Confidently guess the answer and hope the inspector doesn’t notice
Answer a different question that you do know the answer to
Keep asking the inspector to repeat the question until they give up
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: Tell the inspector that you don’t know and then seek information from a more senior person

CD0594 — Ship inspections.question: Which of the following best completes the following sentence? ‘If you are asked a question by an inspector…’
options: ‘…answer them clearly and confidently, and only answer the questions asked.’
‘…speak clearly and confidently about a subject you know a lot about to show them how competent you are.’
‘…keep your answers as brief as possible so that you don’t make a mistake.’
‘…answer it by asking a question of your own until they seem satisfied.’
Yes, that’s correct! The inspector wants to see whether you know the answer to their question, and so they may become frustrated if you answer a question they didn’t ask.
No, that is incorrect. The inspector wants to see that you can clearly and confidently answer the question they have asked.
CD0594 — Ship inspections.answer: ‘…answer them clearly and confidently, and only answer the questions asked.’

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: A seafarer has an accident whilst carrying out a familiar task that does not require a lot of conscious thought. What type of human error is this classified as?
options: An action error (sometimes called slips and lapses).
A thinking error.
A mistake.
A violation.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: An action error (sometimes called slips and lapses).

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Who should undertake maintenance of safety equipment?
options: Trained, competent personnel.
Any of the ship’s staff.
Only the ship’s junior officers.
Only the ship’s senior officers.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Thinking errors are decision making failures. These can occur when we think we are doing the right thing, but lack the knowledge or skill to make the correct decision or judgement. Which of the following is a good strategy for avoiding these errors?
options: Stop and ask for help. Get the training and experience necessary before accepting responsibility for a task.
Stop and go back to the beginning and try again until you get it right.
Don’t worry. Everybody makes this type of error to begin with. Just carry on.
Make sure you get someone else to do the task.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Stop and ask for help. Get the training and experience necessary before accepting responsibility for a task.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Regulations and guidelines often form the basis of maintenance and inspection programmes. What should be borne in mind when following these programmes aboard ship?
options: The regulations and guidelines might not cover all the possible deficiencies or events.
The regulations and guidelines are the only information that needs to be consulted.
The maintenance and inspection programmes must never exceed the regulations.
The maintenance should always take place after the time required in the regulation.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: The regulations and guidelines might not cover all the possible deficiencies or events.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Which of the following is a good strategy for avoiding mistakes?
options: Make sure you understand the instructions. If you are unclear, ask for clarification and always confirm by repeating your understanding of an instruction.
Make sure that you get all instructions in writing, read them carefully, and sign them when you understand everything that you are to do.
Don't worry. Mistakes are how we learn. The more mistakes you make, the better you will learn the task.
Make sure you get someone else to do the task.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Make sure you understand the instructions. If you are unclear, ask for clarification and always confirm by repeating your understanding of an instruction.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: During a lifeboat drill, as you are mustering at your assigned lifeboat, you notice that it does not seem to be sitting correctly on its chocks. What action should be taken?
options: Report it to the officer in charge and stop the drill until the reason for the boats position is discovered.
Carry on with the drill. Lifeboats move all the time in their davits. This will cause no problem.
Point it out to the person next to you and ask them what they think about it.
Make sure you stand back and are not chosen to be a crewmember if the boat is to be lowered or launched.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Report it to the officer in charge and stop the drill until the reason for the boats position is discovered.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: At sea, an off watch AB discovers that a fire extinguisher is missing from its mounting bracket in the messroom. What action should they take?
options: Report it immediately to the officer on watch or supervisor.
Go and find another extinguisher from a less used part of the accommodation block and replace the one missing from the messroom.
Nothing. The messroom is not the responsibility of the ABs.
Report it to the officer of the watch or supervisor when they go back on watch.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Report it immediately to the officer on watch or supervisor.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Why do accidents keep happening even with planned maintenance and inspection systems in place?
options: Accidents can be due to deficiencies in standards and/or deficiencies in execution of procedures.
Accidents are always due to deficiencies in procedures.
Accidents are always due to people making mistakes.
Accidents are due to deficiencies in machinery and deficiencies in training.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Accidents can be due to deficiencies in standards and/or deficiencies in execution of procedures.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Regulations require that portable fire extinguishers must be tested by being discharged at five year intervals. What type of maintenance is this an example of?
options: Planned maintenance.
Condition based maintenance.
Age based maintenance.
Deficiency based maintenance.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Why is it good practice to combine maintenance inspections of safety equipment with inspection before drills or emergency use and general surveillance by all the ship’s crewmembers?
options: To make sure everyone is taking some responsibility for the safety equipment. Its condition and readiness will therefore be better maintained, and accidents reduced.
To make sure that the crew learn where the safety equipment is located and that they are encouraged to take care of it.
It is not good practice to have ship’s crewmembers involved in inspection of safety equipment as they might damage it.
This practice helps everyone in the crew become better team members.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: To make sure everyone is taking some responsibility for the safety equipment. Its condition and readiness will therefore be better maintained, and accidents reduced.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: A seafarer has an accident whilst using equipment that they are unfamiliar with. What type of human error is this classified as?
options: A thinking error.
An action error (sometimes called slips and lapses).
A mistake.
A violation.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Most safety and risk management systems are based on creating multiple barriers to prevent accidents. In every model of this kind, what or who provides the final accident prevention barrier?
options: The personnel.
The operating procedures.
Physical barrier.
Equipment design.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: In what condition must safety equipment be maintained?
options: Clean, undamaged and ready for use.
Clean and undamaged.
Ready for use.
Properly stowed, clean and undamaged.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Clean, undamaged and ready for use.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Which of the following is regarded as an integral part of a good safety culture?
options: Everyone accepting personal responsibility for reporting or dealing with defects or deficiencies.
Personnel knowing who is responsible for dealing with each type of defect or deficiency and sending them a text.
Personnel not following procedures so that safety equipment maintenance can be completed more quickly.
Working with other personnel and chatting together whilst completing safety equipment maintenance tasks.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Everyone accepting personal responsibility for reporting or dealing with defects or deficiencies.

CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.question: Which of the following correctly describes condition based maintenance?
options: Condition based maintenance is where equipment is maintained based on the outcome of an inspection of the state of the item.
Condition based maintenance is where equipment is maintained based on the time it has been in service.
Condition based maintenance is where equipment is maintained based on instructions from the Chief Officer.
Condition based maintenance is where all maintenance and inspection is undertaken by the ship’s officers.
Yes, that’s correct!
No, that is incorrect. Condition based maintenance is where equipment is maintained based on the outcome of an inspection of the state of the item.
CD0595 — Inspection and maintenance of s.answer: Condition based maintenance is where equipment is maintained based on the outcome of an inspection of the state of the item.

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: When is it important to familiarise yourself with a vessel?
options: Every time you join a vessel
The first time you join a vessel
Only when joining a vessel as a cadet
Only when joining a new vessel type
Yes, that’s correct! You should familiarise yourself with a vessel every time you join.
No, that is incorrect. You should familiarise yourself with a vessel every time you join.
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: Every time you join a vessel

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the options BEST COMPLETES the following sentence? ‘Engaging fully with the ship familiarisation program will help you to work safer, be more productive and increase your enjoyment of the ship environment…’
options: ‘…whether you are joining a ship for the first time or re-joining.’
‘…when you join a ship for the first time.’
‘…but only when you have already been on the ship.’
‘…if you wait until you are fully familiarised before starting your duties.’
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: ‘…whether you are joining a ship for the first time or re-joining.’

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: ‘During an emergency, uncertainty increases response time and the risk of accidents for everyone on board.’
‘During an emergency, uncertain individuals will only affect their own safety.’
‘During an emergency, response time is not affected by uncertain individuals as long as the key members of the emergency team are present.’
‘During an emergency, uncertainty will always lead to an accident, possibly resulting in death.’
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: ‘During an emergency, uncertainty increases response time and the risk of accidents for everyone on board.’

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: It is important to actively engage in the familiarisation process
It is important to only do what is asked of you during the familiarisation process
Reading through the procedures will be sufficient to familiarise you with the vessel
The familiarisation process is the responsibility of the officer in charge, so just relax and enjoy it
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: It is important to actively engage in the familiarisation process

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following BEST COMPLETES the following sentence? ‘A principal rule is that you should…’
options: ‘…never work with equipment you are not trained to use.’
‘…only work with equipment you are not trained to use if there is an experienced first aider nearby.’
‘…never work with equipment that has a sharp edge.’
‘…only work with equipment that you can take apart and reassemble.’
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: ‘…never work with equipment you are not trained to use.’

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following will NOT be included in your vessel’s SMS?
options: The Master’s standing orders
Drug and alcohol policy
Disciplinary procedures
Smoking regulations

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: What is the BEST way to find out where your muster station will be in an emergency?
options: Check the Muster List
Ask a fellow crewmember
Ask the Master
You don’t need to know. Just report to the nearest muster station when you hear an alarm

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: What effect does familiarisation have on the number of accidents on board a vessel? Select the BEST answer.
options: Reduced number of accidents
Increased awareness of the causes of accidents
It has no effect
Reduced severity of accidents that do occur

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following should NOT be given priority at the start of a familiarisation program for a member of the deck crew?
options: Bridge watchkeeping procedures
Emergency muster stations
Firefighting duties
Operation of equipment used in role

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why on board familiarisation should be undertaken as quickly as possible?
options: Senior officers are unwilling to spend a prolonged period helping newcomers become familiar on board
Smaller crews require everyone on board to understand their role
Familiarisation helps create stronger teams and a positive environment on board
All crewmembers must be familiarised so that they know how to respond in an emergency
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: Senior officers are unwilling to spend a prolonged period helping newcomers become familiar on board

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: According to this module, which of the following is NOT a typical response when personal safety is threatened?
options: Faint
Fight
Flight
Freeze

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: How quickly should you be able to put a lifejacket on?
options: Under one minute
Under two minutes
Under five minutes
Less than five seconds

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Which of the following BEST COMPLETES the following sentence? ‘Familiarisation programs are essential, as they…
options: …inform you of the correct actions to take in an emergency, whilst enabling you to do your job safely and effectively.
…are required by regulations and must be completed to show compliance.
…focus solely on the actions to take in an emergency.
…give you the opportunity to tell people on board the ship how to do their job better.
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: …inform you of the correct actions to take in an emergency, whilst enabling you to do your job safely and effectively.

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: Where are each company’s ship familiarisation procedures and checklists found?
options: SMS
Personnel handbook
Master’s standing orders
They are issued by the company prior to boarding

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: What is the BEST way to check that you are familiar with the nearest accommodation exit and route to your muster station?
options: Walk the route from your cabin to the exit and muster station
Identify the route on the vessel plan
Wait until an emergency and follow your fellow crewmembers
Talk through the route with colleagues
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: Walk the route from your cabin to the exit and muster station

CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.question: In what time period is a crewmember required to be trained in the use of the ship’s lifesaving and firefighting appliances?
options: Within two weeks of coming on board
Within two months of coming on board
Within two hours of coming on board
Before they are allowed on board
CD0596 — On board familiarisation, Intro.answer: Within two weeks of coming on board

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Which of the answers most accurately describes what happens when gas starts to leak from a tank container?
options: There may not be immediate indications of leakage.
Odour will always be the first sign of escape or leakage of gas or vapour.
The pressure gauge reading will always be seen to fall.
The sound of the PRD activating will always be the first sign of leakage.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: There may not be immediate indications of leakage.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: What would the following sign indicate when seen on the side of a portable tank container?
options: It is the UN number of the dangerous goods in the tank.
It is a code to indicate the size and type of tank container.
It is a number representing the code of the owner of the tank container.
It is a numbered code indicating the country of origin of the tank container.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: It is the UN number of the dangerous goods in the tank.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Where can specific information be found for dealing with a fire involving hazardous liquids from portable tank containers?
options: IMDG code SUPPLEMENT.
IMDG Code Volume 1.
IMDG Code Volume 2.
Hazardous cargo manifest.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: According to the IMDG code, what colour rectangle must be used to display the UN number on the shell of a tank container holding dangerous goods?
options: Orange.
White.
Yellow and black diagonal stripes.
Black.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: On a tank container with a bottom opening, how many devices must be fitted to avoid possible leakage?
Which of the following abbreviations relates to emergency schedules in the IMDG code?
options: EmS.
Em-Sh.
ES.
ESh.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Which of the following containers is designed to carry up to 27,000 litres of dangerous liquid?
options: Portable tank container.
An enclosed container with the liquid in small packages.
Intermediate bulk container.
Multi Element Gas Container.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Which of the following might be an indication of a leakage of corrosive liquid?
options: Discolouration or the blistering of paint.
Smell of leaking chemicals.
Change in the level gauge.
The PRD will be heard to activate.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: Discolouration or the blistering of paint.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: In the event of a fire or spillage from a portable tank container, what document covers the initial response?
options: Contingency plan for shipboard emergencies.
The IMDG code.
The MSDS for the cargo(s) attached to the portable container.
The cargo handling procedures.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: In what way are the markings on this tank container incomplete or incorrect?
options: The UN number should include the UN number of the hazardous substance.
The UN number of the hazardous substance must always be displayed on an orange rectangle.
Substances with 5.1 must be carried in a type T23 container, not T11 as shown.
The elevated temperature symbol must always be displayed for hazard class indicated.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: The UN number should include the UN number of the hazardous substance.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Where is the pressure relief device located on a portable tank container?
options: Centre spill box.
Rear spill box.
Next to the bottom opening.
On the middle of the end of the tank, opposite the bottom opening.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Which of the following describes a Multi Element Gas Container?
options: An assembly of tubes and bundles of cylinders interconnected by a manifold contained within a framework.
A tank having a capacity of more than 450L fitted with service equipment and structural equipment necessary for the transport of refrigerated and non-refrigerated liquefied cargoes.
A flat rack container with structures containing portable gas cylinders, each of which is less than 47kg.
Two or more pressurised tanks supported in a steel frame and interconnected by a common manifold.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: An assembly of tubes and bundles of cylinders interconnected by a manifold contained within a framework.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Under the IMDG code, what is meant by an emergency schedule?
options: A table providing specific information for dealing with fire or spillage involving particular dangerous goods types.
A table providing specific information for dealing with injury or illness of those exposed to particular dangerous goods types.
A table providing specific information for dealing with fire involving particular dangerous goods types.
A table providing specific information for dealing with marine pollution involving particular dangerous goods types.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: A table providing specific information for dealing with fire or spillage involving particular dangerous goods types.

CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.question: Which of the following actions will BEST help you identify the name of the product contained in a portable tank container?
options: Enter the UN number into the Dangerous Goods List.
Enter the T-code into the Dangerous Goods List.
Enter the eleven digit container identification number into the Dangerous Goods List.
Check the hazard label on the portable tank.
CD0597 — Portable tanks, Carrying danger.answer: Enter the UN number into the Dangerous Goods List.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: To avoid detection, when are attempted stowaways most likely to board the vessel?
options: Shortly before the vessel is due to leave port.
When the vessel first berths, as everyone will be at their busiest.
During shift or watch changes as no-one will be looking then.
At lunchtime, because no one will be taking notice.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Shortly before the vessel is due to leave port.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of these places would be most attractive to someone attempting to hide and stowaway?
options: Under engine room bilge plates.
In one of the crew’s work gear locker.
In the galley pantry.
In the cargo office or control room.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Your ship is in port. Whilst going to the mess room you notice that the ventilator screen on a cabin door has been loosened. What should you do?
options: Inform your supervisor or an officer.
Set off the nearest fire alarm.
Open the door and investigate what might have caused it to come loose.
Fix the ventilator back in place as it is a safety hazard.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Inform your supervisor or an officer.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of the following items of PPE are recommended for search teams to wear?
options: Non-slip shoes or boots, protective coveralls, goggles, face mask, gloves and hard hat.
Non-slip shoes or boots, protective coveralls, facemask, gloves, knee pads and hard hat.
Non-slip shoes or boots, protective coveralls, goggles, shin pads, gloves, knee pads and hard hat.
Non-slip shoes or boots, protective coveralls, body armour, shin pads, gloves, knee pads and hard hat.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Non-slip shoes or boots, protective coveralls, goggles, face mask, gloves and hard hat.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of these is the most important factor in being able to detect whether an attempted stowaway might be in an accommodation space?
options: Familiarity with the space and its contents.
Having a checklist.
Good teamwork and communication skills.
Having a torch and radio.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Familiarity with the space and its contents.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Ideally, when should a pre-departure stowaway search take place?
options: After cargo is complete and all stevedores and other shore personnel are known to have left the ship.
After cargo is complete, but before all stevedores and other shore personnel have left the ship.
Before the cargo hatches are closed but after all stevedores and other personnel have left the ship.
After cargo operations where possible, but always before dark on the day of departure.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: After cargo is complete and all stevedores and other shore personnel are known to have left the ship.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of these is a danger that might be encountered during a pre-departure stowaway search?
options: Having to search an enclosed space.
Having to search the engine room.
Having to search an open cargo hold.
Having to search the accommodation.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Having to search an enclosed space.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What is the ship’s first line of defence against attempted stowaways?
options: Secure access procedures, including security patrols and monitoring people boarding the vessel whilst working cargo.
Secure access procedures, including security patrols and a quick pre-departure search.
Security guards at the dock gates and patrols around the terminal.
Dog patrols in the terminal grounds.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Secure access procedures, including security patrols and monitoring people boarding the vessel whilst working cargo.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: According to this module, which of the following actions is recommended after a space has been searched for attempted stowaways?
options: It should be locked or otherwise secured against subsequent entry.
It should be closed and marked with a “do not enter” sign.
A guard should be left at the entrance.
The door should be clearly marked with a black indelible marker as having been searched.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: It should be locked or otherwise secured against subsequent entry.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of these is possibly a sign that an attempted stowaway might be in a space?
options: An re-arranged stow of paint in the paint locker.
A smell of cooking.
A closed and locked hold access hatch.
An unopened sack of potatoes in the galley.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: An re-arranged stow of paint in the paint locker.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What is the recommended response to discovery of a stowaway or stowaways?
options: Immediately inform your supervisor and, if possible to do so safely, detain the stowaway in the space where they are discovered.
Immediately remove the stowaway to a safe place for interrogation.
Have the stowaway lie face down with their hands on their head.
Immediately inform the supervisor and then continue the search.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: Immediately inform your supervisor and, if possible to do so safely, detain the stowaway in the space where they are discovered.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of the following are key behaviours in achieving an effective stowaway search?
options: Being patient and methodical.
Being quick and impatient.
Being as fast as possible.
Being slow and careless.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What do attempted stowaways do when they enter a space where they are more likely to be found?
options: They hide and, in doing so, they often have to move or rearrange things into the wrong places.
They hide and, in doing so, they always leave footprints.
They hide and, in doing so, they will make noise that will be heard.
They hide and, in doing so, they damage equipment.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: They hide and, in doing so, they often have to move or rearrange things into the wrong places.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: According to this module, what is the recommended action if an attempted stowaway threatens you after being discovered?
options: Retreat and raise the alarm.
Overpower them and raise the alarm.
Call for help and fight back.
Close the door or hatch of the space and lock them in.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What are the organisational procedures that will lead to effective searches?
options: Good planning and diligent execution.
Good planning and fast execution.
Quick planning and fast execution.
Slow planning and fast execution.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What is the minimum number of personal that should be in a team searching a space for attempted stowaways?
What are the operational requirements of effective stowaway searches?
options: They are thorough and establish that the ship has no attempted stowaways aboard.
They find any stowaways before the ship reaches the next port.
They are as fast as possible, so the ship is not delayed.
They are thorough and conducted by trained shore-based personnel.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: They are thorough and establish that the ship has no attempted stowaways aboard.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: Which of these are signs that a stowaway might be in a space?
options: A storeroom door lock has been tampered with.
A locker door is closed but not locked in the work gear changing room.
The frozen provisions room temperature is low.
The door to the stationary locker, which is normally locked, is unlocked.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: A storeroom door lock has been tampered with.

CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.question: What is the difference between a stowaway and an attempted stowaway?
options: A stowaway is someone who has stayed on a ship without permission after the ship has left port. An attempted stowaway is someone who has stayed on a ship without permission and is found before the ship has left port.

An attempted stowaway is someone who has stayed on a ship without permission after the ship has left port. A stowaway is someone who stayed on a ship without permission and is found before the ship has left port.

An attempted stowaway is someone who has legally boarded the ship and is found aboard after the ship has left port. A stowaway is someone who has boarded the ship and is found aboard before the ship has left port.

A stowaway is someone who has legally boarded the ship and is found aboard after the ship has completed cargo. An attempted stowaway is someone who has legally boarded the ship and is still aboard, not realising that the ship has left port.
CD0598 — Search techniques, Ship and sto.answer: A stowaway is someone who has stayed on a ship without permission after the ship has left port. An attempted stowaway is someone who has stayed on a ship without permission and is found before the ship has left port.

CD0599 — Search techniques, Personnel an.question: Which of the following requires visitors to a ship to be searched either randomly or at specified time periods?
options: The Ship’s Security Plan.
The Ship’s Safety Management System.
The Ship’s Muster List.
The Ship’s Dangerous Goods List.

CD0599 — Search techniques, Personnel an.question: Which of the following is the BEST course of action to take if you cannot easily identify an object?
options: Politely ask the person what it is.
Refuse to let the visitor board the ship.
Take the object out of the bag to find out what it is.
Throw the object overboard.
CD0599 — Search techniques, Personnel an.answer: Politely ask the person what it is.

CD0599 — Search techniques, Personnel an.question: As a minimum, how many people should be part of a baggage search team?
According to this module, which of the following is the most important element in creating a suitable environment for searching personnel boarding the ship?
options: Ship’s crew demonstrate a polite, professional and courteous attitude to everyone coming aboard.
Ship’s crew stop and identify everyone coming aboard before searching them.
Posting of the search policy at the foot of the gangway.
