‘…not consider the personnel involved.’

CD2543 — Effective security drills.question: Which of the following describes the four elements that all effective training and drills will include?
options: Planning, Preparation, Execution and Evaluation.
Approval, Preparation, Execution and Observation.
Planning, Approval, Execution and Evaluation.
Planning, Preparation, Observation and Execution.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: When does an oil spill become oil pollution? Select the BEST answer.
options: When spilled oil enters the water.
Oil spilled will always enter the water, so it is always classed as oil pollution.
When the oil is on the side of the ship.
Oil pollution can only be as a result of an accidental overboard discharge of oil.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: When spilled oil enters the water.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: What is meant by an emergency pollution plan? Select the BEST answer.
options: A plan to prevent or minimise pollution.
A plan to satisfy the flag State requirements.
A plan held on board as a precautionary measure.
A plan to use if assisting another vessel with a clean up.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: A plan to prevent or minimise pollution.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: How does a crewmember know what their role is in the emergency pollution plan? Select the BEST answer.
options: They will be briefed for it and it may also be shown on the muster list.
They will have to consult the printed version of the plan.
When they join a vessel, they will be instructed by a senior officer.
They will not know it until there is an oil spill, in which case they will adopt one.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: They will be briefed for it and it may also be shown on the muster list.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Why should pollution from oil spills be avoided as much as possible? Select the BEST answer.
options: All of the other three answers are correct.
Damage to people and the environment.
Possible effect on the vessel charters.
Financial penalties and possible jail.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: All of the other three answers are correct.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Why is it important to have pollution drills? Select the BEST answer.
options: They ensure that planned procedures will work.
To stop non-conformances from an inspector.
It is not, as they just frustrate the crew.
Because the crew cannot be trusted to do it themselves.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: They ensure that planned procedures will work.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: During an oil spill response, what should the crew always have to stay safe? Select the BEST answer.
options: Good situational awareness.
A casual attitude.
A slow approach to working.
Good motion awareness.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: Good situational awareness.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Why should a vessel have an emergency pollution plan? Select the BEST answer.
options: To make sure the correct actions are taken when oil is spilled.
Because it is a requirement of MARPOL.
To be used to monitor the acceptable discharge of oil from bilges allowed under MARPOL.
To be able to log actions taken when the vessel has had a pollution incident.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: To make sure the correct actions are taken when oil is spilled.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Why should crew follow the guidance in an emergency pollution plan when there is an oil spill? Select the BEST answer.
options: There will already be a procedure in place to deal with such a spillage efficiently.
Because the chief officer will be annoyed if they do not.
Because it complies with MARPOL and the company’s emergency procedures.
Not following the plan may lead to a crewmember being blamed if the oil goes into the water.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: There will already be a procedure in place to deal with such a spillage efficiently.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Select the answer that BEST completes the following statement: ‘Positive behaviour means...’
options: ‘...having the correct attitude.’
‘...never criticising drills.’
‘...always doing ANYTHING that you are told to do.’
‘...never feeling tired when working.’
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: ‘...having the correct attitude.’

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘A chemical carrier will always have an individual SOPEP for oil and an SMPEP for chemicals.’
options: The statement is false.
The statement is true.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The statement is false.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Can crew using social media ever affect the vessel or its managing company? Select the BEST answer.
options: Yes, if their posts are damaging and seen by others.
Yes, as crew are usually informed not to use it at all.
No, because only friends and family see the posts.
No, because press around the world would not believe the posts.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: Yes, if their posts are damaging and seen by others.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: What part of a vessel’s emergency pollution plan involves the crew? Select the BEST answer.
options: The steps taken to control discharge of oil following an incident.
The organisation of people to control an oil spill or discharge of oil.
The list of shore authorities to contact when oil is spilled into the sea.
The communications between ship and shore that is required when oil pollution has occurred.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The steps taken to control discharge of oil following an incident.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Which of the following demonstrates a positive type of behaviour?
options: Responsive.
Unhelpful.
Unsafe.
Bored.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: Responsive.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Why is it important to exercise an oil spill emergency pollution plan? Select the BEST answer.
options: It is the only way to see that it works properly.
It is devised by people ashore and probably not suitable for the vessel.
It gives the crew something to do when work is a bit slack.
Because legislation, namely MARPOL, requires it to be done.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: It is the only way to see that it works properly.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Which option correctly completes the following statement? ‘If the crew show positive behaviour during an oil spill...’
options: ‘...they will work strongly as a team.’
‘...they will have a casual attitude.’
‘...they will be more at risk of an accident.’
‘...they will not be working as a team.’
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: ‘...they will work strongly as a team.’

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: What could be in an oil spill emergency pollution drill? Select the BEST answer.
options: Any foreseeable event that might cause pollution.
It only covers cargo oil spills from manifolds and pipes.
It is limited to a stock check of equipment in the SOPEP locker.
It prepares the crew for actions if there is a hull crack discovered.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: Any foreseeable event that might cause pollution.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: If crew show NEGATIVE behaviour during an oil spill response, what is the worst effect on a vessel? Select the BEST answer.
options: The spill might become pollution.
The spill is cleaned up more slowly.
The crew work as individuals.
It will be delayed on the berth.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The spill might become pollution.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: According to this module, what are the benefits of a positive attitude to an oil spill drill? Select the BEST answer.
options: A crewmember might see a way of improving a practice or procedure.
A crewmember will be considered favourably by the officer in charge.
A crewmember will be ready in the event of an oil spill drill if required during a port state inspection.
The SMS requires that all drills are carried out as if it was a real emergency.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: A crewmember might see a way of improving a practice or procedure.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Is the following statement true or false: ‘A person’s behaviour has been learned from an early age and cannot be changed.’
options: The statement is false.
The statement is true.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The statement is false.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Is the following statement true or false: ‘People can behave differently during a real event rather than a drill.’
options: The statement is true.
The statement is false.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The statement is true.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Crewmembers can contribute to the emergency pollution plan.’
options: True.
False.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: True.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: Is the following statement true or false: ‘Shipping companies are not bothered about what is said about them in the world press.’
options: The stement is false.
The stement is true.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: The stement is false.

CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.question: What items are covered by a SOPEP emergency pollution plan?
options: Fuel and cargo oil.
General items of garbage from the vessel waster bins.
Any overboard discharges from the engine room.
Sewage and ‘grey’ or ‘black’ water discharges.
CD2551 — SOPEP, Your role.answer: Fuel and cargo oil.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: How can an operator view loaded chart file names on the ECDIS? Select one of the given options.
options: From the ECDIS chart portfolio menu.
By loading the world chart and looking at the outlined chart cells.
By checking the base installation disk for the loaded list.
From the ECDIS electronic chart supplier.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: From the ECDIS chart portfolio menu.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select from the given options the result of clicking the ‘reset hide’ button in the manual chart update menu.
options: Manual update objects, if hidden, appear for five seconds.
Manual update objects are permanently shown on the screen.
Manual update objects are all hidden.
Manual update objects, if hidden, appear for one second.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Manual update objects, if hidden, appear for five seconds.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly explains why sometimes two ship outlines can be seen, one black the other orange.
options: Because position one and position two navigation sensors are selected.
One outline is based on the GPS receiver position the other on the CCRP.
One outline is from a log file being played back the other from GPS.
One outline is from the GPS signal, the other from radar returns.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Because position one and position two navigation sensors are selected.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options which best describes the large red circle seen in the following illustration.
options: The large red circle indicates the waypoint arrival circle.
The large red circle is the VRM set on the next waypoint.
The large red circle is the ‘advance’ before the next wheel over point.
The large red circle is a warning that the next waypoint is approaching.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The large red circle indicates the waypoint arrival circle.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options which best describes the small blue circle seen in the following illustration.
options: The small blue circle indicates the next waypoint.
The small blue circle is the VRM set on the next waypoint.
The small blue circle is the ‘advance’ before the next wheel over point.
The small blue circle indicates the wheel over point.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The small blue circle indicates the next waypoint.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: When would an operator change a sensor signal from the LAN to a local port? Select one option for your answer.
options: When there has been a failure in the LAN.
When the sensor has an outside tolerance error on it.
When the ECDIS is in planning mode, to stop the navigation alarm.
When the mother board on the ECDIS computer fails to bypass it.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: When there has been a failure in the LAN.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: If the cursor has changed to that shown, select the one correct option that explains what the cursor would now be used for.
options: To interrogate a chart object.
To open up a menu on the chart ‘settings’.
To set an ‘enhanced list’ of targets.
To position a manual update on the chart.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: To interrogate a chart object.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that correctly explains why a white arrow is sometimes seen alongside an item in a drop down menu.
options: It is an indication that there are further menu choices.
It is an indication that the function has integrity.
It is an indication that there is no further detail.
It is the back button for the function.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It is an indication that there are further menu choices.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one given option which correctly describes how to obtain information from the ECDIS on the loaded chart.
options: Right mouse click when the cursor is on the chart display.
Check with the chart supplier.
Left mouse click when the cursor is on the chart display.
Check on the bridge passage planning computer.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Right mouse click when the cursor is on the chart display.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: The illustration shows a section of chart with orange cross lines inside the 10 metre contour. Select one of the given options to correctly explain why these are seen.
options: The ‘shallow pattern’ has been activated.
The ’deep pattern’ has been activated.
The lines indicate a ‘cautionary area’.
The lines indicate a ‘precautionary area’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The ‘shallow pattern’ has been activated.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best explains the quickest way to browse around a chart on the JRC ECDIS.
options: Left click and hold whilst on the chart screen and use the trackball
Use the arrow keys located on the operation panel.
Set the desired latitude and longitude.
Use the menu system to locate a desired position.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Left click and hold whilst on the chart screen and use the trackball

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘The word ‘free’ when seen on the display panel indicates that...
options: ...The chart was shifted to a location where the ship symbol is not visible.
...the cursor has been detached from the trackball’.
...the ECDIS is free to select a type of electronic chart’.
...the VRM and EBL are not centred on own-ship’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...The chart was shifted to a location where the ship symbol is not visible.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option that best explains the significance of the letter ‘P’ alongside the tracked radar target in the illustration.
options: The target originates from the port side radar.
The target is predicted to pass to port of own-ship.
The target is dangerous because the ‘P’ stands for ‘priority’.
The ‘P’ stands for ‘past’ so the target is safe.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The target originates from the port side radar.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one given option that best explains the function of the AIS filter.
options: It is a function that allows values to be set for displaying AIS targets.
It allows settings for fusing the radar and AIS targets on the ECDIS screen.
It removes class B AIS targets from the screen.
It can be set to only display stand on targets under the collision regulations
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It is a function that allows values to be set for displaying AIS targets.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Some AIS targets set off an alarm even when they are outside the geographical limits set. Select one option to best explain this.
options: The target has infringed set limits for CPA or TCPA.
The target is a stand on vessel under the collision regulations.
The target has sent an alarm signal to the vessel’s receiver.
The target is a stationary navigation AIS such as a lighthouse.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The target has infringed set limits for CPA or TCPA.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that correctly states how many AIS targets the JRC ECDIS is capable of displaying.
Select the correct option to complete the statement correctly.^MOn start-up a JRC ECDIS will go into ‘ ......’ automatically if no other function is selected from the four button menu.
options: Navigation and planning mode
ENC and ARCS chart portfolio
C-Map chart manager
Playback
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Navigation and planning mode

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the option that best completes the following statement. ‘The JRC ECDIS computer is started with...
options: ...a single push on the power button.
...a three second push on the power button
...a main switch on the front panel of the ECDIS
...a double push on the power button
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...a single push on the power button.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Which one of the given options best describes the content stored on the ‘D’ drive of the JRC 901B or 701B ECDIS computer?
options: Charts and user files.
The JRC ECDIS operating system.
Chart files only.
The Windows operating system.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Charts and user files.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Which one of the given options best describes the content stored on the ‘E’ drive of the JRC 901B and 701B ECDIS computer?
options: Copies of the loaded charts
The JRC ECDIS operating system
Chart files only
The Windows operating system
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Copies of the loaded charts

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? 'The JRC ECDIS can be set to alarm if an AIS target infringes set limits'.
options: True
False
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: True

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that correctly explain the use of the ‘auto sail’ settings when the vessel is under track control (TCS).
options: ‘Auto sail’ fine tunes the steering control settings for the conditions.
Clicking ‘auto sail’ activates the TCS function.
‘Auto sail’ fine tunes how the engine will be set on each leg of the route.
Clicking ‘auto sail’ disables the TCS function on the ECDIS.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ‘Auto sail’ fine tunes the steering control settings for the conditions.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that correctly completes the following statement. ‘An AIS target will be left sleeping if...
options: ...it does not infringe the set limits for AIS targets’.
...it outside a five mile radius’.
...it is a class B AIS device transmitting’.
...it is the give way vessel under the collision regulations’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...it does not infringe the set limits for AIS targets’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to explain the use of the ‘auto detect’ button on the ECDIS chart portfolio menu.
options: When clicked the ECDIS looks for new charts or updates.
When clicked the ECDIS looks for out of date charts on the ‘D’ drive.
When clicked the ECDIS connects with the internet to download updates.
When clicked the ECDIS connects to the internet to download new charts.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: When clicked the ECDIS looks for new charts or updates.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Manual chart updates can only be installed with the ECDIS in ‘Chart manager’ mode’.
options: False
True
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: False

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that best describes the ‘priority’ function seen on the AIS target menu of the JRC ECDIS.
options: When over 300 targets are visible, dangerous AIS targets are shown in preference to others.
AIS targets that are close to the vessel are given priority.
AIS targets ahead of the vessel are given priority.
The ECDIS takes the AIS position as priority over the radar position.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: When over 300 targets are visible, dangerous AIS targets are shown in preference to others.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best explains why a leg of the loaded route shows as an enlarged red line.
options: The safety check has identified a problem with it.
It is the next leg of the passage plan.
It is the final leg of the passage plan.
It is a route leg where the safety check cannot be made.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The safety check has identified a problem with it.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option that correctly explains the meaning of the word ‘hand’ when seen on the menu panel.
options: The route is ‘normal’ being manually steered.
The route is a ‘TCS’ route.
The autopilot has been disengaged, the wheel being used instead.
The cursor has changed to a hand symbol to grab information.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The route is ‘normal’ being manually steered.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that correctly explains the ‘associate’ function on the target menu
options: It allows the merging of AIS and radar targets
It attaches a radar target to a specified route for it.
It associates a radar target with a VHF radio transmission.
It distinguishes between a moving and static radar target.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It allows the merging of AIS and radar targets

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly identify the two methods of ETA calculation used on the JRC ECDIS.
options: Using a set value or the actual speed of the vessel.
Using a set value or the average speed over the last four hours.
Using the average speed or the vessel’s maximum speed.
Using the actual water speed of the vessel or the passage plan set value.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Using a set value or the actual speed of the vessel.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly identify the function of the following icon seen on the chart information part of the menu panel.
options: When clicked it opens the event mark menu.
When clicked it opens the man overboard menu.
When clicked it opens the no-go area menu.
When clicked it opens the log menu.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: When clicked it opens the event mark menu.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which correctly describes the normal appearance of the cursor.
options: A vertical cross shape (+).
A diagonal cross shape (x).
A circular shape.
A box shape.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A vertical cross shape (+).

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly describe how to set the ECDIS to be able to see the Admiralty Information Overlay on the display.
options: Select ‘other’ as the display type.
Select ‘base’ as the display type.
Select ‘standard’ as the display type.
Select ‘AIO’ as the display type.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Select ‘other’ as the display type.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly explain why an event mark may not be seen on the chart display.
options: It is invisible at the selected chart scale.
The time of the event is outside the four hour time limit.
The chart is not set at the compilation scale.
Because the font colour is incorrect.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It is invisible at the selected chart scale.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly complete the following statement. ‘When a pre-planned route is loaded it...
options: ...is automatically in monitor mode’.
...may not have been safety checked previously.’
...will always be safe.’
...has to be set into monitor mode before use’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...is automatically in monitor mode’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘An event mark will always be seen on the chart display’.
options: False
True
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: False

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly explain where the man overboard button is located.
options: On the menu and the operation panel.
On the menu panel only.
On the operation panel only.
On the operation panel and the drop down menu.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: On the menu and the operation panel.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best describes how the second EBL is distinguished from the first EBL.
options: The second EBL is of a dash-dot construction.
The second EBL is coloured green.
The second EBL is a dash construction.
The second EBL is coloured yellow.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The second EBL is of a dash-dot construction.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘The size of the text fonts describing a lighthouse can be changed’
options: True
False
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: True

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘The volume of the alarm cannot be altered.’
options: False.
True.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: False.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly complete the following statement. ‘On the 901B and 701B models the normal setting on the drive organisation tab for the ‘D’ and ‘E’ drives is to...
options: ...select dual drive’.
...select ‘D’ drive only’.
...select ‘E’ drive only’.
...select ‘D’ as priority over ‘E’ drive’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...select dual drive’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly explains why the illustrated alert has been activated.
options: A chart object normally seen in a ‘standard’ display is removed.
The ‘other’ type of chart display has been selected.
Some synthetic graphics have been added to the chart display.
The chart display has the passage plan active on it.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A chart object normally seen in a ‘standard’ display is removed.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which best explains the significance of the letter ‘D’ alongside EBL1 in the illustration.
options: The EBL is offset.
The EBL is positioned on Racon ‘D’.
The EBL is temporarily disabled.
The EBL origin is not visible on the chart display.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The EBL is offset.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘User created areas...
options: ...can be set up to highlight and detect dangers’.
...are not useful as they do not cause an alarm’.
...only cause an alarm when the ship symbol is on them’.
...create an alarm when radar targets are in them’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...can be set up to highlight and detect dangers’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best describes when the display is ‘course-up’ how the ship’s head automatically resets towards the top of the screen.
options: A numerical value is input that once exceeded causes a reset.
There is a button on the ‘chart info’ menu to manually reset the display.
The display has a default value that once exceeded allows a reset.
The ‘course up’ display will reset every ten degrees of deviation.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A numerical value is input that once exceeded causes a reset.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘There is only one button to stop the ECDIS alarm’.
options: False
True
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: False

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that correctly explains the function of the ‘PANEL’ button seen on the operation panel.
options: The button dims the operation panel in five steps.
The button dims the display screen in five steps.
The button tests the panel illumination.
The button brings the menu panel on and off the screen display.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The button dims the operation panel in five steps.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option that correctly explains the function of the ‘VIDEO’ button on the operation panel.
options: It adjusts the brilliance of displayed radar echoes.
It adjusts the display screen brightness.
It adjusts the speed that the log video files playback.
It overlays radar return from connected radar.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It adjusts the brilliance of displayed radar echoes.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘The offset VRM and EBL can be returned to the CCRP...
options: ...by clicking on the letter ‘D’ in the ‘tools’ menu’.
...by clicking on ‘reset’ in the ‘tools’ menu’.
...by clicking on the ship symbol’.
...by clicking on the VRM and EBL intersection point’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...by clicking on the letter ‘D’ in the ‘tools’ menu’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which correctly explains the use of the icon with the red exclamation mark seen in the illustration.
options: Clicking on the icon returns the display to ‘standard’.
Clicking on the icon returns the display to ‘other’.
Clicking this icon temporarily removes synthetic graphics.
Clicking this icon activates the route.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Clicking on the icon returns the display to ‘standard’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘Clicking on the ‘alarm list’ button...
options: ...gives access to the alarm log and information or warnings’.
...gives access to the current alarm only’.
...gives access to the alarm log only’.
...gives access to the alarm log and system status only’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...gives access to the alarm log and information or warnings’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the option that correctly completes the following statement. ‘The JRC web site should be...
options: ...consulted regularly for ECDIS software updates’.
...checked regularly for chart updates’.
...consulted to download the public key’.
...checked regularly for new editions of charts’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...consulted regularly for ECDIS software updates’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which correctly explains why the position information, seen on the top right hand side of the menu panel, has a blue background.
options: A position offset has been applied to the GPS position.
The GPS input has failed to the ECDIS.
There is a discrepancy between the two connected GPS receivers.
The position fix is at the incorrect datum for the chart in use.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A position offset has been applied to the GPS position.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which explains the use of the ‘rotation’ function with the ECDIS set in true motion, north up.
options: The function allows the north direction to be set on the screen.
The function is the ‘course up’ reset value.
The function when activated allows the ship’s head to vary with the gyro.
The function changes the radar rotation speed seen on the ECDIS display.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The function allows the north direction to be set on the screen.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly explains why the alarm button located on the menu panel is in two parts.
options: To show both immediate and active alarms.
To enable two alarms to be read by the operator at the same time.
So that multi alarms can be acknowledged as fast as possible.
To have some redundancy when one alarm acknowledge button fails.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: To show both immediate and active alarms.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Why do some items in the 'chart settings' menu have the letter ‘O’ against them? Select the one correct option from those given.
options: This indicates they are always seen on the ‘other’ display.
This indicates they are optional items.
This indicates they are always seen on an ‘open’ display.
This indicates they are an overlaid item.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: This indicates they are always seen on the ‘other’ display.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select an option that correctly completes the following statement. ‘If there is no hardware key board fitted...
options: ...the onscreen key board will be used’.
...one has to be obtained and connected to the ECDIS’.
...it is not possible to enter text’.
...only enter numbers using the up and down range button’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...the onscreen key board will be used’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select an option that correctly explains the function of the ‘HOME’ button on the operation panel.
options: Pressing the button returns the ship symbol to the chart screen.
Pressing the button locates the chart in the home port.
Pressing the button returns the cursor to the centre of the display.
Pressing the button centres the VRM and EBL.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Pressing the button returns the ship symbol to the chart screen.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option to correctly explain why the over scale ‘prison bars’ warning can be seen on one half of a chart display only.
options: There are two chart cells loaded with different compilation scales.
The warning is only displayed over land.
There are both an ARCS and a vector chart loaded together.
Only half is used so that the operator can see detail on the other half.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: There are two chart cells loaded with different compilation scales.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘The ECDIS alarm is acknowledged...
options: ...using either the button on the menu or on the operation panel’.
...using a button located on the chart screen’.
...automatically after a ten second timeout’.
...when the operator changes the item causing the alarm’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...using either the button on the menu or on the operation panel’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options to correctly identify the function of the red ‘pizza’ shape in the illustration.
options: It is the danger detection sector.
It shows the extent of the forward scanning depth sounder.
It is a danger area on the chart.
It shows the vessel is entering a red sector of a navigation light.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It is the danger detection sector.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the option that correctly completes the following statement. ‘The chart portfolio window gives access to...
options: ...delete old versions of permits and load new ones’.
...view chart cells loaded and rename regular use charts’.
...delete chart updates once applied to the chart’.
...view the stored passage plan files’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...delete old versions of permits and load new ones’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options which best describes a ‘normal’ route on the JRC ECDIS.
options: It is one that is steered by the bridge team.
It is one that is created as a rhumb line.
It is one following all normal planning conventions.
It is one use for track control steering.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: It is one that is steered by the bridge team.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that would activate the danger detection function on the JRC ECDIS.
options: Ensure that there is a tick against ‘vector’ in the alarm setting menu.
Ensure that there is a tick against ‘display vector area’ in the alarm setting menu.
Ensure that the ship vector is set to a long time period.
Ensure there is a tick against ‘detect danger’ in the alarm setting menu.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Ensure that there is a tick against ‘vector’ in the alarm setting menu.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: When a route safety check is completed with an ECDIS set in ‘base’ display how does the check highlight a dangerous but invisible object? Select one of the given options.
options: A black triangle is placed in the position of the dangerous object.
It does not highlight the dangerous object as it is not detected.
It makes the dangerous object appear on the chart display.
It changes the display to ‘standard’ to display all objects.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A black triangle is placed in the position of the dangerous object.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select from the given options the correct meaning of the symbol in the illustration.
options: A manually inserted light vessel.
An automatically inserted light vessel.
A manually deleted light vessel.
An automatically deleted light vessel.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: A manually inserted light vessel.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: The danger detection box is not visible surrounding the ship symbol in the illustration; does this mean danger detection is not active? Select one of the given options that correctly answer the question.
options: The danger detection may be still active.
The danger detection is not active.
The danger detection is active because the vector is visible.
The danger detection has temporarily been disabled.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The danger detection may be still active.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘The ECDIS automatic route safety check is sufficient to see all dangers with the planned route’.
options: False
True
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: False

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best explains why a waypoint detail has a red coloured font in the waypoint table.
options: The safety check has identified a problem with it.
It is the next leg of the passage plan.
It is the final leg of the passage plan.
It is a route leg where the safety check cannot be made.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The safety check has identified a problem with it.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that correctly describe how the depth values are shown when they have a value below the safety depth setting.
options: Values are shown in a bold font.
Values are shown in a red coloured font.
Values are not shown at all.
Values are shown in the same way as any depth value.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: Values are shown in a bold font.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that correctly complete the following statement. ‘For full danger protection a vessel...
options: ...should have both the danger detection vector and sector active’.
...should have the danger detection vector displayed’.
...should have the danger detection sector displayed’.
...should have both the danger detection vector and sector displayed’.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: ...should have both the danger detection vector and sector active’.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best explains why a section of a depth contour shows as an enlarged black line.
options: The safety check has detected a route conflict with it.
It is the one hundred metre contour.
It is a section of contour with a doubtful value.
The safety check identifies that it is in an incorrect position.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The safety check has detected a route conflict with it.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select one of the given options that correctly explain what the red circle surrounding the vessel symbol represents on the following illustration.
options: The red circle represents the anchor swinging circle.
The red circle causes an automatic target detection alarm.
The red circle represents a Racon in the area.
The red circle represents the danger detection sector as a full sector.
CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.answer: The red circle represents the anchor swinging circle.

CD4014 — JRC ECDIS.question: Select the one option which best explains the function of the ‘view sync’ seen in the waypoint table.
options: When clicked, the chart screen locates at the waypoint position.
When clicked, all waypoints are set with the same speed value.
When clicked, all waypoints are set with the same cross track limit.

Using a planned or the average speed over the last four hours.
Using the average speed or the vessel’s maximum speed.
Using the actual water speed of the vessel or the planned speed.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Using the planned or the actual speed of the vessel.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option correctly describes how the depth values are shown when they have a value below the safety depth setting?
options: Values are shown in a bold font.
Values are shown in a red coloured font.
Values are not shown at all.
Values are shown in the same way as any depth value.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Values are shown in a bold font.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What happens when this button is pressed?
options: It returns the ship symbol to the chart screen.
It locates the chart in the home port.
It returns the cursor to the centre of the display.
It centres the VRM and EBL.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It returns the ship symbol to the chart screen.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option describes when a true motion display will reset?
options: According to the ‘Border’ setting.
When the ship’s head has deviated by 10 degrees.
According to the ‘Limit’ setting.
A true motion never resets as the symbol is stopped.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: According to the ‘Border’ setting.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is this button used for?
options: It adjusts the display screen brightness.
It adjusts the brilliance of displayed radar echoes.
It adjusts the speed of the log video files playback.
It overlays radar return from connected radar.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It adjusts the display screen brightness.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Why does this alarm stay visible in the alert strip after being acknowledged?
options: It is still active.
It is an alarm rather than a warning.
It still needs to be entered into the log book.
It has not yet been added to the ‘Alert’ list.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It is still active.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option correctly completes the following statement? ^M‘When a pre-planned route is loaded, it...’
options: ‘...is active in monitor mode’.
‘...may not have been safety checked previously’.
‘...will always be safe’.
‘...has to be set into monitor mode before use’.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: ‘...is active in monitor mode’.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What function does the ‘Node fixed EBL/VRM’ have?
options: They always stay on the vessel symbol.
They are located in a position where they stay.
Once set, they update with the ground course and speed.
The EBL is set at 90 degrees to the vessel symbol.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: They always stay on the vessel symbol.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Why would sensor information seen in the own-ship information panel have an orange background?
options: The necessary information is missing.
A position offset has been applied to the GPS position.
There is a discrepancy between the two connected GPS receivers.
The ECDIS is set for ground speed not the impellor log.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: The necessary information is missing.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Is the following statement true or false? ^M‘The alert sound is different for an alarm and a warning.’
options: True
False
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: True

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option correctly completes the following statement? ^M‘For full danger protection, a vessel monitoring with ECDIS should have...’
options: ‘...the look-ahead danger detection active.’
‘...the ground track vector displayed.’
‘...‘All’ chart details displayed.’
‘...narrow cross track limits in the passage plan.’
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: ‘...the look-ahead danger detection active.’

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is this button used for?
options: It sets the chart scale the same as the compilation scale.
It opens up the passage planning window.
It opens up the passage monitoring window.
It enables charts to be loaded from an opened window.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It sets the chart scale the same as the compilation scale.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is this button used for?
options: It dims the operation panel.
It dims the display screen.
It tests the panel illumination.
It activates the fitted hardware keyboard.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It dims the operation panel.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Why is the black anchor swinging circle not centred on the vessel symbol but offset a small distance?
options: The circle is based on the position of the anchor, not the CCRP.
The circle is based on the CCRP, not the position of the anchor.
The circle is based on an earlier position and the vessel has dragged anchor.
The circle has been placed in an incorrect position on the vessel.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: The circle is based on the position of the anchor, not the CCRP.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What does it mean if the look-ahead danger detection is not visible on the vessel symbol?
options: Danger detection is not active.
Danger detection is active in the background.
The danger detection sector is active because the vector is visible.
The danger detection has temporarily been disabled.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Danger detection is not active.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Why does the menu button have the rotating graphic on it?
options: To indicate that the computer is running correctly.
To indicate that there is a connected radar.
To indicate that a menu window is open on the chart screen.
To indicate that the computer has locked up and needs to be restarted.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: To indicate that the computer is running correctly.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is the function of the ‘Sync’ button?
options: It synchronises the route to all work stations in the network.
When pressed, all waypoints are set with the same course and speed values.
It synchronises time across the LAN to all work stations.
When pressed, the view is set from waypoint to waypoint sequentially.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It synchronises the route to all work stations in the network.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option best completes the following statement? ^M‘Clicking on the ‘alert list’ button gives access to...’
options: ‘...the alert log and active alerts.’
‘...the current alert only.’
‘...active and logged alarms.’
‘...the alert log and system status.’
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: ‘...the alert log and active alerts.’

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is a ‘Logbook’ recording?
options: It is a recording made by the bridge team during a voyage.
It is a recording officially made by ECDIS.
It is a recording of the master’s standing orders.
It is a copy of the passage plan.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It is a recording made by the bridge team during a voyage.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: How would you know that the look-ahead danger detection function is active?
options: It is visible on the chart screen.
It is always active whether seen or not.
Ensure that the ship vector is set to a long time period.
Ensure there is a tick against ‘Look-ahead’ in the ‘Tools’ menu.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It is visible on the chart screen.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Why would red highlight appear on a chart object close to a route being monitored?
options: The safety check has identified that it could be dangerous.
It is the next leg of the passage plan.
It is the final leg of the passage plan.
It is a route leg where the safety check cannot be made.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: The safety check has identified that it could be dangerous.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What does the colour blue indicate when used as a highlight or a line colour?
options: Whatever it is highlighting or underlined is selected.
Nothing, as this is a standard form of presenting text messages.
The item with highlight or underline needs operator attention.
It relates to a secondary route that is being planned.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Whatever it is highlighting or underlined is selected.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option correctly explains the target ‘associate’ function?
options: It allows the merging of AIS and radar targets.
It attaches a radar target to a specified route.
It associates a radar target with a VHF radio transmission.
It distinguishes between an active and sleeping AIS target.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It allows the merging of AIS and radar targets.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is probably represented by the black circle surrounding the vessel symbol seen in this illustration?
options: The anchor swinging circle.
An automatic target detection alarm.
A Racon in the area.
The danger detection sector as a full sector.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: The anchor swinging circle.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What is this button used for?
options: It switches to day and night modes.
It adjusts the brilliance of displayed AIS targets.
It gives access to the help menu.
It highlights manual chart updates.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It switches to day and night modes.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option best completes the following statement? ^M‘The ECDIS alert is acknowledged...’
options: ‘...using either the button in the alert message or in the list.’
‘...using a button located on the chart screen.’
‘...automatically after a ten second timeout.’
‘...when the operator changes the item causing the alert.’
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: ‘...using either the button in the alert message or in the list.’

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: What colour is an active route on the chart screen?
options: Red
Blue
Green
Orange
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Red

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Is the following statement true or false? ^M‘An event mark will ALWAYS  be seen on the chart display’.
options: False
True
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: False

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Where is the ‘Man overboard button’ located?
options: Just below the alert strip.
On the chart information strip.
On the trackball unit.
On the menu button.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Just below the alert strip.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option best explains why an event mark might not be seen on the chart display?
options: It is invisible at the selected chart scale.
The time of the event is outside the four hour time limit.
The chart is not set at the compilation scale.
Because the font colour is incorrect.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: It is invisible at the selected chart scale.

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: Which option correctly completes the following statement? ^M‘User created areas...’
options: ‘...can be set up to highlight danger areas.’
‘...are not useful as they do not cause an alert.’
‘...only cause an alert when the ship symbol is on them.’
‘...create an alert when radar targets are in them.’
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: ‘...can be set up to highlight danger areas.’

CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.question: How are the various EBLs and VRMs distinguished from each other?
options: Using different colours.
With text labels.
Using different line thicknesses.
They are not - the operator should know which one they are manipulating.
CD4020 — JRC ECDIS, models JAN-7201, 920.answer: Using different colours.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Is a post inspection meeting with the crew required?
options: No, there is no point in wasting time on this.
Yes.
No it is not required; however it is suggested in order to inform the crew about the inspection result.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: No it is not required; however it is suggested in order to inform the crew about the inspection result.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Must a vetting inspector wear appropriate personal protection equipment at all times?
options: Yes, but only if the Master requires him to do so.
Yes, he must set a good example with respect to personal safety procedures whilst on board the vessel and in the terminal.
No, as he is an accredited vetting inspector he is exempted from this.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: Yes, he must set a good example with respect to personal safety procedures whilst on board the vessel and in the terminal.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: When does a vetting inspection commence?
options: Immediately after the opening meeting.
As soon as the vetting inspector informs the Master.
From the moment the inspector takes his first step onto the gangway.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: From the moment the inspector takes his first step onto the gangway.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Must a vetting inspector identify himself at the gangway?
options: Yes, all persons must show ID at the gangway.
No, his attendance has been approved by the agent and Master in advance.
Yes, but only if the gangway watch requires it.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: Yes, all persons must show ID at the gangway.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: If the inspector asks you a question, and you don’t know the answer, what is the best way to reply?
options: I think it is better if you ask the captain.
I just arrived yesterday, and I don’t know enough about this ship yet.
I am not sure, but let me investigate and get back to you shortly.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: I am not sure, but let me investigate and get back to you shortly.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Is the inspector entitled to walk around on the vessel unaccompanied?
options: Yes.
No.
No, however if the crew is busy he can occasionally do part of the inspection on his own.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Why would it be a good idea to re-check the engine room compartment shortly before the vetting inspection?
options: To ensure that no work is ongoing.
To ensure that it is clean and tidy.
To ensure that all safety equipment is in place and has not been removed.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: To ensure that it is clean and tidy.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Is the entire crew required to participate in the inspection?
options: Yes.
No.
Only as necessary.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: Which accident was the first to draw public attention to the danger of transporting oil at sea?
options: Exxon Valdez.
Torrey Canyon.
Erika.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: What is the overall objective of a vetting inspection?
options: To provide a record of the vessel’s condition and standard of operation at the time of the inspection to the vessel’s owner.
To provide a record of the vessel’s condition and standard of operation at the time of the inspection and, in turn, allow other companies to see the report.
To provide a factual record of the vessel’s condition and standard of operation at the time of the inspection and, in turn, allow an assessment of the risk that use of the vessel might pose.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: To provide a factual record of the vessel’s condition and standard of operation at the time of the inspection and, in turn, allow an assessment of the risk that use of the vessel might pose.

CD4054 — VettingAss1.question: How many pre-vetting meetings with the crew are required prior to an inspection?
options: None.
As many meetings as deemed necessary.
One.
CD4054 — VettingAss1.answer: As many meetings as deemed necessary.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Which of the following pre-vetting checks should be completed in the office?
options: Integrated Contingency Plans, tank inspection reports and Class Status reports.
Officers matrix, technical inspection reports, open audit reports and near-miss reports.
Environmental reports, Port State reports and Document of Compliance.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Officers matrix, technical inspection reports, open audit reports and near-miss reports.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Handing out relevant VIQ chapters to the responsible officers is a good idea. But why?
options: Because it enables them to check all the questions and complete a good pre-vetting.
Because the VIQ chapters are prepared especially for pre-vetting inspections and contains the tick-boxes for exactly this purpose.
Because the VIQ guidelines include directions for pre-vetting inspections.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Because it enables them to check all the questions and complete a good pre-vetting.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Which of the following reports should at least be reviewed during vetting preparation?
options: Only the most recent vetting inspection report with unclosed observations.
Latest internal reports only.
Latest Port State Control report, ISM & ISPS reports, Technical inspection report and vetting report
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Latest Port State Control report, ISM & ISPS reports, Technical inspection report and vetting report

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: In which VIQ Chapter is CAS (Condition Assessment Scheme) located?
options: Chapter 2.
Chapter 3.
Chapter 4.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Chapter 2.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Who should attend the opening meeting?
options: The vetting inspector and the Captain.
The vetting inspector, the Captain and any other senior officer he may decide upon.
The vetting inspector and the entire crew.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: The vetting inspector, the Captain and any other senior officer he may decide upon.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Are onboard officers required to hold valid original Flag State endorsements?
options: Yes. Valid Flag State endorsement must always follow the individual officer.
Preferably yes. Alternatively evidence that an endorsement application has been issued must be onboard.
No.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Preferably yes. Alternatively evidence that an endorsement application has been issued must be onboard.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is the purpose of having a pre-vetting meeting with the majority of the crew prior to an inspection?
options: To brief the crew about the role of involved individuals during the inspection
To tell the crew that they must ensure that no reasons for observations are found by the inspector.
There is no need for a pre-vetting meeting with the crew
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: To brief the crew about the role of involved individuals during the inspection

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is Chapter 11 in the VIQ about?
options: General appearance and condition
Engine and steering compartments
Cargo and ballast systems
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Engine and steering compartments

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: In which VIQ Chapter do you find questions about UKC (Under Keel Clearance)?
options: Chapter 4.
Chapter 5.
Chapter 6.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Chapter 4.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Does the VIQ indicate which edition each required publication must have?
options: Yes, but in general this should be disregarded as the various publication are frequently renewed.
No, it is only required to have the publications on board, there is no requirement for specific editions.
Yes.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Yes.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Is the inspector obliged to respect rest hours on board during an inspection?
options: Yes.
No.
Yes in general, but he may ask individual crew members to deviate if needed.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Yes.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Is the vetting inspector obliged to leave a note with observations on board before he leaves?
options: No, and if he doesn't the Master should make a list of the observations during the closing meeting.
No, and it doesn’t matter because the final report will be submitted to the Company later.
Yes, always.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: No, and if he doesn't the Master should make a list of the observations during the closing meeting.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: In case a CDI inspection is being planned the Inspector will:
options: Accept a SIRE VPQ in the absence of a CDI VPQ.
Require a CDI VPQ.
Just need a VPQ irrespective of which format.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Require a CDI VPQ.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is the maximum validity of a Class Status Report before an observation regarding lack of an updated Class status report is raised during an inspection?
options: 2 months.
3 months.
4 months.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: 4 months.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Who should attend the closing meeting?
options: The vetting inspector and the Captain.
The vetting inspector, the Captain and any other senior officer he may decide upon.
The vetting inspector and the entire crew.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: The vetting inspector, the Captain and any other senior officer he may decide upon.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Is an inspection valid if conducted during night time operation only?
options: Yes, this is common practice.
No.
Yes, but the value of the inspection as a whole is questionable, hence it is not common practice.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Yes, but the value of the inspection as a whole is questionable, hence it is not common practice.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is the overall purpose of a vetting inspection?
options: To ensure that your vessel is operated and maintained in a safe manner adhering to all relevant rules and regulations.
To provide the inspection company with a report for their filing system.
To assure the Charterers that your vessel is safe to charter.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: To ensure that your vessel is operated and maintained in a safe manner adhering to all relevant rules and regulations.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: In addition to the vetting inspection and the owners’ comments, the charterer will also:
options: Contact the owners to discuss the observations before a decision is made regarding “acceptance”.
Screen the latest Port State Control report and then issue an “acceptance”.
Screen any other available information about the owner and his operation before a decision is made regarding “acceptance”.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Screen any other available information about the owner and his operation before a decision is made regarding “acceptance”.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Is the Inspector always correct when he notes observations?
options: Yes.
No, but he is entitled to rely on his own subjective opinion.
No, but if the Master disagrees the issue may be raised during the closing meeting.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: No, but if the Master disagrees the issue may be raised during the closing meeting.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is the HVPQ?
options: A software program that ship owners use to compile ship particulars data.
A list of vetting questions used by the inspector.
The inspection scheme used by OCIMF.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: A software program that ship owners use to compile ship particulars data.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: The closing meeting provides the Master with:
options: An opportunity to have those observations deleted, which are not applicable.
An opportunity to challenge a doubtful observation
An opportunity to discuss the final report and have all incorrect observations deleted immediately.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: An opportunity to challenge a doubtful observation

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: Are cargo operations required during an inspection?
options: Yes.
No.
No, but cargo operations are preferred during an inspection since the value of the inspection as a whole would be questionable without it.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: No, but cargo operations are preferred during an inspection since the value of the inspection as a whole would be questionable without it.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What is INTERTANKO?
options: The International Association of Individual Terminal Operators.
The International Association of Indian Tanker Managers.
The International Association of Independent Tanker Owners.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: The International Association of Independent Tanker Owners.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: What are Best Practices issued by Oil Majors?
options: Additional requirements highlighting areas of concern.
The best method of completing a vetting inspection.
A company specific guideline for correct loading procedures.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: Additional requirements highlighting areas of concern.

CD4055 — VettingAss2.question: How long does an inspection usually take?
options: 2-4 hours.
6-8 hours.
8-12 hours.
CD4055 — VettingAss2.answer: 6-8 hours.

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: If you are contacted by a journalists to discuss company affairs or a recent incident you should:
options: Be honest, tell them what you know and what you have seen
Hang up on them
Tell them that you are not the correct person to speak to but you can take their contact details and get the appropriate person to call
Get angry
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: Tell them that you are not the correct person to speak to but you can take their contact details and get the appropriate person to call

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: If an incident happens on board your vessel you should:
options: Keep calm and wait until your superiors instruct you
Take photos and post them on social media
Send social media posts about the incident to your friends and family
Tweet about the incident so that the media hear the story from your side before anyone else’s
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: Keep calm and wait until your superiors instruct you

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: Can journalists find information about you on your personal social media accounts?
options: Yes, if your privacy settings are not set to maximum
No, as long as you only share information with friends
No, they can’t track things you delete
Yes, but only if they get special access
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: Yes, if your privacy settings are not set to maximum

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: You should check regularly that your privacy settings are set to the maximum?
options: TRUE
FALSE

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: Can you lose your job from just one simple social media post?
options: No you cannot
Yes you could be fired if you post something the company doesn’t like
If you aren’t breaking any rules, they can’t do anything
Yes, because a social media post could be misinterpreted and cause serious damage to a company’s reputation
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: Yes, because a social media post could be misinterpreted and cause serious damage to a company’s reputation

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: A post on social media can be copied and spread around the world in seconds?
options: TRUE
FALSE

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: Once you have uploaded an image to social media channels, can you take it back and delete it forever?
options: Yes. Once you have deleted a photo it entirely deletes it from the internet
It can be deleted, but it might take 24 hours to delete from other internet sites
No, you can’t delete a photo once it has been posted
If you contact the social media sites, then they can put a stop to it
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: No, you can’t delete a photo once it has been posted

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: Do things on the Internet get deleted after a certain amount of time?
options: Yes, nothing is kept on the internet forever
If your accounts have been inactive for 5 years they will be deleted
No, nothing will ever disappear on the internet
Your posts and photos are owned by you so even if they don’t get deleted no one will be able to re-use them anyway
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: No, nothing will ever disappear on the internet

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: If you post information that is not accurately marked with a time and a place   a potential consequence could be that _____
options: Your name and social media accounts will rank higher in search engines, e.g. google
Journalists are allowed to fill in the time and place themselves
Researchers will have restricted access to your posts
Journalists will assume what they want to get a good story
CD4060 — Social Media awareness.answer: Journalists will assume what they want to get a good story

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: If you are in a critical situation and you need to give a message to family or friends, what should you do?
options: Post a public status message
Post a photo of the situation and tag them
Give them a phone call
Contact the agent

CD4060 — Social Media awareness.question: What you post on social media can possibly damage your company’s reputation.
options: True, because others might misunderstand the posts and get a different story from them
True, but only if my posts and photos are manipulated
False, because photos cannot be interpreted in many ways
False, because posts can be hidden and deleted permanently

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: On board which vessels is it required to have a working environment committee?
options: On board vessels required to have a safety representative and having ^Mnot less than eight persons working on board.
On board all Norwegian flagged vessels.
On board vessels required to have at least two safety representatives.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: On board vessels required to have a safety representative and having ^Mnot less than eight persons working on board.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Your vessel will pass an area known for pirate activity. Does Norwegian law allow armed guards on board?^MIf so, under whose command are the armed guards while on board?
options: Norwegian law does not allow the use of armed guards.
Norwegian law allows the use of armed guards. They must be accompanied by an officer ^Mwho will make any decisions on the use of force.
Norwegian law allows the use of armed guards. They are under the Master’s command.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: Norwegian law allows the use of armed guards. They are under the Master’s command.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Due to a problem with the autopilot, your ship has to use a helmsman. The crew is busy with tank cleaning. ^MCould the helmsman also function as look-out between sunset and sunrise?
options: No.
Yes.
Yes, but only if the position of the steering stand allows a clear view in all directions.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: One of your crewmembers wants to become an officer. He has worked in the company for two years, ^Mbut also has several years of experience from other companies. ^MDoes he have to resign from his position in order to go to school?
options: No, he is entitled to leave for up to three years.
Yes, but he must be given priority when applying for a position in the same ^Mcompany after having completed his education.
Yes.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: No, he is entitled to leave for up to three years.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: One of your crewmembers is going to be a father. ^MWhat are the rights of the father in connection with childbirth?
options: He is entitled to two weeks’ leave of absence.
He is entitled to four weeks’ leave of absence.
The father has no particular rights in connection with childbirth.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: He is entitled to two weeks’ leave of absence.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: You are in a foreign port outside the European Economic Area and you have received a delivery of PPE. ^MIt turns out that the PPE is not carrying the CE marking. Can it still be used on board?
options: Yes, PPE does not need to carry CE marking.
No, all PPE must carry CE marking.
Yes, if it is not possible to get CE marked PPE and the equipment is of an equivalent quality.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: Yes, if it is not possible to get CE marked PPE and the equipment is of an equivalent quality.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: If the Master is absent, who makes decisions that cannot be postponed?
options: The senior mate present.
The Chief Engineer.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: How can the crew know whether or not exemptions have been made from Norwegian regulations on board?
options: The exemptions are noted in collective bargaining agreements.
It is not possible to make exemptions from Norwegian regulations.
Every ship will have its own booklet containing exemptions from regulations.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: The exemptions are noted in collective bargaining agreements.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Who is responsible for ensuring safety at sea?
options: The state under whose flag the ship is registered.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries.
The Norwegian Petroleum Safety Authority.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: The state under whose flag the ship is registered.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: What is The Excerpts from the Norwegian Passenger and Cargo Ship Legislation?
options: A collection of rules and regulations that are relevant for Norwegian flagged vessels.
Norwegian rules and regulations that are relevant for all international vessels.
Exeptions in rules and regulations that are not relevant for Norwegian flagged vessels.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: A collection of rules and regulations that are relevant for Norwegian flagged vessels.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: EEA citizens who are holders of certificates that will be recognised by the Norwegian Maritime Authority^M in accordance with the regulations will be issued a Certificate of Receipt of Application (CRA) once ^Mthey have submitted a complete application for endorsement. For how long can the applicant ^Mwork on board with a CRA?
options: Until the application has been processed and decided.
For a maximum of three months.
For a maximum of six months.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: Until the application has been processed and decided.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Who shall ensure that loading and discharge are carried out and the voyage performed with due dispatch?
options: The Master.
The Chief Officer.
The NMA.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that Norwegian laws are complied with on board?
options: The Master.
The Company.
The Company’s Designated Person.
The Superintendent.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Where can you find information on who to contact in case of an accident?
options: On the Norwegian Maritime Authority’s home page.
In the Excerpts from the Norwegian Passenger and Cargo Ship Legislation.
In the Ship Safety and Security Act.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: On the Norwegian Maritime Authority’s home page.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Where can you find a comprehensive list of publications and documents that must be carried on board?
options: In the Excerpts from the Norwegian Passenger and Cargo Ship Legislation.
At lovdata.no
In the Ship Labour Act.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: In the Excerpts from the Norwegian Passenger and Cargo Ship Legislation.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Who is responsible for supervising NIS flagged vessels?
options: The Classification Societies.
The NMA.
The Norwegian Coast Guard.
Norwegian Police.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: Your Chief Mate wants to inspect a tank where there is a danger of lack of oxygen. ^MAfter having completed the tank entry permit, including gas measurement, he plans ^Mon posting a tank watch with a BA set and a radio when entering the tank. Is this sufficient?
options: No, there has to be at least two persons present at the tank.
Yes, that is sufficient.
No, the tank watch must also have rescue equipment available.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: No, there has to be at least two persons present at the tank.

CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.question: One of your seafarers has become injured and is sent ashore for treatment. ^MYour ship is now below minimum safe manning. Can the ship still leave port?
options: Yes, but only for a short passage if all other requirements are fulfilled.
No, it is strictly prohibited to leave port if the ship is not manned ^Min accordance with the safe manning document.
Yes, you may operate the vessel until a replacement can be sent onboard.
CD4150 — Norwegian maritime rules and re.answer: Yes, but only for a short passage if all other requirements are fulfilled.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What action should be avoided during the approach to the anchorage?
options: Crossing in front of an anchored vessel at short distance.
Passing behind an anchored vessel at short distance and slow speed.
Passing behind another vessel that is manoeuvring towards anchorage.
All three answers.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Crossing in front of an anchored vessel at short distance.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: How should you secure the anchor cable when your vessel is anchored?
options: By using the cable stopper and windlass brake, with slight slack on the cable between the stopper and the brake.
By using lashing wires and the brake.
By using the anchor windlass brake and leaving the motor in gear.
By using the cable stopper.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: By using the cable stopper and windlass brake, with slight slack on the cable between the stopper and the brake.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Which movements of the vessel could increase the ship's draft and reduce the Under keel Clearance?
options: Squat, pitching in a seaway, heeling due to rapid alterations of course
Unmarked wrecks or seabed features.
Uncharted areas of seabed.
Changes in the vessel's passage plan.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Squat, pitching in a seaway, heeling due to rapid alterations of course

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What data can be found on a ship's Manoeuvring Poster?
options: Turning circles in the ballast and loaded conditions.
Emergency contact numbers for CSO.
Blind sectors for RADARs.
All three answers.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Turning circles in the ballast and loaded conditions.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: At which speed could the ship's bow (or stern) thruster be mechanically damaged?
options: At a ship's speed of more than five knots.
At a ship's speed of more than two knots.
When the vessel is stopped.
When the vessel is running astern at a speed of less than two knots.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: At a ship's speed of more than five knots.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What means should be used when securing the anchor for sea?
options: It should be secured by the windlass brake, cable stopper and lashing wire.
It should be secured by the windlass brake, ready for immediate use.
In good weather it can be secured by the windlass brake only.
