It should be secured by engaging the gipsy and securing the brake.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: It should be secured by the windlass brake, cable stopper and lashing wire.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: You are on a ULCC of 300,000 tonne DWT in calm conditions and you are supposed to anchor in 90 metres depth. How much chain should you use?
options: About eleven shackles.
About three shackles.
About five shackles.
About eight shackles.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: About eleven shackles.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: At which speed is the bow (or stern) thruster ineffective?
options: At a ship's speed of more than five knots.
At a ship's speed of more than two knots.
When the vessel is stopped.
When the vessel is running astern at a speed of less than two knots.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: At a ship's speed of more than five knots.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What information can you find from the ship's turning circles posted on the Manoeuvring Posters?
options: Information about the "wheel-over point".
Information on the stopping distance while the vessel carries out a full turn in ballast condition.
All three answers.
Information about the stopping distances in zig-zag manoeuvres.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Information about the "wheel-over point".

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: You meet another vessel port to port in a narrow channel. What interaction could you expect of both ships?
options: The bows of both ships will be pushed away from each other and the aft parts of the vessels could make contact.
The bows of both ships will be sucked together and the forward parts of the vessels could make contact.
Only the ship with the deepest draft will be affected.
Only the ship with the lightest draft will be affected.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: The bows of both ships will be pushed away from each other and the aft parts of the vessels could make contact.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What could reduce the effect of squat on your vessel?
options: Decreasing the speed of the vessel.
Increasing the ship's speed.
Maintaining your ship's present speed and course.
Trim the vessel by stern as much as possible.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Decreasing the speed of the vessel.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Why is it important to have the length of the ship's forward and aft vertical blind sectors listed on the Manoeuvring Posters?
options: To know the length of the blind area under the ship's forecastle or behind the stern that is not directly visible from the wheel-house.
It is a class requirement for them to be listed on the Manoeuvring Posters.
This information is required when taking compass bearings with the bridge wing gyro repeaters.
It enables the Officer of the Watch to estimate speed through the water.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: To know the length of the blind area under the ship's forecastle or behind the stern that is not directly visible from the wheel-house.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What should be undertaken before you switch from sea to manoeuvring speed?
options: Give one-hour notice to the engine room before requesting them to slow down from Sea to Manoeuvring Speed.
Check the length of the remaining voyage before commencing to manoeuvring.
Check the ship's ETA.
Inform the Master and the Pilot.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Give one-hour notice to the engine room before requesting them to slow down from Sea to Manoeuvring Speed.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: If you are sailing in shallow water with 20% UKC (Under Keel Clearance), how will your ship's stopping distance be affected, relative to deep water?
options: Longer than normal.
The same as for deep waters.
Shorter than normal.
About 1.5 ships longer.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Longer than normal.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What should be done as a first response to the "Man Overboard Emergency"?
options: Raise the Emergency Alarm, drop the MOB buoy on the side of the man overboard, place wheel hard over on the side of man overboard, place engines on standby.
Mark the event on the GPS set.
Inform the Master and await his arrival to the bridge.
Inform the DPA.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Raise the Emergency Alarm, drop the MOB buoy on the side of the man overboard, place wheel hard over on the side of man overboard, place engines on standby.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What actions should be taken immediately by the Officer of the Watch if the vessel starts dragging anchor?
options: Call the Master, inform the engine room that the main engine is required
Give one hours notice to the engine room that the main engine is required
Inform the vessel behind you that your vessel is dragging anchor.
Inform the Port Authority or Coast Guard.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Call the Master, inform the engine room that the main engine is required

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What would be the correct method of approach to a busy anchorage area?
options: Slow down well in advance, approach in a controlled manner and identify a suitable anchoring position.
Proceed at full manouvering speed and look for a suitable anchorage.
Stop a few nautical miles before the designated anchorage area and wait for the anchorage area to clear-up.
Proceed at dead slow ahead until the anchorage area is clear.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Slow down well in advance, approach in a controlled manner and identify a suitable anchoring position.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: From which direction does the wind have the greatest effect on the vessel's manoeuvring?
options: On the beam, with the vessel in ballast condition.
From right ahead.
From right astern.
On the quarter, with the vessel in loaded condition.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: On the beam, with the vessel in ballast condition.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: If your vessel is turning to starboard in shallow water with 20% UKC (Under Keel Clearance), what will be the diameter of the turn when compared with deep water?
options: The turn will be wider than a normal deep water turn.
The turn will be wider on the port side and tighter on the starboard side than a normal deep water turn.
The turn will be same as a deep water turn.
The turn will be tighter than a normal deep water turn.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: The turn will be wider than a normal deep water turn.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: How long can the main engine be run on critical revolutions?
options: Long enough for the transfer from one speed setting to another.
As long as required.
It should not be run on critical revolutions at all.
As long as the Chief Engineer permits.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Long enough for the transfer from one speed setting to another.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Why should the maximum air draft be carefully calculated?
options: So that the air clearance is known when passing under bridges or electrical cables over channels or rivers.
Because the Officer of the Watch requires this information when using the sextant.
Because this information is always required by port operators.
This information is required for the GMDSS Log book.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: So that the air clearance is known when passing under bridges or electrical cables over channels or rivers.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What is the correct way of anchoring in deep water?
options: Approach the anchorage at slow speed, walk out the anchor to above the water line, stop the vessel, and then walk out the chain by the windlass to the required amount when ready.
Approach the anchorage at slow speed, pay out the anchor for one shackle and drop the anchor by the brake.
Approach the anchorage at slow speed, stop the vessel, pay out the anchor for one shackle and drop out the anchor by the brake.
Approach the anchorage at slow speed, stop the vessel and drop the anchor from the hawe pipe.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Approach the anchorage at slow speed, walk out the anchor to above the water line, stop the vessel, and then walk out the chain by the windlass to the required amount when ready.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What means of position-fixing should you use during the approach to anchorage?
options: All available means.
Radar only, due to the increased workload on the bridge team.
GPS, because it is more accurate.
Visual methods, such as buoys.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: All available means.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What should you watch for if you are overtaking a similar size vessel in a narrow channel?
options: The bow of your vessel could be sucked towards the other vessel and the stern pushed away as you pass.
That the other vessel is not decreasing its speed.
That you keep your vessel at full sea speed during overtaking.
Make sure you maintain course because the bow of your vessel could be pushed away from the other vessel.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: The bow of your vessel could be sucked towards the other vessel and the stern pushed away as you pass.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What is the formula to calculate squat in open sea conditions?
options: The speed in knots squared, multiplied by the block coefficient.
One and a half times the speed in knots squared, plus the block coefficient.
The draught in metres, times the speed in knots, times the block coefficient.
The draught in metres squared, multiplied by the block coefficient.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: The speed in knots squared, multiplied by the block coefficient.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What is the "pivot point"?
options: It is the imaginary point around which the vessel turns.
It is the point where the forward light mast is posted.
It is the point where the ship's centre manifolds are fitted.
It is the point where the forward tugboats should be secured for towing.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: It is the imaginary point around which the vessel turns.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: What equipment must be tested before anchoring?
options: The steering gear, anchor windlass, and main engine ahead and astern.
The fire alarm system.
The anchor lights and deck lighting.
Main and emergency fire pumps.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: The steering gear, anchor windlass, and main engine ahead and astern.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: A "Williamson Turn", can be used in a Man Overboard situation, what is the first action when executing such a turn?.
options: Put the wheel hard over towards the man in the water.
Reduce engine speed to Dead Slow Ahead.
Alter course 60 degrees to starboard.
Stop engines.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Put the wheel hard over towards the man in the water.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: You are sailing on a small coaster, approaching the berth port side at the speed of one knot, and have moderate wind from the starboard side and no tug. How could you assist yourself in the situation described?
options: Let go starboard anchor and pay out the cable controlling the bow as you are approaching the berth.
Let go port anchor and gradually release the chain as you are approaching the berth.
Give the rudder hard a starboard.
Increase the speed and drop port anchor one shackle in the water.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Let go starboard anchor and pay out the cable controlling the bow as you are approaching the berth.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Which communications links should be tested before anchoring?
options: Between the bridge and the forecastle, engine room, and steering gear
Between the ship and the port authority or traffic information service.
All GMDSS equipment.
Between the bridge wings and the wheelhouse.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Between the bridge and the forecastle, engine room, and steering gear

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Where is the best place to anchor in a crowded anchorage?
options: At the edge of the anchorage.
In the fairway entrance.
In the centre of the crowded anchorage.
In the deepest part of the crowded anchorage.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: At the edge of the anchorage.

CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.question: Your vessel has a conventional right-hand propeller. How would you position your rudder before going full power astern?
options: Amidships.
Hard a port.
Hard a starboard.
Ten degrees to port.
CD7001 — TOTS 1A-Ship Handling and Chara.answer: Amidships.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When is the final "pilotage passage plan" agreed with the Pilot?
options: As soon as he arrives on the bridge.
By VHF prior to his arrival.
The local agent will keep him informed.
By VTS (Vessel Traffic Services).
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: As soon as he arrives on the bridge.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The weather is extremely bad with a poor forecast, so disembarking the pilot would be very dangerous. What actions would you take?
options: Proceed with the pilot to the next port or suitable rendezvous position.
Anchor and wait for an improvement in the weather.
Return to the port.
Check with the charter party for a deviation clause.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Proceed with the pilot to the next port or suitable rendezvous position.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When a helm order is given by the Pilot, the Helmsman will..
options: repeat and execute the order.
execute the order.
ask the Captain.
wait for the Officer of the Watch to confirm.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: repeat and execute the order.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: If you do not agree with the Pilot's intended actions, would you..
options: immediately discuss the action with the Pilot and Master.
not interfere since he is the Pilot.
inform the VTS (Vessel Traffic Services).
consider asking him later after the passage.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: immediately discuss the action with the Pilot and Master.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: What is your understanding of mixed moorings?
options: Natural or man-made fibre ropes that are used in conjunction with wire ropes.
A combination wire.
Different diameters of wire ropes.
Some mooring lines that are secured on a winch while others are secured on the bitts.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Natural or man-made fibre ropes that are used in conjunction with wire ropes.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The wind and sea are on the starboard bow, however, the swell is on the port beam. What would your initial action be regarding pilot disembarkation?
options: To fully discuss the circumstances with the Pilot.
Ask the pilot boat.
Ask VTS (Vessel Traffic Services).
Rig the pilot ladder on the port side.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: To fully discuss the circumstances with the Pilot.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The vessel's freeboard is 9.5 metres. How would you disembark the Pilot?
options: Using a pilot ladder combined with an accommodation ladder.
Being just inside the regulations, using a pilot ladder only would be satisfactory.
Obtain the services of a helicopter.
Using the accommodation ladder only.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Using a pilot ladder combined with an accommodation ladder.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: What is a "Pilot Card"?
options: It's a detailed description of the vessel, the main engine characteristics and operational status, and the limitations of various equipment.
It's the card the Master signs to enable the Pilot to receive his fee.
It's confirmation of the Pilot's attendance on board.
It contains details of the Pilot's name and the maximum size of vessel he can pilot.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: It's a detailed description of the vessel, the main engine characteristics and operational status, and the limitations of various equipment.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Why is it important to monitor the vessel's progress in pilotage waters?
options: To ensure that the vessel is proceeding safely as per agreed passage plan.
It is only important in reduced visibility.
So as to ensure that the ETA at the berth is maintained.
It is not important but it's advisable.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: To ensure that the vessel is proceeding safely as per agreed passage plan.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Is a Canal Helmsman compulsory?
options: It depends on the local Pilotage Authorities' regulations and the conditions of pilotage.
Yes, always.
No, never.
Only in poor visibility.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: It depends on the local Pilotage Authorities' regulations and the conditions of pilotage.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: You observe that the Canal Helmsman is not following the Pilot's instructions. What action would you take?
options: Immediately alert the Pilot to the circumstances.
Take no action as he is an experienced helmsman for those waters.
Check that the course the Helmsman has taken is not dangerous.
Alert the Pilotage Authority .
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Immediately alert the Pilot to the circumstances.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: What information should be passed to the Pilot when he arrives on the bridge?
options: The Master/Pilot Exchange information card.
The location of life-saving appliances.
The VHF channels being monitored.
ISPS procedures.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The Master/Pilot Exchange information card.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When the vessel is under pilotage, where would you find information regarding the bridge team compliment and respective responsibilities?
options: The company's SMS (Safety Management System).
The Admiralty Sailing Directions.
The Master's standing orders.
The Pilot Card.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The company's SMS (Safety Management System).

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The agreed language is English, however the Canal Helmsman repeats orders in a different language. What action would you take?
options: Immediately remind the Pilot and the Helmsman that the agreed language is English and to comply accordingly.
As long as the vessel is on course and the pilot and helmsman understand each other it does not matter
Let the Pilot and the Helmsman communicate how they wish.
Make a complaint to the Pilotage Authority.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Immediately remind the Pilot and the Helmsman that the agreed language is English and to comply accordingly.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The Wheel-house Poster contains information regarding..
options: specific manoeuvring information / characteristics of the vessel.
boarding arrangements for pilots.
similar information to the Pilot Card.
the owners / managers standing orders.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: specific manoeuvring information / characteristics of the vessel.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The wind and sea are on the port bow. Which side would you rig the pilot ladder?
options: The starboard side.
The port side.
Ask the pilot which side.
Ask the VTS (Vessel Traffic Services) which side.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The starboard side.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Your gyro compass has failed. Would you..
options: inform the Pilot?
switch on the radar?
tell the agent?
keep quiet in case it affects the pilot's concentration.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: inform the Pilot?

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When a canal helmsman is being used, the ship's helmsman should..
options: remain on the bridge in case he is required.
stand-by in the messroom.
get some rest while he can.
take the opportunity to clean the wheel-house.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: remain on the bridge in case he is required.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The Pilot requires a seaman to stand-by forward for the whole pilotage. Do you..
options: organise your available manpower accordingly and post a seaman forward?
explain to the Pilot that it is not in the vessel's SMS (Safety Management System) and so you are unable to do so?
simply refuse as you do not have the manpower?
refuse on the basis of fatigue?
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: organise your available manpower accordingly and post a seaman forward?

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: What would your actions be if the Canal Helmsman requested a short rest due to fatigue?
options: Upon obtaining the Pilot's agreement, the vessel's own Helmsman would take over under close supervision.
He should not be allowed to rest under any circumstances.
Let the Pilot steer the vessel.
The Officer of the Watch would take over.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Upon obtaining the Pilot's agreement, the vessel's own Helmsman would take over under close supervision.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When would you use a combination ladder for pilot boarding?
options: When the vessel's freeboard exceeds 9 metres.
When the pilot ladder is damaged.
When the accommodation ladder faces forward.
Only when the pilot requests it.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: When the vessel's freeboard exceeds 9 metres.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: What is described by the "Air draft"?
options: The height of the highest point of the vessel above the waterline.
The ship's draft in different terms.
The wind force at pilot boarding position.
The wind force on board a vessel when approaching port.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The height of the highest point of the vessel above the waterline.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Would you expect a Canal Helmsman to only take helm orders from the Pilot?
options: No, he is under the Master's direct authority also.
It's not important as the Master would probably not interfere.
It may depend upon the local Pilotage Authorities' regulations.
Yes, the Pilot is in charge.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: No, he is under the Master's direct authority also.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When discussing the UKC with the Pilot, what is your understanding of the term "controlling depth"?
options: The minimum depth of water within the limits of a channel.
The maximum draft the vessel can transit at.
The sounding on a chart close to where you want to transit.
An allowance for squat.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The minimum depth of water within the limits of a channel.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Which volume of the Admiralty List of Radio Signals gives contact information for marine pilots?
options: Volume 6.
Volume 2.
None. Information is only from Guide to Port Entry.
The Mariner's Handbook.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: Volume 6.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Why does a berthing pilot need to know the propeller's direction of turn (left or right-handed)?
options: The direction of turn of the propeller affects which way the bow may move when operating astern propulsion.
It affects the speed of the vessel.
It effects the response time of the main engine.
The allowance for squat may be affected.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: The direction of turn of the propeller affects which way the bow may move when operating astern propulsion.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: Where would you find your company instructions regarding UKC?
options: In the Company's SMS (Safety Management System).
On the Pilot Card.
In the approved Trim & Stability book.
In the SOLAS training manual.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: In the Company's SMS (Safety Management System).

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: If the Captain is unable to contact the Pilot Authority directly, he may pass a message via the..
options: local agent.
local ship handler.
Port State Control.
local coastguard.
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: local agent.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: When making verbal contact with the pilot station, the ship will be identified by name and..
options: its call sign.
its IMO number.
its telex number.
its nationality (flag).
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: its call sign.

CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.question: The presence of a pilot on the ship does not relieve the master or officer in charge of the navigational watch from their duties and obligations for the safe conduct of the ship.
options: True
False
CD7002 — TOTS 1A-Pilotage.answer: True

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the first task of the Officer in Charge of the mooring station upon arrival at the station?
options: To check the communication with the wheel-house / the Master.
To check that all of his crew are stand-by.
To check that all of his crew are available at the mooring station.
To check that all of the mooring equipment is ready for mooring.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: To check the communication with the wheel-house / the Master.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: During ship-to-ship operations, vessels use fenders. What is the purpose of the "secondary fenders"?
options: These small fenders which are suspended near the ship's bow or stern protect the vessel from ship-to-ship contact.
These small fenders (tyre type) are used from the deck during an emergency.
These small fenders (Manila Fender ball) are used by the crew during an emergency.
These large fenders are used on the "mother vessel" for separating the two ships.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: These small fenders which are suspended near the ship's bow or stern protect the vessel from ship-to-ship contact.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: During ship-to-ship operations, vessels use fenders. What is the purpose of the "primary fenders"?
options: These are large fenders, which float between the ships, and are made to absorb the impact of two ships approaching during berthing and later when sailing together.
These fenders are fixed to the bow of the attending Tender Vessel during the transfer of the transfer hose.
These small fenders (tyre type) are used from the deck during an emergency.
These small fenders (Manila Fender ball) are used by the crew during an emergency.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: These are large fenders, which float between the ships, and are made to absorb the impact of two ships approaching during berthing and later when sailing together.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You are on a ULCC of 300,000 tonne DWT and you are supposed to anchor in 90 metres depth. How much chain should you pay out?
options: Eleven shackles.
Three shackles.
Five shackles.
Eight shackles.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Eleven shackles.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: If your vessel is turning in shallow water with 20% UKC (Under Keel Clearance), what will be the diameter of the turn when compared with deep water?
options: The turn will be wider than a normal deep water turn.
The turn will be wider on the port side and slighter on the starboard side than a normal deep water turn.
The turn will be same as a deep water turn.
The turn will be tighter than a normal deep water turn.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The turn will be wider than a normal deep water turn.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: If you are sailing in shallow water with 20% UKC (Under Keel Clearance), what will be your ship's stopping distance?
options: Longer than normal.
The same as for deep waters.
Shorter than normal.
About 1.5 ships longer.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Longer than normal.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Why is the Master-to-Pilot exchange of information procedure important for the safety of the berthing or unberthing operation?
options: Because it is confirmation that the plan for berthing between the Pilot and Master has been discussed and agreed.
Because it contains the Pilot Card.
Because it contains the berthing plan by the Master.
Because it contains the berthing plan by the Pilot.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Because it is confirmation that the plan for berthing between the Pilot and Master has been discussed and agreed.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What should you watch for if you are overtaking a similar size vessel in a narrow channel?
options: The bow of your vessel could be sucked towards the other vessel and the stern pushed away as you pass.
That the other vessel is not decreasing its speed.
That you keep your vessel at full sea speed during overtaking.
There is nothing particular you need to watch for.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The bow of your vessel could be sucked towards the other vessel and the stern pushed away as you pass.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What ships are required to be fitted with the aft ETA (Emergency Towing Arrangement) system?
options: Tankers over 20,000 tonnes DWT.
All ships over 20,000 tonnes DWT.
Tankers over 20,000 tonnes displacement.
All ships over 20,000 tonnes displacement.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Tankers over 20,000 tonnes DWT.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: When will a vessel need the assistance of Tugs?
options: When it reduces speed, is no longer under total self-control and does not have sufficient sea room to manoeuvre safely without external assistance.
Only when it starts the mooring operation (i.e. sending mooring ropes ashore).
Only when it starts the unberthing operation (i.e. letting go of the mooring ropes).
Only when the Pilot recommends it to the Master.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: When it reduces speed, is no longer under total self-control and does not have sufficient sea room to manoeuvre safely without external assistance.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: How could you define "squat"?
options: The increase in the ship's draught of the point of your ship that is closest to the bottom.
The decrease of the draught of your ship.
The decrease of the speed of your ship in confined waters.
The decrease of the speed and draft of your ship in confined waters.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The increase in the ship's draught of the point of your ship that is closest to the bottom.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What could minimise the effect of squat on your vessel?
options: Decreasing the speed of the vessel as much as safe navigation permits.
Increasing the ship's speed if you are not already on full ahead.
Maintaining your ship's present speed and course.
Trim the vessel by stern as much as possible.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Decreasing the speed of the vessel as much as safe navigation permits.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What moorings should be avoided if leading in the same direction?
options: Mixed mooring ropes of various quality and strength.
Mooring wires not fitted with mooring tails.
Soft mooring ropes of various ages.
Mooring wires not fitted with a non-friction link between the wire and tail.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Mixed mooring ropes of various quality and strength.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What important design feature should be met for the construction of the aft ETA (Emergency Towing Arrangement) system?
options: The aft ETA should be pre-rigged and capable of being deployed in a controlled manner in controlled conditions in not more than 15 minutes by one person.
The aft ETA should have a SWL of at least 200 tonnes.
The aft ETA should have a towing cable of at least 100 metres in length.
The aft ETA should be able to be remote-controlled from the stern during deployment.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The aft ETA should be pre-rigged and capable of being deployed in a controlled manner in controlled conditions in not more than 15 minutes by one person.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: When synthetic (other than nylon) mooring tails are used in combination with mooring wire, what SWL should they have?
options: 25% more SWL than mooring wire.
50 % more SWL than mooring wire
10% more SWL than mooring wire.
37.5% more SWL than mooring wire.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: 25% more SWL than mooring wire.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the most dangerous part of mooring operations?
options: The crew staying in rope "snap-back" and "rope-tight" areas.
Anchoring in rivers.
Berthing with the use of a Pilot and tugs in restricted visibility conditions.
Berthing of a vessel in high tidal ports.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The crew staying in rope "snap-back" and "rope-tight" areas.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What important design feature should be met for construction of the forward ETA (Emergency Towing Arrangement) system?
options: The forward ETA should be capable of being deployed in harbour condition in not more than one hour.
The forward ETA should be capable of being deployed in not more than one hour by two crew members.
The forward ETA should be able to be used for normal berthing of a vessel alongside the terminal.
The forward ETA should be fitted on the centre line of the vessel.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The forward ETA should be capable of being deployed in harbour condition in not more than one hour.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: When should the emergency towing wires (fire wires) be deployed?
options: When the vessel is berthed at the terminals and tugs are available.
Only on terminals where the vessel is secured alongside the jetty.
Whenever the vessel is not in navigation.
Whenever the vessel is anchored or berthed at the terminals.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: When the vessel is berthed at the terminals and tugs are available.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Why are the non-friction type of mooring tail shackles important to  use between mooring wires and tails?
options: Because they are the safest connection between the mooring wire and the soft (i.e. nylon) mooring tail and they extend the lifetime of the mooring eyes on the wires and tails.
Because they are made of anti-sparking material and prevent sparking when the mooring wire is paid out or pulled in on board.
Because they are required by Oil Major Vetting Inspectors.
They are a requirement of the PSC and USCG for large crude carriers and ULCC ships.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Because they are the safest connection between the mooring wire and the soft (i.e. nylon) mooring tail and they extend the lifetime of the mooring eyes on the wires and tails.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the MBL of mooring ropes or wires?
options: Minimum Breaking Load.
Minimum Braking Load.
Maximum Breaking Load.
Minimum Braking Length
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Minimum Breaking Load.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You meet another vessel port to port in a narrow channel. What interaction could you expect of both ships?
options: The bows of both ships will be pushed away from each other and aft parts could make contact.
The bows of both ships will be sucked together and the ships could make contact with forward parts.
Both ships will proceed on their planned courses and tracks.
This does not apply to tankers.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The bows of both ships will be pushed away from each other and aft parts could make contact.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You are sailing on a small coaster, approaching the berth port side at the speed of one knot, and have moderate wind from the starboard side and no tug. How could you assist yourself in the situation described?
options: Let go starboard anchor and pay out the cable controlling the bow as you are approaching the berth.
Let go port anchor and gradually release the chain as you are approaching the berth.
Give the rudder hard a starboard.
Increase the speed and drop port anchor one shackle in the water.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Let go starboard anchor and pay out the cable controlling the bow as you are approaching the berth.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What information should be available on board for each mooring rope or mooring wire?
options: A certificate of quality stating the construction, the material and MBL/SWL, the position of the rope on board and the age (time of use of particular rope).
The SWL of mooring ropes or wires.
The MBL of mooring ropes or wires.
The type of construction material of the mooring ropes and wires in order to avoid using mixed mooring in the same direction.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: A certificate of quality stating the construction, the material and MBL/SWL, the position of the rope on board and the age (time of use of particular rope).

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What safe practices should be enforced during mooring operations?
options: All three answers.
The use of Personal Protective Equipment.
The familiarisation of new personnel with mooring equipment (e.g. winches, brakes, SWL of bitts).
The mooring station should always be manned with a sufficient number of trained and skilled Officers in Charge and crew.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: All three answers.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the principal purpose of the emergency towing wires (fire wires) on tankers?
options: To be used if there is a fire on board or at the terminal and the ship needs to be pulled off the terminal.
To be used for normal unberthing operation of the vessel.
To be used to extend the towing rope of the tugboat during unberthing.
To be used for shifting the vessel alongside the jetty.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: To be used if there is a fire on board or at the terminal and the ship needs to be pulled off the terminal.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: When nylon mooring tails are used in combination with mooring wire, what SWL should they have?
options: 37.5% more SWL than mooring wire.
25% more SWL than mooring wire.
50% more SWL than mooring wire.
10% more SWL than mooring wire.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: 37.5% more SWL than mooring wire.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: If you are using one tugboat to assist the vessel for turning bow to port in a narrow channel (with the ship's main engine also being used), where should you position the tug and how should you use it?
options: Make the tug fast on port shoulder and use it for pulling.
Make the tug fast aft on starboard shoulder and use it for pulling.
Make the tug fast on starboard aft shoulder and use it for pushing.
Make the tug fast forward through centre fairlead and start pulling.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Make the tug fast on port shoulder and use it for pulling.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Is it acceptable to travel at the speed of four knots in the approach to the berth?
options: It's too fast.
It's normal.
It's sufficient for manoeuvring.
It is up to the Pilot to decide.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: It's too fast.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Your vessel has a conventional right-hand propeller. How would you position your rudder before going full power astern?
options: Amidship.
Hard a port.
Hard a starboard.
Ten degrees to port.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Amidship.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You are turning your vessel in a narrow channel by using two tugs of the same bollard pull (same size tugs). The wind is strong and of variable force. Where you should position the tugs and how should you use them?
options: Make them fast to the vessel and use them for pushing.
Use them for pushing but not made fast to the vessel.
Make them fast to the vessel and use them for pulling.
Do not make them fast to the vessel and use one tug for pushing and other for pulling.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Make them fast to the vessel and use them for pushing.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Why are the mooring equipment records important for the safe operation of a vessel?
options: Because they contain all of the information on the construction of the mooring ropes and/or wires and their records of maintenance.
Because they are required by Oil Major Vetting Inspectors.
Because they are a requirement of the Company Planned Maintenance System.
Because they are a requirement of the ISM Code, Port State Control and USCG.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Because they contain all of the information on the construction of the mooring ropes and/or wires and their records of maintenance.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the CPP?
options: All three answers.
The CPP is when the pitch of the ship's propeller is controlled by the hydraulic system working through the propeller shaft.
The CPP is a special type of propeller that can be rotated around its long axis to change its pitch.
The CPP is the propeller that has a variable pitch in order to obtain the optimum efficiency in relation to a ship's load so that fuel can be saved.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: All three answers.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You are approaching the berth and only one tug is available. Where should you position it and how should it be used?
options: Make it fast on forward shoulder and use it for pulling and pushing.
Make it fast aft through the centre lid and use it for pulling.
Make it fast forward through the centre lid and use it for pulling.
Make it fast on the ship's  amidship side and use if for pushing and pulling when required.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Make it fast on forward shoulder and use it for pulling and pushing.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Your vessel is berthing starboard side on the terminal jetty. How could you use two tugs for berthing?
options: Make the tugs fast on the ship's flat sides and use them for pushing or pulling when required.
Make the tugs fast forward and aft through the centre lead.
Use the tugs to push the flat side of the vessel but not fast.
Make one tug fast forward through the centre lead for pulling, while the other is positioned on the aft port quarter for pushing.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Make the tugs fast on the ship's flat sides and use them for pushing or pulling when required.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Who has the overriding authority for decision-making on berthing over the tide?
options: The Master.
The Charterers.
The Company DPA.
The ship's Commercial Operator.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The Master.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Who is responsible for selecting the number of tugs to be used during mooring operations?
options: The Master.
The Pilot.
The Port Authorities.
The vessel agents in port.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The Master.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: You are on a 300,000 tonne DWT ULCC and the terminal is asking if your vessel is provided with SPM mooring according to OCIMF requirements. What is the requirement for fittings that should be complied with?
options: Two tongue-type chain stoppers of 200 tons SWL for a 76mm chain and separate closed fairleads of at least 450 x 600 mm in size.
One tongue-type chain stopper of 200 tonnes SWL for a 76mm chain and the centre line positioned closed fairlead of at least 450 x 600 mm in size.
Two tongue-type chain stoppers of 200 tonnes SWL for a 76mm chain and one centrally positioned closed fairlead of at least 450 x 600 mm in size.
One Smith-type bracket of 150 tonnes SWL for a 76mm chain and one closed fairlead of at least 450 x 600 mm in size.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Two tongue-type chain stoppers of 200 tons SWL for a 76mm chain and separate closed fairleads of at least 450 x 600 mm in size.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the "Bollard Pull" of the tugboat?
options: All three answers.
It is the indicator of a tug's power to push or pull.
It is the measure of a tug's thrust at zero speed through water with full engine RPM.
It is the main criteria of a tug and displays the pulling force expressed in tonnes.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: All three answers.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is it important to discuss during the pre-berthing briefing between the Master and the ship's officers?
options: The specific berthing operation for the forthcoming berthing, the use of tugs and the position of the mooring ropes/wires to be used.
Which officer will be on the forecastle and which on the stern during mooring operations.
The size (pulling power) of the tugs to be used during berthing.
How many crew members should be called for berthing operations.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The specific berthing operation for the forthcoming berthing, the use of tugs and the position of the mooring ropes/wires to be used.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is it important to avoid during berthing operations?
options: The mooring rope fouling around the turning propeller.
The forward and aft winches working at the same time.
The mooring stations remaining without communication by hand-held walkie-talkies with the wheel-house.
The mooring winches set on the correct speed and load setting.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The mooring rope fouling around the turning propeller.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: At what height should the eyes of the emergency towing wires (fire wires) be positioned?
options: They should be run out and maintained at the waterline or about two metres above it.
They should be kept secured not less than two metres above the waterline.
They should be kept at least two metres above the maximum loaded draught level.
They should be kept at least two meters above the minimum ballast draught level.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: They should be run out and maintained at the waterline or about two metres above it.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Your vessel is unmooring from the terminal and you have to use two tugs. How should you position and use them?
options: Make fast forward and aft in the centre line and pull the vessel from the jetty.
Make fast fwd tug on shoulder and keep aft tug on stand-by.
Make fast on ship's flat side and use the tugs for pulling the berth.
Use both tugs for pushing only until the vessel's ropes are cleared.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Make fast forward and aft in the centre line and pull the vessel from the jetty.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What should be done when a vessel is approaching the Pilot Station with the Pilot on board, and the Chief Engineer advises the bridge that engine trouble could be expected during mooring operations?
options: The Master should inform the Pilot, abort mooring operations and drop anchor in a safe location, if possible.
The Master should be advised so he can decide if mooring operations should continue.
The Master should call the Company DPA for advice and instructions.
The Master should do nothing and continue with berthing as planned.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The Master should inform the Pilot, abort mooring operations and drop anchor in a safe location, if possible.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the definition of "make fast"?
options: To secure the rope.
To act fast.
To release fast
To coil the rope around a storage drum.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: To secure the rope.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What should be the type and size (SWL) of the rope stoppers used for securing synthetic mooring ropes during mooring operations?
options: Double tail stoppers with a rope SWL of 25% of the mooring rope SWL.
Double tail stoppers with a rope SWL of 50% of the mooring rope SWL.
A single tail stopper with 50% SWL of the mooring rope.
A single tail stopper with 25% SWL of the mooring rope.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Double tail stoppers with a rope SWL of 25% of the mooring rope SWL.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What signals should be displayed by ships engaged in ship-to- ship operations while approaching one another?
options: Signals for vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre.
No special signals are required during daylight.
Signals for vessels not under command.
Signals for vessels in tow.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Signals for vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Why should the mooring rope (or wire) not be kept on winch brakes with an additional engaged winch gear?
options: It could cause damage to the winch, drum shaft and wire.
It could be broken more easily since the brake could not slip out.
It is not permitted by the terminal and OCIMF mooring equipment guidelines.
It is not a sign of good seamanship on board.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: It could cause damage to the winch, drum shaft and wire.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the recommended angle to be maintained between two ships after unberthing from ship-to-ship operations?
options: 5 degrees.
20 degrees.
2 degrees.
45 degrees.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: 5 degrees.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What signals should be displayed by ships engaged in ship-to- ship operations (while berthed together and underway)?
options: Signals for vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre.
No special signals are required during daylight.
Signals for vessels not under command.
Signals for vessels in tow.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: Signals for vessels restricted in their ability to manoeuvre.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the recommended procedure for securing synthetic rope on a pair of bitts?
options: To make an initial full turn around the outboard bitt and then secure the rope by using a figure eight on both bitts.
To make the rope fast on the outboard bitt only.
To make the rope fast on the inner bitt only.
To make the rope fast in a figure eight on both bitts.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: To make an initial full turn around the outboard bitt and then secure the rope by using a figure eight on both bitts.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the recommended procedure if your vessel is equipped with "self-stowing automatic tension" winches and your vessel is moored alongside the loading jetty with fixed loading arms?
options: All mooring ropes should be left secured by the manual mooring brakes and all winches should be left out of gear.
All winches should be kept in "auto-tension" mode.
Head and stern line winches should be kept in "auto-tension" mode and breast and spring ropes should be kept manually secured by brakes.
Spring line winches should be kept in "auto-tension" mode and all other ropes should be kept secured by manual brakes.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: All mooring ropes should be left secured by the manual mooring brakes and all winches should be left out of gear.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is the correct procedure for carrying out the winch brake test?
options: The winch brake lever is tightened by the torque wrench and the torque force is increased/adjusted until the required rendering force of the winch brake is reached.
The MBL of the mooring ropes/wires is calculated at 60% along with the required hydraulic jack force based on test equipment design characteristics.
The MBL of the mooring rope/wire is calculated at 80% along with the required hydraulic jack force based on test equipment design characteristics.
The winch brake lever is tightened by hand and tested with the hydraulic brake until the required brake force is achieved.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: The winch brake lever is tightened by the torque wrench and the torque force is increased/adjusted until the required rendering force of the winch brake is reached.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: How often should the mooring winch brake on tankers be tested?
options: At least every 12 months or after each change of brake band lining.
At fixed 12-month intervals.
At fixed 24-month intervals.
At each repair or dry-docking.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: At least every 12 months or after each change of brake band lining.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: How should you secure the anchor chain while your vessel is being anchored?
options: By using the chain stopper and windlass brake, with slight slack on the chain between the chain stopper and the brake.
By using lashing wires and the brake.
By using the anchor windlass brake and leaving the motor in gear.
By using the chain stopper.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: By using the chain stopper and windlass brake, with slight slack on the chain between the chain stopper and the brake.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: During a vessel's stay on a SPM berth, it is required to continuously monitor the ship's mooring.
options: True
False
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: True

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Your mooring winches are fitted with a brake-holding capacity of 60 tonnes. What size mooring ropes should you request?
options: 100 tonne MBL.
60 tonne MBL.
80 tonne MBL.
72 tonne MBL.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: 100 tonne MBL.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: What is an advantage of split-type mooring drums?
options: All three answers.
The mooring wires are not "crushed" under load.
There is a smaller chance that the mooring rope will be "jammed" on the storage part of reel.
The use of the split drum uses the winch braking capacity to its maximum.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: All three answers.

CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.question: Your ULCC-sized vessel is anchoring in deep water anchorage. Who should be in charge of anchoring operations on the forecastle?
options: An experienced licensed ship officer.
A licensed ship officer.
An experienced bosun.
Any experienced crew member appointed by the Master for this operation.
CD7003 — TOTS 1A-Mooring Equipment and O.answer: An experienced licensed ship officer.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: During appraisal what sources should the Navigating Officer use to gain information?
options: From every available source.
From official sources approved by the relevant Hydrographic Office.
From official sources approved by Company regulations.
From sources agreed by the Master.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What are the four stages of Passage Planning?
options: Appraisal, planning, execution, monitoring.
Pilotage outwards, sea passage, anchoring, pilotage inwards.
Planning on paper, preparing the route on the charts, discussion with the Master, correction of any errors.
Appraisal, preparation, approval, execution.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: If, during the Appraisal it is realised that one or more up to date charts at the best possible scale are not available on board, what action should be taken?
options: The necessary charts should be requisitioned.
The next best scale charts should be used.
Cancelled charts can be used with caution.
The route should be changed to use only acceptable charts.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: The necessary charts should be requisitioned.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What would you use a gnomonic chart for during Passage Planning?
options: To plot Great Circle courses and waypoints.
To show the complete passage conveniently on one chart.
To plot Rhumb Line courses and waypoints.
To show sections of the route for which suitable passage charts were not available.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: To plot Great Circle courses and waypoints.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: If a vessel is fitted with an unapproved electronic chart system, how can it be used in Passage Planning?
options: It should not be used for Passage Planning.
It can be used in the appraisal, but this must then be checked by another method.
It can be used fully, but positions must be plotted on a paper chart.
Any electronic chart system can be used with confidence, even if it has not been officially approved.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: It should not be used for Passage Planning.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is the "tidal window"?
options: It is the times between which the tide has achieved a required height, and it is safe for the ship to transit an area.
It is the time when the vessel can go alongside and start discharging cargo to reach the required safe draft.
It is the time required for the vessel to reach the berth from safe anchorage in a tidal area.
It is the maximum time permitted for the vessel to reach the berth from safe anchorage in a tidal area.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: It is the times between which the tide has achieved a required height, and it is safe for the ship to transit an area.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What information should you record in the Bell Book and the Deck Log Book about the navigation of the vessel?
options: Sufficient information to enable the reconstruction of the ship's movement if required at a later date.
Only the manoeuvring changes and status of the main engine should be recorded.
Only the times that are important for the charterers' commercial operations (like EOSP, Pilot on board, all fast etc should be recorded).
Only the information that is instructed by the Master to be recorded.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: Sufficient information to enable the reconstruction of the ship's movement if required at a later date.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is the meaning of the term "margin of safety"?
options: It is a line parallel to the track, within which the vessel will always be in safe water.
It is another phrase meaning "no-go areas".
It is not a phrase which should be used within the plan.
It is the distance from the nearest danger.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: It is a line parallel to the track, within which the vessel will always be in safe water.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: Why would you use risk assessment techniques during Passage Planning?
options: To reduce, and where possible eliminate risks from navigational hazards.
To reduce, and where possible eliminate risks to the Bridge Team personnel during the passage.
There is no requirement for risk assessment to be used.
To comply with Flag State or Company regulations.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: To reduce, and where possible eliminate risks from navigational hazards.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is the meaning of the term "abort point"?
options: It is the latest position where the vessel may abandon the planned passage and either return or stop safely.
It is any position on the passage where the vessel can abandon the planned passage.
It is the safe area, specified in the plan and marked on the chart, where the vessel can wait if the plan is abandoned.
It is not a phrase which should be used within the plan.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: It is the latest position where the vessel may abandon the planned passage and either return or stop safely.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What actions must the vessel be able to safely take at the abort point?
options: Turn around, stop in safe water, or anchor.
Reduce speed to minimum steerage way.
Pick up the Pilot, providing a lee if necessary.
Test the main engine ahead and astern.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: Turn around, stop in safe water, or anchor.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What type of markers can be used on nautical charts?
options: Soft 2B pencil and permanent magenta ink.
HB pencils only.
Ball-point pens.
White correction fluid.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: Soft 2B pencil and permanent magenta ink.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is achieved by the "appraisal" phase of passage planning?
options: Appraisal is the part of passage planning where all pertinent information is gathered and the firm foundation for the plan is built.
Appraisal is the part of passage plan where all the information on required charts is collected, and it is confirmed that all required charts are available on board.
Appraisal is the part of the passage plan where the Master decides which route the vessel will take between two ports.
Appraisal is the part of the passage plan that needs to approved by office.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: Appraisal is the part of passage planning where all pertinent information is gathered and the firm foundation for the plan is built.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is achieved by carefully selecting "no-go areas" on the nautical charts required for the ship's passage?
options: It indicates all areas where the vessel cannot go with present draft.
It indicates all areas where the vessel cannot go on deepest draft.
It indicates all areas where the vessel is advised not to go on deepest draft.
It indicates all areas where the vessel should not go when loaded.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: It indicates all areas where the vessel cannot go with present draft.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: Why should the passage plan be updated on receipt of Navarea Warnings or T&P notices during the voyage?
options: Because they may contain important and urgent navigational information and warnings that were not available on board at the beginning of the voyage.
Because they may contain instructions from owners or charterers regarding the voyage.
Because they may contain important commercial information regarding the availability of berths, tugs, pilots etc.
Because they may contain urgent weather warnings.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: Because they may contain important and urgent navigational information and warnings that were not available on board at the beginning of the voyage.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is the primary reason for the ship's passage plan to be discussed between the navigating officers and the Master before the beginning of a voyage?
options: In order to fully inform all navigation officers about the particular voyage, its specific issues and concerns.
In order to satisfy the Company's Navigational Procedures requirement.
In order to inform the officers and crew about the destination port.
In order to inform the Chief Officer and the 3rd Officer about the particular voyage and its specific issues and concerns.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: In order to fully inform all navigation officers about the particular voyage, its specific issues and concerns.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: When is the UKC (Under Keel Clearance) calculation required to be completed?
options: The UKC should be calculated and applied for all ships loading and discharging from ports, irrespective of any local regulations and requirements.
The UKC should be calculated for tankers while sailing to US ports.
The UKC should be calculated for loaded tankers while sailing to US ports.
The UKC should be calculated for all tankers while arriving and departing from US ports.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: The UKC should be calculated and applied for all ships loading and discharging from ports, irrespective of any local regulations and requirements.

CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.question: What is the meaning of the term "parallel index"?
options: A radar-based constant update of a ship's cross track error.
Information on radar about the ship's position in relation to a ship's longitudinal track error .
A navigational instrument used for plotting bearings on a chart.
Information on radar about the ship's position in relation to a fixed object ashore.
CD7004 — TOTS 1A-Passage Planning and Na.answer: A radar-based constant update of a ship's cross track error.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What actions required by the Collision Regulations should the Officer of the Watch comply with during periods of restricted visibility?
options: All three answers.
To sound the fog signals.
To proceed at a safe speed.
To have the ship's engines ready for immediate manoeuvres.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: When restricted visibility is encountered or is expected, who should be informed?
options: The Master.
The Lookout.
The Helmsman.
The Company Operator / DPA.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What standard sound signal must a vessel over 100 meters in length make at anchor in an area of restricted visibility?
options: Sounding the anchor bell forward immediately followed by sounding the gong aft.
Sounding the gong aft followed immediately by sounding the anchor bell forward.
Sounding the gong forward immediately followed by sounding the anchor bell aft.
Sounding the anchor bell aft immediately followed by sounding the gong forward.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: Sounding the anchor bell forward immediately followed by sounding the gong aft.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What additional sound signal may a vessel over 100 meters in length make at anchor in an area of restricted visibility?
options: Three blasts in succession, one short one prolonged and one short.
Three blasts in succession, two short and one prolonged.
Five short blasts in succession.
Three blasts in succession, one prolonged and two short.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: Three blasts in succession, one short one prolonged and one short.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: When is Rule 19 of COLREGS applicable, and to which ships?
options: This rule applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility.
This rule applies to all vessels sailing in an area of restricted visibility.
This rule applies to all power-driven vessels navigating in an area of restricted visibility.
This rule applies only to power-driven vessels navigating in an area of restricted visibility.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: This rule applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What sound signal should a towed vessel sound during periods of restricted visibility?
options: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts.
Two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts.
Two prolonged blasts.
Three prolonged blasts.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: In which publications can specific guidance and instructions on navigation in restricted visibility be found?
options: In the Bridge Procedures Guide, in COLREGS and in the Mariners' Handbook.
In the Bridge Procedures Guide, in Bridge Team Management and in the Passage Planning Guide.
In the Deck Log Book and in the Company Navigation Manual.
In the Master's Night Order Book.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: In the Bridge Procedures Guide, in COLREGS and in the Mariners' Handbook.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What action should you take when you hear the fog signal of another vessel apparently forward of the beam, or when you cannot avoid a close quarters situation with another vessel forward of the beam?
options: Reduce speed to the minimum and if necessary take all way off and in any event navigate with extreme caution.
Identify the other vessel by AIS, and then establish contact with the vessel to agree the intended course of action to avoid the danger.
Identify the other vessel by VHF using the ships call sign, and then establish the other vessels intended course of action to avoid the danger.
Sound five short blasts on the ships whistle to indicate doubt about the others intention.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: Reduce speed to the minimum and if necessary take all way off and in any event navigate with extreme caution.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What additional sound signal may a pilot vessel sound when engaged in pilotage duties?
options: Four short blasts.
Three short blasts.
Four long blasts.
Two short blasts followed two long blasts.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: If the vessel is fitted with two whistles that are spaced apart more than 100 metres, how should the whistles be arranged?
options: They should be arranged so that they are not sounded simultaneously.
They should be arranged so that they are sounded simultaneously.
They should be arranged so that only one can be used at a time.
They should be arranged so that the forward whistle always sounds first and then the aft whistle sounds with a 10 second delay.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: They should be arranged so that they are not sounded simultaneously.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: When a pushing vessel and a vessel being pushed ahead are rigidly connected in a composite what sound signal should they sound when in or near an area of restricted visibility when underway and making way.
options: One prolonged blast.
Two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts.
Two prolonged blasts.
Two short blasts

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What sound signal should a power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water sound during periods of restricted visibility?
options: Two prolonged blasts.
One prolonged blast.
Four prolonged blasts.
Two prolonged blasts followed by two short blasts.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What sound signal should a power-driven vessel making way through the water sound during periods of restricted visibility?
options: One prolonged blast
Two prolonged blast.
one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts
Two prolonged blasts followed by one short blast.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: At what intervals should a power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water sound two prolonged blasts in or near an area of restricted visibility?
options: At intervals of not more than two minutes.
At intervals of not more than one minute.
At intervals of not less than two minutes.
At intervals of not less than five minutes.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: At intervals of not more than two minutes.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: At what intervals should a vessel not under command, or a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, a vessel constrained by her draft, a sailing vessel, a vessel engaged in fishing and a vessel engaged in towing or pushing another vessel, sound three blasts in succession when in or near an area of restricted visibility?
options: At intervals of not more than two minutes.
At intervals of not more than one minute.
At intervals of not less than two minutes.
At intervals of not less than five minutes.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: At intervals of not more than two minutes.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: What is the meaning of the term "restricted visibility"?
options: Any condition in which visibility is restricted by fog, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar weather conditions.
Where visibility is restricted to within two nautical miles due to fog, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar weather conditions.
Where visibility is restricted to within three nautical miles due to fog, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar weather conditions.
Where visibility is restricted to within five nautical miles due to fog, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar weather conditions.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: Any condition in which visibility is restricted by fog, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar weather conditions.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: Where is the ship-specific information about restricted visibility declared?
options: In the Master's Bridge Standing Orders.
In the Company's Navigation Standing Orders.
In the Deck Log Book.
In the Master's Night Order Book.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: In the Master's Bridge Standing Orders.

CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.question: At what intervals should a power-driven vessel under way and making way through the water, sound one prolonged blast in or near an area of restricted visibility?
options: At intervals of not more than two minutes.
At intervals of not more than one minute.
At intervals of not less than two minutes.
At intervals of not less than five minutes.
CD7005 — TOTS 1A-Navigating in Restricte.answer: At intervals of not more than two minutes.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term "glacier ice"?
options: Ice originating from a glacier, either on land or floating on the sea as icebergs, bergy bits, growlers, or ice islands.
Any ice originating from large icebergs made of fresh water.
Any ice originating from fresh water.
Any ice originating from fresh water melted from glaciers.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Ice originating from a glacier, either on land or floating on the sea as icebergs, bergy bits, growlers, or ice islands.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term "sea ice"?
options: Any form of ice found at sea which originated from the freezing of seawater.
Any form of ice that is found on the open sea irrespective of the origin of the ice.
Any form of ice that is free floating away from the ice.
Any form of ice that is floating on the sea.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Any form of ice found at sea which originated from the freezing of seawater.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term "growler"?
options: A rounded piece of glacier ice, often transparent but appearing green or black in colour, extending less than 1 metre above the sea surface and normally occupying an area of about 20 m2.
A smaller piece of iceberg, extending about 5 metres above the sea surface, normally occupying an area of about 100 m2.
A special type of iceberg that is only found in the Antarctic that is about 5 metres in height and green or black in colour.
An iceberg that grows from packed sea ice and extends less than 1 metre above sea level.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: A rounded piece of glacier ice, often transparent but appearing green or black in colour, extending less than 1 metre above the sea surface and normally occupying an area of about 20 m2.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What are the main types of "sea ice" that ships encounter?
options: Drift and fast ice.
Icebergs and packed ice.
Growlers.
Glacier ice.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Drift and fast ice.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the general freezing point of seawater?
options: About - 2º C
About - 4º C
About 0º C
About - 5 º C
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: About - 2º C

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What can cause vessel icing on ships in freezing conditions?
options: All three answers.
Fog.
Rain or wet snow.
Sea spray or water breaking over the ship.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What are the signs of ice in the vicinity of the vessel?
options: All three answers.
Ice blink.
Sighting of small fragments of ice.
Abrupt moderation of the sea and swell.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What problems can occur on board from icing from fresh water?
options: Ice can accumulate on the rigging, and radar, and radio equipment failures can occur due to ice on the aerials.
Fresh water supplies will stop functioning
Ice can prevent the opening of all accommodation openings.
Heating systems will trip out on overload
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Ice can accumulate on the rigging, and radar, and radio equipment failures can occur due to ice on the aerials.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: In relation to navigating in ice conditions, the term beset means that the ship has found itself in a position where it is surrounded by ice and is unable to move. True or False?
options: True.
False.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: True.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is it important to know in order to decide the best course of action if the storm is suspected to be in the vessel's vicinity?
options: It is important to know the bearing of the centre of the storm and the path of the storm.
It is important to know where the nearest port of refuge is.
It is important to know the difference of pressure between the centre of the storm and the position of the vessel to calculate the strength of wind.
It is important to monitor the barometric pressure and wind strength and direction.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It is important to know the bearing of the centre of the storm and the path of the storm.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What action should you take if you find yourself within the dangerous semi-circle of a tropical storm in the Southern hemisphere and the wind is backing?
options: You should put the wind on the port bow and proceed at full available speed, altering the course to port as the wind backs.
You should put the wind on the port quarter and proceed as fast as possible in a southerly direction.
You should put the wind on the starboard quarter and proceed as fast as possible in a northerly direction.
