You should bring the wind on to the port quarter and proceed with all available speed turning to starboard as the wind changes direction.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: You should put the wind on the port bow and proceed at full available speed, altering the course to port as the wind backs.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term "ramming"?
options: Attempting to break the ice by repeatedly driving the ship as far forward as possible, backing the ship out and repeating the process.
The noise caused by icebreakers breaking the ice.
The unpleasant noise caused by the propeller grinding through the ice when the vessel is running ahead in the ballast condition.
The unpleasant noise caused by the propeller grinding through the ice when the vessel is running astern.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Attempting to break the ice by repeatedly driving the ship as far forward as possible, backing the ship out and repeating the process.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What impact could occur at a high speed while sailing through the ice?
options: The ship's hull could be damaged by collision with floes.
The ship could "run aground" on thick ice and not be able to back up if required.
A vessel navigating at a high speed through the ice could have problems with icing of the sea-boxes (water suctions).
A vessel navigating at a high speed through the ice could not keep the track through the passage opened by the icebreaker.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: The ship's hull could be damaged by collision with floes.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: You are in the vicinity of a tropical storm in the Northern hemisphere and the wind is remaining in a steady direction. If the vessel is in the navigable semi-circle, you should continue the voyage in the planned direction. True or False?
options: False.
True.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: False.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the "dangerous semicircle" of a tropical storm in the Southern hemisphere?
options: The dangerous semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye.
The dangerous semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the starboard side of the cyclone path and its eye.
The dangerous semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is 250 Nm fwd of the eye of the storm directly in her path.
The dangerous semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is 80 Nm fwd of the eye of the storm directly in her path.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: The dangerous semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What impact could vessel icing have on the ship?
options: Vessel icing may impair the stability and safety of the ship.
Vessel icing may impair the manoeuvring of the vessel.
Vessel icing may impair the visibility from the bridge
Vessel icing may impair the security of the vessel.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Vessel icing may impair the stability and safety of the ship.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is considered "new ice"?
options: Frazil ice, Slush, Sluga and Grease ice with a thickness of up to 2.5 cm
Young ice that has less than 10 cm of thickness.
First-year ice that has less than 30 cm of thickness.
First-year ice that has a thickness of between 30 to 70 cm.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Frazil ice, Slush, Sluga and Grease ice with a thickness of up to 2.5 cm

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: If the vessel is in port, what is the best option if a tropical cyclone is passing within 80 nautical miles or so?
options: The best option is to sail out to sea in time to avoid the worst of the storm.
The best option is to stay in sheltered waters, and, if possible, on special moorings.
The best option is to stay at anchorage and make the vessel as heavy as possible by adding as much full ballast as possible.
The best option is to stay alongside the well fendered berth that is on the lee-side of the wind.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: The best option is to sail out to sea in time to avoid the worst of the storm.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the indication of an approaching depression?
options: A falling barometer.
A rising barometer.
The wind is rising and the temperature is falling.
The wind is subsiding and the temperature is rising.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: A falling barometer.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the most serious danger to a "beset" vessel (i.e. a vessel that has become surrounded by ice and is unable to move)?
options: Pressure from the ice that can crush the hull or nip off the bottom.
Danger of running aground as it's carried by the moving drift ice.
Danger of icebergs capsizing the vessel.
Danger of the ice causing damage to the rudder and the propeller.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Pressure from the ice that can crush the hull or nip off the bottom.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is of vital importance when encountering a tropical cyclone in the vessel's vicinity?
options: It is imperative to avoid passing at 80 Nm or closer to the centre of the storm.
It is imperative to sail in the opposite direction of the storms track
It is imperative to carry out an emergency drill in order to prepare for a worse case scenario.
It is imperative to send out a SECURITE message to all ships in the vicinity warning them of the approcahing eye of the storm.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It is imperative to avoid passing at 80 Nm or closer to the centre of the storm.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What type of ice formation is most dangerous for navigation?
options: Icebergs.
Old ice.
New ice.
Sea ice.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Icebergs.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What should be the most important task when navigating in the vicinity of strong tropical storms (e.g. cyclones, hurricanes, typhoons)?
options: To stay as far as possible from the path forward of the tropical storm.
To monitor carefully all tropical storm area weather reports.
To frequently monitor the ship's barometer.
To inform the crew to secure all loose objects and equipment to avoid them being lost or damaged.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: To stay as far as possible from the path forward of the tropical storm.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: The vessel is in port and is due to sail in a few hours, however severe weather is forecast that may endanger the vessel. What should the Master do?
options: Based on risk assessment, the Master should make the decision on whether the vessel is in a "Go" or "No Go" situation and therefore determine if the ship should sail or remain in port.
The Master should make the decision based on available weather reports/forecasts and then wait for the company's advice.
The Master should evaluate the weather conditions and try to solve the problem without causing a commercial delay for the vessel.
The Master should call the company's operator for advice and further instruction.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Based on risk assessment, the Master should make the decision on whether the vessel is in a "Go" or "No Go" situation and therefore determine if the ship should sail or remain in port.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What are the characteristics of "trade winds" in the Southern hemisphere?
options: They have a south-easterly direction and a steady average wind speed of force 4 to 5
They have a south-easterly direction and mainly a variable wind speed of above force 6.
They have a north-easterly direction and mainly a variable wind speed of above force 6.
They have a north-easterly direction and a steady average wind speed of force 4 to 5
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: They have a south-easterly direction and a steady average wind speed of force 4 to 5

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the "navigable semicircle" of a tropical storm in the Northern hemisphere?
options: The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the starboard side of the cyclone path and its eye
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is 250 Nm aft of the eye of the storm directly behind her path
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is at least 80 Nm aft of the eye of the storm behind on her path
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the first principle for successful passage through the ice?
options: To maintain freedom of manoeuvre.
To maintain radio watch in order to receive all ice reports and information.
To stay out of the ice as much as possible.
To sail through the ice during the day only.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: To maintain freedom of manoeuvre.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the difference between hurricanes and typhoons?
options: A hurricane develops in the Atlantic or East Pacific while Typhoons develop in the West Pacific.
A hurricane is a storm with winds of over 64 knots and a typhoon is between 48 and 56 knots.
A hurricane develops in the western Pacific and a typhoon in the central and eastern Pacific.
A hurricane is a tropical storm and a typhoon is a storm of the mid-latitudes (above 40 degrees).
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: A hurricane develops in the Atlantic or East Pacific while Typhoons develop in the West Pacific.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: Why should the Master regulate the ship's speed in heavy weather?
options: All three answers.
To avoid the possibility of damage to the ship.
To avoid the possibility of damage to the cargo.
To prevent needless expenditure of fuel.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the first basic ship-handling rule in ice concentrations?
options: Keep moving, even if very slowly.
Try to avoid icing of the ship's superstructure.
Try to keep the vessel sailing only after the icebreakers.
Try to keep the vessel sailing only in convoys through the ice.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Keep moving, even if very slowly.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term the "wind is backing"?
options: It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).
It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).
It's a change of direction in the wind from ahead to astern.
It's a change of direction in the wind from  astern to ahead.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: Where can the Master or Officer of the Watch find details regarding ice reporting schemes and the radio stations transmitting them?
options: In the Admiralty List of Radio Signals, Volume 3.
In the Mariner's Handbook.
In the Company SMS manuals.
In the Bridge Procedures Guide.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: In the Admiralty List of Radio Signals, Volume 3.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What precautions should be carried out on deck before encountering heavy weather?
options: All loose objects and equipment should be secured.
All crew should be given heavy weather clothing, including raincoats and boots.
All crew should be instructed not to leave their cabins.
All equipment should be greased.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All loose objects and equipment should be secured.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What warnings and instructions should be given before the vessel encounters heavy weather?
options: All three answers.
Warning and instructions should be issued to the crew on deck access.
Warning and instructions should be issued to the engine room crew.
Instructions to rig safety lines where necessary.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the Master required to do by SOLAS when his ship encounters dangerous ice?
options: He is required to communicate the fact to all ships in the vicinity by all means available
He is required to stop his ship and communicate with the nearest coastal state.
He is required to communicate the fact to his DPA
He is required to exhibit lights and shapes declaring that his vessel is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: He is required to communicate the fact to all ships in the vicinity by all means available

CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term the "wind is veering"?
options: It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).
It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).
It's a change of direction in the wind from  astern to ahead.
It's a change of direction in the wind from ahead to astern.
CD7006 — TOTS 1A-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What would be the required action if a steering gear failure takes place in a busy shipping lane?
options: All the answers are correct.
Switch to emergency steering and reduce speed.
SECURITE call to other ships in the vicinity so they can take evasive action.
Alert the VTS station and check if it's possible to anchor.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the first reporting requirement in the event of a toxic liquid release at anchor?
options: The incident should be reported to the nearest Coastal State in detail without delay.
The ship's staff must first check with the ship's managers before taking action.
If the effect is not visible on the surface of the water there is no need to report the incident.
The agent should be informed immediately and he will take necessary action.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The incident should be reported to the nearest Coastal State in detail without delay.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Which party is to be notified first in the event of a probable spill or actual spill?
options: The Coastal State Authority
The Company
The local agents
The P&I Club
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The Coastal State Authority

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What are the different types of foam extinguishing media that may be found on board?
options: High expansion, medium expansion and/or low expansion foam
High Expansion Foam only.
Medium Expansion Foam only.
Low Expansion Foam only.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: High expansion, medium expansion and/or low expansion foam

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do foam compounds after an initial 3 year period have to be tested annually?
options: All the answers.
Because it is a Flag requirement.
Because the foam compounds are likely to deteriorate over time.
Because deterioration of the foam can reduce its properties.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What should the Officer on Watch do in the event of a 'Man Overboard' ?
options: Raise the alarm and turn the ship towards the side of the man overboard.
Turn the ship away from the side of the man overboard.
Inform The Master and wait for his arrival.
Call the Chief officer.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Raise the alarm and turn the ship towards the side of the man overboard.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do dry powder installations require periodical checking?
options: Solidification of the compound can occur on board over a period of time.
The powder tends to change colour and loose effectiveness.
Dry powder evaporates and disappears over time.
Other extinguishing media are more stable.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Solidification of the compound can occur on board over a period of time.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are proper records required to be maintained for routine tests, checks and maintenance of fire-fighting equipment?
options: For ease of reference and to allow proper and effective planning of testing and maintenance. Also plans and records must be available for inspection when required by the Administration.
Because the company auditors can ask for all records of inspections.
Because the Port State Control is likely to detain the ship if records are unavailable.
Because the quality system requires records to be maintained to provide evidence.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: For ease of reference and to allow proper and effective planning of testing and maintenance. Also plans and records must be available for inspection when required by the Administration.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of galley equipment must be fitted with an automatic or manual fire fighting system?
options: Deep fat cooking equipment.
Electrical equipment.
Galley stove hotplates
Galley ovens
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Deep fat cooking equipment.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are environmental issues discussed during HSE or environmental team meetings?
options: To raise awareness among the crew on issues that affect the environment and promote pollution prevention.
Because there are so many rigid regulations to comply with.
For financial reasons as the commercial viability of ship may be affected.
To discuss tactics in the eventuality of an incident involving environmental activists such as Greenpeace.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To raise awareness among the crew on issues that affect the environment and promote pollution prevention.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the purpose of a Safety Meeting on board?
options: To review safety matters and improve the Safety Management System.
To discuss operational problems and the maintenance programme.
To receive and review crew complaints with regard to crew matters.
To ensure the paperwork, as required by ISM, is completed.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To review safety matters and improve the Safety Management System.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Does the paint locker require a fixed fire fighting installation?
options: Yes, a fixed system is mandatory.
A portable installation is acceptable if within easy reach.
The regulations require a portable extinguisher in the locker.
It is only important to be able to quickly access some type of extinguishing system.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes, a fixed system is mandatory.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fixed fire-fighting installations may be fitted for the machinery spaces?
options: Any of the types mentioned.
Fixed Gas Fire Extinguishing system.
Fixed High Expansion Foam system.
A fixed high pressure water spraying system.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Any of the types mentioned.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fire alarm detectors are used on a ship?
options: They can be smoke detectors, heat detectors, flame sensors or any combination of the three.
A smoke detection system.
Heat detectors.
Flame sensors.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: They can be smoke detectors, heat detectors, flame sensors or any combination of the three.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the requirement for manually operated call points on a fixed fire detection and alarm system?
options: They shall be capable of immediate operation at all times.
No manually operated call points are required since the system is fixed.
Manual operation can only be overridden by the automatic system from the bridge.
In case the automatic system fails then the manual call point is to be used.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: They shall be capable of immediate operation at all times.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fixed fire-fighting installations may be fitted for the cargo pump room?
options: It should be fitted with a system suitable for machinery spaces of category A.
Pump rooms should be fitted with a fixed high expansion foam extinguishing system only.
Pump rooms must be fitted with a gas fire extinguishing system only.
The type of system is based on the type of cargo the ship is carrying.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It should be fitted with a system suitable for machinery spaces of category A.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What size of tanker must be fitted with a fixed deck fire-extinguishing system?
options: Tankers of 20,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.
Tankers of 5,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.
Tankers of 50,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.
All tankers must be fitted with a fixed system.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Tankers of 20,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is it mandatory to have a fire blanket in the galley?
options: Yes, it is mandatory as stated by SOLAS.
It depends how committed the ship manager is to safety.
The Port State Control insists on having one in the galley.
It is up to the chief cook to decide.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes, it is mandatory as stated by SOLAS.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where are the operating instructions for the emergency fire pump located?
options: In a clear, visible place near the emergency fire pump.
Adjacent to the international ship/shore connection for use by the shore fire services.
On the ship's bridge and the Engine Control Room.
On the bulkhead next to the ship's fire plan.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: In a clear, visible place near the emergency fire pump.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are Vessel Management Meetings held?
options: To promote effective team-working, planning, clarity on tasks, execution and monitoring of jobs.
The Management level staff is required by the regulations to hold these meetings.
To comply with the Company Auditors who periodically check to make sure the meetings have been carried out.
To provide an opportunity for the vessel management team to discuss the issues raised at the HSE meetings.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To promote effective team-working, planning, clarity on tasks, execution and monitoring of jobs.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are the Accident, Incident and Near-Miss Reporting system used?
options: To analyse and learn from the errors and to work towards improvement.
To ensure the internal ISM and Auditor's paperwork requirements are met.
To ensure the Company Policies are followed rigidly.
It is a requirement once The Master has signed off from the ship.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To analyse and learn from the errors and to work towards improvement.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where shall the isolating valve on the fire main be fitted?
options: It shall be fitted in an easily accessible and tenable position outside the machinery space.
It shall be fitted anywhere on open deck spaces; the ship's main deck being the most appropriate.
It can be fitted anywhere as long as it serves the purpose of isolating the section of fire main for machinery space.
It shall be fitted in the accommodation as the crew are always available in that area.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It shall be fitted in an easily accessible and tenable position outside the machinery space.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the requirement for galleys that have deep-fat cooking equipment?
options: All the answers are correct.
They shall be fitted with an automatic or manual fire extinguishing system.
There must be an automatic shut off of electrical power when the fire extinguishing system is activated.
There should be clear instructions for crew concerning manual operation of the system.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How many foam applicators must a fixed foam extinguishing system have on deck?
options: A minimum of 4.
A minimum of 2.
At least 4 on each side.
10 in total.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: A minimum of 4.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is high expansion foam suitable to fight a fire on deck?
options: It is unsuitable for use in open areas in outside locations as it is easily dispersed in light winds.
It is suitable since it gives a larger coverage area on deck.
It is better to use water jets to clear the deck of the combustible substance.
It depends on the expansion ratio of the foam.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is unsuitable for use in open areas in outside locations as it is easily dispersed in light winds.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Can cargo be restarted immediately once a leaking or burst pipe has been repaired?
options: No. It's important to ensure that all the hazards from the released oil are eliminated.
Yes, cargo can be restarted since the problem has been rectified.
No, cargo cannot be started until a full incident investigation is completed.
Yes. Working of cargo is based on the commercial pressures on the ship.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: No. It's important to ensure that all the hazards from the released oil are eliminated.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: When should a new crew member undergo on-board safety familiarization?
options: As soon as practicable upon joining the vessel.
No later than two months after joining the ship.
No later than one month after joining the ship.
The training schedule is subject to the time available between operations.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: As soon as practicable upon joining the vessel.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why is Risk Assessment carried out before carrying out operations?
options: To improve safety and minimise or reduce the possibility of incidents and accidents.
To hold senior staff accountable and responsible in the event of an accident happening.
Because The Port State Control Officer checks the Risk Assessment records.
It is a requirement of the ISO 9001:2000 Quality standard.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To improve safety and minimise or reduce the possibility of incidents and accidents.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the first action that must be taken in the case of a hose burst, pipe work fracture or cargo overflow?
options: All operations must be immediately stopped and the alarm sounded.
Quickly repair the leakage and keep operations going to prevent the ship from being delayed.
Stop all operations and wait for the Coast Guard and terminal people to arrive.
Sound the alarm, inform the Master and wait for his instructions.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All operations must be immediately stopped and the alarm sounded.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do tankers require isolation valves to be fitted in the fire main at the poop front and on the tank deck at intervals of no more than 40 metres?
options: To preserve the integrity of the fire main system in case of fire or explosion.
Because additional isolation valves help to provide quick access.
Because deck fire fighting becomes easier when different sections of fire main can be isolated.
Because it makes it easier to renew damaged sections of the fire main while the fire pump is running.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To preserve the integrity of the fire main system in case of fire or explosion.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why is a fire control plan stored in a prominently marked weathertight enclosure outside the deckhouse?
options: It is to assist shore side fire-fighting personnel in an emergency.
It is stored so that crew can access the information during a drill on deck.
It is kept there because the Port State Control Inspector will look for it.
It is kept outside in case of an accommodation fire on board.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is to assist shore side fire-fighting personnel in an emergency.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Who is the person identified in the Vessel Response Plan who acts on behalf of the Owner for oil spill response in USA?
options: A Qualified Individual.
A designated person ashore.
An authrorized person.
The owner's representative.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: A Qualified Individual.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the minimum frequency (for the majority of vessels) for an abandon ship drill and a fire drill for the crew, according to SOLAS Chapter lll?
options: There shall be at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month.
There shall be at least one drill every week while the ship is at sea.
The frequency of the drill is left to the discretion of the Master.
There shall be at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every three months.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: There shall be at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What would be the immediate action taken in the event of a bunker spill?
options: Stop all transfer operations, inform, sound the alarm and initiate Emergency response.
Stop operations, investigate the occurrence and inform based on the quantity of the spill.
Stop operations and work out a solution to cover up in collusion with the barge.
Stop operations, check if anyone has noticed and then take any necessary action.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Stop all transfer operations, inform, sound the alarm and initiate Emergency response.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What details of the main and emergency fire pumps are described on the Fire Control Plan?
options: The capacity of the pumps is clearly indicated.
The identity of the makers and model number is included.
There is no such requirement for details.
Only the location of the fire pumps are marked.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The capacity of the pumps is clearly indicated.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: When would you use the Emergency Response Service of the Class Society?
options: For damage stability and longitudinal strength calculations after a casualty.
It is useful for any emergency situation on board where Class is affected.
They are called in for support if the ship is involved in a pollution incident.
They are contacted if the ship has an accidental release of cargo in USA waters.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: For damage stability and longitudinal strength calculations after a casualty.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Who approves the ship's Fire Control Plan?
options: The Flag Administration or Recognised Organisation.
The Port State Control.
The ship's Technical Managers.
The ship's Protection and Indemnity Club.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The Flag Administration or Recognised Organisation.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why is it important to follow a drill with a debriefing session?
options: To review and discuss the lessons learnt and continually improve.
To advise the crew about their faults and assign blame to individuals.
To motivate crew and make good use of any remaining time left over from the drill.
It is a requirement of the Company Safety Policy.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To review and discuss the lessons learnt and continually improve.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Which of the following elements should generally be included in a fire drill?
options: All of these answers
The starting of a fire pump, using at least two jets of water
Checking the operation of watertight doors, fire doors, fire dampers and main inlets and outlets of ventilation systems in the drill area.
Checking of the fireman's outfits, personal rescue equipment and communications equipment.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All of these answers

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What must be covered in the familiarisation of the fixed fire-fighting system on the cargo deck area?
options: All the answers are correct.
The fire-fighting medium storage area.
The location and operation of the fixed fire extinguishing system.
The remote and local activation points and procedures.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: A few drops of oil spill into the water but no traces are visible anymore. Is it still necessary to report the incident?
options: The incident shall be reported regardless of the size of the incident.
Since no traces of oil are visible there is no need to report it.
Wait and watch to see what the reaction is, then decide accordingly.
It's advisable to ignore the incident to prevent legal issues arising, especially if there are few witnesses.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The incident shall be reported regardless of the size of the incident.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: You have a small bunker spill in port. All notifications are done and the cleanup is completed. What do you do concerning the record collection?
options: Obtain calculations of relative quantities on board, in the pipelines and in the barge.
Leave matters to the local agent and feel relieved that the emergency is over.
Leave the record collection to the company who are not on site.
Forget the records and hope the estimated spilt quantity will be relatively accurate.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Obtain calculations of relative quantities on board, in the pipelines and in the barge.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is uncontrolled venting an allowed practice while loading cargo?
options: No. Venting of tanks should be only through mast risers in a controlled fashion.
Yes. If the wind speed is good there is no problem with uncontrolled venting.
Yes. Uncontrolled venting is unavoidable due to the vapour pressure while loading.
Yes. It is not a problem since so many precautions have already been taken.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: No. Venting of tanks should be only through mast risers in a controlled fashion.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the minimum required service duration of an EEBD?
options: 10 minutes.
12 minutes.
15 minutes.
20 minutes.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What should you do if the ship spills oil into the water in a port and you are contacted by the Media?
options: Be courteous, state facts and suggest the reporter contacts the company, and do not commit yourself on any issues you are not sure about.
Don't be afraid to be direct and explain to them the difficulties of life on board and working with companies.
If they become aggressive, treat aggression with aggression and ask the crew to physically remove them.
Blame the other parties and deny any wrongdoing by you or the ship.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Be courteous, state facts and suggest the reporter contacts the company, and do not commit yourself on any issues you are not sure about.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Can the SMPEP and SOPEP be combined into one manual?
options: Yes. Since the requirements are similar, they can be combined into one plan.
No. They address different regulations so cannot be combined.
No. The SMPEP is a dry cargo ship contingency plan while the SOPEP is for tankers.
No. The SMPEP is for a particular cargo while the SOPEP is a general plan.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes. Since the requirements are similar, they can be combined into one plan.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: In the event of a collision what are the duties to the other vessel?
options: Render assistance without jeopardising the safety of your own personnel and vessel.
Since it is a collision incident , the Master should take details before continuing with the voyage.
Issue a notice of arrest to the other ship on behalf of the Company
If oil has been spilt the Master should take down details and try to avoid becoming involved in a pollution incident.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Render assistance without jeopardising the safety of your own personnel and vessel.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What actions should be initiated by the damage control team after grounding?
options: All the answers are correct.
They should visually inspect the ship and check the draft/trim/list.
They should sound all compartments, sound around the ship and check the nature of the seabed.
They should check the watertight integrity of the compartments in contact.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the mariner's role in collecting evidence during and after an incident?
options: All the answers are correct.
Ensure that log books, rough note books and all other relevant documentation is collected and retained for the vessel's lawyers.
Examine the scene of the incident, taking photographs and using sketches where appropriate.
It is good practice to record facts straight after the incident while it is still fresh.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the order of priority when dealing with contingencies?
options: Safety of life, the environment and then property.
Safety and protection of the environment.
Safety of property and cargo.
Safety of the ship and the environment.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Safety of life, the environment and then property.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: The ship suffers a collision. The bridge waste paper basket contains some small pieces of paper with scribbled notes on. What should the Master do?
options: Collect these pieces of paper and keep them as a record, as they may contain relevant information.
Treat them as waste and ignore them as they have already been thrown away.
It might be an idea to falsify the scribbled notes after the collision so you will not be held responsible.
There is already so much evidence available that it's not necessary to keep these small pieces of paper.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Collect these pieces of paper and keep them as a record, as they may contain relevant information.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What are the IMO guidelines concerning the types or reports that should be sent in the event of a probable spill or actual spill?
options: An initial report, an additional report and a supplementary report should be sent.
An initial report should be sent.
An additional report should be sent.
A supplementary report should be sent.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: An initial report, an additional report and a supplementary report should be sent.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What are SOPEP / VRP / SMPEP / PCSOPEP?
options: Oil Spill Contingency plans based on different regulations.
Different plans as required by different nations of the world.
Manuals segregated by the company for ease of use.
Manuals required by the ISO 9001 standards.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Oil Spill Contingency plans based on different regulations.

CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How is the SMPEP different from a SOPEP?
options: It is the contingency plan for ships carrying Noxious Liquid Substances.
SMPEP deals with Oil Pollution only.
It is the same plan, only called by different names based on the individual company.
Different Flag Administrations use different terminology for the same plan.
CD7007 — TOTS 1A-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is the contingency plan for ships carrying Noxious Liquid Substances.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What cargo information is required to enable accurate quantity calculations?
options: The API (S.G.) and load temperature.
The density.
U.S. barrels per long tonne.
American Petroleum Institute tables.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The API (S.G.) and load temperature.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Which document gives the necessary information for the safe handling of the cargo?
options: The MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet).
The code of safe working practices.
The MARPOL consolidated edition.
SOPEP.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet).

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What restrictions on personnel movement would you make if the vessel was to load a cargo with a high content of H2S?
options: Only those crew members actually involved in the cargo operation would be allowed on deck and each would have to do the appropriate PPE.
No particular restrictions as it is only sour crude.
To ensure that all personnel are wearing dust masks and are walking slowly.
To allow just two crew members on deck at any one time.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: Only those crew members actually involved in the cargo operation would be allowed on deck and each would have to do the appropriate PPE.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: The terminal advises a low flash point. What is a "flash point"?
options: The lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off sufficient gas to form a flammable gas mixture.
The loading temperature of the cargo.
The minimum temperature the cargo can be discharged at.
The auto-ignition temperature.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off sufficient gas to form a flammable gas mixture.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why must you advise of the cargo plan / loading sequence to the terminal prior to arrival?
options: To ensure that the cargo is available and, in particular, that the terminal can supply in the sequence required.
To comply with the charter party.
It is not really necessary to advise it as it will all change anyway.
The Loading Master may not agree.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: To ensure that the cargo is available and, in particular, that the terminal can supply in the sequence required.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: ISGOTT recommends that the transmission power setting of VHF and UHF equipment is set at..
options: One watt or less during cargo operations.
Ten watts or less
The recommendation is only for AIS and not VHF/UHF equipment.
five watts or less
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: One watt or less during cargo operations.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: For a safe and efficient cargo transfer, the ship and terminal must..
options: maintain good communication and cooperation throughout the operation.
keep a good record of events.
check the moorings regularly.
ensure that safe access to the vessel is maintained at all times.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: maintain good communication and cooperation throughout the operation.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: The inert gas fails. What is your initial response?
options: To immediately inform the terminal and cease discharging.
To just reduce the discharge rate. There is no need to inform the terminal.
To keep discharging and say nothing.
To advise the terminal of the circumstances and pass along frequent updates as appropriate.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: To immediately inform the terminal and cease discharging.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: How would the Chief Officer normally express the maximum loading rate to the terminal?
options: In cubic metres per hour (m3/hr) or barrels per hour (brls/hr).
Always in metric tonnes per hour.
Always in long tonnes per hour.
He would ask the Loading Master which units he prefers.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: In cubic metres per hour (m3/hr) or barrels per hour (brls/hr).

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Who completes the Ship/Shore Safety Check List?
options: Responsible personnel from the vessel and the terminal.
The ship's duty Officer
The Loading Master and Chief Engineer.
The ship's agent with the terminal representative.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: Responsible personnel from the vessel and the terminal.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What does the code letter "P" indicate when completing the Ship / Shore Safety Check List? (ISGOTT)
options: That the particular operation must not commence until permission has been granted by the proper authority.
That permission has been granted to continue with the operation.
That permission is not required.
Petroleum.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: That the particular operation must not commence until permission has been granted by the proper authority.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is the "topping off rate"?
options: The rate at which the cargo tank is finally completed to the required ullage.
The rate at which it is safe to ullage cargo tanks.
The rate requested by the Chief Engineer to commence bunkering.
A steady rate to ensure safe loading.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The rate at which the cargo tank is finally completed to the required ullage.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is "topping up"?
options: The introduction of inert gas into a tank that is already in the inert condition.
Topping up the water in the deck seal.
Filling a cargo tank.
Topping off a bunker tank.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The introduction of inert gas into a tank that is already in the inert condition.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Does the Ship / Shore Safety Check List address Crude Oil Washing?
options: Yes, it does.
No, it doesn't.
Only regarding inert gas.
Only regarding cargo tank atmosphere.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: Yes, it does.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why are pre-cargo transfer meetings conducted?
options: In order to discuss all aspects of the proposed cargo transfer and, in particular, any safety issues or particular circumstances which may affect a safe and efficient cargo operation.
In order to complete the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
In order to agree on loading and or discharging rates.
In order to discuss firefighting equipment related to the proposed cargo transfer.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: In order to discuss all aspects of the proposed cargo transfer and, in particular, any safety issues or particular circumstances which may affect a safe and efficient cargo operation.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: At what stage will the agreed communication methods be confirmed?
options: During completion of the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
Prior to arrival at the terminal.
The agent will inform the Master.
At the Master's discretion.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: During completion of the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why is it important to compare cargo figures between ship and shore at regular intervals?
options: To identify any discrepancies.
To ensure the cargo transfer rate is being maintained.
It assists in determining the vessel experience factor.
It is good to check the remote ullaging facility.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: To identify any discrepancies.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: The loading rate is only about 60% of what was agreed at the pre-cargo transfer meeting. What action would the Master take?
options: He would inform the terminal / Loading Master and issue a Note of Protest.
He would protest verbally to terminal and make a note in the logbook.
He would Inform the terminal.
He would recalculate the ETD and inform the owners accordingly.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: He would inform the terminal / Loading Master and issue a Note of Protest.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why is the item "emergency towing off pennants" coded with the letter "R"?
options: Because the emergency towing off pennants need tending as the vessel's freeboard changes to ensure a tug boat can always reach the eye of the pennant.
Because the pennant is liable to part under strain.
Because the deck crew need to be available to rig the pennant if required.
Because only the emergency towing off wire needs tending, the fire wire does not.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: Because the emergency towing off pennants need tending as the vessel's freeboard changes to ensure a tug boat can always reach the eye of the pennant.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is the advantage to all parties if the vessel is advised of reducer size prior to arrival?
options: The vessel can be fully prepared thus saving time and contributing to efficient cargo transfer.
To make sure the vessel complies with ISGOTT regarding reducers.
It is one more thing off the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
It means that a pre-cargo transfer meeting will not have to be conducted.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The vessel can be fully prepared thus saving time and contributing to efficient cargo transfer.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: The hardarm (chickson) operating envelope is only important at low water.
options: False
True
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: False

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Referring to the Ship / Shore Safety Check List, what does the letter "R" indicate?
options: That the item has to be rechecked at agreed intervals.
That there is restricted access.
That the item is to be removed from the check list.
That the item has been reinstated to the check list at the terminal's agreement.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: That the item has to be rechecked at agreed intervals.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Mooring winches must be used on self-tensioning.
options: False
True
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: False

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: When would emergency signals and procedures be discussed?
options: At the pre-cargo transfer meeting / safety meeting.
Prior to arrival when the Chief Officer has a meeting with the Master and the Chief Engineer.
When the Pilot boards.
The emergency signal is already posted on the muster list.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: At the pre-cargo transfer meeting / safety meeting.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Crude Oil Washing (COW) is to be carried out. What will be the terminal's requirements relating to oxygen?
options: The oxygen content in the cargo tank must not exceed 8%.
The oxygen content in the cargo tank must not exceed 11%.
The oxygen content is not important as the tank is over rich.
The oxygen content in the tank will depend upon the COW manual.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: The oxygen content in the cargo tank must not exceed 8%.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why is it important to have the vessel properly manned during cargo transfer?
options: So that there are sufficient personnel available to conduct cargo transfer operations safely and deal with any emergency that may arise.
To try and engage in maintenance operations during cargo transfer.
The ship may have to take on stores.
The vessel may have to bunker.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: So that there are sufficient personnel available to conduct cargo transfer operations safely and deal with any emergency that may arise.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is the "odour threshold"?
options: It is the lowest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.
It is the highest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.
It is the permissible odour when handling cargos with high H2S content.
It is the smell you get from spiked crude.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: It is the lowest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Why will the terminal advise a maximum discharge pressure at the manifold?
options: Because the terminal will know its own safety limits thus ensuring a safe cargo transfer.
Because the discharge pressure will assist in complying with the charter party.
Because the shore tanks may be almost full.
Because the shore tanks are far away.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: Because the terminal will know its own safety limits thus ensuring a safe cargo transfer.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: Portable VHF/UHF equipment must be..
options: intrinsically safe and of an approved type.
capable of transmitting at 25 watts power.
not have an aerial.
always worn in a case.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: intrinsically safe and of an approved type.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is the "Terminal Operating Manual"?
options: It is a working document that includes procedures, practices and drawings relevant to the specific terminal.
A general booklet applicable to most tanker terminals.
An advertising brochure.
It forms part of the Code of Safe Working Practice.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: It is a working document that includes procedures, practices and drawings relevant to the specific terminal.

CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.question: What is a "berthing plan"?
options: It's the plan provided by the terminal giving relevant information relating to the position and lines required to ensure the vessel's safety throughout the cargo transfer.
It's the plan indicating the crew and visitors' accommodation layout and sleeping arrangements.
It's the plan the Navigating Officer makes which forms part of the passage plan.
It's the list of moorings available on board.
CD7008 — TOTS 1A-Ship and Shore Interfac.answer: It's the plan provided by the terminal giving relevant information relating to the position and lines required to ensure the vessel's safety throughout the cargo transfer.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Which ship should complete the Ship / Shore Safety Checklist?
options: Both ships.
The discharging ship.
The receiving ship.
Neither ship.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Both ships.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should the Ship / Shore Safety Checklist be completed?
options: It should be fully completed before starting cargo operations.
It need not be completed as it is only for use with cargo operations at shore terminals.
It should be completed during the planning stage.
It should be fully completed before finishing cargo operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: It should be fully completed before starting cargo operations.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Under what circumstances should helicopter operations be permitted?
options: When there is no cargo or bunker transfer, or ballasting into cargo tanks.
When wind speed is less than ten knots.
In an emergency only.
When permitted by local regulations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: When there is no cargo or bunker transfer, or ballasting into cargo tanks.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What speed should the constant heading ship maintain during the STS berthing procedure?
options: Her minimum steerage way (usually about five knots).
Half ahead.
Sufficient to allow for wind and current.
Approximately one knot.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Her minimum steerage way (usually about five knots).

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Who should initiate changes of heading during the STS berthing procedure?
options: Changes of course may be requested by the manoeuvring ship, and followed by the constant heading ship.
The constant heading ship will make any changes her Master considers necessary. The manoeuvring ship will then conform to these.
No changes of heading should be undertaken once the berthing manoeuvre has started.
Each ship must be manoeuvred as her Master sees fit.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Changes of course may be requested by the manoeuvring ship, and followed by the constant heading ship.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What is the position and function of secondary fenders?
options: Positioned at the bow and stern, they give protection against accidental contact during berthing operations.
Positioned on the constant heading ship, they give protection after the initial contact with the primary fenders.
As the smaller fenders, they are positioned along the ship's side to give additional protection.
Positioned on the side of the constant heading ship away from STS operations, they give protection to tugs and workboats etc.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Positioned at the bow and stern, they give protection against accidental contact during berthing operations.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should Check List 4 be completed?
options: Before commencement of cargo transfer operations.
Before completion of cargo transfer operations.
Before commencement of STS operations.
Before completion of STS operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Before commencement of cargo transfer operations.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should Check List 5 be completed?
options: Before commencement of unmooring operations.
After completion of unmooring operations.
Before commencement of cargo transfer operations.
Before commencement of STS operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Before commencement of unmooring operations.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What is the position and function of the primary fenders?
options: Positioned along the parallel body of the ship, they give maximum mutual protection.
Positioned on the aft of the ship, it is the first fender that the manoeuvring ship makes contact with.
As the largest fender, it is usually positioned to give protection during berthing.
The primary fenders are located at the forward end of the ship, and are used during berthing.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Positioned along the parallel body of the ship, they give maximum mutual protection.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: If two ships are carrying out an STS transfer while underway, what rudder and engine movements should the former manoeuvring ship undertake?
options: None. Her engine should be stopped and rudder amidships.
Her rudder and engine should conform as closely as possible to the constant heading ship.
Her rudder and engine should be used as requested by the constant heading ship.
The Master of the manoeuvring ship must make such rudder and engine movements as he thinks necessary to maintain the agreed heading and speed.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: None. Her engine should be stopped and rudder amidships.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What smoking regulations should be in force during an STS cargo transfer?
options: Those similar to a shore terminal.
It's at the Master's discretion.
Strictly no smoking.
Those of the ship's normal at-sea regulations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Those similar to a shore terminal.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: To what extent can STCW or ILO 180 working hour's requirements be relaxed during STS operations?
options: They cannot be relaxed. STCW or ILO 180 requirements remain in force.
Working hour's requirements can be suspended for up to 48 hours during STS operations.
Working hour's requirements can be suspended for personnel actually involved in STS operations.
STCW working hour's requirements do not apply to STS operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: They cannot be relaxed. STCW or ILO 180 requirements remain in force.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: If two ships are carrying out an STS transfer while underway, who is responsible for keeping a navigational watch?
options: Both ships must maintain a full navigational watch.
The ship which is using her engine must maintain a full navigational watch.
Neither. Both ships must maintain a full deck watch.
Either ship, as agreed by the two Masters.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Both ships must maintain a full navigational watch.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Why is it recommended that the diameter of fenders used in an STS operation should be less than half the freeboard of the smallest ship?
options: In order to prevent the fender from accidentally boarding the ship during rough weather.
In order to ensure that the distance between the two ships is not excessive.
So that the fenders can be more easily handled by rigging crews.
In order to reduce the drag of the fenders on the manoeuvring ship.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: In order to prevent the fender from accidentally boarding the ship during rough weather.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What navigational lights and shapes must be shown by the smaller of the two ships involved in an STS operation?
options: The lights and shapes for a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.
Normal lights for a vessel underway.
The smaller vessel should not show any navigational lights or shapes.
The lights and shapes for a vessel under tow.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The lights and shapes for a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What factors would influence the agreed STS cargo transfer rate?
options: Hose characteristics, design of the receiving ship's pipework and vents, and weather conditions which may cause movement in the hoses.
Total volume of cargo parcel, and time available within the STS window.
The temperature and density of the cargo.
The instructions from the vessel's technical managers or local authorities.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Hose characteristics, design of the receiving ship's pipework and vents, and weather conditions which may cause movement in the hoses.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Who should normally complete and sign Check List 3?
options: The Master or the Chief Officer.
The STS Superintendent.
A Company representative.
The Chief Engineer.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The Master or the Chief Officer.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should Check List 3 be completed?
options: Before commencement of the approach and mooring  operations.
As soon as Check List 2 has been completed, and the other ship has been advised.
At a convenient time before or during the STS operation.
Before commencement of cargo transfer operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Before commencement of the approach and mooring  operations.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What action must be taken if excessive cargo vapours are detected around the manifold of the discharging ship?
options: The STS transfer operation must be suspended until the problem is resolved.
The Master should Note Protest due to the condition of the hose.
Pressure should be reduced on the manifold.
Tests should be undertaken to verify the level of vapour concentration.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The STS transfer operation must be suspended until the problem is resolved.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: The "weather threshold" is the point at which the mooring line loads become unacceptable. What is the effect on the weather threshold if the displacement of the discharging ship is increased?
options: The weather threshold is increased in line with the displacement of the discharging ship.
The weather threshold is reduced due to the extra wind resistance.
Increased displacement has no effect on the weather threshold.
The effect of increased displacement depends on many more parameters, and cannot be accurately predicted.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The weather threshold is increased in line with the displacement of the discharging ship.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What measures can be taken to reduce abrasion damage to the rubber skin of the fender?
options: They should be fitted with rubber sleeves and tyres.
The two ships should be kept slightly apart with rudder and engine movements.
The closing speed should be kept to a minimum during berthing operations.
Only new fenders in good condition should be used for STS operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: They should be fitted with rubber sleeves and tyres.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Who can abort the operation if an emergency arises during an STS berthing procedure?
options: The Master of either ship, or the STS Superintendent.
The Master of the constant heading ship.
Only the STS Superintendent.
The Master of the manoeuvring ship.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The Master of either ship, or the STS Superintendent.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: The Berthing Coefficient is used when selecting the fenders to be used in an STS operation. What is the formula used to obtain the Berthing Coefficient?
options: (2 x displacement ship A x displacement ship B) / (displacement ship A + displacement ship B)
(2 x displacement ship A x displacement ship B) / (velocity ship A - velocity ship B)
(2 x displacement ship A + displacement ship B) / (displacement ship A x displacement ship B)
(2 x velocity ship A x velocity ship B) / (displacement ship A + displacement ship B)
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: (2 x displacement ship A x displacement ship B) / (displacement ship A + displacement ship B)

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Who should advise the Master that Check List 1 has been satisfactorily completed?
options: The operator / charterer of each ship.
The Port State Authority.
The Master of the other ship.
The coastguard.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The operator / charterer of each ship.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What language should be used for communications between two ships?
options: The language will be mutually agreed between the two Masters.
English must be used.
The language of the local Port State should be used.
Masters should use phrases from the International Code of Signals.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The language will be mutually agreed between the two Masters.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: The "weather threshold" is the point at which the mooring line loads become unacceptable. What is the effect on the weather threshold of increasing the number of head and stern lines deployed?
options: Increasing the number of moorings has little or no effect on the weather threshold.
The weather threshold is reduced due to the extra rigidity of the mooring system.
Increasing the number of moorings increases the weather threshold.
The effect of increased head and stern lines depends on many more parameters, and cannot be accurately predicted.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Increasing the number of moorings has little or no effect on the weather threshold.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What action must be taken if a significant leak occurs at the manifold of the receiving ship?
options: The STS transfer operation must be suspended until the cause of the leak is eliminated.
The Master of the discharging ship should Note Protest due to the condition of the hose.
The discharging ship should be requested to reduce the pumping rate.
The Master of the receiving ship should Note Protest due to the condition of the hose.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The STS transfer operation must be suspended until the cause of the leak is eliminated.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Which STS check lists must be completed by each ship before commencement of cargo transfer operations?
options: Check Lists 2, 3 and 4.
All Check Lists 1 to 5.
Check Lists 1 and 2.
Check Lists 1 to 5, as required by the circumstances.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Check Lists 2, 3 and 4.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should a Navigational Warning be broadcast concerning an STS operation?
options: Before commencement of operations, and then regularly according to local requirements.
If an emergency occurs and immediate assistance is required.
After completion of STS operations.
At least 24 hours before the commencement of transfer operations.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Before commencement of operations, and then regularly according to local requirements.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Which two parties would normally exchange Check List 1?
options: The operator / charterer of each ship and the STS organiser.
The Master of each ship and his own operator / charterer.
The Masters of the two ships.
The Master of each ship and the organiser.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The operator / charterer of each ship and the STS organiser.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When mooring wires are used for STS operations, rope tails should be employed. What characteristics should the tails have?
options: At least 11 metres long, and at least 125% of the wire's breaking strength.
Less than 11 metres long, and the same breaking strength as the wire.
They must float, and be of suitable size for the ship's mooring equipment.
The breaking strength must be at least 11% higher than the wire.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: At least 11 metres long, and at least 125% of the wire's breaking strength.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: Which STS check lists must be completed by each ship after completion of cargo transfer operations, and before unmooring?
options: Check List 5.
All Check Lists 3 to 5.
No check lists required after completion of cargo transfer.
Check Lists 3 to 5, depending on the circumstances.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Check List 5.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What information is required to be broadcast in an STS Navigational Warning?
options: The name and flag of the ships involved, location of operations, heading of ships, type of operations, starting time and expected duration and the request for wide berth.
The name and call sign, the nature of the emergency, the position of the ship, and the assistance required.
The name and call sign, and the position and nature of the navigational hazard.
The name, flag and call sign of the ships involved, the type of cargo being transferred, and the request for wide berth.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The name and flag of the ships involved, location of operations, heading of ships, type of operations, starting time and expected duration and the request for wide berth.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What action must be taken if STS hoses are found to have been critically damaged while taking them aboard?
options: They should be withdrawn from use for further inspection or repair.
The pumping rate should be reduced until the hoses are proved not to be leaking.
The pumping rate should be reduced throughout the transfer.
The Master should Note Protest in case a leak develops from the hose.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: They should be withdrawn from use for further inspection or repair.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should Check List 1 normally be completed?
options: When the STS operation is being planned.
24 hours before starting the STS operation.
Seven days before the STS operation.
At a convenient time before or during the STS operation.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: When the STS operation is being planned.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: When should Check List 2 be completed?
options: Before commencement of the STS operation.
24 hours before starting the STS operation.
As soon as the STS operation starts.
At a convenient time before or during the STS operation.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Before commencement of the STS operation.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What is the recommended length for the flexible hose string normally used in an STS transfer operation?
options: Twice the maximum difference in manifold heights.
Approximately 50 metres.
The total of the distances between the two ships' rails and their manifolds, plus 30%.
Twice the horizontal difference in the manifold positions.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: Twice the maximum difference in manifold heights.

CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.question: What is the effect on mooring loads of variations in the wave period, or period of encounter?
options: The load on the moorings increases as the wave period becomes longer.
The mooring load increases as the wave period becomes shorter.
The length of the wave period does not affect the load on the moorings.
CD7009 — TOTS 1A-Ship to Ship Transfer.answer: The load on the moorings increases as the wave period becomes longer.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why, if possible, should two emergency operating areas, one on each side of the ship, be selected?
options: To allow for wind direction if the ship is unable to manoeuvre.
One may have obstructions greater than 3 metres in height.
It's safer for the deck party.
To allow a greater chance of success.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To allow for wind direction if the ship is unable to manoeuvre.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: What is the maximum recommended winching height?
options: 6m
Twice the height of the nearest obstruction.
It's at the Pilot's discretion.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why should an alternative winching area be located near the side of the ship?
options: So that most of the manoeuvring zone extends over the ship's side.
To minimise the effect of air turbulence.
So that if the helicopter crashes, it will fall into the sea.
To make the foam hydrants more accessible.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: So that most of the manoeuvring zone extends over the ship's side.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should you consider using a lifeboat as an emergency operating area?
options: When it is not safe to use any part of the ship due to permanent obstructions.
When the wind is less than force 4.
Due to circumstances when fire- fighting equipment is not available.
At the helicopter pilot's request.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: When it is not safe to use any part of the ship due to permanent obstructions.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why must the hook handler be equipped with rubber gloves and rubber-soled shoes?
options: To avoid shocks from static charge.
To protect him from the helicopter down-draught.
So that the helicopter pilot can identify the hook handler.
To protect the hook handler against the wind and sea.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To avoid shocks from static charge.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why do some vessels have only a winching area?
options: Because they are unable to comply with safe landing area requirements.
Because of SOLAS regulations.
Because they are unable to illuminate a large landing area.
Because the ship does not have sufficient fire fighting equipment onboard to land a helicopter on deck.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Because they are unable to comply with safe landing area requirements.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: In landing and winching area diagrams, what does the letter "D" stand for?
options: The overall length of the helicopter with the rotors turning.
Danger zone.
Designated helicopter area.
Positioning of deck party personnel.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: The overall length of the helicopter with the rotors turning.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should the excessive cargo tank (IG) pressure be released?
options: Not more than 30 minutes before helicopter operations commence.
When the ambient temperature is above 20C.
It does not matter.
Only when the helicopter is landing.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Not more than 30 minutes before helicopter operations commence.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should the fire pumps be started?
options: Before commencing helicopter operations.
When the helicopter has just landed, or when winching operations have commenced.
Only if the helicopter Pilot requests it
If fire breaks out.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Before commencing helicopter operations.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: If a fire breaks out during helicopter operations, the Master/Officer of the Watch will immediately..
options: sound the appropriate fire alarm.
inform the owners/managers.
make an announcement on the loud speaker
request information from the Officer in Charge of the deck party
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: sound the appropriate fire alarm.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Where on the helicopter is the most likely cause of ignition after an accident?
options: In the engine area.
In the fuel tanks.
Around the cabin structure.
In the winch motor.
