CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: In the engine area.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should the aerials be lowered or secured?
options: Before landing or winching operations commence.
It does not matter.
Never, it is required for communication.
At the helicopter pilot's request.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Before landing or winching operations commence.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should the ship's rescue boat be ready for immediate lowering?
options: Prior to landing or winching operations.
Only if the weather is good enough.
Only when the helicopter is winching.
Only when the helicopter is landing.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Prior to landing or winching operations.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: What is the most likely use of the axe and wire cutters after a helicopter accident?
options: To cut into the cabin structure and rescue the air crew and passengers.
To cut the winch cable.
To cut the fuel lines, thus stopping the engines.
To cut the wreckage free of the ship's aerials and awnings.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To cut into the cabin structure and rescue the air crew and passengers.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When using the poop deck as a winching area, the winch cable must be hooked onto the ship's rail.
options: False
True
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: False

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why are landing or winching areas not placed near the bow?
options: Because of the increased air flow turbulence.
Because they are too far from the accommodation.
Because fire-fighting equipment is not readily available.
Because the rescue boat is located aft.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Because of the increased air flow turbulence.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: How is normal communication conducted between ship and helicopter?
options: By VHF.
By signal lamp.
With flares.
With flags.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: By VHF.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Where can you view a suggested action plan for a helicopter accident?
options: In Appendix D of the "Guide to Helicopter/Ship Operations".
In the muster list on the bridge.
In the SOLAS training manual.
In the International Safety Management Code (ISM code).
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: In Appendix D of the "Guide to Helicopter/Ship Operations".

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: After a helicopter accident, what actions would the crew members who were not involved in helicopter operations take?
options: They would go to their emergency stations.
They would report to the Officer in Charge on deck.
They maintain their current positions onboard the ship.
They would assist with any casualties.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: They would go to their emergency stations.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why should rope messengers be available during landing operations?
options: In case the helicopter needs to be secured.
To assist with passing stores between the helicopter and the deck party.
To rope off the landing area.
To latch down any loose equipment affected by the helicopter's down- draught.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: In case the helicopter needs to be secured.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: After a helicopter accident, why would the Master alter course?
options: To keep the fire and smoke clear of the deck.
Due to the swell.
To bring the ship's head to the wind.
To stem the tide.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To keep the fire and smoke clear of the deck.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Once a helicopter fire has been extinguished, what actions should be taken by the Officer in Charge and the Chief Engineer?
options: To investigate the damage and check the reignition risk.
To stand by for instructions from the bridge.
To muster all personnel and check for any injuries.
To inform the owners/managers that the fire has been extinguished.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To investigate the damage and check the reignition risk.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: What is the purpose of the Guide to Helicopter/Ship Operations?
options: To encourage safe and efficient helicopter operations.
For helicopter recognition.
Because it's part of SOLAS.
To assist with fire-fighting training.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To encourage safe and efficient helicopter operations.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: A single-engine helicopter is not suitable for..
options: hovering operations.
landing on deck.
carrying personnel.
night flying.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: hovering operations.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: According to recommendations what should you bear in mind concerning muster lists and helicopter drills?
options: You should follow Appendix D of the "Guide to Helicopter/Ship Operations" and its suggested action plan.
You should consider the number of crew on board.
You should consider the type of ship.
You should bear in mind the capacity of the foam tank.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: You should follow Appendix D of the "Guide to Helicopter/Ship Operations" and its suggested action plan.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: After a helicopter crash, what is a water spray used for?
options: To cover for helicopter crew, passengers and rescue party.
To cool the surrounding area.
To control the fire caused by igniting fuel.
To ensure the crash area is clear of debris.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: To cover for helicopter crew, passengers and rescue party.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why would the poop deck be used as a winching area?
options: Because there is no other suitable area available on board.
Because of its proximity to the accommodation for easy access.
Because mooring winches are available.
Because it's the safest area on the ship.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Because there is no other suitable area available on board.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: In which direction should the fire and foam nozzles be pointing?
options: Away from the helicopter operating area.
Directly at the operating area.
Towards the accommodation.
It does not matter.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Away from the helicopter operating area.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why are helicopter operations only carried out on chemical/parcel tankers in exceptional circumstances?
options: Because their special construction relating to vertical pipes, ventilator pipes and deck tanks means no suitable area is available.
Because the nature of the cargo does not allow helicopter operations.
Because helicopter pilots require a special endorsement to operate on this type of vessel.
Because hull insurance is invalid if helicopter operations are conducted
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Because their special construction relating to vertical pipes, ventilator pipes and deck tanks means no suitable area is available.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Why may the control of a helicopter be difficult when using the poop deck as a winching area?
options: Because of the turbulent airflow above the accommodation and the funnel.
Because of blind sectors.
Because of excessive down- draught.
Because of the ship rolling.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Because of the turbulent airflow above the accommodation and the funnel.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: Communication with the bridge is by..
options: walkie-talkie.
torch.
flares.
hand signals.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: walkie-talkie.

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: The Captain decides if the helicopter is to be secured.
options: True
False
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: True

CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.question: When should the ship's side rails be lowered?
options: Prior to landing operations.
At the helicopter pilot's request.
If the helicopter's landing gear consists of skids, not wheels.
Only during the hours of daylight.
CD7010 — TOTS 1A-Helicopter Operations.answer: Prior to landing operations.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Prior to exchanging ballast the master must..
options: perform a risk assessment.
inform the Port Administration.
perform a course change.
inform the vessel superintendent.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: It is illegal to discharge bilge effluent overboard when the oil content is..
options: 150ppm.
15ppm.
1.5ppm.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: After having performed a ballast operation the master must..
options: complete the ballast water management log.
inform the Port Administration.
perform a course change.
inform the vessel superintendent.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: complete the ballast water management log.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Discharge of sewage is prohibited when..
options: the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 3 knots.
the ship is 24 nautical miles from land and has a functioning certified sewage treatment plant.
the sewage is comminuted and disinfected and the vessel is 5 nautical miles from the nearest land.
the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 7 knots.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 3 knots.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: When is it good practice to check the pressure-vacuum valves?
options: Prior to cargo transfer.
During cargo transfer operations.
After cargo transfer operations.
Before the next dry-docking.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: When first using a cleansing agent in the machinery space, the crew should..
options: confirm that it won't form an emulsion.
confirm that it will form an emulsion.
use it liberally.
use it sparingly.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: confirm that it won't form an emulsion.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: What can happen if an emulsion is taken up by the OWS?
options: It can lead to a false reading on the oil content monitor.
It can completely block the system piping.
It can cause damage to the pump bearings.
nothing.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: It can lead to a false reading on the oil content monitor.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Uncontrolled release of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are an environmental problem because..
options: they contribute to low-level ozone pollution in populated areas.
they react with hydrogen creating acid rain.
they contaminate the sea.
they react with CO2.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: they contribute to low-level ozone pollution in populated areas.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: A ship demonstrates compliance with MARPOL Annex IV by..
options: having a valid International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate.
having a surveyor inspect the sewage system every six years.
having a stand-by sewage treatment plant.
having a sewage holding tank volume of 100 litres per person on board.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: having a valid International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following is NOT an option to comply with MARPOL Annex IV?
options: An approved comminuting plant.
A certified sewage treatment plant.
An approved comminuting and disinfection plant.
Holding tanks with an approved volume.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: To reduce cargo tank vapour release which of the following should be checked?
options: That the tightness of cargo tank hatch dogs are checked after every cargo operation.
That the hatch gasket is checked every year.
That header valves are unseated.
That the cargo pump deepwell bleed valve is open.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: That the tightness of cargo tank hatch dogs are checked after every cargo operation.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following would increase the fuel consumption on board the ship?
options: Leaving steam system leaks unattended.
Reducing speed in heavy weather.
Turning off lights in empty compartments.
Maintaining steam traps.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: How long must the receipts be held with the Garbage Record Book for?
options: Two years.
Six months.
Five years.
One year.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: When is the Master to sign the Garbage Record Book?
options: After each completed page.
After each discharge operation.
At the end of the day.
After the incinerator has been used.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following would reduce energy consumption?
options: Maintaining an unfouled hull.
Running at normal sea speed
Cooling accommodation spaces to 19°C.
Heating accommodation spaces to 25°C.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following substances is ozone-depleting?
options: Halons.
CO2.
Ammonia.
Neon.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: False entries in the Oil Record Book can lead to criminal penalties for the master and chief engineer?
options: True.
False.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: The oil record book shall be completed on each occasion that the cargo tanks are cleansed.
options: True.
False.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: The oil record book shall be completed on each occasion that ballast is discharged from segregated ballast tanks.
options: False.
True.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Operational malpractice of the oil filtering equipment can lead to criminal penalties for the vessel master and chief engineer?
options: True.
False.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: An environmental policy in line with ISO14001 is a commitment from..
options: company top management.
class society.
flag administration.
the IMO.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: What should the Master refer to In the event of an accidental discharge of oil?
options: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan.
The ship environmental management system.
The cargo tank plan.
The ballast water management plan.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following disposals would be permitted?
options: Food waste from a vessel outside a special area and 12 miles from the nearest land.
Food waste from a vessel outside a special area and 10 miles from the nearest land.
Paper products from a vessel inside a special area and 15 miles from the nearest land.
Food waste from a vessel inside a special area and 10 miles from the nearest land.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: Food waste from a vessel outside a special area and 12 miles from the nearest land.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following is NOT a method for detecting leaks of refrigerant gases?
options: Torch.
Soapy water bubble test.
Halide torch.
Gas detector.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan shall contain details of a list of authorities to be contacted in the event of an incident.
options: True.
False.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: In the event of an oil pollution incident MARPOL Annex I requires that an oil tanker of 5,000 tonnes deadweight shall have prompt access to..
options: computerised shore-based damage stability and residual structural strength programs.
the nearest port.
an empty oil tanker of equal deadweight.
computerised models of the ship's cargo tank system.
CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.answer: computerised shore-based damage stability and residual structural strength programs.

CD7011 — TOTS 1A-Pollution Prevention an.question: Where on board might ozone depleting substances be found?
options: In refrigeration systems.
In compressed air systems.
In sewage treatment plants.
In electronic equipment.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the correct method of closing off unused cargo and bunker connections?
options: All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and are to be fully bolted.
All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and have every second bolt secured by a nut.
Unused connections may be left unblanked so long as two valve separation exists between the connection and the line in use.
Unused connections on the shore-side of the vessel must be closed and fully blanked. The offshore-side may be left unblanked.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and are to be fully bolted.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What would be the minimum recommended firefighting equipment to have available when alongside a terminal?
options: Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles run out forward, aft and adjacent to the manifold in use. Also a dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold.
One fire hose and one dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles or fire extinguishers adjacent to the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles forward and aft of the manifold and a fire blanket adjacent to the manifold in use.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles run out forward, aft and adjacent to the manifold in use. Also a dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What should personnel on board barges or other craft obey when moored alongside?
options: All of these answers.
Smoking restrictions.
Prohibition of naked lights.
Restrictions on the use of cooking appliances.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What should happen to deck scuppers during periods of heavy rain when engaged in cargo or bunker handling?
options: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of a deck oil spill.
Open all deck scuppers to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
All deck scuppers must be kept fully closed at all times and never opened until cargo and bunker operations are completed.
Only deck scuppers on the outboard side of the vessel are to be opened to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of a deck oil spill.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: The International Shore Fire Connection is used for what purpose?
options: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.
To enable the foam line onboard to be connected to an external foam supply from shore.
To enable carbon dioxide to be used from shore to fight engine room fires.
To enable the ship to assist in extinguishing a fire ashore.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: A Risk Assessment can be a useful tool when preparing a Permit-to-Work on electrical circuits.
options: True
False

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following questions would NOT be part of a Permit-to-Work check list for allowing small craft to come alongside?
options: Has the ship been inerted or gas freed?
Is adequate illumination available?
Has the Master of the small craft been advised of all appropriate safety regulations (e.g. emergency signals, smoking regulations etc)?
Are all deck and cargo openings closed?
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Has the ship been inerted or gas freed?

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: On a Permit-to-Work for pipeline/pressure vessels, which of the following questions would NOT likely be included as part of the checks?
options: Is the lifeboat/rescue boat ready for use?
Has the pressure been bled off the section to be worked on?
Has the part of the system to be worked upon been isolated?
Have all personnel been equipped with the correct personal protective equipment?
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Is the lifeboat/rescue boat ready for use?

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Where hot work is planned to be carried out, what should the Lower Flammable Limit (LFL) reading of the atmosphere be?
options: Less than 1% LFL.
Greater than 1% LFL.
1% LFL.
Between 1% and 2% LFL.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What should the ship's Master do if an unauthorised craft comes alongside and attempts to secure to the vessel when at a terminal?
options: Report the craft to the terminal and if necessary stop cargo operations.
Sound the emergency alarm.
Turn fire hoses onto the small craft.
All of these answers.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Report the craft to the terminal and if necessary stop cargo operations.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Before cargo or ballast operations commence, the Master (or his representative) and the terminal representative should do what?
options: All three of the above
Agree in writing on the transfer procedures, including the maximum loading or unloading rates
Agree in writing on the action to be taken in the event of an emergency during cargo or ballast handling operations
Complete and sign the Ship/Shore Safety Checklist.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the recommended minimum breaking load (MBL) and length for emergency towing-off pennants (fire wires) for a ship of between 100,000 and 300,000 dwt?
options: MBL = 100 tonnes, L = 60 metres.
MBL = 55 tonnes, L = 45 metres.
MBL = 55 tonnes, L = 60 metres.
MBL = 100 tonnes, L = 45 metres

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Loading cargo "over the top" delivers charged liquid to a tank. What danger can result from this operation?
options: The production of a charged mist and an increase in petroleum gas concentration in the tank.
The production of a gas mist.
The production of an increase in petroleum gas concentration in the tank.
The production of excess tank pressure.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: The production of a charged mist and an increase in petroleum gas concentration in the tank.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: During tanker operations what happens if the material has a low relaxation time?
options: Little or no static electricity accumulates.
Sediments quickly settle at the bottom.
Decanting takes longer.
Stratification into various densities occurs much faster.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Little or no static electricity accumulates.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: During tanker operations, what is the relaxation time of the material mainly related to?
options: Conductivity.
Viscosity.
The pour point.
The flashpoint.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following examples must NOT be electrically bonded?
options: The ship/shore insulating flange.
Manual ullaging and sampling equipment.
Portable tank cleaning machines.
All of these answers.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the name of an oil that is able to retain a significant electrostatic charge and has a conductivity of less than 50 pS/m?
options: Static accumulator oil.
Static non-accumulator oil.
Static insulating oil.
Electrostatic charged oil.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: If petroleum is considered to be volatile, what will the flashpoint temperature be?
options: Below 60 degrees Celsius.
Above 50 degrees Celsius.
38 degrees Celsius and below.
Above 40 degrees Celsius.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the process where a type of gas has been introduced into the tank atmosphere and the oxygen content is reduced, thus making it incapable of burning?
options: Inerted.
Too lean.
Non-inert.
Gas free.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the percentage of oxygen content reduced to in a tank if an inert condition has been achieved during tanker operations?
What is the name of a sudden increase in the pressure of the liquid in a pipeline, caused by a sudden change in flow velocity?
options: A pressure surge.
Back pressure.
Flashback.
Backflow.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What do the terms "threshold limit value" and "permissible exposure limit" refer to?
options: Toxicity.
Suppression value.
Contact limit.
Immersion limit.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the flashpoint temperature of petroleum that is considered to be non-volatile?
options: 60 degrees Celsius or above.
Below 60 degrees Celsius.
38 degrees Celsius and below.
Above 50 degrees Celsius.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What washing mediums must never be used?
options: Recirculated water.
Heated water.
Chemicals.
Heated water plus chemical additive.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: In what range does the TLV/TWA for H2S lie (Threshold Limit Value for the Time Weighted Average 8 hour day)?
options: More than 50PPM.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the word that describes petroleum when it's inhaled or ingested and causes adverse physiological symptoms?
options: Toxic.
Irritant.
Corrosive.
Convulsive.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the name of an atmosphere made incapable of burning by deliberate reduction of the hydrocarbon content to below Lower Flammable Limit?
options: Too lean.
Inerted.
Non-inert.
Gas free.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: The MSDS for a cargo usually contains H2S content in PPM by weight. The H2S content in the vapour space is going to be..
options: greater.
the same.
less.
possibly all of these answers.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What equipment is used for testing gas levels in a non-inert atmosphere?
options: An Explosiemeter.
A tankscope.
A gascope.
An oxygen analyser.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What word describes the unrestricted fall of liquid into a tank during tanker operations?
options: Free fall.
Load on top.
Overflow.
Impingement.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the name for the lowest temperature where a liquid gives off sufficient gas to form a flammable gas mixture near the surface?
options: The flashpoint.
Flammability temperature.
Thermal mass.
Gas emission level.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: At what levels should the tank atmosphere gas level be measured prior to and during tank washing?
options: At various levels.
At the top level.
At the bottom level.
At the middle level.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: H2S is normally associated with crude oils, particularly after loading. What other products can contain H2S?
options: All of these answers.

Bitumen.
Gas oil.

options: Over rich.
Flammable.
Explosive.
Non-inert.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Why is there a limit to the maximum throughput of tank washing machines when washing in a non-inert atmosphere?
options: To reduce the risk of introducing electrostatically charged mist.
To prevent water build up in cargo tanks with resulting free surface.
To reduce the risk of inflammable gas evolution.
It's a MARPOL regulation.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: To reduce the risk of introducing electrostatically charged mist.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When venting is being carried out during the loading of a cargo containing H2S, when should cargo operations be stopped?
options: When there is no wind to disperse the cargo vapours.

When the wind is variable in direction.
When there is a combination of wind and rain.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: When there is no wind to disperse the cargo vapours.

Only when 20.7 % oxygen is achieved.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the flammable range of a hydrocarbon gas and air mixture?

From 0% hydrocarbon to the Lower Flammable Limit.
From the Lower Flammable Limit to 100% hydrocarbon content.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Between the Lower and Upper Flammable Limits.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Where the concentration of H2S in cargo is high, what term is often used to describe the oil?
options: Sour.

Salty.
Acidic.

The maximum 35% LFL at the bottom level.
The maximum 35% LFL at the top level.
More than 10%LFL at any level.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: The maximum 35% LFL at any level.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: The tank bottom and lines should be flushed with water prior to tank cleaning in a non-inert atmosphere. How should this be done?
options: Using main cargo lines.
Using tank washing machines.

Using a hose by a team inside the tank.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Liquids are considered to be non-conductors when they have conductivities less than 50 pS/m. Such liquids are often referred to as static accumulators. Which of the following liquids is NOT a static accumulator?

Kerosene.

Xylene.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the name of the process where petroleum liquid is ignited through heating rather than using a naked flame?

Thermal combustion.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: By what means are ships naturally "earthed"?
options: Via the sea.
Via the mooring lines.
Via the loading arms.
Via the main switchboard.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What gas level is to be obtained in a tank before tank washing can be started?

Less than 100% LFL (Lower Flammable Limit).
Less than 25% by volume.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the correct definition of a "spark"?
options: It is an almost instantaneous discharge between two conductors where almost all of the energy is converted into heat.
It is a diffuse discharge from a single sharp conductor that slowly releases some of the available energy.
It is a diffuse discharge from a highly charged non-conductive object to a single blunt conductor.
It is a rapid high energy discharge from a sheet of material of high dielectric strength with the two surfaces highly charged but of opposite polarity.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: It is an almost instantaneous discharge between two conductors where almost all of the energy is converted into heat.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When should tank washing in an inert atmosphere be stopped?

When the tank atmosphere pressure falls below 250mmWC.
When the tank atmosphere pressure exceeds 250mmWC.
When the tank atmosphere pressure falls below 1000mmWC.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: When the tank atmosphere pressure is no longer positive.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What is the name of the practice during tanker cargo operations where all cargo tank apertures, such as ullage pipes and sighting ports, are securely closed?

Hermetically sealed operation.
Non-intrusive procedure.
Sealed load and discharge.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following is NOT considered to be an enclosed space?
options: The engine room.
A domestic fresh water tank.
The pumproom.
A duct keel.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What percentage of oxygen should be inside the tank when tank washing in an inert atmosphere?

The oxygen level should not fall below 8%.
The oxygen level should not exceed 5%.
The oxygen level should not fall below 5%.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: The oxygen level should not exceed 8%.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When H2S is known to be present, self-contained breathing apparatus must be used in which of the following activities?

Open gauging and sampling.
Removing blanks for connecting the cargo loading arm.
Mopping up spills.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When can controlled hot work be carried out within a hazardous area on a tanker?
options: When the ship is in ballast condition.
When the ship is carrying out gas freeing operations.
When the ship is carrying out inerting operations.
When the ship is carrying out cargo operations.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: What happens to a Permit-to-Work upon completion of work?

It is transferred to another location where similar work is to be carried out.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: A single work permit is issued..

for a variety of tasks.
to keep paperwork up-to-date.

Amend the work permit conditions.

20 minutes after completion of loading.
One hour after completion of loading.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: No hot work should be carried out in the vicinity of bunker tanks unless which of the following is carried out?
options: The tank has been cleaned to hot work standard.
The tank contains fuel with a flashpoint below 60 degrees Celsius.
The tank contains fuel with a flashpoint above 60 degrees Celsius.
The tank is greater than 90% full.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: The tank has been cleaned to hot work standard.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Where should the ship's emergency fire control plans be located?
options: In a prominently marked weather-tight enclosure outside the accommodation block.
With the Deck Officer of the Watch at all times.
In a prominently marked wallet contained within the cargo control room.
At the bottom of the gangway.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: In a prominently marked weather-tight enclosure outside the accommodation block.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When are items on the ship/shore safety check list checked when a vessel is at a terminal?
options: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.
Immediately upon berthing and before starting cargo operations.
Upon commencing cargo operations.
During cargo operations.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following could be considered a "designated space" where hot work is able to be carried out safely?
options: The engine room workshop.
The poop deck.
The engine room.
The forecastle deck.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Bonding links on portable equipment must not be disconnected until..
options: after the equipment is no longer in use.
after cargo operations are started.
after testing for gas levels.
after requesting permission from shore.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: after the equipment is no longer in use.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: When carrying out hot work with electric welding equipment, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The ship's structure should not be used as an earthing point.
The cable route to the working area should be the shortest and most direct route.
The Direct Current output source should be in excess of 70 Volts.
The person carrying out the welding operation can work alone so long as a work permit has been issued.
CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.answer: The ship's structure should not be used as an earthing point.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: The Code of Safe Working Practices requires that any faults relating to cargo handling equipment, testing instruments and alarm systems must be..
options: reported immediately.
repaired immediately.
repaired in dry dock.
reported when cargo operations are completed.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: Where does the Code of Safe Working Practices recommend guidance on general precautions be taken from?
options: All of these answers.
The International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals.
Safety in Oil Tankers.
The Company's Safety Management System.

CD7012 — TOTS 1A-General Tanker Section.question: A Permit-to-Work on electrical circuits is important in order to prevent what?
options: Electrical shock.
The use of non-intrinsically safe equipment on deck.
Non-scheduled planned maintenance tasks being carried out.
All of these answers.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Inert gas quality in slop tanks may be degraded when tank washings from non-inerted tanks are added: Why?
options: Air would be trapped in the washings, particularly if an eductor was in use.
The turbulence in the slops caused by adding washings would result in increased evolution of hydrocarbon vapours.
The higher temperature of the slops caused by adding washings would result in increased evolution of hydrocarbon vapours.
Adding washings would increase the pressure in the tank, forcing inert gas out via the vent line.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air would be trapped in the washings, particularly if an eductor was in use.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: In practical terms, what figures can be used for the Lower and Upper Flammability Limits of oil tanker cargoes?
options: 1% and 10% of gas.
5% and 50% of gas.
5% and 21% of oxygen.
19% and 21% of oxygen.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1% and 10% of gas.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of butane?
options: 1.9% by volume in air.
5.9% by volume in air.
9% by volume in air.
19% by volume in air.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.9% by volume in air.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: If cargo tank openings are opened frequently for operations such as sampling and dipping, inert gas quality may be affected. How so?
options: Air could enter the tanks through the openings.
Inert gas would escape, lowering the tank pressure.
Moisture from the atmosphere could enter the tank.
The hydrocarbon content of the tank atmosphere would be increased.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air could enter the tanks through the openings.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by natural gasoline's can be represented by those of pentane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of pentane?
options: 1.5% by volume in air.
4.5% by volume in air.
7.8% by volume in air.
21% by volume in air.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.5% by volume in air.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, would you consider it to be safe to purge with inert gas with an oxygen content of 8%?
options: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
No, the tank must first be gas freed with fresh air.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by natural gasoline's can be represented by those of pentane. What is the relative density of pentane?
Define the "Upper Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of propane?
options: 2.2% by volume in air.
5.2% by volume in air.
10% by volume in air.
22% by volume in air.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 2.2% by volume in air.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the relative density of butane?

After inerting a cargo tank, the oxygen content was found to be 7.5%, and the hydrocarbon gas content 2%. Using the Flammability Diagram, would you consider the tank to be safely inerted before gas freeing?
options: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
No, inerting must be continued.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is meant by the "Displacement" method of inerting cargo tanks?
options: The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the bottom of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is mixed with fresh air, and introduced rapidly into the tank.
The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Displacement" method of inerting cargo tanks, inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank. Why?
options: Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the inert gas is hotter than the tank atmosphere, and it is necessary to avoid violent mixing.
Because inert gas is denser than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the incoming inert gas will mix with the tank atmosphere throughout the tank.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the relative density of propane?
Explain why the atmosphere in a cargo tank must be sampled at different depths?
options: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Dilution" method of inerting a cargo tank, inert gas is introduced rapidly into the tank. Why?
options: Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the inert gas is hotter than the tank atmosphere, and it is necessary to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and form a stable interface.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What oxygen content would normally be expected from an independent inert gas generator?
options: 1.5-2.5% by volume.
5% by volume.
8-10% by volume.
Approximately 12% by volume.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.5-2.5% by volume.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Define the "Lower Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much gas to support and propagate combustion.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, why would it be necessary to dilute the atmosphere to point H with inert gas before gas freeing with fresh air?
options: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.
To help prevent corrosion in the tank.
To reduce the oxygen level to below the critical dilution line.
To increase the hydrocarbon level above the Upper Flammable Limit.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What are the main components of inert gas delivered from a flue gas plant?
options: Nitrogen 83%, Carbon Dioxide 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%
Nitrogen 60%, Carbon Dioxide 30%, Oxygen 10%
Carbon Dioxide 83%, Nitrogen 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%
Carbon Dioxide 63%, Nitrogen 22-24%, Oxygen 10-12%
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Nitrogen 83%, Carbon Dioxide 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Dilution" method of inerting, it is essential that only a small number of cargo tanks are open. Why?
options: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because the inert gas plant works more efficiently when the back pressure is higher.
Because it is difficult to monitor the hydrocarbon levels properly if a large number of tanks are open.
Because the incoming inert gas must form a stable interface with the tank atmosphere.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the relative density of hydrocarbon gas at concentrations near the Lower Flammable Limit?
options: Approximately 1.0, the same as air.
Approximately 1.5, heavier than air.
Approximately 0.7, lighter than air.
Approximately 2.0, much heavier than air.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Approximately 1.0, the same as air.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is meant by the "Dilution" method of inerting a cargo tank?
options: The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is mixed with fresh air, and introduced rapidly into the tank.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the bottom of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What inert gas monitoring instrumentation must be fitted in the cargo control room of a tanker?
options: Instruments to continuously indicate and permanently record the oxygen content and deck main pressure.
A device to permanently record the times of stopping and starting the inert gas plant.
Instrumentation showing the cargo tank temperature and pressure.
Instrumentation showing all operating parameters of the inert gas plant.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Instruments to continuously indicate and permanently record the oxygen content and deck main pressure.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point D?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, what would be the effect of diluting with fresh air?
options: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The oxygen level would be increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Displacement" method of inerting, it is common practice to inert several tanks at the same time. Why?
options: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a slow enough rate to enable the formation of a stable horizontal interface.
Because the inert gas plant works more efficiently when the back pressure is lower.
Because it is easier to compare the hydrocarbon levels in the tanks if a large number are open.
Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a slow enough rate to enable the formation of a stable horizontal interface.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: A gas turbine with afterburner will produce similar inert gas to an independent inert gas generator. What level of oxygen might typically be delivered?
options: 1.5-2.5% by volume.
5% by volume.
8-10% by volume.
Approximately 12% by volume.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.5-2.5% by volume.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the maximum oxygen content which should be maintained in a cargo tank during operations?
options: Not more than 8%, except when gas freeing.
Not more than 1%, except when gas freeing.
Not more than 18%, except when loading.
Not more than 21%, except when loading.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Not more than 8%, except when gas freeing.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Why is it essential that the deck and engine departments cooperate in the maintenance and operation of the inert gas plant?
options: To ensure that the cargo tanks are in the required atmospheric condition at all times, and that there is no risk of flammable vapours entering the engine room.
To comply with working hours regulations, and keep overtime under control.
To ensure the minimum time is spent working cargo in port.
To comply fully with the requirements of the planned maintenance system.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To ensure that the cargo tanks are in the required atmospheric condition at all times, and that there is no risk of flammable vapours entering the engine room.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point A?
options: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Pressure in the cargo tanks may be reduced due to low night time temperatures. How could this affect inert gas quality?
options: Air could be drawn into the system.
The rate of evolution of cargo vapours could be increased.
Components of the inert gas may break down at low pressure.
The inert gas may condense into the cargo at low temperatures.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air could be drawn into the system.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: It is generally accepted that an atmosphere with less than 11% oxygen cannot burn. Why is the figure of 8% usually specified as the maximum oxygen content of a cargo tank?
options: To allow a safety margin.
Because gas detection equipment is not accurate enough.
Because hydrocarbon gas will be produced during cargo operations.
To allow for operator error using the equipment.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To allow a safety margin.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the operating principle of a dry type deck seal in an inert gas system?
options: A dump valve is fitted, which opens, filling the lower chamber with water to form a seal when the inert gas supply stops.
A large diameter non-return valve is fitted, which will close when the inert gas supply stops.
The chamber is drained when the inert gas plant is prepared for operation, but can be filled with water when the plant is not in use, forming a seal.
The chamber contains a number of baffles which prevent solid materials from entering the cargo tanks, and help regulate the pressure of the inert gas main line.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: A dump valve is fitted, which opens, filling the lower chamber with water to form a seal when the inert gas supply stops.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Why is an oxygen content of not more than 8% considered to be the safe limit in a cargo tank atmosphere?
options: Because the atmosphere is safely outside the Flammable Range.
Because 8% hydrocarbon gas is below the Lower Flammable Limit.
Because 8% hydrocarbon gas is above the Upper Flammable Limit.
Because the tank atmosphere was outside the Flammable Range at the time the readings were taken.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the atmosphere is safely outside the Flammable Range.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point B?
options: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point C?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the maximum oxygen content allowed by SOLAS in the output from an inert gas plant?
options: Not more than 5%.
Not more than 1%.
Not more than 8%.
Not more than 21%.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Not more than 5%.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the current deadweight, above which tankers must be fitted with an inert gas system?
options: 20000 tonnes.
15000 tonnes.
2000 tonnes.
50000 tonnes.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 20000 tonnes.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: Explain how very cold weather conditions can cause over-pressurisation of cargo tanks?
options: Ice could form on the vents, or the P/V or high velocity vent valves could freeze.
Low temperatures will increase the viscosity of the cargo, and may make it unpumpable.
Cold weather may cause malfunctioning of cargo monitoring equipment, including pressure monitors.
The increased density of the cargo could lead to overloading.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Ice could form on the vents, or the P/V or high velocity vent valves could freeze.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What action must be taken if the inert gas plant fails during cargo discharge operations?
options: You should prevent air from entering the tanks, and stop discharge from inerted tanks.
You should reduce the discharge rate until the plant is repaired.
You should continue discharge, monitoring oxygen and gas concentration in the cargo tanks.
You should carefully allow fresh air into the tanks to prevent under-pressurisation.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: You should prevent air from entering the tanks, and stop discharge from inerted tanks.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the minimum recommended pressure for cargo tanks connected with an inert gas main?
options: 100 mm water gauge.
500 mm water gauge
One bar.
0.25 bars.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 100 mm water gauge.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is pyrophoric iron sulphide, and what hazard is associated with it?
options: It's a compound formed by hydrogen sulphide and iron oxide which becomes incandescently hot in the presence of oxygen.
It's a compound found in inert gas, which increases corrosion in ballast and cargo tanks.
It's a compound which causes the "rotten eggs" smell of some crude oil, and it is toxic.
It's a crystalline substance found in inert gas which can build up in vents, filters etc., and can cause a blockage.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It's a compound formed by hydrogen sulphide and iron oxide which becomes incandescently hot in the presence of oxygen.

CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.question: When a tanker is carrying sour crude, it is possible for pyrophoric iron sulphide to form. What special precautions must be taken following a failure of the inert gas plant?
options: The inert gas plant must be repaired, or an alternative supply arranged, before resuming discharge.
Cargo tanks must be water washed after discharge to remove iron sulphide deposits.
Continue discharge, monitoring oxygen and hydrogen sulphide concentration in the cargo tanks.
Cargo tanks must be thoroughly cleaned before loading the next cargo.
CD7013 — TOTS 1A-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The inert gas plant must be repaired, or an alternative supply arranged, before resuming discharge.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which an infrared gas detector operates?
options: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.
It compares the electrical resistance of the sample with fresh air.
It measures the resistance of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
It compares the relative density of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must chemical absorption tubes only be used with pumps from the same manufacturer?
options: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.
Because the tubes will not fit correctly into another manufacturer's pump.
Because using different tubes breaks the terms of the contract with the manufacturer.
Because using the wrong tubes may lead to contamination of the pump.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which chemical absorption indicators operate?
options: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.
To sense the proportion of a sample which is absorbed by a catalyst.
To show whether a toxic gas will be absorbed by the human body.
To compare the chemical absorption rate of the sample with fresh air.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Pellistor"?
options: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.
It's a balancing resistor between the sensing element and a fixed compensator.
It's a protective device which removes contaminants.
It's a filter which prevents the spread of flame.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instrument should you use to test for very low levels of oxygen before loading a sensitive cargo?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A paramagnetic oxygen analyser.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why is it necessary to use a water-retaining filter in the sample line of an oxygen analyser?
options: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.
Because water in the sample will corrode the internal parts of the instrument.
Because water will build up in the sample line, reducing the flow.
Because water reacts with the measuring cell, giving a false reading.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What effect will inert gas have on the operation of an infrared type gas detector?
options: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.
It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
Small particles may obscure the mirrors.
It will Increase the reading by increasing the temperature of the chamber.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When changing high purity cargo grades, what instrument should be used to ensure that tanks are free of the previous product?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A tankscope.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which a thermal conductivity meter works?
options: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show change in the density of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
To show a change in temperature of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show a change in the conductivity of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Multi-toxic gas detectors normally use electro-chemical detectors. What level of accuracy can be expected?

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: After washing and gas-freeing from a toxic cargo, what type of gas detection equipment should you use before entering a cargo tank?

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Sintered Filter", and what is its purpose?

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using an oxygen analyser?

The strength of a magnetic field is reduced in the presence of oxygen.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What will be the effect of hydrogen sulphide on the reading shown on a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter)?

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What level of accuracy can be expected when using toxic gas detection tubes?
options: Approximately 1 ppm, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 10%, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 100 ppm, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 30%, depending on the type of tube in use.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of sensor is fitted in a tankscope?

A catalytic filament resistor.

A magnetic induction sensor.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How will leaks in the sampling line affect the operation of portable gas detection equipment?

Excess pressure may cause errors in the readings.

options: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.
It will cause higher readings due to increased flow rate.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When starting to test a sample using a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter), the needle immediately flicks to maximum deflection, then returns to zero. What is indicated?

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using a tankscope?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self-testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.

options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

Checking the battery level and self- testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.

CD7014 — TOTS 1A-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the composition of the span gas generally used to zero a portable oxygen analyser?

consult a general arrangement and a capacity plan?
look for a similar cargo in the cargo record book?
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: consult the Approved Trim and Stability Manual?

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: A combination carrier loaded with crude oil has two tanks, each only 60% full. What affect will this have on the vessel's stability?

It will increase the rolling period.
The vessel will trim by the head.
It will increase in permissible bending moments.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: There will be a virtual loss of GM.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you find information relating to intact stability and stress limitations?
options: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.
The Safety Management System.
The SOPEP Manual.
MARPOL publications.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Ship Inspection Report Programme (SIRE) states that the loading programme must be checked by means of an approved test programme at least..
options: Quarterly.
Annually.
At the Chief Officer's discretion.
As directed by the Master.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Quarterly.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When calculating the UKC, what is the "controlling depth"?
