It's the draught of the vessel when proceeding in a narrow channel.
It's the depth of water allowing for height of tide.
It's a figure required to calculate squat.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It's the least depth of water on the vessel's proposed track.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: At commencement of loading, the generation of static is controlled by..
options: limiting the flow rate at the tank inlet.
earthing the manifold.
only having one loading arm connected.
monitoring the cargo temperature.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: limiting the flow rate at the tank inlet.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Permissible bending moments are greater in which condition?
options: In harbour condition.
There is no difference between sea and harbour condition.
It depends upon the amount of segregated ballast.
It depends upon the mean draught.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In harbour condition.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: A vessel is to maintain light ballast condition, however if logged and permissible bending moments have been exceeded, you would..
options: reduce ballast in Fore & After Peaks, maintaining propeller immersion and minimum draught forward?
ballast amidship cargo tanks?
do nothing, it is only a short voyage?
move bunker fuel aft?
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: reduce ballast in Fore & After Peaks, maintaining propeller immersion and minimum draught forward?

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When discharging segregated ballast, the overboard discharge must be monitored..
options: for contaminated ballast.
to help calculate the rate of discharge.
to observe when de-ballasting has been completed.
Monitoring is not required.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: for contaminated ballast.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Flammability and toxicity of proposed cargo can be obtained from..
options: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS).
ISGOTT.
The Approved Trim and Stability Manual.
The SOPEP file.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS).

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Vessels Inspection Questionnaire (VIQ) states the maximum interval between the calibration of temperature and pressure gauges to be..
options: 30 months.
12 months.
24 months.
at the Master's discretion.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: 30 months.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where are temperature and pressure gauges normally calibrated?
options: In a competent shore-based establishment.
In an Engineer's workshop.
With the local ship handler.
Always at the head office.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In a competent shore-based establishment.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Different grades on a product tanker are normally segregated by..
options: Two valve separation.
A single valve.
A spade blank.
It does not matter as different densities will keep them separated.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Two valve separation.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: If the shore fails to deliver cargo at the requested rate, what action would the Master take?
options: He would issue a letter of protest.
He would inform the local P&I Club.
He would inform the Class.
He would take no action.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: He would issue a letter of protest.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What does code "R" indicate in the Ship / Shore Safety Check List?
options: Re-checking at intervals not to exceed an agreed time.
Restricted access.
Regular checks not required.
Checks to be repeated only upon the instructions of the Chief Officer.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Re-checking at intervals not to exceed an agreed time.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Sequential and flow through methods form part of..
options: the ballast exchange plan.
the composition of a sounding book.
the plan to clean cargo tanks.
the ballast water analysis.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the ballast exchange plan.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you use the Chief Officer's personally developed loading / stress monitoring computer programme?
options: Never.
Occasionally, if the approved one is non-operational.
All the time, if the results appear correct.
Once a month to check the results of the approved system.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Never.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What competent body would normally approve a loading instrument / programme?
options: The Classification Society.
SOLAS.
The P&I Club.
The ship's Master.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Classification Society.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: The port / cargo operations log will form the basis of..
options: the statement of facts.
crew overtime.
ISPS implementation.
compliance with SOLAS.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the statement of facts.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Ship / Shore Safety Check List states that temporarily removed scupper plugs must be..
options: constantly monitored.
stowed in a safe place.
clearly labelled as to location.
only removed by the person responsible for cargo operations.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: constantly monitored.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: How long must logbooks and other cargo records be kept on board?
options: As detailed in the owners/managers Safety & Quality Management System.
For 12 months after discharge.
At the Master's discretion.
For the life of the vessel.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: As detailed in the owners/managers Safety & Quality Management System.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Night orders must be signed by the appropriate personnel..
options: every night when new orders are issued.
once per port only.
once per cargo grade only.
It does not matter.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: every night when new orders are issued.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: A Ship to Shore Safety Checklist can be found in which publication?
options: ISGOTT.
ISPS code.
SOPEP.
The Mariner's Handbook.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: ISGOTT.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you find approved information regarding the vessel structural strength?
options: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.
The deck logbook.
The Certificate of Class.
The OCIMF Ship Inspection Report Programme.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you need to check the intact stability at intermediate stages of cargo transfer?
options: On each and every occasion.
If the Master directed you to do so.
When the vessel developed a list.
Seldom as it's not really required.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: On each and every occasion.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: During cargo transfer, what action would you take if the Inert Gas System fails?
options: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.
Increase the rate of discharge.
Advise the terminal and continue discharging.
Review the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When must the Chief Officer's standing orders be followed?
options: Throughout all cargo transfer, ballasting operations and tank cleaning.
Only in port.
Only during ship to ship transfer operations.
When the Captain is ashore.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Throughout all cargo transfer, ballasting operations and tank cleaning.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Emergency shutdown valves in liquid piping should fully close under all service conditions within..
options: 30 seconds.
60 seconds.
90 seconds.
5 seconds.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: 30 seconds.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: How do you ensure that pre-cargo transfer stability and stress calculations are correct?
options: Only by using an approved loading instrument which has been regularly tested with an approved test programme.
By looking at similar cargoes in the cargo record book.
By trusting your personal previous experience.
This should not be necessary.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Only by using an approved loading instrument which has been regularly tested with an approved test programme.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: How does "free surface effect" (sloshing) affect the ship's stability?
options: It reduces the metacentric height.
It has no effect.
It causes an angle of loll.
It increases the metacentric height.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It reduces the metacentric height.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is it important to pre-plan all aspects of cargo operations?
options: To ensure a smooth, pollution free and safe cargo transfer.
To calculate the time required.
To satisfy the ISM code.
It's a Company requirement.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To ensure a smooth, pollution free and safe cargo transfer.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When should P/V valves be checked for free movement?
options: Prior to the commencement of each cargo operation as required by the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
As per the Plan Maintenance System.
As per the ISM code.
As per the ISPS code.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Prior to the commencement of each cargo operation as required by the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: On what occasions will a pre-cargo transfer meeting be minuted?
options: On each and every occasion.
When there is something special to say.
When the Captain attends.
Whenever the port stay is estimated to be greater than 24 hours.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: On each and every occasion.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where on the cargo manifold are pressure gauges fitted?
options: Out board of the manifold valves.
Inboard of the manifold valves.
On the manifold flange.
Fitted to the offshore manifold.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Out board of the manifold valves.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: In the loading limit formula, at which temperature is the pR value expressed?
options: At reference temperature.
At ambient temperature.
At sea temperature.
At 45 degrees Centigrade.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: At reference temperature.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Damage due to sloshing is a direct result of the tank..
options: being partially filled (slack).
being filled more than 98%.
having the tank pressure too high.
None of these answers.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: being partially filled (slack).

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question:
Under normal operations, a cargo tank should not be
filled higher than..
options: the level at which the overfill alarm is set.
as per the Approved Trim and Stability Book.
as per appropriate SOLAS regulation.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the level at which the overfill alarm is set.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: The principle purpose of a pre-cargo transfer meeting is to..

inform the technical officers when cargo pumps will be required.
arrange shore leave.
discuss the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What material should manifold reducers be made of?

Cast iron.
GRP (glass reinforced plastic).
None of these answers.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: In which language would you expect the operational and technical manuals to be written?
options: The official working language of the vessel.
English.
Several languages.
It depends upon the nationality of the manufacturer.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The official working language of the vessel.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Cargo transfer operational information will normally be available in..
options: the cargo control room (CCR).
the SOLAS training manual located in the officers' and crew lounge.
the Chief Engineer's office.
the wheel-house.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the cargo control room (CCR).

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you exceed the maximum pressure ratings of the cargo system?
options: Never. All pressure ratings must be adhered to.
When circumstances dictated a departure from safe operating procedures.
When you think it is safe, according to your own personal experience exceeding pressures on other occasions.
Whenever instructed to do so by the head office.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When can cellular mobile phones be used to assist with cargo transfer communications?
options: Never.
When portable VHF/UHF's are not available.
When the terminal agrees.
When GMDSS equipment is switched off.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: When starting a centrifugal cargo pump, the discharge valve should be initially..

Open.
It does not matter.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is the name of the diagram that is superimposed on the cargo control console?

The tank plan.
The cargo lines.
The pumping plan.

An exact technical drawing.
An approximate drawing.
The general arrangement plan.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Before loading, you should ensure that..

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: A cargo tank wash plate improves intact stability.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is meant by the operating envelope when referring to loading arms?

It is the vertical reach of the loading arm.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It is the maximum amount the vessel can safely range up and down the berth and generally move without damaging the loading arms.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: How does the Chief Officer ensure the approved stress and stability computer is giving accurate results?
options: By running an approved test programme on the computer.
By comparing the results to his own homemade programme.
By comparing results to previous similar conditions.
It never goes wrong, and so does not need checking.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: By running an approved test programme on the computer.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Prior to cargo transfer, where would you expect to see a reference to valves and gauges?
options: In an appropriate Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
In the Safety Management System (SMS).
In the statement of facts.
In the Vessel Inspection Questionnaire.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In an appropriate Ship / Shore Safety Check List.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What precaution must be taken when removing a blank flange?

Ensuring that the cock on the pressure gauge is closed.
Ensuring that the correct spanner size is used to remove the bolts.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Ensuring that the section between the blank flange and last valve does not contain oil under pressure.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Vessels with large width tanks are more susceptible to..
options: a loss of intact stability due to free surface effect.
developing an angle of loll.
an inability to maintain a minimum draught forward.
having problems with propeller immersion.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: a loss of intact stability due to free surface effect.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is it important to keep the cargo manifold area clear of obstructions?

Simply to keep the space tidy and ship shape.
For easy access in case of a pollution incident.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: What medium is used to purge cargo tanks that have previously carried crude oil?
options: Inert gas.
Oxygen.
Water.
A mixture of oxygen and water.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Inert gas.

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you normally expect to find a full set of cargo operation instructions?
options: The cargo control room (CCR).
The Master's cabin.
In the wheel-house.
The SOLAS training manual in the crew's lounge.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The cargo control room (CCR).

CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.question: Shore cargo hard arms are commonly known as..
options: chicksans.
hose strings.
cargo lines.
manifold lines.
CD7016 — TOTS 1A-Familiarisation prior C.answer: chicksans.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: In which publication would you find the MFAG table number?
options: The IMDG Code Supplement.
The Ship Captain's Medical Guide.
USCG CFR 33.
ISGOTT.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What describes the lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off sufficient gas to form a flammable gas mixture near the surface of the liquid?
options: The Flash Point.
The auto Ignition Point.
The threshold Limit Value.
The load temperature.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Why would a vessel be in possession of an NLS (Noxious Liquid Substances) certificate?

The certificate is required on a petroleum product tanker.
The certificate is not mandatory and would usually be kept by the owner.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: It's required for any vessel carrying a MARPOL Annex II cargo that does not have a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Chemicals.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the goggles on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.
They must be lightweight.
They must have 2 headbands for extra safety.
Nothing in particular, chipping goggles are adequate
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What would you do if you looked down a cargo tank and saw a colleague apparently unconscious?
options: Raise the alarm and wait for assistance.
Immediately enter the tank to give first aid.
Don breathing apparatus and enter the tank.
Look at the permit to see who is down the tank.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: Raise the alarm and wait for assistance.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: The vessel is on time charter. The master is concerned about bunker ROB's. Who should he address his concerns to?

He should inform the brokers who will deal with it.
He should inform the local agent at the next port.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The time charterer who is responsible for supplying bunkers.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is Odour Threshold?
options: The lowest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.
The highest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.
The permissible odour when handling cargos with a high H2S content.
It is the smell you get from spiked crude.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The lowest concentration of vapour in the air that can be detected by smell.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: According to the IBC code where should in use protective equipment be stowed?

In the accommodation.
At the top of the pumproom.
At the forecastle head.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: In special lockers in easy accessible places.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the lifeline and belt that form part of the safety equipment on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?

The length of the lifeline must be at least double the tankers moulded depth.
The equipment must be inspected at least annually.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the inspection criteria for breathing apparatus on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?

A weekly inspection by the 3rd officer.
The Chief Engineer inspects all the apparatus monthly.
It should be inspected by a class surveyor annually.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A monthly inspection by a responsible officer and annual inspection and testing at an approved facility.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is essential for an oxygen/air resuscitator to operate efficiently?
options: The casualty's airway must be clear.
The casualty must be unconscious.
The casualty must weigh over 90 KG.
The casualty must not have facial hair.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Where would you find information on the cargo to be loaded relating to health hazards?
options: The MSDS (Material Safety data Sheets).
The World Health organisation.
The Ship Captain's Medical Guide.
SOLAS consolidated edition.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the "pumping clause"?

It's the maximum number of cargo pumps that can be operated at one time.
None of these answers are correct.
CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: It's the maximum time to discharge the entire cargo or a minimum average pressure at the discharge manifold.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Why is the first 0 to 4 minutes critical for the casualty?

The casualty will always survive if oxygen is given within this time frame.
The casualty will always die if oxygen is given after this time frame.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is deadfreight?

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is a charter party?

A group of ship brokers.
A non-binding agreement between any two parties.
Renting a vessel for an event.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What clause relating to unsuitable cargoes is incorporated by the charter party to protect the vessel's owner?

The Paramount clause.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the "Cargo Retain Clause"?

It addresses the owner's right to claim for cargo not discharged.
It deals with cleanage after bulk discharge.
It deals with the amount of cargo retained as samples.

CD7017 — TOTS 1A-Cargo Information, Prec.question: The charter party includes information on STS transfer. What is meant by STS transfer?
options: Ship To Ship.
Suitable Tank System.
Suitable Tanker Stability.
Safe Tanker System.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What minimum starting air pressure is normally required to start a main engine?
options: 12 bars.
10 bars.
15 bars.
17 bars.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: 12 bars.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: During manoeuvring what condition would you expect to consistently apply to the starting air system?
options: The starting air pressure should be kept at the maximum possible level at all times.
The bridge should be informed of the status of the starting air capacity on a regular basis.
Only one air compressor should be run at all times and the second one kept on stand-by.
At least two air compressors should be running at all times.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: The starting air pressure should be kept at the maximum possible level at all times.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the maximum allowed sulphur content in "Low Sulphur Fuel"?
What does "Power Management System" mean?
options: It is the electric generators automatic load sharing and distribution system.
It is the automatic shut-down of all "non-essential consumers".
It is the automatic shut-down of the cargo pumps.
It is the automatic start of the steam boilers.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: It is the electric generators automatic load sharing and distribution system.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: If one unit of the main engine is out of order, what action should be taken concerning the cylinder liner lubrication?
options: Increase the lubrication.
Decrease the lubrication.
Shut off the lubrication.
No action is required.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Increase the lubrication.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the normally accepted method for testing automatic start-up of stand-by equipment?
options: By manually stopping the in service unit.
By running both units simultaneously.
By checking that the standby unit switch is correctly set.
By doing a black-out simulation.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: By manually stopping the in service unit.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: In what configuration should the starting air system bottles be set prior to arrival manoeuvring?
options: All air bottles should be fully charged with one online and one on stand-by.
All air compressors should be switched to MANUAL mode.
All air bottles should be charged and fully open.
All air-operated deck equipment should be isolated.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: All air bottles should be fully charged with one online and one on stand-by.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action should be carried out when one fuel pump becomes defective during manoeuvring?
options: The fuel pump should be hung up, the inlet valve shut and the bridge informed of the problem.
The main engine should be stopped immediately and the bridge informed of the problem.
The main engine's revolution should be increased to recover the loss of power on one cylinder.
The main engine's revolution should be decreased to avoid overloading other cylinders.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: The fuel pump should be hung up, the inlet valve shut and the bridge informed of the problem.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What affects the distribution of electrical load between electric generators in parallel?
options: Changing individual prime mover revolutions.
Adjusting individual generator voltage.
Adjusting individual exitation current.
Removal of consumer load demand.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Changing individual prime mover revolutions.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action should be carried out if an electrical black-out occurs in the engine room during manoeuvring?
options: After the emergency diesel generator starts, run only minimum machinery for safe manoeuvring.
Inform the bridge of the situation and try to restart the diesel generators.
Wait for the emergency diesel generator to start and evacuate the engine room immediately.
Give assistance to the Electrician and try to bring back the electrical power as soon as possible.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: After the emergency diesel generator starts, run only minimum machinery for safe manoeuvring.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action would you take if the main engine lubricating oil pressure dropped suddenly during manoeuvring ?
options: Request permission from the bridge to stop the main engine as soon as possible and warn them that it may stop automatically.
The main engine's revolutions should be reduced.
The main engine revolutions should be increased to compensate.
The main engine should be kept running while waiting for the stand-by oil pump to start.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Request permission from the bridge to stop the main engine as soon as possible and warn them that it may stop automatically.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is one of the first actions that should be carried out during manoeuvring if one or more of the main engine's turbochargers is defective?
options: Check that all auxiliary electric-powered blowers are switched on and operating correctly.
The main engine should be stopped and shore assistance should be called.
The main engine's revolutions should be reduced.
The main engine's revolution should be increased for more power.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Check that all auxiliary electric-powered blowers are switched on and operating correctly.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: If one unit of the main engine is out of order due to a fracture in the liner, what action should be taken with respect to the scavenge air supply to the unit before manoeuvring?
options: The scavenge air should be isolated from the unit.
No action needs to be taken with respect to the scavenge air.
The exhaust valve should be adjusted to remain open during the full cycle to prevent build up of air pressure.
The scavenge air should be increased to improve cylinder cooling.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: The scavenge air should be isolated from the unit.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Would you expect the Engine Room itself to have personnel engaged in watchkeeping duties during manoeuvring?
options: Yes.
No, due to Company requirements.
No, due to safety requirements.
Yes, as required by the Master.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Yes.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action should be carried out FIRST if a fire has broken out in the engine room during manoeuvring?
options: Ensure the fire alarm is raised.
Stop the main engine by pushing the emergency stop button.
Call the bridge and ask for assistance.
Call the Emergency Party.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Ensure the fire alarm is raised.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What condition should stand-by equipment be in prior to arrival / departure manoeuvring?
options: All stand-by equipment should be operable / available and in standby condition.
All stand-by equipment should be switched ON and running.
All stand-by equipment should be switched OFF.
All stand-by equipment should be running but not delivering its intended service.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: All stand-by equipment should be operable / available and in standby condition.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the main purpose of the "Arrival / Departure Checklist"?
options: To confirm that all systems necessary for manoeuvring are in working order.
To ensure personnel changes on board are documented.
To provide Company data required by the office.
To be used as a teaching aid to junior ranks.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: To confirm that all systems necessary for manoeuvring are in working order.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: If, during manoeuvring, you find that a fire had broken out in the purifier room what action should you take after raising the alarm and advising the bridge of the situation?
options: Try to extinguish the fire using portable fire fighting equipment.
Evacuate all non-required personnel from the engine room.
Call the designated person ashore for help.
Call a vessel in the vicinity for help.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Try to extinguish the fire using portable fire fighting equipment.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Would you expect the Control Room to be manned during manoeuvring in an UMS classed vessel?
options: Yes.
No manning is required due to UMS conditions.
No manning is required even if no UMS conditions apply.
Yes, as required by the Master.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Yes.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Why is water not suitable for extinguishing main engine scavenge fires?
options: It will flash off and the fire may develop into a hydrogen fire.
It will cool the space too quickly and cause the liner to crack.
It will leak into the crankcase space and contaminate the lubricating oil.
It will cause the liner, piston rod and scraper box parts to rust.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: It will flash off and the fire may develop into a hydrogen fire.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: As per SOLAS requirements, where should the quick close fuel valves' release cabinets be located?
options: Outside the engine room.
Inside the engine room.
Near the engine control room.
On the navigation bridge.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Outside the engine room.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: How many generators would you expect to have running during manoeuvring?
options: Sufficient to allow for continuous supply should one alternator trip.
Sufficient for 100% normal seagoing load.
All available generators.
One running and one on standby.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Sufficient to allow for continuous supply should one alternator trip.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the purpose of a steering gear "Creep Test"?
options: To check the condition of the steering gear hydraulic system seals and valves.
To check if the steering gear autopilot is in good order.
To check if the steering gear non-follow up control system is in good order.
To check that the steering gear does not fall back from the hard-over position.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: To check the condition of the steering gear hydraulic system seals and valves.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What activities related to arrival manoeuvring does the International Safety Management Code (ISM) require to be logged in the Engine Log Book?
options: All pre-arrival checks and tests carried out.
All tests carried out as per arrival check lists.
All function tests carried out on the main propulsion system.
All function tests carried out on communications (Bridge / Engine Room).
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: All pre-arrival checks and tests carried out.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Is there a requirement to increase Main Engine Cylinder Lubrication during manoeuvring?
options: No, unless special circumstances apply.
Yes, as manoeuvring is considered a special circumstance.
Yes, as per the lubrication oil company requirements.
No, as per MARPOL requirements.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: No, unless special circumstances apply.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action should be carried out if the CO2 alarm is raised in the engine room?
options: All personnel should be evacuated from the engine room immediately.
The Master should be informed immediately of the alarm.
It should be re-checked to make sure it is not a false alarm.
All running equipment should be stopped first and then all personnel should leave the engine room.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: All personnel should be evacuated from the engine room immediately.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What practical preparations can be carried out, before manoeuvring, if the stern tube is found to be defective and oil leakage is observed (apart from dealing with environmental issues)?
options: The stern tube oil gravity tank can be lowered until oil leakage stops.
Leakage may be ignored if only a minor quantity of oil is present.
The stern tube oil gravity tank can be raised until oil leakage stops.
Stop all operations and call for shore assistance to stop overboard leakage.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: The stern tube oil gravity tank can be lowered until oil leakage stops.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: While on Main Engine stand-by during a river passage towards a port, you get a high exhaust temperature alarm on one main engine cylinder. What would you do?
options: Call the bridge and advise the Master of the problem.
Stop the main engine.
Acknowledge the alarm and watch to see if the temperature increases.
Acknowledge the alarm until you get into port.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Call the bridge and advise the Master of the problem.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Which of the following tests would NOT normally be carried out as part of a pre-arrival standby routine?
options: The testing of the fuel system quick-closing valves.
The testing of main engine starting ahead and astern.
Testing communications between the bridge and engine room.
The testing of the steering gear.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: The testing of the fuel system quick-closing valves.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: In the event of a main engine scavenge fire, which of the following options is the best course of action to take immediately?
options: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.
Speed up the engine in an effort to blow the fire out.
Stop the engine and keep it in one position until the fire is out.
Start the auxiliary blowers.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What preparations should be carried out first before manoeuvring if the main engine's electronic governor is found to be defective?
options: Disconnect the governor from the fuel rack and regulate the rack manually.
Stop manoeuvring until the governor has been repaired.
Contact the maker and ask for assistance.
The governor should be blocked into the middle position and then manoeuvring can proceed.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Disconnect the governor from the fuel rack and regulate the rack manually.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What action would you take if, during manoeuvring operations the main engine oil mist detector alarm was activated, the engine automatically slows down and the alarm condition clears?
options: Advise the Master and prepare to stop the engine as soon as it is practical for the manoeuvring operations.
Advise the Master and stop the engine immediately to inspect the crankcase.
Advise the Master and continue with slow speed operation, until the completion of manoeuvring.
Advise the Master of the alarm activation and continue with the normal engine operations.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Advise the Master and prepare to stop the engine as soon as it is practical for the manoeuvring operations.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What should be done if the remote control of the steering system from the bridge becomes defective during manoeuvring?
options: Change over to local control and engage one person for steering.
Stop all operations immediately.
Call tugboats for assistance and proceed with manoeuvring.
Stop manoeuvring until the remote control has been repaired.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Change over to local control and engage one person for steering.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the usual acceptable time for the steering rudder to swing from "hard to port" to "hard to starboard"?
options: 28 seconds.
18 seconds.
38 seconds.
48 seconds.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: 28 seconds.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: Does SOLAS legislation exist stating how many steering gear hydraulic pump units are directly connected to the emergency switchboard?
options: Yes, according to SOLAS legislation there should be a minimum of one pump.
According to SOLAS legislation all the pumps should be connected.
SOLAS do not have the power to legislate on this requirement.
No such requirement exists.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Yes, according to SOLAS legislation there should be a minimum of one pump.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: What is the first action you should take if the main engine oil mist detector alarm sounds?
options: Slow down the main engine immediately and inform the bridge of the problem.
Inform the bridge and re-check the main engine's bearing temperatures.
Check if the alarm is genuine before initiating any action.
Call the Technical Superintendent for help immediately.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Slow down the main engine immediately and inform the bridge of the problem.

CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.question: When, during manoeuvring, would you expect to changeover from heavy oil to diesel oil on a vessel where the two fuels are utilised?
options: Prior to manoeuvring.
At a suitable time during manoeuvring.
Just before shutting down allowing time to flush through the fuel system.
It is optional dependent on whether overhaul work will be carried out on the engine.
CD7020 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations.answer: Prior to manoeuvring.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: If the local engine side control is used in order to overcome problems with starting astern..
options: only the low lub oil trip and mechanical overspeed trip continue to work in the normal way.
all interlocks and protection devices with the exception of those connected with reversing, operate in the normal way.
all interlocks and protection devices continue to work in the normal way.
all interlock and protection devices are over ridden.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: only the low lub oil trip and mechanical overspeed trip continue to work in the normal way.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: The safeguard against starting a slow speed direct drive engine with the fuel cam in the incorrect position is..
options: a wrong way alarm and interlock.
a wrong way alarm only.
a fuel cut off interlock only.
not fitted as it will automatically correct itself.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: a wrong way alarm and interlock.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: It is normal good practice to operate the engine in standby mode with..
options: one air bottle on line and the other topped up with its supply valve shut.
both air bottles on line and the main air compressor start and stop on manual control.
both air bottles on line and the main air compressor start and stop on automatic control.
both bottles on line with one compressor on auto and the other on manual start/stop.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: one air bottle on line and the other topped up with its supply valve shut.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: What is the number of consecutive ahead and astern starts a slow speed direct drive engine should be capable of?
options: More than 8 on each air bottle.
Less than 8 but more than 5.
At least 5 on each air bottle.
Less than 8.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: More than 8 on each air bottle.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: If a significant limitation of engine power due to cooling problems is experienced before stand by..
options: you need to resolve the problem as emergency power may be needed unexpectedly.
you can wait until you have finished manoeuvring as manoeuvring speed is less than full sea speed.
you should stop immediately as any such limitation could result in engine damage.
you may ignore the problem until you have time to carry out repairs.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: you need to resolve the problem as emergency power may be needed unexpectedly.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed main engine, direct drive installation, with more than 1 turbo charger, a turbine failure..
options: requires that the rotor be removed and blanking plates fitted.
does not require that the rotor be removed and blanking plates fitted.
does not affect full power operation provided the engine can be kept running.
means the engine cannot be run on reduced power.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: requires that the rotor be removed and blanking plates fitted.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: An intermittent failure to start astern at the first try is..
options: not very significant if the engine starts on the second or subsequent attempts.
significant and must be immediately rectified, and pilots and shore management notified.
not very significant provided the engine starts astern on local control.
very significant and must be investigated at the next port.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: not very significant if the engine starts on the second or subsequent attempts.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: Unavailability of stand-by coolant supply pumps is..
options: significant and must be rectified as soon as possible.
significant and must be rectified before the engine is started.
not very significant and UMS operation of the engine room may be continued.
not very significant as one pump is enough for cooling.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: significant and must be rectified as soon as possible.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: It is normally expected that starting on local engine side control uses up..
options: less starting air than bridge control.
the same amount of starting air as bridge control.
more starting air than control room control.
more starting air than bridge control but only on astern movements.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: less starting air than bridge control.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: If ,during the sea passage, oil is observed leaking from the sterntube inboard seal header tank, what should you do?
options: Fit an oil tight cap to the header tank and monitor the inboard seal for leakage until repairs can be carried out.
Add thicker oil to the sterntube system in order to minimise the oil loss until repairs can be carried out.
Reduce the header tank level to reduce the leakage by maintaining minimum positive pressure on the seals.
Collect the leaking oil and return it to the header tank to minimise the oil loss until repairs can be carried out.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: Fit an oil tight cap to the header tank and monitor the inboard seal for leakage until repairs can be carried out.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On restoration of electrical power following a short duration electrical power failure in open water, the main engine may be re-started..
options: only after checking that all the ancillary equipment has restarted and that all pressures and temperatures are normal.
directly on power being restored.
only after the turning gear has been engaged and the engine turned over.
only after another generator has been put on line to ensure there is no further failure of the electrical power supply.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: only after checking that all the ancillary equipment has restarted and that all pressures and temperatures are normal.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: Stand by coolant supply pumps should auto start in the event of..
options: pump failure alarm and low pressure alarm.
high coolant temperature alarm.
pump failure alarm only.
low pressure alarm only.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: pump failure alarm and low pressure alarm.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: If a fuel pump is identified as defective on one unit and spares are unavailable, the main engine..
options: can continue to be run at reduced power with the fuel pump hung up and isolated.
can continue to be run at full power until the next port of call.
can continue to be run, but all other fuel pumps should be adjusted to balance exhaust temperatures.
can continue to be operated at lower load or reduced RPM once the pump has been removed from the engine.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: can continue to be run at reduced power with the fuel pump hung up and isolated.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On restoration of electrical power following an electrical power failure during a confined water transit, the main engine must be re-started..
options: only after checking with the bridge that it is OK to do so.
directly power is restored in order to minimise any delay to the vessel.
as soon as the engineer is satisfied that the power supply is stable and that the engine is ready to start.
as soon as the engineer confirms that the steering gear is running and the engine is ready to start.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: only after checking with the bridge that it is OK to do so.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed main engine, direct drive installation, where a crankcase oil mist has been detected, the likely cause of the oil mist is due to..
options: a bearing overheating.
a crankcase door not being closed properly allowing air to enter the crankcase.
running the engine with the lub oil pressure too high.
a blockage of the crankcase vent pipe.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: a bearing overheating.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed main engine, direct drive installation, a turbo-charger failure..
options: requires that the auxiliary blowers be used to operate the engine at reduced power.
puts the propulsion plant out of use as the engine cannot operate with natural aspiration.
does not affect full power operation provided the engine can be kept running.
does not affect full power operation provided the auxiliary blowers are fully operational.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: requires that the auxiliary blowers be used to operate the engine at reduced power.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a Steam turbine propulsion, set astern manoeuvring power is..
options: less than 40% of ahead power.
greater than ahead power.
equal to ahead power.
90% of ahead power.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: less than 40% of ahead power.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a vessel where the bridge control of the steering gear is found to be defective, how should the steering gear be operated?
options: Directly from the steering gear space local control position, only after local communications with the bridge have been set in place and tested.
From the engine room by a crew member with communications via the engine control room.
From the steering gear compartment with communications from the bridge via the engine control room and OOW.
By the non-follow up steering control.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: Directly from the steering gear space local control position, only after local communications with the bridge have been set in place and tested.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: How is it ensured that important operations are carried out according to set procedures?
options: By using the appropriate critical operations check list.
By following the Chief Engineer's standing orders.
By using the manufacturer's operating / instruction manuals.
By using the Company operating manual.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: By using the appropriate critical operations check list.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed main engine, direct drive installation, where both the Bridge Control system and the engine control room system are defective, the main machinery should be operated from the local (engine side) control..
options: by an engineer, and only after operating procedures have been implemented and communications with the bridge tested satisfactorily.
by a deck department crew member after establishing direct communication to the bridge for manoeuvring instructions.
only by the Chief Engineer who will have communications directly to the Master on the bridge, for manoeuvring instructions.
while the engine is being manoeuvred and unmanned operation can be resumed when the vessel is on passage.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: by an engineer, and only after operating procedures have been implemented and communications with the bridge tested satisfactorily.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: If, during the sea passage, oil is observed leaking from the sterntube outboard seals, what should you do?
options: Reduce the header tank level to maintain minimum positive pressure on the seals, and monitor the water level in the sterntube oil to ensure any ingress is controlled.
Add thicker oil to the sterntube system in order to minimise the oil loss until repairs can be carried out, and reduce the engine speed to prevent overheating.
Reduce the header tank level to below sea level to ensure that there is no possibility of pollution, and monitor the sterntube temperature for any overheating.
Raise the sterntube oil pressure to ensure there is no possibility of water entering the sterntube and causing damage to the sterntube bearing.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: Reduce the header tank level to maintain minimum positive pressure on the seals, and monitor the water level in the sterntube oil to ensure any ingress is controlled.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a vessel with 2 generators, while preparation is being made to depart on a 3 day voyage, one generator breaks down but cannot be repaired due to lack of a spare part. What should you do?
options: Cancel the departure and do not sail until the generator is back in service or a backup package generator is fitted.
Sail as planned and have the generator repaired in the next port as the voyage is very short.
Advise the office of the problem and agree to sail as the spare part will be arranged for the next port.
Sail as planned as the owner's representative is insisting that the vessel must not be delayed.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: Cancel the departure and do not sail until the generator is back in service or a backup package generator is fitted.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: In the event of full astern emergency being requested on a slow speed engine on sea passage you should..
options: immediately bring the speed control to stop, wait for the engine rotation to slow, then put starting air to turn the engine in the astern direction.
immediately bring the speed control to stop, wait for ahead rotation to stop, then put starting air to turn the engine in the astern direction.
immediately bring the speed control to stop and put starting air to turn the engine in the astern direction.
stop the engines and open the air bottles in preparation for starting astern.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: immediately bring the speed control to stop, wait for the engine rotation to slow, then put starting air to turn the engine in the astern direction.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed direct drive engine, the safety device which prevents fuel and starting air being simultaneously applied to the engine is..
options: the fuel air interlock.
the wrong way alarm and cut out.
the turning gear interlock.
the camshaft wrong-position indicator.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: the fuel air interlock.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: In case of any malfunction or breakdown of critical equipment during navigation what is the first action you should take?
options: Inform the bridge to alert them.
Raise the general alarm.
Man the engine room until normal manned operation commences and then inform Engine Staff.
Inform the Chief Engineer and 2nd Engineer.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: Inform the bridge to alert them.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a vessel where the bridge control of the steering gear has failed during the voyage, the vessel should not continue on voyage until the steering gear..
options: has been changed to local control with the operating position manned at all times, tested and communications with the bridge established.
has been fully overhauled and the defect fully identified and rectified.
is secured in amidships position, with tug assistance for the duration of the voyage to a port of refuge.
creep test has been carried out.
CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.answer: has been changed to local control with the operating position manned at all times, tested and communications with the bridge established.

CD7021 — TOTS 1B-Engine Room Operations-.question: On a slow speed main engine, the engine can be brought back into service after extinguishing a scavenge fire..
options: only after the cause of the fire is determined and the scavenge space cleaned out and inspected for damage.
as soon as the bridge confirms that the engine may be restarted.
