CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: Which of the following would provide the most reliable assessment of the insulation resistance of a motor winding?
options: A megger tester.
A digital multimeter on resistance setting.
An analogue AVO meter on resistance setting.
Earth lamps/monitoring unit on the main switchboard.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What is the fail safe condition for digital input switches connected to a ship's central alarm and monitoring system?
options: It can be open or closed depending on the application.
It is normally open.
It does not matter.
It is normally closed.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: It can be open or closed depending on the application.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What is the most appropriate method of simulating a particular temperature output from a PT100 probe?
options: Connect a known resistance to the sensor cabling.
Apply a 4-20mA signal to the sensor cabling.
Apply a mV signal to the sensor cabling.
Short circuit the sensor cabling.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: Connect a known resistance to the sensor cabling.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: For Direct on Line (DOL) Starting, what would you expect the starting current to be?
options: 6 - 10 x normal current.
2 - 3 x normal current.
10 - 20 x normal current.
0.5 - 1 x normal current.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: In a battery system, the most effective method of determining a cell's capacity to maintain its charge is by measuring the cell voltage..
options: under fully loaded condition.
while on boost charge.
when removed from the circuit.
when off load.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: In which compartments would you expect to find intrinsically safe electrical apparatus?
options: The battery compartment.
The engine control room.
The engine room.
The wheel-house.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: The power supply at a ship's main switchboard has an unsteady frequency. What is the most likely cause of this condition?
options: A faulty generating engine governor.
An Automatic Voltage Regulator fault.
The loss of excitation.
Alternator winding over-temperature.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: In addition to maintaining the output voltage of a generator at a pre-set level, what is the function of the Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR)?
options: To ensure equal loading of kVAR between generators operating in parallel.
To ensure that generators operating in parallel always run at matching speeds.
To control the system power factor.
To ensure equal loading of kW between generators operating in parallel.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: To ensure equal loading of kVAR between generators operating in parallel.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: A pump motor is found to be running at abnormally high temperatures. Which of the following would be the most likely cause of this condition?
options: A fouled or damaged impeller.
A loose terminal connection.
Low winding insulation.
The thermal overload is set too low.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: The emergency generator automatic starting system must be capable of a minimum of..
options: three starts.
one start.
five starts.
ten starts.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: Where might you expect to find static electricity on a tanker?
options: In an electrical charge produced during tank cleaning operations.
In any motor, as it is the electricity that remains as a charge within a motor when it has stopped running.
In an alternator, as a differential electrical voltage between two generators during synchronisation.
In the battery compartment when they are being charged.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: In an electrical charge produced during tank cleaning operations.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: How should you check to see if an item of electrical equipment is overloaded?
options: By checking the ammeter to ensure it is not drawing excess current.
By conducting Megger tests to confirm that the insulation value is satisfactory.
Overlaod trips are fitted so that, if the equipment does not trip, then it is operating correctly.
Monitor the heat generated, and also vibration and noise levels.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: By checking the ammeter to ensure it is not drawing excess current.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What is the most important aspect of portable or fixed electrical equipment in a hazardous area?
options: The equipment should be intrinsically safe.
The equipment should be correctly earthed.
The equipment is class approved.
The equipment is safely secured to prevent damage.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: The equipment should be intrinsically safe.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: How often would you expect the operation of standby equipment to be checked? How would you do this?
options: Weekly, by switching over to alternate standby machinery.
Daily, by switching over to alternate standby machinery.
Monthly, by switching over to alternate standby machinery.
Quarterly, by switching over to alternate standby machinery.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: Weekly, by switching over to alternate standby machinery.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: In preparing for maintenance on any critical equipment what should be considered first?
options: Has a risk assessment been prepared?
Are the spare parts onboard that are required for the work?
Is there sufficient man power to complete the job?
Is permission from the port authorities required?
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: Has a risk assessment been prepared?

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What is the purpose of a reverse power trip?
options: It trips the main breaker of a generator that is losing power, to prevent it being driven by another generator(s) on the same bus bar.
It trips the main breaker of a generator to prevent it driving another generator.
If a motor's electrical terminals are incorrectly connected, it trips the motor breaker and activates an alarm.
In an emergency, it senses a dropping load demand and trips an alarm.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: It trips the main breaker of a generator that is losing power, to prevent it being driven by another generator(s) on the same bus bar.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What is the purpose of a preferential trip?
options: When a generator goes into a predetermined overload condition, certain non-essential power is tripped to reduce load and prevent tripping of the generator main breaker.
When a generator is overloaded, the preferential trip automatically starts the standby alternator / engine to share the load / demand, and prevent damage and blackout.
When two generators / alternators are operating and the load does not dictate the requirement for 2 alternators, one will automatically stop.
It is the process of shutting down machinery when entering dry dock, prior to switching to shore power.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: When a generator goes into a predetermined overload condition, certain non-essential power is tripped to reduce load and prevent tripping of the generator main breaker.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: How is it possible to ensure that various alarms and cut outs are working?
options: By a regular simulation test to confirm their function.
They are tested and certified during dry docking.
The Alarm Panel would indicate an error if not operating correctly.
They are checked during the daily rounds of the Duty Officer.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: By a regular simulation test to confirm their function.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: Which of the following should be entered into a vessel's maintenance system following work carried out on an electric motor? (1) Whether work scheduled or unplanned. (2) Details of the work done. (3) Details of parts used while carrying out the work.
What is the purpose of a shaft earthing device?
options: To ensure that there is no voltage differential between the shafting, propeller and the hull.
To provide one single point for all earths to be dissipated into the stern of the vessel.
It is associated with the operation of the vessel's cathodic protection system.
It prevents static electricity within the crankcase of the main engine and therefore reduces the possibility of a crankcase explosion.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: To ensure that there is no voltage differential between the shafting, propeller and the hull.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: Why should equipment be earthed?
options: To discharge electrical current to earth in the event of a short circuit.
To prevent damage to the vessels computer systems.
To prevent an earth alarm indication on the main switch board.
To enhance machinery performance and extend the life cycle of equipment.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: To discharge electrical current to earth in the event of a short circuit.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: If a circuit breaker is fitted with a shunt release, the circuit breaker will trip..
options: when voltage is applied to the shunt release.
when there is a wire break in the control circuit.
when the voltage is removed.
when there is a faulty contact.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: when voltage is applied to the shunt release.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What system is the most important in order to prevent the collapse of a computerised control system in the event of a power failure.
options: The UPS system must be maintained in good order.
Back up of files / documents must be completed.
Up-to-date anti virus software must be installed.
There should be an annual service and health check of the computer systems. This should be carried out by the manufacturer's technician.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: The UPS system must be maintained in good order.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: How would you ensure that all Electrical equipment has a satisfactory insulation value?
options: By regular megger testing.
By routine maintenance.
By ensuring the equipment is dry and free from moisture.
By operating and observing the operational performance and running amperage.

CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.question: What action should you take if the insulation on the earth meter shows low readings?
options: Isolate each piece of equipment in turn to identify which one has low insulation.
Switch all the equipment on, then turn off one by one to identify which has low insulation.
Megger test all related equipment to identify the one which has low insulation.
Observe the operation of all equipment for abnormalities.
CD7024 — TOTS 1B-Electrical, Electronic.answer: Isolate each piece of equipment in turn to identify which one has low insulation.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: An increase in main engine crankshaft deflection readings may be an indication of..
options: excessive wear of main bearing shells.
excessive wear of thrust bearings.
excessive weight of piston and connecting rod.
excessive torsional stress.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: excessive wear of main bearing shells.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Main engine cylinder liners normally have ‘directional’ air inlet ports in order to?
options: Induce swirling of the air inside the cylinder.
Minimize air turbulence.
Push hot gases away from the liner wall.
Cool the piston crown.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Induce swirling of the air inside the cylinder.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What needs checking if there are high levels of chromium in the crank case lub oil?
options: The piston rings.
The crosshead bearings.
The main bearings.
The cylinder liner.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The piston rings.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What measurements are taken during the overhaul of a unit of the Main engine?
options: Liner calibration, piston groove measurements and piston rod measurements.
Liner calibration.
Piston groove measurements.
Piston rod measurements.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Liner calibration, piston groove measurements and piston rod measurements.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is a piston profile gauge used for?
options: To check for burn down of the piston crown.
To measure the piston groove wear.
To measure the piston rod wear.
To measure the piston clearance in the liner.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: To check for burn down of the piston crown.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What does the presence of copper in the crank case lub oil sample indicate?
options: Bearing wear.
Liner wear.
Piston wear.
Scraper box wear
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Bearing wear.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: After the overhaul of a main bearing and after crankcase inspection, what needs to be done first before manoeuvring with the engine?
options: Turn the engine on turning gear with the lub oil pump running.
Turn the engine on turning gear.
Blow through the engine from Control room to test controls.
Blow through engine using Local / Manual control
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Turn the engine on turning gear with the lub oil pump running.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: In which direction is the engine turned when taking crankshaft deflections?
options: Ahead.
Astern.
Both ahead and astern.
Any direction.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Ahead.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Excessive crankshaft deflections are taken as an indication of..
options: an engine misalignment or worn main bearings.
only an engine misalignment.
only worn main bearings.
a bent crank shaft.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: an engine misalignment or worn main bearings.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Where would you find the correct value for clearances of the main engine main bearings?
options: In the main engine instruction manual.
In the main engine spare parts manual.
In the main engine lubricating oil piping diagram.
In the Official log book
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: In the main engine instruction manual.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Which of the following is the first and most basic step you take when you start work on a unit of the Main engine?
options: To engage the turning gear.
To remove the fuel pipes.
To remove the jacket water pipes.
To remove the starting air pipes.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: To engage the turning gear.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: For accurate readings the deflection gauge should be ..
options: at the same temperature as the engine.
at room temperature.
at a higher temperature than the engine.
at a lower temperature than the engine.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: at the same temperature as the engine.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Crankshaft deflections are normally taken when the engine is..
options: hot.
cold.
either hot or cold.
at any temperature.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: hot.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What could be the most common reason for the hydraulic pump in a hydraulic pack to trip on high oil temperature?
options: A fouled oil cooler.
A broken suction valve.
A broken discharge valve.
A broken pump.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A fouled oil cooler.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What measurements would you take during the overhaul of a reciprocating pump?
options: Plunger, slide valves and bottom end bearing measurements.
Plunger measurements.
Slide valve measurements.
Bottom end bearing measurements.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Plunger, slide valves and bottom end bearing measurements.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Where should the dial gauge be placed while taking crankshaft deflections?
options: As far as possible from the axis of the crank pin.
As close as possible to the axis of the crank pin.
The centre of the crank web.
Anywhere on the crank web but as indicated in the Planned Maintenance System.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: As far as possible from the axis of the crank pin.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What needs to be checked on the liner before putting back the piston during the replacement of the main engine liner?
options: The flow of cylinder lub oil.
The flow of system lub oil.
The flow of camshaft lub oil.
The flow of jacket cooling water.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The flow of cylinder lub oil.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What type of pump would you expect to find in a hydraulic power pack?
options: A positive displacement pump.
A single stage centrifugal pump.
A multi stage centrifugal pump.
A sliding shoe pump.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A positive displacement pump.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What position of the piston are exhaust valve clearances adjusted?
options: During the compression stroke.
During the power stroke.
During the intake stroke.
During the exhaust stroke.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: During the compression stroke.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Where would you look for, and expect to find, the position of various engine room double bottom tanks?
options: In the general Arrangement plan.
In the tank calibration tables.
In the stability booklet.
In the Engine Room Piping Schematic drawings.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: In the general Arrangement plan.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: How often would you normally expect to carry out water washing of the exhaust gas economiser?
options: Once a month.
Once every 6 months.
Once a year.
Once every two years.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Once a month.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the most common source of damage found on centrifugal pump impellers?
options: Cavitation damage.
Corrosion damage.
Fatigue cracks.
Impact damage.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Cavitation damage.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Why is an air compressor started in the unloaded condition?
options: To avoid high starting torque.
To avoid condensate carry over.
To avoid high discharge pressure.
To avoid damage to the suction and discharge valves.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: To avoid high starting torque.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Which of the following tools would be required for replacement of a main engine cylinder liner?
options: A liner lifting tool, a piston lifting tool and a cylinder head lifting tool.
A liner lifting tool.
A piston lifting tool.
A cylinder head lifting tool.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A liner lifting tool, a piston lifting tool and a cylinder head lifting tool.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What type of pump would you use for a high volume, low pressure application?
options: Centrifugal.
Reciprocating.
Screw.
Lobe.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Centrifugal.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the possible consequence of prolonged oil carry over from a starting air compressor?
options: It could cause an air line explosion.
It could cause low starting air pressure.
It could cause lifting of the air compressor relief valve.
It could cause a high starting air temperature.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: It could cause an air line explosion.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What material are welding gloves normally made of?
options: Leather.
Cotton.
Wool.
Rubber.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Leather.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What type of fire detection would you find in the engine room workshop?
options: A smoke detector.
A thermal detector.
A flame detector.
Solely a Manual Push / Break Glass system.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A smoke detector.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What checks would you carry out before starting an air compressor after an overhaul?
options: Check for debris from the overhaul, freedom of movement of the bottom end bearing and turn the compressor by hand.
Check pressure in the starting air bottles.
Check for freedom of movement of the bottom end bearing.
Turn the compressor by hand.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Check for debris from the overhaul, freedom of movement of the bottom end bearing and turn the compressor by hand.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Which clearance would have the maximum effect on the pumping efficiency of a centrifugal pump?
options: Impeller and wear ring clearances.
Bearing clearances.
Shaft seal clearances.
Coupling clearances.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Impeller and wear ring clearances.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Which of the following tools are required for overhauling a turbocharger?
options: A rotor locking tool, a bearing extracting tool and a spanner for the bearing nut.
A rotor locking tool.
A bearing extracting tool.
A spanner for the bearing nut.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A rotor locking tool, a bearing extracting tool and a spanner for the bearing nut.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the most important issue which must be borne in mind while inspecting critical equipment?
options: Reduction of possible risk to the vessel
Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA).
Repair methodology.
It must not be carried out at sea.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Reduction of possible risk to the vessel

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the recommended DC voltage output from a welding machine?
options: Less than 70V.
Less than 240V.
Less than 110V.
Less than 440V.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Less than 70V.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: If preventive maintenance work on critical equipment is overdue, what is the accepted course of action to proceed with this work?
options: Carry out a Risk Assessment and discuss maintenance options before making decision.
This has to be carried out immediately, even if it involves stopping the ship.
Carry on and schedule the work at the next port of call.
Carry it out before completing other items whose overhaul is due at the same time.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Carry out a Risk Assessment and discuss maintenance options before making decision.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Where would you expect to find damping wire used in a turbocharger?
options: The gas side.
The air side.
Both gas and air sides
The bearings.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The gas side.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Where does the concept of critical equipment come from?
options: The ISM code.
The ISPS code.
SOLAS.
MARPOL.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The ISM code.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the most common cause of turbocharger failure?
options: Debris from the main engine.
Lubrication failure.
Bearing failure.
Bad fuel quality.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Debris from the main engine.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What is the requirement for the space where oxygen and acetylene bottles are stored on a ship?
options: They should be stored in separate well ventilated compartments on the deck.
They should be stored in separated well ventilated compartments in the engine room workshop.
They should be stored in a well ventilated compartment in the accommodation.
They should be stored in an enclosed space.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: They should be stored in separate well ventilated compartments on the deck.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: In addition to a deck mounted emergency stop button what type of safety device would you expect to find on a grinder to protect the operator?
options: A glass shield.
A high voltage trip.
An over current trip.
A reverse current trip.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: A glass shield.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What do you particularly check for, in the crank case, after an engine liner replacement?
options: Water ingress.
Abnormal noise.
Lub oil ingress.
Piston Clearance
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Water ingress.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Which of the following parts of the bilge discharge system need calibration?
options: The 15 ppm monitor.
The opening angle of overboard discharge solenoid valve.
The recirculation solenoid valve position.
Bilge water Inlet flow meter.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The 15 ppm monitor.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Why is it important to ensure Boiler Sliding Feet are maintained and kept correctly lubricated.
options: To ensure the Boiler is allowed to expand freely when it changes temperature.
To allow the boiler to move as the steam pipes expand under high loading.
To allow limited movement of the boiler as the ship rolls and pitches in a seaway.
It is not important as the provision of the sliding feet were to allow easy location of the boiler when it was being fitted.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: To ensure the Boiler is allowed to expand freely when it changes temperature.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: The purpose of fine mesh screens on bunker tank vent heads is to?
options: Prevent flames from passing into the tank.
Prevent dirt from getting into the fuel tank.
Prevent accidental overflow from the tank.
Prevent the fumes from the tank affecting personnel working close by.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Prevent flames from passing into the tank.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Prior to putting an Oily Water Separator into operation, should you?
options: Fill it completely with clean sea water.
Partially fill it and pressurize it with air.
First drain it completely.
Flush the oily contents through with sea water prior to switching on the oil content monitor.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Fill it completely with clean sea water.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: On a diesel engine, if the tappet clearances are greater than the manufacturer’s recommend setting, the cylinder head valves will..
options: open late and close early.
open late and close late.
open early and close late.
open early and close early.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: open late and close early.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: During routine rounds of the main engine, you note that the pipe leading to one of the air start valves is hot. Do you?
options: Contact the bridge and request permission to stop immediately.
Attach a portable temperature gauge to record the temperature.
Advise the watch keepers to monitor it and report if the temperature increases.
Apply portable ventilators to cool the pipe down.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Contact the bridge and request permission to stop immediately.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: In a large slow speed diesel engine, which of the following would you expect to be directly cooled by Sea Water?
options: Scavenging air.
Turbocharger.
Cylinder heads.
Fuel valves.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Scavenging air.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: In a large 2 stroke diesel engine, which bearing half takes the highest loading?
options: Crosshead bearing lower half.
Main bearing upper half.
Connecting rod bearing lower half.
The crosshead bearing upper half.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Crosshead bearing lower half.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: In the event of a main engine scavenge fire, which of the following options is the best course of action to take immediately?
options: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.
Speed up the engine in an effort to blow the fire out.
Stop the engine and keep it in one position until the fire is out.
Start the auxiliary blowers.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: What action is needed if the fuel has a high water content?
options: Frequent draining of settling and service tanks.
Maintain a higher fuel oil temperature.
Maintain a lower fuel oil temperature.
Advance the fuel timing.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: Frequent draining of settling and service tanks.

CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.question: Why is the TBN value of the crankcase lubricating oil of a Medium/High speed Diesel Engine so important?
options: The TBN is necessary to combat any acidic combustion products that enter the crankcase.
The TBN is necessary to maintain the viscosity of the oil at high temperatures.
The TBN is necessary to reduce any corrosion caused by any water entering the crankcase.
The TBN is necessary to maintain the lubrication of the liner in the combustion area.
CD7025 — TOTS 1B-Maintenance and Repair.answer: The TBN is necessary to combat any acidic combustion products that enter the crankcase.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: The Steering Gear has 2 electric motors. How is the power normally supplied?
options: Independently from the Main switchboard.
Both are supplied from the Main Switchboard on a common power supply.
Both are connected via the Emergency Switchboard.
One is supplied from the shaft generator.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Where would you look to find your prime responsibilities in the event of a fire?
options: The Company Management manuals.
The Emergency Stations (Muster List) poster.
The Shipboard Training Manual.
The Safety Equipment Certificate.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: During a Port State Inspection a discrepancy is found in the Engine Room. The item is recorded, but the Ship is not detained and sails without the discrepancy being cleared. What action should the Inspector take?
options: The Inspector should inform the Port State authority at the vessel's next port.
The Inspector should contact the Company.
The Inspector does not need to take any action as the discrepancy is not a "detainable" item.
The Inspector should inform the Class Society.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: The Inspector should inform the Port State authority at the vessel's next port.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: On an indicator card, taken to calculate the power of a single acting 2-sroke engine, where is the atmospheric line on the card?
options: At the bottom.
At the side.
At the top.
At about mid-point of the diagram.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: In order to prevent inadvertent direct overboard discharge of bilge water the main Engine Room bilge system should be...
options: secured.
blanked.
displaying a warning notice.
checked regularly by a watchkeeper.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: An Industry Vetting Inspector finds a deficiency in the Engine Room. What would the Chief Engineer expect the Vetting Inspector to do?
options: To discuss the deficiency with him, but take no responsibility for any corrective actions discussed.
To discuss the deficiency with him and agree on how to correct it.
Just to record the deficiency.
To assist him to rectify the deficiency.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: To discuss the deficiency with him, but take no responsibility for any corrective actions discussed.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: One result of poorly maintained fire dampers could be...
options: feeding the fire with oxygen.
a build up of toxic fumes.
the fixed foam system being ineffective.
faster cooling of the fire.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: The Emergency Generator is required to have clear operating instructions. Who must be familiar with the operation?
options: The ship's crew.
The Chief Engineer.
Deck Ratings.
The Training superintendent.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: An internal audit of the vessel's Safety Management System must be carried out...
options: every 12 months.
every 6 months.
every 24 months.
every 18 months.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: On a tanker, which of the following best describes a segregated Ballast System?
options: All ballast tanks, pipes and valves are independent of those used for cargo.
Ballast is only taken after cargo has been flushed from the line.
Ballast and cargo tanks are separated by void spaces.
All ballast is discharged via an oil discharge monitor (O.D.M.E).
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: All ballast tanks, pipes and valves are independent of those used for cargo.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: The Chief Engineer's Standing Orders must contain which of the following?
options: Duties of the watchkeeping Engineers and Ratings.
Duties of the Engineers in an emergency.
Duty times of the watchkeeping Engineers and Ratings.
Operation of the Dead Man Alarm.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: Duties of the watchkeeping Engineers and Ratings.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Lifting and loose gear which is not part of the ship's equipment should be examined by a competent person at least once every...
options: 12 months.
24 months.
3 years.
5 years.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: The US Pollution Prevention Regulations (33 CFR) require that any oil spillage in US waters should be reported immediately to...
options: the Agents and local Harbour Authority.
the US Coast Guard.
the vessel's Owners.
the local Oil Spill Resource Centre.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: the Agents and local Harbour Authority.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: With reference to the Safety Management Certificate, what is a document of compliance?
options: It is a document that the company is issued with by the flag state.
It is a document that the ship receives when it has no non - conformities.
It is a document that certifies that the ship complies with all the regulations.
It is a certificate that a ship receives after being audited.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: It is a document that the company is issued with by the flag state.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: The Planned Maintenance System should be inspected by which of the following to confirm that it has been implemented according to Company procedures?
options: An Auditor.
A Class Surveyor.
A Port State Control inspector.
An authorised shore technician.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Which of the following would contribute to an increased risk of accidents?
options: Unsafe working conditions.
Regular inspections.
Good housekeeping in the Engine Room.
Proper risk assessments.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: What would the Auditor report if he found that a laid down procedure was not being correctly carried out?
options: A non-conformity.
A non-correctness.
A non- adherence.
A non -appliance.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Having emptied, cleaned and ventilated a bunker tank for hot work, how would you ensure that the atmosphere in the tank is not combustible?
options: Test the atmosphere with an explosimeter.
Test the atmosphere with a portable oxygen meter.
Take a sample of the atmosphere in the tank and test it with an open flame.
Leave the tank lids open for 24 hours.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: Test the atmosphere with an explosimeter.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: When calculating bunkers for a voyage, the amount of extra bunkers required to provide a safe margin is calculated according to...
options: the Company's procedures.
the direction given by the Charterer.
the Chief Engineer's own experience.
the Master's instructions.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Oil Pollution Regulations require that any transfer of oil onboard a vessel should be recorded in...
options: the Oil Record Book.
the Bridge log book.
the Engine Room log book.
the Master's Official log book.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: An auxiliary engine has reached the running hours for major overhaul, but is due a survey in 2 months. Which of the following would be the correct course of action?
options: Overhaul it, and bring forward the survey to suit.
Overhaul it, and do the survey later.
Postpone the overhaul until the survey date.
Seek advice from the Class surveyor.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: Overhaul it, and bring forward the survey to suit.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: What is the normal survey interval for machinery items?
options: Once every 5 years.
Once every 3 years.
Once every 4 years.
Once every 2.5 years.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: When an Exhaust Gas Boiler is surveyed who is responsible for setting the safety valves?
options: The Chief Engineer.
The Class Surveyor.
The Company Superintendent.
The Shore Technician.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: A Garbage Record Book must be kept. When plastic has been incinerated what should you do with the ash?
options: Land the ash to reception facilities.
Dispose of it into the sea 25 miles from the nearest land.
Mix it with the other ash and dispose of it into the sea.
Mix it with plastic garbage and dispose to shore.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: Land the ash to reception facilities.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: When bunkering, you note that you have some leakage from the connection manifold flange, but the Master is pressing you to depart as soon as possible to make the tide. What do you do?
options: Stop bunkering and repair the leak?
Spread absorbent material on the deck to soak up any spillage?
Reduce the pumping pressure to minimize the leakage?
Notify the local authority of a potential oil spill?
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: Stop bunkering and repair the leak?

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: A risk assessment should be carried out and a Hot Work Permit issued before any hot work is carried out...
options: outside the Engine Room workshop.
during manoeuvring.
at night.
during bunker operations.

CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.question: Before entering an empty Fresh Water tank for inspection and cleaning, you should...
options: ventilate and test the atmosphere with a calibrated oxygen indicator.
open and ventilate the tank at least 1 hour before entry.
ventilate and test the atmosphere with a calibrated combustible gas detector.
put on a Breathing Apparatus set and enter the tank.
CD7027 — TOTS 1B-Management of the Engin.answer: ventilate and test the atmosphere with a calibrated oxygen indicator.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: The ship suffers a collision. The bridge waste paper basket contains some small pieces of paper with scribbled notes on. What should the Master do?
options: Collect these pieces of paper and keep them as a record, as they may contain relevant information.
Treat them as waste and ignore them as they have already been thrown away.
It might be an idea to falsify the scribbled notes after the collision so you will not be held responsible.
There is already so much evidence available that it's not necessary to keep these small pieces of paper.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Collect these pieces of paper and keep them as a record, as they may contain relevant information.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: You have a small bunker spill in port. All notifications are done and the cleanup is completed. What do you do concerning the record collection?
options: Obtain calculations of relative quantities on board, in the pipelines and in the barge.
Leave matters to the local agent and feel relieved that the emergency is over.
Leave the record collection to the company who are not on site.
Forget the records and hope the estimated spilt quantity will be relatively accurate.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Obtain calculations of relative quantities on board, in the pipelines and in the barge.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What are SOPEP / VRP / SMPEP / PCSOPEP?
options: Oil Spill Contingency plans based on different regulations.
Different plans as required by different nations of the world.
Manuals segregated by the company for ease of use.
Manuals required by the ISO 9001 standards.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Oil Spill Contingency plans based on different regulations.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How is the SMPEP different from a SOPEP?
options: It is the contingency plan for ships carrying Noxious Liquid Substances.
SMPEP deals with Oil Pollution only.
It is the same plan, only called by different names based on the individual company.
Different Flag Administrations use different terminology for the same plan.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is the contingency plan for ships carrying Noxious Liquid Substances.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where should the main control station of the deck fixed foam fire fighting system be installed?
options: Outside the cargo area, adjacent to the accommodation, readily accessible and operable in event of fire.
Inside the accommodation so that it is accessible and operable in event of fire.
Inside the cargo pump room since all cargo operations are controlled from there.
On one of the superstructure decks in an easily accessible location for use in event of fire.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Outside the cargo area, adjacent to the accommodation, readily accessible and operable in event of fire.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are proper records required to be maintained for routine tests, checks and maintenance of fire-fighting equipment?
options: For ease of reference and to allow proper and effective planning of testing and maintenance. Also plans and records must be available for inspection when required by the Administration.
Because the company auditors can ask for all records of inspections.
Because the Port State Control is likely to detain the ship if records are unavailable.
Because the quality system requires records to be maintained to provide evidence.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: For ease of reference and to allow proper and effective planning of testing and maintenance. Also plans and records must be available for inspection when required by the Administration.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do dry powder installations require periodical checking?
options: Solidification of the compound can occur on board over a period of time.
The powder tends to change colour and loose effectiveness.
Dry powder evaporates and disappears over time.
Other extinguishing media are more stable.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Solidification of the compound can occur on board over a period of time.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where can the fixed fire fighting installation be located?
options: All three answers are correct.
It can be located inside protected space.
It can be located in a room behind the fwd collision bulkhead, used for no other purpose.
It can be located no more than one deck below open deck and directly accessible from open deck.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All three answers are correct.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fixed fire-fighting installations may be fitted for the machinery spaces?
options: Any of the types mentioned.
Fixed Gas Fire Extinguishing system.
Fixed High Expansion Foam system.
A fixed high pressure water spraying system.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Any of the types mentioned.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fixed fire-fighting installations may be fitted for the cargo pump room?
options: It should be fitted with a system suitable for machinery spaces of category A.
Pump rooms should be fitted with a fixed high expansion foam extinguishing system only.
Pump rooms must be fitted with a gas fire extinguishing system only.
The type of system is based on the type of cargo the ship is carrying.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It should be fitted with a system suitable for machinery spaces of category A.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How many foam applicators must a fixed foam extinguishing system have on deck?
options: A minimum of 4.
A minimum of 2.
At least 4 on each side.
10 in total.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: A minimum of 4.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do foam compounds after an initial 3 year period have to be tested annually?
options: All the answers.
Because it is a Flag requirement.
Because the foam compounds are likely to deteriorate over time.
Because deterioration of the foam can reduce its properties.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What are the different types of foam extinguishing media that may be found on board?
options: High expansion, medium expansion and/or low expansion foam
High Expansion Foam only.
Medium Expansion Foam only.
Low Expansion Foam only.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: High expansion, medium expansion and/or low expansion foam

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What size of tanker must be fitted with a fixed deck fire-extinguishing system?
options: Tankers of 20,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.
Tankers of 5,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.

All tankers must be fitted with a fixed system.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Tankers of 20,000 tonnes deadweight and upwards.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Does the paint locker require a fixed fire fighting installation?
options: Yes, a fixed system is mandatory.
A portable installation is acceptable if within easy reach.
The regulations require a portable extinguisher in the locker.
It is only important to be able to quickly access some type of extinguishing system.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes, a fixed system is mandatory.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why does the ship require an International Shore Connection?
options: To provide a standardised connection between the ship's fire main and shore systems which may have different couplings.
It is called by that name since the ship trades in International waters.

It is used only in the drydock to keep the fire main pressurised since the ship's pumps are off.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To provide a standardised connection between the ship's fire main and shore systems which may have different couplings.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where can you find the action to be taken and procedures to follow in an emergency?
options: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan.
In the Shipboard Safety Manual.
In the International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals.
In SOLAS
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of galley equipment must be fitted with an automatic or manual fire fighting system?
options: Deep fat cooking equipment.
Electrical equipment.
Galley stove hotplates
Galley ovens

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What must be covered in the familiarisation of the fixed fire-fighting system on the cargo deck area?
options: All the answers are correct.
The fire-fighting medium storage area.
The location and operation of the fixed fire extinguishing system.
The remote and local activation points and procedures.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is high expansion foam suitable to fight a fire on deck?
options: It is unsuitable for use in open areas in outside locations as it is easily dispersed in light winds.

It depends on the expansion ratio of the foam.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is unsuitable for use in open areas in outside locations as it is easily dispersed in light winds.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the importance of operating instructions posted at local positions for fire-fighting equipment?
options: Ease of operation when it's necessary to use the equipment in an emergency.
It is instructed by the Master as part of normal standard procedures.

It helps with the problem of language barriers between different nationalities.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Ease of operation when it's necessary to use the equipment in an emergency.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the purpose of a Safety Meeting on board?
options: To review safety matters and improve the Safety Management System.
To discuss operational problems and the maintenance programme.

To ensure the paperwork, as required by ISM, is completed.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To review safety matters and improve the Safety Management System.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are environmental issues discussed during HSE or environmental team meetings?
options: To raise awareness among the crew on issues that affects the environment and promotes pollution prevention.
Because there are so many rigid regulations to comply with.
For financial reasons as the commercial viability of ship may be affected.
To discuss tactics in the eventuality of an incident involving environmental activists such as Greenpeace.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To raise awareness among the crew on issues that affects the environment and promotes pollution prevention.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where are the operating instructions for the emergency fire pump located?
options: In a clear, visible place near the emergency fire pump.
Adjacent to the international ship/shore connection for use by the shore fire services.
On the ship's bridge and the Engine Control Room.
On the bulkhead next to the ship's fire plan.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: In a clear, visible place near the emergency fire pump.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where is the fire alarm control panel located?
options: On the ship's navigating bridge.
In the Engine Control Room.
In the Emergency headquarters.
At the general muster point.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: On the ship's navigating bridge.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How can the fire stations and lockers be identified on board?
options: Because they are marked with internationally recognised IMO signs.
One can check the general arrangement plan and search for the lockers/stations when necessary.
It is the duty of the ship's Safety Officer to show the crew where the specific locations are.
By following the crew reporting to their stations when the emergency alarm sounds.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why do tankers require isolation valves to be fitted in the fire main at the poop front and on the tank deck at intervals of no more than 40 metres?
options: To preserve the integrity of the fire main system in case of fire or explosion.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the requirement for manually operated call points on a fixed fire detection and alarm system?

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: When should a new crew member undergo on-board safety familiarization?

No later than one month after joining the ship.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why are Vessel Management Meetings held?

To comply with the Company Auditors who periodically check to make sure the meetings have been carried out.
To provide an opportunity for the vessel management team to discuss the issues raised at the HSE meetings.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To promote effective team-working, planning, clarity on tasks, execution and monitoring of jobs.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What kind of fire alarm detectors are used on a ship?
options: They can be smoke detectors, heat detectors, flame sensors or any combination of the three.
A smoke detection system.
Heat detectors.
Flame sensors.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: They can be smoke detectors, heat detectors, flame sensors or any combination of the three.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where shall the isolating valve on the fire main be fitted?
options: It shall be fitted in an easily accessible and tenable position outside the machinery space.
It shall be fitted anywhere on open deck spaces; the ship's main deck being the most appropriate.
It can be fitted anywhere as long as it serves the purpose of isolating the section of fire main for machinery space.
It shall be fitted in the accommodation as the crew are always available in that area.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What details of the main and emergency fire pumps are described on the Fire Control Plan?
options: The capacity of the pumps are clearly indicated.
The identity of the makers and model number is included.
There is no such requirement for details.
Only the location of the fire pumps are marked.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: How is it possible to ensure thermal stresses do not affect the compressor when the BA set air bottles are filled?

By making sure overheating does not take place during operation.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the minimum frequency (for the majority of vessels) for an abandon ship drill and a fire drill for the crew, according to SOLAS Chapter lll?
options: There shall be at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the importance of a running hours log on the BA set air bottle filling compressor?
options: To ensure periodical maintenance is carried out as required by the manufacturer.
The running hour's log is maintained as the company periodically requests to see it.
It indicates when a new compressor needs to be ordered.
It ensures the crew on board are doing their job by looking at the running hours log.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To ensure periodical maintenance is carried out as required by the manufacturer.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Where would you find details of the fire dampers, fire flaps and ventilation on board the ship?
options: In the Fire Control Plan.
In the ship's Emergency Action Plan.
In the ship's General Arrangement Plan.
In the ship's Airconditioning Plan.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: In the Fire Control Plan.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the requirement for galleys that have deep-fat cooking equipment?
options: All the answers are correct.
They shall be fitted with an automatic or manual fire extinguishing system.
There must be an automatic shut off of electrical power when the fire extinguishing system is activated.
There should be clear instructions for crew concerning manual operation of the system.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why is a fire control plan stored in a prominently marked weathertight enclosure outside the deckhouse?
options: It is to assist shore side fire-fighting personnel in an emergency.
It is stored so that crew can access the information during a drill on deck.
It is kept there because the Port State Control Inspector will look for it.
It is kept outside in case of an accommodation fire on board.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: It is to assist shore side fire-fighting personnel in an emergency.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Why is it important to follow a drill with a debriefing session?
options: To review and discuss the lessons learnt and continually improve.
To advise the crew about their faults and assign blame to individuals.
To motivate crew and make good use of any remaining time left over from the drill.
It is a requirement of the Company Safety Policy.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: To review and discuss the lessons learnt and continually improve.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Which of the following elements should generally be included in a fire drill?
options: All of these answers
