Checking of the fireman's outfits, personal rescue equipment and communications equipment.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All of these answers

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What information is available on the ship's Fire Control Plan?
options: The firefighting arrangements and location of all firefighting equipment on board.
The location of all Safety Equipment (LSA & FFA) on board.
The location of the Fixed fire fighting system fitted on board.
The location of all portable fire-fighting equipment on board.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The firefighting arrangements and location of all firefighting equipment on board.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is it mandatory to have a fire blanket in the galley?
options: Yes, it is mandatory as stated by SOLAS.
It depends how committed the ship manager is to safety.
The Port State Control insists on having one in the galley.
It is up to the chief cook to decide.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes, it is mandatory as stated by SOLAS.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What would be the required action if a steering gear failure takes place in a busy shipping lane?
options: All the answers are correct.
Switch to emergency steering and reduce speed.
SECURITE call to other ships in the vicinity so they can take evasive action.
Alert the VTS station and check if it's possible to anchor.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the order of priority when dealing with contingencies?
options: Safety of life, the environment and then property.
Safety and protection of the environment.
Safety of property and cargo.
Safety of the ship and the environment.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Safety of life, the environment and then property.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: If a man falls overboard, what type of message should be sent to alert the ships in the vicinity?
options: PAN - PAN
MAYDAY.
SECURITE.
NONE.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: PAN - PAN

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Is uncontrolled venting an allowed practice while loading cargo?
options: No. Venting of tanks should be only through mast risers in a controlled fashion.
Yes. If the wind speed is good there is no problem with uncontrolled venting.
Yes. Uncontrolled venting is unavoidable due to the vapour pressure while loading.
Yes. It is not a problem since so many precautions have already been taken.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: No. Venting of tanks should be only through mast risers in a controlled fashion.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What would be the immediate action taken in the event of a bunker spill?
options: Stop all transfer operations, inform, sound the alarm and initiate Emergency response.
Stop operations, investigate the occurrence and inform based on the quantity of the spill.
Stop operations and work out a solution to cover up in collusion with the barge.
Stop operations, check if anyone has noticed and then take any necessary action.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Stop all transfer operations, inform, sound the alarm and initiate Emergency response.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Can the SMPEP and SOPEP be combined into one manual?
options: Yes. Since the requirements are similar, they can be combined into one plan.
No. They address different regulations so cannot be combined.
No. The SMPEP is a dry cargo ship contingency plan while the SOPEP is for tankers.
No. The SMPEP is for a particular cargo while the SOPEP is a general plan.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Yes. Since the requirements are similar, they can be combined into one plan.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the minimum required service duration of an EEBD?
options: 10 minutes.
12 minutes.
15 minutes.
20 minutes.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What should the Officer on Watch do in the event of a 'Man Overboard’?
options: Raise the alarm and turn the ship towards the side of the man overboard.
Turn the ship away from the side of the man overboard.
Inform The Master and wait for his arrival.
Call the Chief officer.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Raise the alarm and turn the ship towards the side of the man overboard.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: A few drops of oil spill into the water but no traces are visible anymore. Is it still necessary to report the incident?
options: The incident shall be reported regardless of the size of the incident.
Since no traces of oil are visible there is no need to report it.
Wait and watch to see what the reaction is, and then decide accordingly.
It's advisable to ignore the incident to prevent legal issues arising, especially if there are few witnesses.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The incident shall be reported regardless of the size of the incident.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: In the event of a collision what are the duties to the other vessel?
options: Render assistance without jeopardising the safety of your own personnel and vessel.
Since it is a collision incident, the Master should take details before continuing with the voyage.
Issue a notice of arrest to the other ship on behalf of the Company
If oil has been spilt the Master should take down details and try to avoid becoming involved in a pollution incident.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Render assistance without jeopardising the safety of your own personnel and vessel.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the first reporting requirement in the event of a toxic liquid release at anchor?
options: The incident should be reported to the nearest Coastal State in detail without delay.
The ship's staff must first check with the ship's managers before taking action.
If the effect is not visible on the surface of the water there is no need to report the incident.
The agent should be informed immediately and he will take necessary action.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: The incident should be reported to the nearest Coastal State in detail without delay.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What is the first action that must be taken in the case of a hose burst, pipe work fracture or cargo overflow?
options: All operations must be immediately stopped and the alarm sounded.
Quickly repair the leakage and keep operations going to prevent the ship from being delayed.
Stop all operations and wait for the Coast Guard and terminal people to arrive.
Sound the alarm, inform the Master and wait for his instructions.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All operations must be immediately stopped and the alarm sounded.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What actions should be initiated by the damage control team after a grounding?
options: All the answers are correct.
They should visually inspect the ship and check the draft/trim/list.
They should sound all compartments, sound around the ship and check the nature of the seabed.
They should check the watertight integrity of the compartments in contact.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: All the answers are correct.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: When would you use the Emergency Response Service of the Class Society?
options: For damage stability and longitudinal strength calculations after a casualty.
It is useful for any emergency situation on board where Class is affected.
They are called in for support if the ship is involved in a pollution incident.
They are contacted if the ship has an accidental release of cargo in USA waters.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: For damage stability and longitudinal strength calculations after a casualty.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: Who is the person identified in the Vessel Response Plan who acts on behalf of the Owner for oil spill response in USA?
options: A Qualified Individual.
A designated person ashore.
An authorised person.
The owner's representative.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: A Qualified Individual.

CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.question: What should you do if the ship spills oil into the water in a port and you are contacted by the Media?
options: Be courteous, state facts and suggest the reporter contacts the company, and do not commit yourself on any issues you are not sure about.
Don't be afraid to be direct and explain to them the difficulties of life on board and working with companies.
If they become aggressive, treat aggression with aggression and ask the crew to physically remove them.
Blame the other parties and deny any wrongdoing by you or the ship.
CD7028 — TOTS 1B-Emergencies, Drills and.answer: Be courteous, state facts and suggest the reporter contacts the company, and do not commit yourself on any issues you are not sure about.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Discharge of sewage is prohibited when..
options: the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 3 knots.
the ship is 24 nautical miles from land and has a functioning certified sewage treatment plant.
the sewage is comminuted and disinfected and the vessel is 5 nautical miles from the nearest land.
the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 7 knots.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: the vessel is 24 nautical miles from the nearest land and travelling at 3 knots.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: After having performed a ballast operation the master must..
options: complete the ballast water management log.
inform the Port Administration.
perform a course change.
inform the vessel superintendent.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: complete the ballast water management log.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The portable pump equipment within the oil spill response kit must be..
options: All three answers
Self priming
safe for use in hazardous areas
fitted with sufficient hoses.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: A ship demonstrates compliance with MARPOL Annex IV by..
options: having a valid International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate.
having a surveyor inspect the sewage system every six years.
having a stand-by sewage treatment plant.
having a sewage holding tank volume of 100 litres per person on board.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: having a valid International Sewage Pollution Prevention Certificate.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following is NOT an option to comply with MARPOL Annex IV?
options: An approved comminuting plant.
A certified sewage treatment plant.
An approved comminuting and disinfection plant.
Holding tanks with an approved volume.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following substances is ozone-depleting?
options: Halons.
CO2.
Ammonia.
Neon.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: What can happen if an emulsion is taken up by the OWS?
options: It can lead to a false reading on the oil content monitor.
It can completely block the system piping.
It can cause damage to the pump bearings.
nothing.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: It can lead to a false reading on the oil content monitor.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Prior to exchanging ballast the master must..
options: perform a risk assessment.
inform the Port Administration.
perform a course change.
inform the vessel superintendent.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: To reduce cargo tank vapour release which of the following should be checked?
options: That the tightness of cargo tank hatch dogs are checked after every cargo operation.
That the hatch gasket is checked every year.
That header valves are unseated.
That the cargo pump deepwell bleed valve is open.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: That the tightness of cargo tank hatch dogs are checked after every cargo operation.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Uncontrolled release of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are an environmental problem because..
options: they contribute to low-level ozone pollution in populated areas.
they react with hydrogen creating acid rain.
they contaminate the sea.
they react with CO2.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: they contribute to low-level ozone pollution in populated areas.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: How long should the oil record book be kept for after it has been completed?
options: Three years.
Six months.
One year.
Two years.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The oil record book part 2 requires which of the following to be recorded after cleaning cargo tanks?
options: All three answers.
The ship's position or port.
The duration of cleaning.
The method of cleaning.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: When is it good practice to check the pressure-vacuum valves?
options: Prior to cargo transfer.
During cargo transfer operations.
After cargo transfer operations.
Before the next dry-docking.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Where on board might ozone depleting substances be found?
options: In refrigeration systems.
In compressed air systems.
In sewage treatment plants.
In electronic equipment.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The oil record book makes references to factors affecting quantity of oil. The accuracy of measuring quantities are affected by…
options: All three answers
Temperature variations.
Accuracy of tank measurement devices.
Tendency of oil to cling to the inside tank walls.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following is not part of the spill response equipment inventory?
options: The pressure washer.
Sorbents.
Emulsifiers.
Non sparking scoops, shovels and buckets.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: When first using a cleansing agent in the machinery space, the crew should..
options: confirm that it won't form an emulsion.
confirm that it will form an emulsion.
use it liberally.
use it sparingly.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: confirm that it won't form an emulsion.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: How long must the receipts be held with the Garbage Record Book for?
options: Two years.
Six months.
Five years.
One year.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The spill response station inventory should include..
options: personal protective equipment.
a supply of water.
brushes.
metal shovels.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: It is legal to discharge oil outside a special area when the oily mixture originates from the cargo pump room bilges on an oil tanker.
options: False.
True.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following would increase the fuel consumption on board the ship?
options: Leaving steam system leaks unattended.
Reducing speed in heavy weather.
Turning off lights in empty compartments.
Maintaining steam traps.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following must be recorded in the oil record book part 1?
options: All three answers
Collection and disposal of oil residues.
Condition of oil filtering equipment.
Bunkering of fuel oil.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: No discharge into the sea shall contain chemicals or other substances in sufficient concentration so as to cause damage to the marine environment.
options: True.
False.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: How many categories of garbage are there in a Garbage Record Book?
When is the Master to sign the Garbage Record Book?
options: After each completed page.
After each discharge operation.
At the end of the day.
After the incinerator has been used.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: It is illegal to discharge oily mixtures from the ship when the vessel is stationary and outside of a special area.
options: True.
False.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The oil spill removal equipment store must be..
options: prominently marked and easily accessible.
a storeroom close to the pump room.
a storeroom in the forward area of the ship.
just off the main engine room.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: False entries in the Oil Record Book can lead to criminal penalties for the master and chief engineer?
options: True.
False.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The cargo manifold working platform surface should be made of..
options: open mesh grating.
chequered plate.
wooden laminate.
perforated sheet steel.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: What should the Master refer to In the event of an accidental discharge of oil?
options: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan.
The ship environmental management system.
The cargo tank plan.
The ballast water management plan.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: During bunker transfer operations deck scuppers should be..
options: plugged to prevent spilled oil flowing overboard.
only fitted to the side of the vessel that bunkers are being loaded to.
attended by crew to collect any spilled oil that approaches.
Plugged when required
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: plugged to prevent spilled oil flowing overboard.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: During cargo or bunker operations, oil response equipment is to be..
options: ready for immediate use.
in its store room.
in the cargo pump room.
used elsewhere in the ship.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following should be checked prior to cargo operations?
options: All three answers
That pipeline drains are blanked correctly.
That save-all drains in way of tank vents are plugged.
That spill tank drain plugs are properly secured.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Operational malpractice of the oil filtering equipment can lead to criminal penalties for the vessel master and chief engineer?
options: True.
False.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: The shipboard oil pollution emergency plan shall contain details of a list of authorities to be contacted in the event of an incident.
options: True.
False.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: In the event of an oil pollution incident MARPOL Annex I requires that an oil tanker of 5,000 tonnes deadweight shall have prompt access to..
options: computerised shore-based damage stability and residual structural strength programs.
the nearest port.
an empty oil tanker of equal deadweight.
computerised models of the ship's cargo tank system.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: computerised shore-based damage stability and residual structural strength programs.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: Which of the following would reduce energy consumption?
options: Maintaining an unfouled hull.
Runnning at normal sea speed
Cooling accommodation spaces to 19°C.
Heating accommodation spaces to 25°C.

CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.question: To prevent inadvertent leaks, bunker manifolds not in use should..
options: have blank flanges fitted with gaskets and tightened with all bolts in place.
have blank flanges fitted with gaskets and tightened with some bolts in place.
have blank flanges fitted and tightened with all bolts in place.
have blank flanges fitted and tightened with some bolts in place.
CD7029 — TOTS 1B-Pollution Prevention an.answer: have blank flanges fitted with gaskets and tightened with all bolts in place.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: If hot work is to be undertaken above the tank deck (higher than 500mm), then cargo and slop tanks must either be cleaned and gas freed, OR emptied purged and inerted, OR filled with water, within a minimum radius around the working area. What is this min
options: 30 metres.
10 metres.
20 metres.
40 metres.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: If hot work is to be undertaken on the tank deck or at a height of less than 500mm above the tank deck, the precautions taken should be the same as for hot work within the tank.
options: True
False

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: When can controlled hot work be carried out within a hazardous area on a tanker?
options: When the ship is in ballast condition.
When the ship is carrying out gas freeing operations.
When the ship is carrying out inerting operations.
When the ship is carrying out cargo operations.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: When the ship is in ballast condition.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following could be considered a "designated space" where hot work is able to be carried out safely?
options: The engine room workshop.
The poop deck.
The engine room.
The forecastle deck.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: A Risk Assessment can be a useful tool when preparing a Permit-to-Work on electrical circuits.
options: True
False

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Where hot work is planned to be carried out, what should the Lower Flammable Limit (LFL) reading of the atmosphere be?
options: Less than 1% LFL.
Greater than 1% LFL.
1% LFL.
Between 1% and 2% LFL.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: If the conditions under which a Hot Work Permit has been issued change, what should be done immediately?
options: Stop the hot work.
Prepare additional firefighting equipment.
Extend the validity of the permit.
Amend the work permit conditions.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: A Permit-to-Work on electrical circuits is important in order to prevent what?
options: Electrical shock.
The use of non-intrinsically safe equipment on deck.
Non-scheduled planned maintenance tasks being carried out.
All of these answers.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: No hot work should be carried out in the vicinity of bunker tanks unless which of the following is carried out?
options: The tank has been cleaned to hot work standard.
The tank contains fuel with a flashpoint below 60 degrees Celsius.
The tank contains fuel with a flashpoint above 60 degrees Celsius.
The tank is greater than 90% full.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: The tank has been cleaned to hot work standard.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items may NOT be considered a critical operation?
options: Switching on the radar.
Starting the emergency generator.
Changing over from heavy fuel to diesel.
Lowering and raising lifeboats.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items can be described as critical machinery?
options: All of these answers.
The main engine.
Generators.
Steering gear.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: When carrying out hot work with electric welding equipment, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The ship's structure should not be used as an earthing point.
The cable route to the working area should be the shortest and most direct route.
The Direct Current output source should be in excess of 70 Volts.
The person carrying out the welding operation can work alone so long as a work permit has been issued.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: The ship's structure should not be used as an earthing point.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What should personnel on board barges or other craft obey when moored alongside?
options: All of these answers.
Smoking restrictions.
Prohibition of naked lights.
Restrictions on the use of cooking appliances.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Critical Operations Check Lists are to be used for what purpose?
options: To ensure that critical equipment is operated, started or restarted correctly so that it will not result in a hazardous situation developing or compromise critical functions.
To ensure that every item of equipment on board is operated according to the manufacturer's instructions.
To ensure that all company procedures are followed at all times.
To ensure that the vessel passes external ISM audits by showing the auditor that Section 10 of the ISM Code is fully complied with.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: To ensure that critical equipment is operated, started or restarted correctly so that it will not result in a hazardous situation developing or compromise critical functions.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What is the correct method of closing off unused cargo and bunker connections?
options: All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and are to be fully bolted.
All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and have every second bolt secured by a nut.
Unused connections may be left unblanked so long as two valve separation exists between the connection and the line in use.
Unused connections on the shore-side of the vessel must be closed and fully blanked. The offshore-side may be left unblanked.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: On a Permit-to-Work for pipeline/pressure vessels, which of the following questions would NOT likely be included as part of the checks?

Has the pressure been bled off the section to be worked on?
Has the part of the system to be worked upon been isolated?
Have all personnel been equipped with the correct personal protective equipment?
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Is the lifeboat/rescue boat ready for use?

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What happens to a Permit-to-Work upon completion of work?
options: It is cancelled by the responsible officer.
It is cancelled by the person carrying out the work.
It is left in place in case further work has to be carried out.
It is transferred to another location where similar work is to be carried out.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: It is cancelled by the responsible officer.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What would be the minimum recommended firefighting equipment to have available when alongside a terminal?

One fire hose and one dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles or fire extinguishers adjacent to the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles forward and aft of the manifold and a fire blanket adjacent to the manifold in use.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Hazardous materials such as chemicals and oil will have a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) available. Which of the following is NOT likely to be included in a MSDS?
options: The name of the vessel.
The physical data (e.g. the flashpoint).
The health effects.
The correct storage.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following questions would NOT be part of a Permit-to-Work check list for allowing small craft to come alongside?
options: Has the ship been inerted or gas freed?
Is adequate illumination available?
Has the Master of the small craft been advised of all appropriate safety regulations (e.g. emergency signals, smoking regulations etc)?
Are all deck and cargo openings closed?
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Has the ship been inerted or gas freed?

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Where should the ship's emergency fire control plans be located?

With the Deck Officer of the Watch at all times.
In a prominently marked wallet contained within the cargo control room.
At the bottom of the gangway.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: In a prominently marked weather-tight enclosure outside the accommodation block.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items of equipment would be found in a chemical storage/handling area?
options: Safety goggles.
Safety shoes.
A dust mask.
Ear plugs.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: A Permit-to-Work should specify the period of validity. According to the Code of Safe Working Practices, this period should not exceed how many hours?
options: 24 hours.
Six hours.
Eight hours.
12 hours.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: A single work permit is issued..
options: only for the work to be undertaken.
for a variety of tasks.
to keep paperwork up-to-date.
to satisfy auditors.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: only for the work to be undertaken.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: When handling oil or waste oil, direct contact should be avoided with the skin by using gloves. What other method can be used to protect the skin?
options: A barrier cream.
A moisturiser cream.
Vaseline.
Talcum powder.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: When are items on the ship/shore safety check list checked when a vessel is at a terminal?
options: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.
Immediately upon berthing and before starting cargo operations.
Upon commencing cargo operations.
During cargo operations.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: The International Shore Fire Connection is used for what purpose?
options: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.
To enable the foam line onboard to be connected to an external foam supply from shore.
To enable carbon dioxide to be used from shore to fight engine room fires.
To enable the ship to assist in extinguishing a fire ashore.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following is the most important way for any company to improve their Safety Management System (SMS)?
options: Receiving constructive feedback and review from the ship's staff.
Receiving criticism from third parties.
Receiving notification of problems by Port State Control.
Receiving information on the introduction of new legislation.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Receiving constructive feedback and review from the ship's staff.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: The Code of Safe Working Practices requires that any faults relating to cargo handling equipment, testing instruments and alarm systems must be..
options: reported immediately.
repaired immediately.
repaired in dry dock.
reported when cargo operations are completed.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Familiarisation of the Safety Management System (SMS) is essential in order to..
options: All of these answers.
ensure that the ship is operated in the safest possible way to avoid injury or damage to the environment.
improve your skills including emergency preparedness.
comply with all the applicable codes, international regulations and best practices.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What should happen to deck scuppers during periods of heavy rain when engaged in cargo or bunker handling?
options: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of an deck oil spill.
Open all deck scuppers to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
All deck scuppers must be kept fully closed at all times and never opened until cargo and bunker operations are completed.
Only deck scuppers on the outboard side of the vessel are to be opened to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of an deck oil spill.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: A company's Safety Management System (SMS) includes the following functional requirements: safety & environmental policy, procedures to ensure the safe operation of the ship, levels of authority amongst ship and shore personnel, procedures to prepare for
options: Procedures for reporting accidents and non-conformities.
Procedures for helicopter operations.
Procedures for training ship's staff.
All of these answers.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Procedures for reporting accidents and non-conformities.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Before cargo or ballast operations commence, the Master (or his representative) and the terminal representative should do what?
options: All three of the above
Agree in writing on the transfer procedures, including the maximum loading or unloading rates
Agree in writing on the action to be taken in the event of an emergency during cargo or ballast handling operations
Complete and sign the Ship/Shore Safety Checklist.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Where does the Code of Safe Working Practices recommend guidance on general precautions be taken from?
options: All of these answers.
The International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals.
Safety in Oil Tankers.
The Company's Safety Management System.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: According to the Code of Safe Working Practices, a Permit-to- Work does not in itself make the job safe but contributes to measures for safe working.
options: True
False

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: What should the ship's Master do if an unauthorised craft comes alongside and attempts to secure to the vessel when at a terminal?
options: Report the craft to the terminal and if necessary stop cargo operations.
Sound the emergency alarm.
Turn fire hoses onto the small craft.
All of these answers.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: Report the craft to the terminal and if necessary stop cargo operations.

CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following statements apply to a storage area where chemicals are kept?
options: It must be kept well ventilated and secure.
It must be located within the engine room workshop only.
It must be stored in the main deck store only.
It must be kept under surveillance by closed circuit television cameras.
CD7030 — TOTS 1B-General Tanker Section.answer: It must be kept well ventilated and secure.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: In practical terms, what figures can be used for the Lower and Upper Flammability Limits of oil tanker cargoes?
options: 1% and 10% of gas.
5% and 50% of gas.
5% and 21% of oxygen.
19% and 21% of oxygen.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of butane?
options: 1.9% by volume in air.
5.9% by volume in air.
9% by volume in air.
19% by volume in air.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by natural gasolines can be represented by those of pentane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of pentane?
options: 1.5% by volume in air.
4.5% by volume in air.
7.8% by volume in air.
21% by volume in air.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, would you consider it to be safe to purge with inert gas with an oxygen content of 8%?
options: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
No, the tank must first be gas freed with fresh air.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by natural gasolines can be represented by those of pentane. What is the relative density of pentane?
Define the "Upper Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of propane?
options: 2.2% by volume in air.
5.2% by volume in air.
10% by volume in air.
22% by volume in air.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the relative density of butane?

After inerting a cargo tank, the oxygen content was found to be 7.5%, and the hydrocarbon gas content 2%. Using the Flammability Diagram, would you consider the tank to be safely inerted before gas freeing?
options: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
No, inerting must be continued.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the relative density of propane?
Explain why the atmosphere in a cargo tank must be sampled at different depths?
options: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: Define the "Lower Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much gas to support and propagate combustion.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, why would it be necessary to dilute the atmosphere to point H with inert gas before gas freeing with fresh air?
options: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.
To help prevent corrosion in the tank.
To reduce the oxygen level to below the critical dilution line.
To increase the hydrocarbon level above the Upper Flammable Limit.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the relative density of hydrocarbon gas at concentrations near the Lower Flammable Limit?
options: Approximately 1.0, the same as air.
Approximately 1.5, heavier than air.
Approximately 0.7, lighter than air.
Approximately 2.0, much heavier than air.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point D?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, what would be the effect of diluting with fresh air?
options: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The oxygen level would be increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point A?
options: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point B?
options: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.

CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point C?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
CD7031 — TOTS 1B-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which an infrared gas detector operates?
options: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.
It compares the electrical resistance of the sample with fresh air.
It measures the resistance of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
It compares the relative density of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must chemical absorption tubes only be used with pumps from the same manufacturer?
options: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.
Because the tubes will not fit correctly into another manufacturer's pump.
Because using different tubes breaks the terms of the contract with the manufacturer.
Because using the wrong tubes may lead to contamination of the pump.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which chemical absorption indicators operate?
options: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.
To sense the proportion of a sample which is absorbed by a catalyst.
To show whether a toxic gas will be absorbed by the human body.
To compare the chemical absorption rate of the sample with fresh air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Pellistor"?
options: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.
It's a balancing resistor between the sensing element and a fixed compensator.
It's a protective device which removes contaminants.
It's a filter which prevents the spread of flame.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instrument should you use to test for very low levels of oxygen before loading a sensitive cargo?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A paramagnetic oxygen analyser.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why is it necessary to use a water-retaining filter in the sample line of an oxygen analyser?
options: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.
Because water in the sample will corrode the internal parts of the instrument.
Because water will build up in the sample line, reducing the flow.
Because water reacts with the measuring cell, giving a false reading.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What effect will inert gas have on the operation of an infrared type gas detector?
options: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.
It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
Small particles may obscure the mirrors.
It will Increase the reading by increasing the temperature of the chamber.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When changing high purity cargo grades, what instrument should be used to ensure that tanks are free of the previous product?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A tankscope.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which a thermal conductivity meter works?
options: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show change in the density of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
To show a change in temperature of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show a change in the conductivity of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Multi-toxic gas detectors normally use electro-chemical detectors. What level of accuracy can be expected?
options: Approximately 1 - 5 ppm..
Approximately 10% by volume.
Approximately 100 - 500 ppm.
Approximately 30% by volume.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1 - 5 ppm..

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must the tank atmosphere be sampled at a variety of positions when testing before entry?
options: To allow for the density of the gas and to ensure that any collected in dead spots is detected.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To allow for the density of the gas and to ensure that any collected in dead spots is detected.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instruments must be provided to comply with the statutory requirements for ships fitted with an inert gas plant?
options: An oxygen analyser and an instrument to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.
An Explosimeter and an oxygen analyser.
At least two instruments to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.
At least two instruments to measure the percentage of oxygen in an inerted atmosphere.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: An oxygen analyser and an instrument to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: After washing and gas-freeing from a toxic cargo, what type of gas detection equipment should you use before entering a cargo tank?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A tankscope.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: For how long must the ventilation of a space be stopped before conducting tests of the atmosphere for an Enclosed Space Entry?
options: 10 minutes.
30 minutes.
The ventilation should be run continuously.
Briefly, while the tests are being carried out.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Sintered Filter", and what is its purpose?
options: It's a flashback arrestor used to prevent flame from escaping from the combustion chamber.
It's an electronic device used to smooth the signal from the sensor.
It's a cotton wad used to prevent water from entering the combustion chamber.
It's a fine metal filter used to prevent contamination of the sensor.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It's a flashback arrestor used to prevent flame from escaping from the combustion chamber.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using an oxygen analyser?
options: Check battery level, reference point with atmospheric air (21%), and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Check battery level, reference point with span gas, and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Check the battery level, and self- test the alarm functions.
Check the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Check battery level, reference point with atmospheric air (21%), and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What property of oxygen is utilised in a paramagnetic oxygen analyser?
options: Oxygen is strongly attracted to a magnetic pole.
The electrical resistance of oxygen changes in a magnetic field.
Oxygen molecules will break up in a magnetic field.
The strength of a magnetic field is reduced in the presence of oxygen.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Oxygen is strongly attracted to a magnetic pole.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using an Explosimeter?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self-testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas, and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What will be the effect of hydrogen sulphide on the reading shown on a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter)?
options: It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
It will give a zero reading by destroying the sensor.
It will increase the reading by raising the sensitivity of the sensor.
It will have no effect because it is non-flammable.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What level of accuracy can be expected when using toxic gas detection tubes?
options: Approximately 1 ppm, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 10%, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 100 ppm, depending on the type of tube in use.
Approximately 30%, depending on the type of tube in use.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1 ppm, depending on the type of tube in use.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of sensor is fitted in a tankscope?
options: A non-catalytic heated filament.
A catalytic filament resistor.
A PT100 temperature sensor.
A magnetic induction sensor.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: A non-catalytic heated filament.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How will leaks in the sampling line affect the operation of portable gas detection equipment?
options: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.
It will cause higher readings due to increased flow rate.
It will cause failure due to low suction pressure.
It will cause failure due to high flow rate.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must the span gas pressure be carefully controlled when calibrating a fixed gas detection system?
options: Excess pressure may damage the catalytic sensing element.
Excess pressure may cause leaks in the system.
Excess pressure may cause errors in the readings.
If the pressure is too high, it could cause an explosion inside the equipment.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Excess pressure may damage the catalytic sensing element.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How will leaks in the sample pipework affect the operation of a fixed gas detection system?
options: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.
It will cause higher readings due to increased flow rate.
It will cause failure due to low suction pressure.
It will cause failure due to high flow rate.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When starting to test a sample using a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter), the needle immediately flicks to maximum deflection, and then returns to zero. What is indicated?
options: That the flammable gas concentration is above the Lower Flammable Limit.
That the battery is incorrectly fitted.
That the instrument was not warmed up, but is now working correctly.
That the sensor element has been contaminated by toxic gas.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: That the flammable gas concentration is above the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using a tankscope?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self-testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using a gascope?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self- testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the composition of the span gas generally used to zero a portable oxygen analyser?
options: High purity nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Fresh air.
Approximately 20% propane in air.
Approximately 2% propane in air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: High purity nitrogen or carbon dioxide.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the gas concentration alarm level on a fixed gas detection system?
options: 30% of Lower Flammable Limit.
10% of flammable gas.
3% of Lower Flammable Limit.
30% of flammable gas.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 30% of Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of sensor is fitted in an Explosimeter?
options: A catalytic filament resistor.
A gas diffusion filter.
A magnetic resonance chamber.
A non-catalytic heated filament.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: A catalytic filament resistor.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: If an Explosimeter is calibrated using span gas containing 1% butane in air, what reading may be expected?
options: Approximately 50% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 10% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 100% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 1% Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 50% Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Cotton filters are sometimes used with hydrocarbon gas detectors. What is their purpose?
options: To remove water from the sample.
To stop pressure surges in the sample line.
To remove dust from the sample.
To prevent chemical contamination of the sample.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To remove water from the sample.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: A fixed gas detection system for toxic gas normally uses electro-chemical detectors. What level of accuracy can be expected?
options: Approximately 5 ppm.
Approximately 10 % by volume.
Approximately 50 ppm.
Approximately 30 % by volume.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 5 ppm.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Span gas is generally used for calibration of a fixed gas detection system. What is the composition of this gas?
options: Approximately 1% butane in air.
Pure nitrogen.
A proprietary mixture of nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
Approximately 40% propane in air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1% butane in air.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What would you use a personal oxygen meter for?
options: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
For testing an enclosed space before starting hot work.
For checking the atmosphere of a ballast tank before entry.
For testing the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the composition of the span gas generally used for calibration of an Explosimeter?
options: Approximately 1% butane in air.
Pure carbon dioxide.
A proprietary mixture of nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
Approximately 40% propane in air.
CD7032 — TOTS 1B-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1% butane in air.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What is the maximum permitted level of toxic gas for an enclosed space entry?
options: The Occupational Exposure Limit, which varies according to the particular gas.
It varies according to the particular gas, but 1% is an acceptable level.
1% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
10% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The Occupational Exposure Limit, which varies according to the particular gas.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What equipment is required to be kept at the entrance of an enclosed space during entry?
options: A resuscitator, breathing apparatus, a lifeline and a harness, a torch or a lamp.
Spare tools and parts for the work being undertaken.
A resuscitator or escape breathing set.
Enough escape breathing sets for all personnel in the space.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: A resuscitator, breathing apparatus, a lifeline and a harness, a torch or a lamp.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For what purpose would you use a personal gas detector?
options: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
To test an enclosed space before starting hot work.
To check the atmosphere of an enclosed space before entry.
To test the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For what purpose would you use a personal oxygen meter?
options: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
Testing an enclosed space before starting hot work.
To check the atmosphere of an enclosed space before entry.
Testing the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why could an unventilated ballast tank fitted with Cathodic Protection contain a hazardous atmosphere?
options: Because hydrogen is produced by the Cathodic Protection.
Because the Cathodic Protection could produce an oxygen enriched atmosphere.
Because hydrocarbons could be produced by the Cathodic Protection.
Because the Cathodic Protection would increase the level of nitrogen in the atmosphere.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Because hydrogen is produced by the Cathodic Protection.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action should be taken if personnel working in an enclosed space get into difficulties?
options: The general alarm should be sounded and the rescue team should enter using breathing apparatus under the direction of the Person In Charge
All personnel should be instructed to leave the space immediately.
The first person on the scene should immediately enter the space to give assistance.
The Watchman should immediately enter the space to give assistance.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The general alarm should be sounded and the rescue team should enter using breathing apparatus under the direction of the Person In Charge

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Who is required to standby at the entrance of an enclosed space during entry?
options: At least one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside and with the Officer of the Watch.
The Officer of the Watch and one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside.
Nobody, provided the personnel inside are equipped to communicate with the Officer of the Watch.
The Officer of the Watch, or whoever signed the Entry Permit.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: At least one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside and with the Officer of the Watch.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For how long must the ventilation of a space be stopped before conducting tests of the atmosphere for an Enclosed Space Entry?
options: 10 minutes.
30 minutes.
The ventilation should be run continuously.
Briefly, while the tests are being carried out.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How many different locations within a tank should be sampled to test the atmosphere before entering a tank?
options: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.
At least three locations.
In one position, at a minimum of three levels.
As close as possible to the centre of the tank.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why must the enclosed space atmosphere be sampled at a variety of positions?
options: To allow for the denisity of the gas and to check for any gas pockets which may have accumulated in blind spots.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To allow for the denisity of the gas and to check for any gas pockets which may have accumulated in blind spots.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why could an unprotected steel space, which has been closed, produce a hazardous atmosphere?
options: Because oxygen in the atmosphere may be depleted by reacting with the steel (i.e. corrosion).
Because the level of nitrogen in the atmosphere would be increased by corrosion.
Because toxic gases may be given off by the process of corrosion.
Because hydrocarbons could be liberated from rust scale in the tank.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Because oxygen in the atmosphere may be depleted by reacting with the steel (i.e. corrosion).

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What gas detection equipment must be used to test the atmosphere of a cargo tank before entry is permitted?
options: An oxygen meter, a combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
An oxygen meter and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
An oxygen meter and a tankscope.
A combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: An oxygen meter, a combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What indication will be given by an Explosimeter in case of oxygen deficiency?
options: No indication.
Approximately 20% of the Lower Flammable Limit
Full scale deflection.
The indication is erratic and jumpy.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What potential hazards would be caused in a machinery space by the release of carbon dioxide for fire extinguishing purposes?
options: A lack of oxygen.
Carbon dioxide which is toxic to breathe.
Vapour, which may reduce visibility.
The carbon dioxide gas would be very cold, and could cause severe cold damage to the skin.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How many people should be allowed to enter an enclosed space to carry out routine work?
options: Only the number actually required to carry out the work.
The number required to carry out the work, plus one extra watchman.
Only two people.
The number required to carry out the work, plus the person in charge and one extra watchman.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Only the number actually required to carry out the work.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How long should ventilation be continued after the atmosphere of an enclosed space has been found suitable for entry?
options: Continuously while the space is occupied, and even during temporary breaks.
For at least one hour after successful testing.
It can be stopped when testing shows that the space is suitable for entry.
It should be continued after testing until the space is actually entered.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Continuously while the space is occupied, and even during temporary breaks.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What actions must be taken to isolate a tank before entry?
options: Blank off the pipelines to the tank, close and secure all valves and inform the Officer of the Watch.
Request the Officer of the Watch to stop all cargo and ballast pumps.
Stop all cargo and ballast operations.
Stop all ventilation and inform the Officer of the Watch.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Blank off the pipelines to the tank, close and secure all valves and inform the Officer of the Watch.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action must be taken when an enclosed space entry permit expires?
options: The space must be vacated and closed.
The work must be completed as soon as possible.
Work can continue until it has been completed.
Additional crew should attend for assistance.
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The space must be vacated and closed.

CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action must be taken if the presence of a toxic gas is suspected for which no specific testing equipment is available?
options: Treat the space as unsafe and follow the procedures according to COSWP 17.11.
Only allow entry after further ventilation.
Test using an Explosimeter, and allow any necessary conversion factors.
Test the space for a similar gas using any available equipment, following the procedures according to COSWP 17.6
CD7033 — TOTS 1B-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Treat the space as unsafe and follow the procedures according to COSWP 17.11.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is a "Class B" fire?
options: Fires involving flammable and combustible hydrocarbon liquids.
Fires involving solid material.
Fires that are not so important.
The type of bulkhead the fire can penetrate.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Fires involving flammable and combustible hydrocarbon liquids.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: When is high expansion foam most effective?
options: When rapid filling of an enclosed space is required.
When the cargo manifold is on fire.
When it is to be used as bridge front cooling.
Generally anywhere on deck.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: When rapid filling of an enclosed space is required.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: Low expansion foam is most effective extinguishing..
options: most hydrocarbon liquid fires.
cabin fires.
main switchboard fires.
ballast tank fires.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is a schematic drawing?
options: A drawing in the form of a diagram and not to scale.
An exact technical drawing.
An approximate drawing.
The general arrangement plan.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: A drawing in the form of a diagram and not to scale.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is carbon dioxide a good medium to fight an electrical fire?
options: Because it is a non-conductor.
Because you can smell it.
Because it has a cooling effect.
Because it generates static electricity.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is the name of the diagram that is superimposed on the cargo control console?
options: The mimic diagram.
The tank plan.
The cargo lines.
The pumping plan.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you expect to locate a mimic diagram of the cargo system?
options: In the cargo control room (CCR) operational panel.
In the Chief Engineer's office.
At the manifold.
Adjacent to the bunkering manifold.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In the cargo control room (CCR) operational panel.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: The principle purpose of a pre-cargo transfer meeting is to..
options: ensure that all involved personnel are aware of the proposed cargo operations, services needed and safety requirements.
inform the technical officers when cargo pumps will be required.
arrange shore leave.
discuss the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: ensure that all involved personnel are aware of the proposed cargo operations, services needed and safety requirements.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: On what occasions will a pre-cargo transfer meeting be minuted?
options: On each and every occasion.
When there is something special to say.
When the Captain attends.
Whenever the port stay is estimated to be greater than 24 hours.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Ship / Shore Safety Check List states that temporarily removed scupper plugs must be..
options: constantly monitored.
stowed in a safe place.
clearly labelled as to location.
only removed by the person responsible for cargo operations.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: During cargo transfer, what action would you take if the Inert Gas System fails?
options: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.
Increase the rate of discharge.
Advise the terminal and continue discharging.
Review the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.

CD7034 — TOTS 1B-Familiarisation prior C.question: A Ship to Shore Safety Checklist can be found in which publication?
options: ISGOTT.
ISPS code.
SOPEP.
The Mariner's Handbook.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Why would a vessel be in possession of an NLS (Noxious Liquid Substances) certificate?
options: It's required for any vessel carrying a MARPOL Annex II cargo that does not have a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Chemicals.
The certificate is required when carrying liquid petroleum gas.
The certificate is required on a petroleum product tanker.
The certificate is not mandatory and would usually be kept by the owner.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: It's required for any vessel carrying a MARPOL Annex II cargo that does not have a Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Chemicals.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: When wearing the EEBD how do you support the air bottle?
options: With a strap around the neck supported on the chest
You carry it under your arm.
You strap it to your back.
You put the air bottle into your chemical suit pocket.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: With a strap around the neck supported on the chest

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the goggles on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.
They must be lightweight.
They must have 2 headbands for extra safety.
Nothing in particular, chipping goggles are adequate
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the lifeline and belt that form part of the safety equipment on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: The line and belt must be fireproof and resistant to the cargo being carried.
They must always be orange in colour.
The length of the lifeline must be at least double the tankers moulded depth.
The equipment must be inspected at least annually.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The line and belt must be fireproof and resistant to the cargo being carried.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is essential for an oxygen/air resuscitator to operate efficiently?
options: The casualty's airway must be clear.
The casualty must be unconscious.
The casualty must weigh over 90 KG.
The casualty must not have facial hair.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The casualty's airway must be clear.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the common name for a Personal Escape Set?
options: EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device).
ELSA set.
Self Contained Breathing Apparatus.
A resuscitator.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the minimum air duration for an EEBD?
options: 10 minutes.
15 minutes.
It depends on the type of tanker.
As per the vessels Safety Management System.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What would you do if you looked down a cargo tank and saw a colleague apparently unconscious?
options: Raise the alarm and wait for assistance.
Immediately enter the tank to give first aid.
Don breathing apparatus and enter the tank.
Look at the permit to see who is down the tank.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: Raise the alarm and wait for assistance.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the inspection criteria for breathing apparatus on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: A monthly inspection by a responsible officer and annual inspection and testing at an approved facility.
A weekly inspection by the 3rd officer.
The Chief Engineer inspects all the apparatus monthly.
It should be inspected by a class surveyor annually.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A monthly inspection by a responsible officer and annual inspection and testing at an approved facility.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: According to the IBC code where should in use protective equipment be stowed?
options: In special lockers in easy accessible places.
In the accommodation.
At the top of the pumproom.
At the forecastle head.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: In special lockers in easy accessible places.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Why is the first 0 to 4 minutes critical for the casualty?
options: After this time permanent brain damage may occur even if the casualty survives.
It gives the rescuers some time to get organised.
The casualty will always survive if oxygen is given within this time frame.
The casualty will always die if oxygen is given after this time frame.
CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: After this time permanent brain damage may occur even if the casualty survives.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Who has the responsibility to ensure the correct health hazard information is passed to the vessel?
options: The supplier of the cargo.
The ship broker.
The ship owner.
MARPOL inspectors.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is cargo ingestion?
options: Cargo being swallowed.
Cargo vapours being inhaled.
Cargo having contact with the skin.
Cargo having contact with the eyes.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Where would you find information on the cargo to be loaded relating to health hazards?
options: The MSDS (Material Safety data Sheets).
The World Health organisation.
The Ship Captain's Medical Guide.
SOLAS consolidated edition.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: The cargo being loaded is described as having highly toxic vapour. What must be worn on the cargo deck?
options: Breathing apparatus.
A dust mask.
Rubber gloves.
A face shield.

CD7035 — TOTS 1B-Cargo Information, Prec.question: On a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances, what is the minimum number of protective equipment sets that must be carried?
options: At least three.
Two.
One, provided it's the one that's required by SOLAS.
