They have a south-easterly direction and mainly a variable wind speed of above force 6.
They have a north-easterly direction and mainly a variable wind speed of above force 6.
They have a north-easterly direction and a steady average wind speed of force 4 to 5
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: They have a south-easterly direction and a steady average wind speed of force 4 to 5

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the "navigable semicircle" of a tropical storm in the Northern hemisphere?
options: The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the starboard side of the cyclone path and its eye
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is 250 Nm aft of the eye of the storm directly behind her path
The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is at least 80 Nm aft of the eye of the storm behind on her path
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: The navigable semicircle is the section of the tropical cyclone that is on the port side of the cyclone path and its eye

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the first principle for successful passage through the ice?
options: To maintain freedom of manoeuvre.
To maintain radio watch in order to receive all ice reports and information.
To stay out of the ice as much as possible.
To sail through the ice during the day only.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: To maintain freedom of manoeuvre.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the difference between hurricanes and typhoons?
options: A hurricane develops in the Atlantic or East Pacific while Typhoons develop in the West Pacific.
A hurricane is a storm with winds of over 64 knots and a typhoon is between 48 and 56 knots.
A hurricane develops in the western Pacific and a typhoon in the central and eastern Pacific.
A hurricane is a tropical storm and a typhoon is a storm of the mid-latitudes (above 40 degrees).
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: A hurricane develops in the Atlantic or East Pacific while Typhoons develop in the West Pacific.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: Why should the Master regulate the ship's speed in heavy weather?
options: All three answers.
To avoid the possibility of damage to the ship.
To avoid the possibility of damage to the cargo.
To prevent needless expenditure of fuel.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the first basic ship-handling rule in ice concentrations?
options: Keep moving, even if very slowly.
Try to avoid icing of the ship's superstructure.
Try to keep the vessel sailing only after the icebreakers.
Try to keep the vessel sailing only in convoys through the ice.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: Keep moving, even if very slowly.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term the "wind is backing"?
options: It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).
It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).
It's a change of direction in the wind from ahead to astern.
It's a change of direction in the wind from  astern to ahead.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: Where can the Master or Officer of the Watch find details regarding ice reporting schemes and the radio stations transmitting them?
options: In the Admiralty List of Radio Signals, Volume 3.
In the Mariner's Handbook.
In the Company SMS manuals.
In the Bridge Procedures Guide.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: In the Admiralty List of Radio Signals, Volume 3.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What precautions should be carried out on deck before encountering heavy weather?
options: All loose objects and equipment should be secured.
All crew should be given heavy weather clothing, including raincoats and boots.
All crew should be instructed not to leave their cabins.
All equipment should be greased.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All loose objects and equipment should be secured.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What warnings and instructions should be given before the vessel encounters heavy weather?
options: All three answers.
Warning and instructions should be issued to the crew on deck access.
Warning and instructions should be issued to the engine room crew.
Instructions to rig safety lines where necessary.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: All three answers.

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the Master required to do by SOLAS when his ship encounters dangerous ice?
options: He is required to communicate the fact to all ships in the vicinity by all means available
He is required to stop his ship and communicate with the nearest coastal state.
He is required to communicate the fact to his DPA
He is required to exhibit lights and shapes declaring that his vessel is restricted in her ability to maneouvre.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: He is required to communicate the fact to all ships in the vicinity by all means available

CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.question: What is the meaning of the term the "wind is veering"?
options: It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).
It's an anticlockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northwest to west to southwest).
It's a change of direction in the wind from  astern to ahead.
It's a change of direction in the wind from ahead to astern.
CD7046 — TOTS 1C-Heavy Weather Navigatio.answer: It's a clockwise change in the direction of the wind (i.e. from northeast to east to southeast).

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What would be the minimum recommended firefighting equipment to have available when alongside a terminal?
options: Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles run out forward, aft and adjacent to the manifold in use. Also a dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold.
One fire hose and one dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles or fire extinguishers adjacent to the manifold in use.
Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles forward and aft of the manifold and a fire blanket adjacent to the manifold in use.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Fire hoses with spray/jet nozzles run out forward, aft and adjacent to the manifold in use. Also a dry chemical extinguisher near the manifold.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What is the correct method of closing off unused cargo and bunker connections?
options: All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and are to be fully bolted.
All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and have every second bolt secured by a nut.
Unused connections may be left unblanked so long as two valve separation exists between the connection and the line in use.
Unused connections on the shore-side of the vessel must be closed and fully blanked. The offshore-side may be left unblanked.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: All unused connections must be closed and blanked. Blank flanges are fitted and are to be fully bolted.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: When are items on the ship/shore safety check list checked when a vessel is at a terminal?
options: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.
Immediately upon berthing and before starting cargo operations.
Upon commencing cargo operations.
During cargo operations.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Before cargo or ballast operations commence and then at regular intervals until hoses are disconnected.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Where should the ship's emergency fire control plans be located?
options: In a prominently marked weather-tight enclosure outside the accommodation block.
With the Deck Officer of the Watch at all times.
In a prominently marked wallet contained within the cargo control room.
At the bottom of the gangway.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: In a prominently marked weather-tight enclosure outside the accommodation block.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Hazardous materials such as chemicals and oil will have a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) available. Which of the following is NOT likely to be included in a MSDS?
options: The name of the vessel.
The physical data (e.g. the flashpoint).
The health effects.
The correct storage.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: The name of the vessel.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: The International Shore Fire Connection is used for what purpose?
options: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.
To enable the foam line onboard to be connected to an external foam supply from shore.
To enable carbon dioxide to be used from shore to fight engine room fires.
To enable the ship to assist in extinguishing a fire ashore.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: To enable the water fire main onboard to be connected to an external water supply from shore.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What should happen to deck scuppers during periods of heavy rain when engaged in cargo or bunker handling?
options: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of an deck oil spill.
Open all deck scuppers to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
All deck scuppers must be kept fully closed at all times and never opened until cargo and bunker operations are completed.
Only deck scuppers on the outboard side of the vessel are to be opened to release the rain water. When the rain stops, the scuppers can then be replugged.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: One or two scuppers may be opened temporarily to allow rain water to escape but must be closed as soon as possible and in the event of an deck oil spill.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Critical Operations Check Lists are to be used for what purpose?
options: To ensure that critical equipment is operated, started or restarted correctly so that it will not result in a hazardous situation developing or compromise critical functions.
To ensure that every item of equipment on board is operated according to the manufacturer's instructions.
To ensure that all company procedures are followed at all times.
To ensure that the vessel passes external ISM audits by showing the auditor that Section 10 of the ISM Code is fully complied with.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: To ensure that critical equipment is operated, started or restarted correctly so that it will not result in a hazardous situation developing or compromise critical functions.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items may NOT be considered a critical operation?
options: Switching on the radar.
Starting the emergency generator.
Changing over from heavy fuel to diesel.
Lowering and raising lifeboats.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Switching on the radar.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items can be described as critical machinery?
options: All of these answers.
The main engine.
Generators.
Steering gear.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: All of these answers.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: When handling oil or waste oil, direct contact should be avoided with the skin by using gloves. What other method can be used to protect the skin?
options: A barrier cream.
A moisturiser cream.
Vaseline.
Talcum powder.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: A barrier cream.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Shipboard management meetings should not be used for what purpose?
options: As a non-constructive platform for complaining to shore management about various issues.
As a structured discussion between members of the shipboard management team relating to the safe and efficient operation of the ship.
As a method of relaying information concerning the safe and efficient operation to shore management.
As a constructive method of raising concerns with shore management about activities affecting the safe and efficient operation of the ship.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: As a non-constructive platform for complaining to shore management about various issues.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Before cargo or ballast operations commence, the Master (or his representative) and the terminal representative should do what?
options: All three of the above
Agree in writing on the transfer procedures, including the maximum loading or unloading rates
Agree in writing on the action to be taken in the event of an emergency during cargo or ballast handling operations
Complete and sign the Ship/Shore Safety Checklist.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: All three of the above

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What happens to a Permit-to-Work upon completion of work?
options: It is cancelled by the responsible officer.
It is cancelled by the person carrying out the work.
It is left in place in case further work has to be carried out.
It is transferred to another location where similar work is to be carried out.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: It is cancelled by the responsible officer.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Persons can conduct safety inspections of areas outside of their direct control (e.g. the Chief Officer inspecting the engine room).
options: True
False
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: True

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following items of equipment would be found in a chemical storage/handling area?
options: Safety goggles.
Safety shoes.
A dust mask.
Ear plugs.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Safety goggles.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following questions could be included in the Safety Officer's Inspection Check List?
options: All of these questions.
Are all openings through which a person could fall suitably fenced?
Is protective equipment and clothing in good condition and being used correctly?
Does the crew in the area have any safety suggestions to make?
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: All of these questions.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: A Permit-to-Work should specify the period of validity. According to the Code of Safe Working Practices, this period should not exceed how many hours?
options: 24 hours.
Six hours.
Eight hours.
12 hours.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: 24 hours.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: A single work permit is issued..
options: only for the work to be undertaken.
for a variety of tasks.
to keep paperwork up-to-date.
to satisfy auditors.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: only for the work to be undertaken.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What should you do if you notice a serious safety deficiency when on board?
options: Report it to a senior officer or the Safety Officer and then ensure steps are taken to rectify the problem without delay.
Ignore it.
Make a note of the problem and then inform the Safety Committee at the next Safety Meeting.
Attempt to rectify the defect on your own.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Report it to a senior officer or the Safety Officer and then ensure steps are taken to rectify the problem without delay.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: What should the Company do with accident and incident reports after they are sent from the ship to the office?
options: Closely examine and analyse them so as to determine the root causes or management failures, then investigate methods on how to avoid a similar accident.
Closely examine and analyse them to determine who is to blame on board the ship and take the relevant disciplinary action.
Closely examine and analyse them so as to determine the direct causes of the accident or incident.
Thank the vessel for the time taken to complete the accident/incident form and then file the report away for future reference.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Closely examine and analyse them so as to determine the root causes or management failures, then investigate methods on how to avoid a similar accident.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: The Code of Safe Working Practices requires that any faults relating to cargo handling equipment, testing instruments and alarm systems must be..
options: reported immediately.
repaired immediately.
repaired in dry dock.
reported when cargo operations are completed.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: reported immediately.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following is NOT likely to be an agenda item in a safety committee meeting?
options: Vessel performance.
Safety equipment under repair.
Emergency / pollution drills conducted.
Matters outstanding from the previous meeting.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Vessel performance.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following statements reflects the importance of near-miss reporting?
options: Lessons can be learned from near misses and by analysing them, steps can be put in place to avoid accidents occurring in the future.
The Company has set targets to meet and the number of near misses sent in is essential to meet those targets.
If a ship reports very few near misses, the Company will be under the impression that the ship is operating safely.
If a ship reports many near misses, the Company will consider that the ship is operating safely.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: Lessons can be learned from near misses and by analysing them, steps can be put in place to avoid accidents occurring in the future.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Where does the Code of Safe Working Practices recommend guidance on general precautions be taken from?
options: All of these answers.
The International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals.
Safety in Oil Tankers.
The Company's Safety Management System.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: All of these answers.

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: According to the Code of Safe Working Practices, a Permit-to- Work does not in itself make the job safe but contributes to measures for safe working.
options: True
False
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: True

CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.question: Which of the following statements apply to a storage area where chemicals are kept?
options: It must be kept well ventilated and secure.
It must be located within the engine room workshop only.
It must be stored in the main deck store only.
It must be kept under surveillance by closed circuit television cameras.
CD7047 — TOTS 1C-General Tanker Section.answer: It must be kept well ventilated and secure.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: If cargo tank openings are opened frequently for operations such as sampling and dipping, inert gas quality may be affected. How so?
options: Air could enter the tanks through the openings.
Inert gas would escape, lowering the tank pressure.
Moisture from the atmosphere could enter the tank.
The hydrocarbon content of the tank atmosphere would be increased.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air could enter the tanks through the openings.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Define the "Upper Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Define the "Lower Flammable Limit" of a hydrocarbon gas?
options: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is not sufficient air to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient oxygen to support and propagate combustion.
It is the gas concentration above which there is too much gas to support and propagate combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: It is the gas concentration below which there is not sufficient gas to support and propagate combustion.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Pressure in the cargo tanks may be reduced due to low night time temperatures. How could this affect inert gas quality?
options: Air could be drawn into the system.
The rate of evolution of cargo vapours could be increased.
Components of the inert gas may break down at low pressure.
The inert gas may condense into the cargo at low temperatures.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air could be drawn into the system.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: In practical terms, what figures can be used for the Lower and Upper Flammability Limits of oil tanker cargoes?
options: 1% and 10% of gas.
5% and 50% of gas.
5% and 21% of oxygen.
19% and 21% of oxygen.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1% and 10% of gas.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Gas detection equipment showed the oxygen content of a cargo tank to be 3%, and the hydrocarbon gas content 8%. Using the Flammability Diagram estimate whether it is safe to gas free the tank with fresh air?
options: No the tank must first be purged with inert gas.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: No the tank must first be purged with inert gas.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the relative density of propane?
With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, what would be the effect of diluting with fresh air?
options: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The oxygen level would be increased, resulting in a safe tank atmosphere.
The hydrocarbon concentration would be increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon concentration would be reduced, and the oxygen level increased, taking the atmosphere into the Flammable Range.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, why would it be necessary to dilute the atmosphere to point H with inert gas before gas freeing with fresh air?
options: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.
To help prevent corrosion in the tank.
To reduce the oxygen level to below the critical dilution line.
To increase the hydrocarbon level above the Upper Flammable Limit.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To reduce the hydrocarbon level below the critical dilution line.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: After inerting a cargo tank, the oxygen content was found to be 7.5%, and the hydrocarbon gas content 2%. Using the Flammability Diagram, would you consider the tank to be safely inerted before gas freeing?
options: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
No, inerting must be continued.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere is below the critical dilution line.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Gas detection equipment showed the oxygen content of a cargo tank to be 2%, and the hydrocarbon gas content to be 2%. Using the Flammability Diagram, is it safe to gas free the tank with fresh air?
options: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
No the tank must first be purged with inert gas.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: A gas turbine with afterburner will produce similar inert gas to an independent inert gas generator. What level of oxygen might typically be delivered?
options: 1.5-2.5% by volume.
5% by volume.
8-10% by volume.
Approximately 12% by volume.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.5-2.5% by volume.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is meant by the "Dilution" method of inerting a cargo tank?
options: The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is mixed with fresh air, and introduced rapidly into the tank.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the bottom of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point H, would you consider it to be safe to gas free using fresh air?
options: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
No, the tank must first be purged with inert gas.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the relative density of butane?
What is meant by the "Displacement" method of inerting cargo tanks?
options: The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is introduced slowly at the bottom of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.
The inert gas is mixed with fresh air, and introduced rapidly into the tank.
The incoming inert gas is mixed with the tank atmosphere to form a homogenous mixture throughout the tank.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank so that a stable horizontal interface is formed.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Why is an oxygen content of not more than 8% considered to be the safe limit in a cargo tank atmosphere?
options: Because the atmosphere is safely outside the Flammable Range.
Because 8% hydrocarbon gas is below the Lower Flammable Limit.
Because 8% hydrocarbon gas is above the Upper Flammable Limit.
Because the tank atmosphere was outside the Flammable Range at the time the readings were taken.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the atmosphere is safely outside the Flammable Range.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, if a cargo tank atmosphere was at point F, would you consider it to be safe to gas free the tank with fresh air?
options: No, the tank must first be purged with inert gas.
No, the tank atmosphere is in the Flammable Range.
Yes, the atmosphere would remain outside the Flammable Range.
Yes, the tank atmosphere would remain too rich to support combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: No, the tank must first be purged with inert gas.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what point on the diagram shows a hydrocarbon concentration at its Lower Flammable Limit, with no inert gas?
options: Point C.
Point A.
Point G.
Point D.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Point C.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the maximum oxygen content which should be maintained in a cargo tank during operations?
options: Not more than 8%, except when gas freeing.
Not more than 1%, except when gas freeing.
Not more than 18%, except when loading.
Not more than 21%, except when loading.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Not more than 8%, except when gas freeing.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Displacement" method of inerting cargo tanks, inert gas is introduced slowly at the top of the tank. Why?
options: Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the inert gas is hotter than the tank atmosphere and it is necessary to avoid violent mixing.
Because inert gas is denser than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the incoming inert gas will mix with the tank atmosphere throughout the tank.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: The characteristics of the vapours given off by natural gasolines can be represented by those of pentane. What is the relative density of pentane?
What are the main components of inert gas delivered from a flue gas plant?
options: Nitrogen 83%, Carbon Dioxide 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%
Nitrogen 60%, Carbon Dioxide 30%, Oxygen 10%
Carbon Dioxide 83%, Nitrogen 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%
Carbon Dioxide 63%, Nitrogen 22-24%, Oxygen 10-12%
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Nitrogen 83%, Carbon Dioxide 12-14%, Oxygen 2-4%

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Dilution" method of inerting, it is essential that only a small number of cargo tanks are open. Why?
options: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because the inert gas plant works more efficiently when the back pressure is higher.
Because it is difficult to monitor the hydrocarbon levels properly if a large number of tanks are open.
Because the incoming inert gas must form a stable interface with the tank atmosphere.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point D?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what point on the diagram shows a hydrocarbon concentration at its Upper Flammable Limit, with no inert gas?
options: Point D.
Point A.
Point C.
Point G.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Point D.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Dilution" method of inerting a cargo tank, inert gas is introduced rapidly into the tank. Why?
options: Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because inert gas is slightly less dense than hydrocarbon vapour, and a stable horizontal interface can be formed.
Because the inert gas is hotter than the tank atmosphere, and it is necessary to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and form a stable interface.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the incoming inert gas must have enough velocity to reach the bottom of the tank and mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What oxygen content would normally be expected from an independent inert gas generator?
options: 1.5-2.5% by volume.
5% by volume.
8-10% by volume.
Approximately 12% by volume.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 1.5-2.5% by volume.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the relative density of hydrocarbon gas at concentrations near the Lower Flammable Limit?
options: Approximately 1.0, the same as air.
Approximately 1.5, heavier than air.
Approximately 0.7, lighter than air.
Approximately 2.0, much heavier than air.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Approximately 1.0, the same as air.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the operating principle of a dry type deck seal in an inert gas system?
options: A dump valve is fitted, which opens, filling the lower chamber with water to form a seal when the inert gas supply stops.
A large diameter non-return valve is fitted, which will close when the inert gas supply stops.
The chamber is drained when the inert gas plant is prepared for operation, but can be filled with water when the plant is not in use, forming a seal.
The chamber contains a number of baffles which prevent solid materials from entering the cargo tanks, and help regulate the pressure of the inert gas main line.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: A dump valve is fitted, which opens, filling the lower chamber with water to form a seal when the inert gas supply stops.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point A?
options: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank contains fresh air, with no hydrocarbon gas, and cannot support combustion.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the purpose of the deck water seal in an inert gas system?
options: To prevent cargo liquid or vapour from entering the engine room.
To cool the inert gas before delivery to the tanks.
To clean the inert gas before delivery to the tanks.
To regulate the pressure of the inert gas main line, and help prevent over-pressurisation of the tanks.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: To prevent cargo liquid or vapour from entering the engine room.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the maximum oxygen content allowed by SOLAS in the output from an inert gas plant?
options: Not more than 5%.
Not more than 1%.
Not more than 8%.
Not more than 21%.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Not more than 5%.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What inert gas monitoring instrumentation must be fitted in the cargo control room of a tanker?
options: Instruments to continuously indicate and permanently record the oxygen content and deck main pressure.
A device to permanently record the times of stopping and starting the inert gas plant.
Instrumentation showing the cargo tank temperature and pressure.
Instrumentation showing all operating parameters of the inert gas plant.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Instruments to continuously indicate and permanently record the oxygen content and deck main pressure.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: At high concentrations, hydrocarbon gas has a high relative density. How will this affect the sampling procedure?
options: The atmosphere must be sampled at different depths, because the gas tends to layer and form pockets.
Gas content readings may be inaccurate due to the higher density.
It may be impossible to obtain samples from the bottom of the tank because the gas is too heavy.
Air may be drawn into the sample line, giving a false reading.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The atmosphere must be sampled at different depths, because the gas tends to layer and form pockets.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point B?
options: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The tank atmosphere is too lean to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: With reference to the Flammability Diagram, what conditions are shown at point C?
options: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere is too rich to support combustion.
The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Upper Flammable Limit.
The tank atmosphere contains no oxygen, and cannot support combustion.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The hydrocarbon gas concentration is at its Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Explain why the atmosphere in a cargo tank must be sampled at different depths?
options: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Due to the high relative density of hydrocarbon gas, it tends to layer, and collect in pockets.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: When using the "Displacement" method of inerting, it is common practice to inert several tanks at the same time. Why?
options: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a slow enough rate to enable the formation of a stable horizontal interface.
Because the inert gas plant works more efficiently when the back pressure is lower.
Because it is easier to compare the hydrocarbon levels in the tanks if a large number are open.
Because the inert gas must be introduced at a high enough rate to mix thoroughly with the tank atmosphere.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Because the inert gas must be introduced at a slow enough rate to enable the formation of a stable horizontal interface.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What are the main factors which could cause over-pressurisation of a cargo tank?
options: All three anwers
Inadequate venting arrangements or overfilling the tank.
Pump failure during discharge.
Excessively high delivery pressure from the inert gas plant or shore delivery supply
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: All three anwers

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What adverse results may occur if cargo tanks are allowed to become over-pressurised?
options: Major deformation or failure of the tank structure could occur, leading to explosion, fire or pollution.
There could be leakage of cargo and vent pipelines.
There could be a loss of cargo due to excessive venting.
There could be difficulty continuing the loading operation due to high pressure.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Major deformation or failure of the tank structure could occur, leading to explosion, fire or pollution.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What action must be taken if the inert gas plant fails during cargo discharge operations?
options: You should prevent air from entering the tanks, and stop discharge from inerted tanks.
You should reduce the discharge rate until the plant is repaired.
You should continue discharge, monitoring oxygen and gas concentration in the cargo tanks.
You should carefully allow fresh air into the tanks to prevent under-pressurisation.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: You should prevent air from entering the tanks, and stop discharge from inerted tanks.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Explain how very cold weather conditions can cause over-pressurisation of cargo tanks?
options: Ice could form on the vents, or the P/V or high velocity vent valves could freeze.
Low temperatures will increase the viscosity of the cargo, and may make it unpumpable.
Cold weather may cause malfunctioning of cargo monitoring equipment, including pressure monitors.
The increased density of the cargo could lead to overloading.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Ice could form on the vents, or the P/V or high velocity vent valves could freeze.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: In addition to the manufacturer's tests of the inert gas plant, what other checks must be performed before inerting operations?
options: Checks of the fixed and portable oxygen meters and gas detectors.
A pressure test of the cargo and inert gas pipework.
An inspection of the cargo tanks.
A test of the crude oil washing system, if fitted.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Checks of the fixed and portable oxygen meters and gas detectors.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: Inert gas quality in slop tanks may be degraded when tank washings from non-inerted tanks are added: Why?
options: Air would be trapped in the washings, particularly if an eductor was in use.
The turbulence in the slops caused by adding washings would result in increased evolution of hydrocarbon vapours.
The higher temperature of the slops caused by adding washings would result in increased evolution of hydrocarbon vapours.
Adding washings would increase the pressure in the tank, forcing inert gas out via the vent line.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: Air would be trapped in the washings, particularly if an eductor was in use.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What is the minimum recommended pressure for cargo tanks connected with an inert gas main?
options: 100 mm water gauge.
500 mm water gauge
One bar.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: 100 mm water gauge.

CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.question: What action should be taken if the pressure in inerted cargo tanks falls to the low pressure alarm level during a ballast passage?
options: The inert gas plant should be used to top up the tanks, and the oxygen content should be less than 5%.
The P/V valve will take care of fluctuations in the tank pressure.
If the tanks are not loaded, they can be opened to atmosphere to prevent under-pressurisation.
The tanks should be gas freed.
CD7048 — TOTS 1C-The Flammability Diagra.answer: The inert gas plant should be used to top up the tanks, and the oxygen content should be less than 5%.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How many different locations within a tank should be sampled to test the atmosphere before entering a tank?
options: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.
At least three.
In one position, at a minimum of three levels.
As close as possible to the centre of the tank.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must the tank atmosphere be sampled at a variety of positions when testing before entry?
options: To allow for the density of the gas and to ensure that any collected in dead spots is detected.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To allow for the density of the gas and to ensure that any collected in dead spots is detected.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using an Explosimeter?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self-testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas, and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Some chemical gases will not be detected by a fixed combustible gas detection system. How does this restrict the use of the system?
options: The system cannot be used to assess the level of toxic gas.
The flammability readings may be unreliable.
The system cannot be used under very cold conditions.
The system cannot be used if the ship is carrying chemicals.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: The system cannot be used to assess the level of toxic gas.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: A fixed combustible gas detection system can only detect a limited range of substances. What are these substances?
options: Hydrocarbon gases up to the Lower Flammable Limit.
Chemical gases up to 100%.
Smoke and combustion products.
Oxygen content up to 21%..
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Hydrocarbon gases up to the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Sintered Filter", and what is its purpose?
options: It's a flashback arrestor used to prevent flame from escaping from the combustion chamber.
It's an electronic device used to smooth the signal from the sensor.
It's a cotton wad used to prevent water from entering the combustion chamber.
It's a fine metal filter used to prevent contamination of the sensor.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It's a flashback arrestor used to prevent flame from escaping from the combustion chamber.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What property of oxygen is utilised in a paramagnetic oxygen analyser?
options: Oxygen is strongly attracted to a magnetic pole.
The electrical resistance of oxygen changes in a magnetic field.
Oxygen molecules will break up in a magnetic field.
The strength of a magnetic field is reduced in the presence of oxygen.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Oxygen is strongly attracted to a magnetic pole.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using an oxygen analyser?
options: Check battery level, reference point with atmospheric air (21%), and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Check battery level, reference point with span gas, and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Check the battery level, and self- test the alarm functions.
Check the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Check battery level, reference point with atmospheric air (21%), and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why must chemical absorption tubes only be used with pumps from the same manufacturer?
options: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.
Because the tubes will not fit correctly into another manufacturer's pump.
Because using different tubes breaks the terms of the contract with the manufacturer.
Because using the wrong tubes may lead to contamination of the pump.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because the pump and tube are matched to ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is tested.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Span gas is generally used for calibration of a fixed gas detection system. What is the composition of this gas?
options: Approximately 1% butane in air.
Pure nitrogen.
A proprietary mixture of nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
Approximately 40% propane in air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1% butane in air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How will leaks in the sample pipework affect the operation of a fixed gas detection system?
options: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.
It will cause higher readings due to increased flow rate.
It will cause failure due to low suction pressure.
It will cause failure due to high flow rate.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When using chemical absorption tubes, why must you use the exact number of pump strokes specified in the instructions?
options: To ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is passed through the tube.
So that the results of all your tests are based on the same data.
Because all tubes require the same number of strokes.
It is not necessary to use the exact number stated, it is only for general guidance.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To ensure that the correct volume of sample gas is passed through the tube.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why is it necessary to use a water-retaining filter in the sample line of an oxygen analyser?
options: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.
Because water in the sample will corrode the internal parts of the instrument.
Because water will build up in the sample line, reducing the flow.
Because water reacts with the measuring cell, giving a false reading.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because water vapour in the sample will cause damage to the measuring cell.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: After washing and gas-freeing from a toxic cargo, what type of gas detection equipment should you use before entering a cargo tank?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A tankscope.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What equipment is required to test an enclosed space for the presence of toxic gas before entry?
options: Chemical absorption tubes.
An Explosimeter.
An oxygen meter.
A tankscope.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical absorption tubes.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What effect will inert gas have on the operation of an infrared type gas detector?
options: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.
It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
Small particles may obscure the mirrors.
It will Increase the reading by increasing the temperature of the chamber.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: None. The instrument is not affected by the absence of oxygen.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which an infrared gas detector operates?
options: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.
It compares the electrical resistance of the sample with fresh air.
It measures the resistance of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
It compares the relative density of a sample which has been heated by an infrared source.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It senses the level of absorption of infrared radiation in the sample.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: An Explosimeter cannot be used in an inerted atmosphere. Why not?
options: Because adequate oxygen is required for combustion of the filament.
Because the inert gas poisons the filament.
Because the presence of carbon dioxide will increase the readings.
Because small particles will clog the filters.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because adequate oxygen is required for combustion of the filament.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of gas detection equipment should you use to test the atmosphere before starting hot work?
options: A Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter).
An oxygen analyser.
A toxic gas meter.
A personal gas detector.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: A Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter).

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by clean products such as motor or aviation gasoline can be represented by those of butane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of butane?
options: 1.9% by volume in air.
5.9% by volume in air.
9% by volume in air.
19% by volume in air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 1.9% by volume in air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: The flammable limits for the vapours given off by crude oil can be represented by those of propane. What is the Lower Flammable Limit of propane?
options: 2.2% by volume in air.
5.2% by volume in air.
10% by volume in air.
22% by volume in air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 2.2% by volume in air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When changing high purity cargo grades, what instrument should be used to ensure that tanks are free of the previous product?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A tankscope.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What range of flammable gas can be detected by a catalytic resistance detector?
options: 0-100% Lower Flammable Limit.
0-10% Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 0-100% Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which chemical absorption indicators operate?
options: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.
To sense the proportion of a sample which is absorbed by a catalyst.
To show whether a toxic gas will be absorbed by the human body.
To compare the chemical absorption rate of the sample with fresh air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: By passing the sample through a proprietary chemical, the gas concentration is indicated by its changing colour.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instrument should you use to test for very low levels of oxygen before loading a sensitive cargo?
options: Chemical indicator tubes.
A paramagnetic oxygen analyser.
An Explosimeter.
An infrared gas detector.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Chemical indicator tubes.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What range of flammable gas can be detected by a thermal conductivity meter?
options: 0-100% Lower Flammable Limit.
0-10% Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: A fixed combustible gas detection system should not be used to assess compartments for entry purposes. Why not?
options: Because it does not indicate the oxygen content or the presence of toxic gases.
Because many spaces are being monitored, and the origin of the sample is not certain.
Because it does not give an accurate enough reading.
Since the sample takes some time to pass through the system, the reading may not be current.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Because it does not indicate the oxygen content or the presence of toxic gases.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the gas concentration alarm level on a fixed gas detection system?
options: 30% of Lower Flammable Limit.
10% of flammable gas.
3% of Lower Flammable Limit.
30% of flammable gas.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 30% of Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What range of flammable gas can be detected by an infrared type detector?
options: 0-100% Lower Flammable Limit.
0-10% Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instruments should be used to check the atmosphere of an enclosed space before entry?
options: An Explosimeter, a portable oxygen analyser, and a toxic gas meter if required.
A tankscope, an oxygen analyser, and a toxic gas meter if required.
An Explosimeter, and a toxic gas meter if required.
A personal gas detector and a personal toxic gas alarm if required.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: An Explosimeter, a portable oxygen analyser, and a toxic gas meter if required.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the principle by which a thermal conductivity meter works?
options: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show change in the density of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
To show a change in temperature of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.
To show a change in the conductivity of a heated gas sample relative to that of air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To show a change in resistance of an electrically heated resistance element, due to heat loss to the gas sample by conduction.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using a gascope?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self- testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the main reason for fitting a fixed gas detection system on a ship?
options: To indicate when a flammable atmosphere exists in a compartment.
To show that compartments are safe for entry.
To indicate that ventilation systems are working correctly.
To show that compartments are safe for hot work.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To indicate when a flammable atmosphere exists in a compartment.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of sensor is fitted in an Explosimeter?
options: A catalytic filament resistor.
A gas diffusion filter.
A magnetic resonance chamber.
A non-catalytic heated filament.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: A catalytic filament resistor.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What instruments must be provided to comply with the statutory requirements for ships fitted with an inert gas plant?
options: An oxygen analyser and an instrument to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.
An Explosimeter and an oxygen analyser.
At least two instruments to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.
At least two instruments to measure the percentage of oxygen in an inerted atmosphere.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: An oxygen analyser and an instrument to measure the percentage of hydrocarbon gas in an inerted atmosphere.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Cotton filters are sometimes used with hydrocarbon gas detectors. What is their purpose?
options: To remove water from the sample.
To stop pressure surges in the sample line.
To remove dust from the sample.
To prevent chemical contamination of the sample.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: To remove water from the sample.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is a "Pellistor"?
options: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.
It's a balancing resistor between the sensing element and a fixed compensator.
It's a protective device which removes contaminants.
It's a filter which prevents the spread of flame.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It's a poison resistant catalytic filament.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Many fixed gas detection systems monitor the atmosphere in the ballast tanks. What precautions must be taken on loaded passages?
options: Sample lines from ballast tanks must be isolated to prevent water from entering the system.
The alarm function must be switched off to prevent a continuous alarm condition.
All sample lines must be isolated to prevent any cargo from entering the system.
The system can be run as normal, but all alarms must be investigated.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Sample lines from ballast tanks must be isolated to prevent water from entering the system.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Many fixed gas detection systems have high and low sampling points. Why is this so?
options: So that they can be switched for cargos of different vapour density.
In order to ensure that all of a compartment is sampled.
In order to ensure that suction pipe runs are of a similar length.
So that they can be switched to account for temperature variations in the sample.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: So that they can be switched for cargos of different vapour density.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What measurements can be made using a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter)?
options: Flammable gas up to the Lower Flammable Limit.
Flammable gas up to 100% concentration.
Toxic gas up to the threshold limit value.
Flammable gas in an inert atmosphere.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Flammable gas up to the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What would you use a personal oxygen meter for?
options: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
For testing an enclosed space before starting hot work.
For checking the atmosphere of a ballast tank before entry.
For testing the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: How will leaks in the sampling line affect the operation of portable gas detection equipment?
options: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.
It will cause higher readings due to increased flow rate.
It will cause failure due to low suction pressure.
It will cause failure due to high flow rate.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will cause lower readings due to dilution of the sample.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What task can a personal multi-gas detector be used for?
options: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
For testing an enclosed space before starting hot work.
For checking the atmosphere of a ballast tank before entry.
For testing the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: For monitoring atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Multi-toxic gas detectors normally use electro-chemical detectors. What level of accuracy can be expected?
options: Approximately 1 - 5 ppm.
Approximately 10% by volume.
Approximately 100 - 500 ppm.
Approximately 30% by volume.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1 - 5 ppm.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: When starting to test a sample using a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter), the needle immediately flicks to maximum deflection, then returns to zero. What is indicated?
options: That the flammable gas concentration is above the Lower Flammable Limit.
That the battery is incorrectly fitted.
That the instrument was not warmed up, but is now working correctly.
That the sensor element has been contaminated by toxic gas.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: That the flammable gas concentration is above the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What type of sensor is fitted in a tankscope?
options: A non-catalytic heated filament.
A catalytic filament resistor.
A PT100 temperature sensor.
A magnetic induction sensor.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: A non-catalytic heated filament.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: For how long must the ventilation of a space be stopped before conducting tests of the atmosphere for an Enclosed Space Entry?
options: 10 minutes.
30 minutes.
The ventilation should be run continuously.
Briefly, while the tests are being carried out.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What will be the effect of hydrogen sulphide on the reading shown on a Combustible Gas Indicator (Explosimeter)?
options: It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
It will give a zero reading by destroying the sensor.
It will increase the reading by raising the sensitivity of the sensor.
It will have no effect because it is non-flammable.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What effect will inert gas have on the operation of a tankscope?
options: None. The sensor does not require oxygen.
It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
Small particles may clog the filters.
It will increase the reading by increasing the temperature of the filament.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: None. The sensor does not require oxygen.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: Why should you avoid high sample pressure when using an Explosimeter?
options: The pressure may damage the catalytic filament.
The pressure may burst the sampling hose.
If the flow rate is too high, the instrument does not have time to measure the gas concentration.
If the pressure is too high, it could cause an explosion inside the instrument.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: The pressure may damage the catalytic filament.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: If an Explosimeter is calibrated using span gas containing 1% butane in air, what reading may be expected?
options: Approximately 50% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 10% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 100% Lower Flammable Limit.
Approximately 1% Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 50% Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the composition of the span gas generally used for calibration of an Explosimeter?
options: Approximately 1% butane in air.
Pure carbon dioxide.
A proprietary mixture of nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
Approximately 40% propane in air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Approximately 1% butane in air.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What indication will be given by an Explosimeter in the case of oxygen deficiency?
options: No indication.
Approximately 20% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
Full scale deflection.
The indication will be erratic and jumpy.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: No indication.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What is the composition of the span gas generally used to zero a portable oxygen analyser?
options: High purity nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Fresh air.
Approximately 20% propane in air.
Approximately 2% propane in air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: High purity nitrogen or carbon dioxide.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What effect will inert gas have on the operation of an Explosimeter?
options: It will inhibit operation, as the sensor requires oxygen.
It will reduce the reading by contaminating the sensor.
Small particles may clog the filters.
None. The sensor does not require oxygen.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: It will inhibit operation, as the sensor requires oxygen.

CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.question: What operational tests should be made routinely before using a tankscope?
options: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.
Checking the battery level and zero using nitrogen or carbon dioxide.
Checking the battery level and self-testing alarm functions.
Checking the reference point with span gas and zero using atmospheric air.
CD7049 — TOTS 1C-Fixed and Portable Gas.answer: Checking the battery level and zero using fresh air.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What indication will be given by an Explosimeter in case of oxygen deficiency?
options: No indication.
Approximately 20% of the Lower Flammable Limit
Full scale deflection.
The indication is erratic and jumpy.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: No indication.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What use can be made of a combustible gas detector when making a Risk Assessment for tank entry?
options: Testing for hydrocarbon vapours up to the Lower Flammable Limit.
Testing for toxic gases up to any concentration.
Testing for hydrocarbon vapours up to 100% concentration.
Testing for oxygen content up to 21%.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Testing for hydrocarbon vapours up to the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What equipment must be used to test an enclosed space for the presence of toxic gas before entry?
options: A toxic gas detector
An explosimeter.
An oxygen meter.
A tankscope.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: A toxic gas detector

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What gas detection equipment must be used to test the atmosphere of a cargo tank before entry is permitted?
options: An oxygen meter, a combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
An oxygen meter and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
An oxygen meter and a tankscope.
A combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: An oxygen meter, a combustible gas indicator and a toxic gas detector if necessary.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What is the maximum permitted level of hydrocarbon gas for an enclosed space entry?
options: 1% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
1% by volume.
10% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
10% of the Occupational Exposure Limit.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: 1% of the Lower Flammable Limit.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How many people should be allowed to enter an enclosed space to carry out routine work?
options: Only the number actually required to carry out the work.
The number required to carry out the work, plus one extra watchman.
Only two people.
The number required to carry out the work, plus the person in charge and one extra watchman.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Only the number actually required to carry out the work.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How long should ventilation be continued after the atmosphere of an enclosed space has been found suitable for entry?
options: Continuously while the space is occupied, and even during temporary breaks.
For at least one hour after successful testing.
It can be stopped when testing shows that the space is suitable for entry.
It should be continued after testing until the space is actually entered.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Continuously while the space is occupied, and even during temporary breaks.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What equipment is required to be kept at the entrance of an enclosed space during entry?
options: A resuscitator, breathing apparatus, a lifeline and a harness, a torch or a lamp.
Spare tools and parts for the work being undertaken.
A resuscitator or escape breathing set.
Enough escape breathing sets for all personnel in the space.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: A resuscitator, breathing apparatus, a lifeline and a harness, a torch or a lamp.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action should be taken if personnel working in an enclosed space get into difficulties?
options: The general alarm should be sounded and the rescue team should enter using breathing apparatus under the direction of the Person In Charge
All personnel should be instructed to leave the space immediately.
The first person on the scene should immediately enter the space to give assistance.
The Watchman should immediately enter the space to give assistance.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The general alarm should be sounded and the rescue team should enter using breathing apparatus under the direction of the Person In Charge

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Who is required to standby at the entrance of an enclosed space during entry?
options: At least one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside and with the Officer of the Watch.
The Officer of the Watch and one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside.
Nobody, provided the personnel inside are equipped to communicate with the Officer of the Watch.
The Officer of the Watch, or whoever signed the Entry Permit.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: At least one watchman, equipped to communicate with the personnel inside and with the Officer of the Watch.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What is the maximum permitted level of toxic gas for an enclosed space entry?
options: The Occupational Exposure Limit, which varies according to the particular gas.
It varies according to the particular gas, but 1% is an acceptable level.
1% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
10% of the Lower Flammable Limit.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The Occupational Exposure Limit, which varies according to the particular gas.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For how long must the ventilation of a space be stopped before conducting tests of the atmosphere for an Enclosed Space Entry?
options: 10 minutes.
30 minutes.
The ventilation should be run continuously.
Briefly, while the tests are being carried out.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: To comply with an Enclosed Space Entry Permit, when must the atmosphere of an enclosed space be tested?
options: Before entry, and at frequent intervals when personnel are in the space.
In the morning, before daily routine work starts.
Every four hours
Before entry and after completion of work.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Before entry, and at frequent intervals when personnel are in the space.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What is the maximum length of time an Enclosed Space Entry Permit can remain valid?
options: Eight hours.
Twenty four hours
Four hours.
The estimated time required to complete a particular task.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Eight hours.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why could an unventilated ballast tank fitted with Cathodic Protection contain a hazardous atmosphere?
options: Because hydrogen is produced by the Cathodic Protection.
Because the Cathodic Protection could produce an oxygen enriched atmosphere.
Because hydrocarbons could be produced by the Cathodic Protection.
Because the Cathodic Protection would increase the level of nitrogen in the atmosphere.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Because hydrogen is produced by the Cathodic Protection.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What documentation should be completed before carrying out welding in a double bottom tank?
options: A Risk Assessment, an Enclosed Space Entry Permit and a Hot Work Permit.
A Risk Assessment and an Enclosed Space Entry Permit.
An Enclosed Space Entry Permit and a Cold Work Permit.
A Risk Assessment and a Hot Work Permit.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: A Risk Assessment, an Enclosed Space Entry Permit and a Hot Work Permit.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What potential hazards would be caused in a machinery space by the release of carbon dioxide for fire extinguishing purposes?
options: A lack of oxygen.
Carbon dioxide which is toxic to breathe.
Vapour, which may reduce visibility.
The carbon dioxide gas would be very cold, and could cause severe cold damage to the skin.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: A lack of oxygen.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: A Permit to Work is required before an enclosed space is entered. Who should complete this permit?
options: The Authorising Officer, normally the head of department.
The person who is to carry out the work.
The Master.
It must be authorised by the Company office.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The Authorising Officer, normally the head of department.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Who is responsible for cancelling an Enclosed Space Entry Permit when work is completed?
options: The person who authorised the permit.
The person who completed the work.
The Master.
Any other senior officer.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The person who authorised the permit.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why could an unprotected steel space, which has been closed, produce a hazardous atmosphere?
options: Because oxygen in the atmosphere may be depleted by reacting with the steel (i.e. corrosion).
Because the level of nitrogen in the atmosphere would be increased by corrosion.
Because toxic gases may be given off by the process of corrosion.
Because hydrocarbons could be liberated from rust scale in the tank.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Because oxygen in the atmosphere may be depleted by reacting with the steel (i.e. corrosion).

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: How many different locations within a tank should be sampled to test the atmosphere before entering a tank?
options: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.
At least three locations.
In one position, at a minimum of three levels.
As close as possible to the centre of the tank.
