CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: At various depths, and through as many openings as possible.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What actions must be taken to isolate a tank before entry?
options: Blank off the pipelines to the tank, close and secure all valves and inform the Officer of the Watch.
Request the Officer of the Watch to stop all cargo and ballast pumps.
Stop all cargo and ballast operations.
Stop all ventilation and inform the Officer of the Watch.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: Blank off the pipelines to the tank, close and secure all valves and inform the Officer of the Watch.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: Why must the enclosed space atmosphere be sampled at a variety of positions?
options: To allow for the density of the gas and to check for any gas pockets which may have accumulated in blind spots.
To obtain an average reading throughout the tank.
To make sure that the detection equipment is working correctly.
To ensure that enough gas is drawn through the equipment to avoid it remaining in the sampling line.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To allow for the density of the gas and to check for any gas pockets which may have accumulated in blind spots.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For what purpose would you use a personal oxygen meter?
options: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
Testing an enclosed space before starting hot work.
To check the atmosphere of an enclosed space before entry.
Testing the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action should be taken if personnel working in an enclosed space feel unwell or suspect the presence of gas?
options: They should leave the space immediately and contact the Person In Charge or Officer of the Watch.
They should request a crew member to bring breathing apparatus into the space.
They should request a crew member to verify the atmosphere.
The Officer of the Watch, or whoever signed the entry permit, should be advised of the situation.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: They should leave the space immediately and contact the Person In Charge or Officer of the Watch.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: What action should be taken if routine tests indicate the presence of gas while personnel are present in an enclosed space?
options: The personnel should leave the space immediately and contact the Person In Charge or Officer of the Watch.
The work must be completed as soon as possible and then vacate the space.
The gas testing equipment should be checked to verify its accurate.
The Watchman should be instructed to bring the breathing apparatus into the space as back up.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: The personnel should leave the space immediately and contact the Person In Charge or Officer of the Watch.

CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.question: For what purpose would you use a personal gas detector?
options: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.
To test an enclosed space before starting hot work.
To check the atmosphere of an enclosed space before entry.
To test the atmosphere of an open space before starting hot work.
CD7050 — TOTS 1C-Enclosed Spaces and Tan.answer: To monitor atmospheric conditions during an enclosed space entry.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is the name of the diagram that is superimposed on the cargo control console?
options: A mimic diagram.
The tank plan.
Cargo lines.
The pumping plan.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: A mimic diagram.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: All cargo system pre-arrival testing must be recorded in the ship's..
options: deck logbook.
ESP file.
SOPEP manual.
Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: deck logbook.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Petroleum cargo pipe lines are to be tested to what pressure?
options: 1.25 times their designed working pressure.
To normal operating pressure.
1.5 times their designed working pressure.
They are only to be tested after maintenance or when repairs have been completed.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: 1.25 times their designed working pressure.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is the atmosphere of void spaces regularly checked?
options: Because it is the first indication of cargo migration due to cracks in welded seams or similar.
Because instructions to do so are contained in the Chief Officer's standing orders.
In order to check for water content.
To ensure adequate oxygen.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Because it is the first indication of cargo migration due to cracks in welded seams or similar.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why must a cargo tank atmosphere be monitored during crude oil washing?
options: To ensure that the oxygen level remains at 8% or less by volume.
To ensure that the washing process is adequate.
To ensure that the cleaning gun cycle is completed.
Overall, to ensure sludge control.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To ensure that the oxygen level remains at 8% or less by volume.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Officer of the Watch must regularly check the cargo tank ullages to..
options: ensure that the cargo is only entering the designated cargo tanks and that there is no escape of cargo into pumprooms and cofferdams.
ensure the loading rate.
ensure the cargo temperature.
determine when the cargo transfer will be completed.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: ensure that the cargo is only entering the designated cargo tanks and that there is no escape of cargo into pumprooms and cofferdams.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you expect to see a notice displayed regarding free surface effect on a combination carrier?
options: Next to the cargo control station.
In the Master's office.
In the cargo manifold.
At the top of the pumproom.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Next to the cargo control station.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: In the cargo control room (CCR), on the inert gas panel, the continuous trace of inert gas oxygen content at delivery during crude oil washing must be..
options: 5% or less.
8% is satisfactory.
none of these. As long as the tank being washed has positive pressure, it does not matter.
dependent upon the Chief Officer's standing orders.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: 5% or less.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would the greater ullage be when a vessel is trimmed by the head?
options: The aft end of the tank.
The forward end of the tank.
There would be no difference.
It depends upon the list.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The aft end of the tank.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why should you monitor void spaces, cofferdams and empty ballast tanks during a loaded passage?
options: To confirm that such spaces remain gas free.
To check for water content.
To practise the use of portable instruments.
To confirm that welded seams are not cracked.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To confirm that such spaces remain gas free.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: If hydrocarbon gases are found in double hull ballast tanks, what action should be taken?
options: Immediately utilise the emergency inerting procedure.
Close the tank down.
Vent to atmosphere.
Read ISGOTT.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Immediately utilise the emergency inerting procedure.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What instrument must be used for measuring hydrocarbon gas in an inert atmosphere?
options: A Tankscope.
An oxygen meter.
Chemical indicator tubes.
An Explosimeter.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: A Tankscope.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would a plan indicating the location of cargo measurement instruments, sensors, pressure gauges, etc normally be found?
options: In the CCR (cargo control room).
In the Chief Engineer's office.
At the manifold.
In the reliquefaction plant.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In the CCR (cargo control room).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: In which documentation would you expect to find duties and responsibilities relating to the cargo system?
options: In the Safety Management System (SMS).
In the SOLAS training manual.
In the Certificate of Fitness.
In the Builders' Cargo Operations Book.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In the Safety Management System (SMS).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Which volume reduction petroleum tables may be used when calculating a crude oil cargo?
options: 6A and / or 6B.
54A or 54B.
Norries tables.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: 6A and / or 6B.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: A tank "sounding" can be referred to as..
options: tank innage.
tank ullage.
tank reference point.
trim correction.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: tank innage.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When entering cargo tank calibration tables, which components affect the resulting volume?
options: Ullage, trim and list.
Only ullage.
The load temperature of the cargo.
Only innage.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Ullage, trim and list.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Which competent body checks and approves a vessel's tank calibration tables?
options: The Classification Society.
MARPOL.
The IMO.
The P&I Club.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Classification Society.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What information is used to obtain the factor for reducing the volume at the observed temperature to the volume at standard temperature?
options: API gravity and observed temperature.
The cargo tank ullage and the temperature.
Capacity in US barrels.
API and the ullage of the cargo tank.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: API gravity and observed temperature.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is the name of the diagram that is superimposed on the cargo control console?
options: The mimic diagram.
The tank plan.
The cargo lines.
The pumping plan.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The mimic diagram.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The approved loading computer programme is malfunctioning, you would..
options: consult the Approved Trim and Stability Manual?
use the Chief Officer's personal programme?
consult a general arrangement and a capacity plan?
look for a similar cargo in the cargo record book?
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: consult the Approved Trim and Stability Manual?

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: A combination carrier loaded with crude oil has two tanks, each only 60% full. What affect will this have on the vessel's stability?
options: There will be a virtual loss of GM.
It will increase the rolling period.
The vessel will trim by the head.
It will increase in permissible bending moments.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: There will be a virtual loss of GM.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you expect to locate a mimic diagram of the cargo system?
options: In the cargo control room (CCR) operational panel.
In the Chief Engineer's office.
At the manifold.
Adjacent to the bunkering manifold.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In the cargo control room (CCR) operational panel.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Ship Inspection Report Programme (SIRE) states that the loading programme must be checked by means of an approved test programme at least..
options: Quarterly.
Annually.
At the Chief Officer's discretion.
As directed by the Master.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Quarterly.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When calculating the UKC, what is the "controlling depth"?
options: It's the least depth of water on the vessel's proposed track.
It's the draught of the vessel when proceeding in a narrow channel.
It's the depth of water allowing for height of tide.
It's a figure required to calculate squat.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It's the least depth of water on the vessel's proposed track.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: At commencement of loading, the generation of static is controlled by..
options: limiting the flow rate at the tank inlet.
earthing the manifold.
only having one loading arm connected.
monitoring the cargo temperature.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: limiting the flow rate at the tank inlet.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Permissible bending moments are greater in which condition?
options: In harbour condition.
There is no difference between sea and harbour condition.
It depends upon the amount of segregated ballast.
It depends upon the mean draught.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: In harbour condition.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: A vessel is to maintain light ballast condition, however if logged and permissible bending moments have been exceeded, you would..
options: reduce ballast in Fore & After Peaks, maintaining propeller immersion and minimum draught forward?
ballast amidships cargo tanks?
do nothing it is only a short voyage?
move bunker fuel aft?
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: reduce ballast in Fore & After Peaks, maintaining propeller immersion and minimum draught forward?

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When discharging segregated ballast, the overboard discharge must be monitored..
options: for contaminated ballast.
to help calculate the rate of discharge.
to observe when de-ballasting has been completed.
Monitoring is not required.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: for contaminated ballast.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Flammability and toxicity of proposed cargo can be obtained from..
options: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS).
ISGOTT.
The Approved Trim and Stability Manual.
The SOPEP file.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: A Ship to Shore Safety Checklist can be found in which publication?
options: ISGOTT.
ISPS code.
SOPEP.
The Mariner's Handbook.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: ISGOTT.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The principle purpose of a pre-cargo transfer meeting is to..
options: ensure that all involved personnel are aware of the proposed cargo operations, services needed and safety requirements.
inform the technical officers when cargo pumps will be required.
arrange shore leave.
discuss the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: ensure that all involved personnel are aware of the proposed cargo operations, services needed and safety requirements.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Different grades on a product tanker are normally segregated by..
options: Two valve separation.
A single valve.
A spade blank.
It does not matter as different densities will keep them separated.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Two valve separation.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: If the shore fails to deliver cargo at the requested rate, what action would the Master take?
options: He would issue a letter of protest.
He would inform the local P&I Club.
He would inform the Class.
He would take no action.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: He would issue a letter of protest.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: On what occasions will a pre-cargo transfer meeting be minuted?
options: On each and every occasion.
When there is something special to say.
When the Captain attends.
Whenever the port stay is estimated to be greater than 24 hours.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: On each and every occasion.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Night orders must be signed by the appropriate personnel..
options: every night when new orders are issued.
once per port only.
once per cargo grade only.
It does not matter.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: every night when new orders are issued.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you use the Chief Officer's personally developed loading / stress monitoring computer programme?
options: Never.
Occasionally, if the approved one is non-operational.
All the time, if the results appear correct.
Once a month to check the results of the approved system.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Never.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What competent body would normally approve a loading instrument / programme?
options: The Classification Society.
SOLAS.
The P&I Club.
The ship's Master.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Classification Society.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What does code "R" indicate in the Ship / Shore Safety Check List?
options: Re-checking at intervals not to exceed an agreed time.
Restricted access.
Regular checks not required.
Checks to be repeated only upon the instructions of the Chief Officer.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Re-checking at intervals not to exceed an agreed time.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What medium is used to purge cargo tanks that have previously carried crude oil?
options: Inert gas.
Oxygen.
Water.
A mixture of oxygen and water.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Inert gas.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: How long must logbooks and other cargo records be kept on board?
options: As detailed in the owners/managers Safety & Quality Management System.
For 12 months after discharge.
At the Master's discretion.
For the life of the vessel.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: As detailed in the owners/managers Safety & Quality Management System.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: During cargo transfer, what action would you take if the Inert Gas System fails?
options: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.
Increase the rate of discharge.
Advise the terminal and continue discharging.
Review the Ship / Shore Safety Check List.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Cease all discharge operations and advise the terminal.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When starting a centrifugal cargo pump, the discharge valve should be initially..
options: Closed.
Open.
It does not matter.
Slightly open.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Closed.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you find approved information regarding the vessel structural strength?
options: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.
The deck logbook.
The Certificate of Class.
The OCIMF Ship Inspection Report Programme.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The Approved Trim and Stability Book.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you need to check the intact stability at intermediate stages of cargo transfer?
options: On each and every occasion.
If the Master directed you to do so.
When the vessel developed a list.
Seldom as it's not really required.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: On each and every occasion.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you normally expect to find a full set of cargo operation instructions?
options: The cargo control room (CCR).
The Master's cabin.
In the wheel-house.
The SOLAS training manual in the crew's lounge.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The cargo control room (CCR).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The Ship / Shore Safety Check List states that temporarily removed scupper plugs must be..
options: constantly monitored.
stowed in a safe place.
clearly labelled as to location.
only removed by the person responsible for cargo operations.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: constantly monitored.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The port / cargo operations log will form the basis of..
options: the statement of facts.
crew overtime.
ISPS implementation.
compliance with SOLAS.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the statement of facts.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: In which language would you expect the operational and technical manuals to be written?
options: The official working language of the vessel.
English.
Several languages.
It depends upon the nationality of the manufacturer.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The official working language of the vessel.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: How does "free surface effect" (sloshing) affect the ship's stability?
options: It reduces the metacentric height.
It has no effect.
It causes an angle of loll.
It increases the metacentric height.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It reduces the metacentric height.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: The location of technical manuals relating to the cargo system..
options: would depend upon who is responsible as per the Plan Maintenance System.
would depend upon where the Captain wants to put them.
are always with the Chief Engineer.
are in the common library on the bridge.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: would depend upon who is responsible as per the Plan Maintenance System.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When must the Chief Officer's standing orders be followed?
options: Throughout all cargo transfer, ballasting operations and tank cleaning.
Only in port.
Only during ship to ship transfer operations.
When the Captain is ashore.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Throughout all cargo transfer, ballasting operations and tank cleaning.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Cargo transfer operational information will normally be available in..
options: the cargo control room (CCR).
the SOLAS training manual located in the officers' and crew lounge.
the Chief Engineer's office.
the wheel-house.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the cargo control room (CCR).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Sequential and flow through methods form part of..
options: the ballast exchange plan.
the composition of a sounding book.
the plan to clean cargo tanks.
the ballast water analysis.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the ballast exchange plan.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: In the loading limit formula, at which temperature is the pR value expressed?
options: At reference temperature.
At ambient temperature.
At sea temperature.
At 45 degrees Centigrade.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: At reference temperature.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Damage due to sloshing is a direct result of the tank..
options: being partially filled (slack).
being filled more than 98%.
having the tank pressure too high.
None of these answers.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: being partially filled (slack).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: A "Statement of Facts" is..
options: an accurate account of happenings in? a time based in chronological order.
a statement regarding the volatility of the cargo.
the Chief Officer's account of the cargo transfer.
an analysis of cargo samples.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: an accurate account of happenings in? a time based in chronological order.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Before loading, you should ensure that..
options: the offshore manifold is closed and blanked.
the pressure gauge is fitted.
the manifold is blanked but the valve is open.
the temperature gauge is fitted between the valve and the blank.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: the offshore manifold is closed and blanked.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: If unable to ground GMDSS equipment during cargo operations, what action may be taken?
options: To switch the equipment off.
To turn the volume down.
To ignore any rules as you cannot comply.
To make a logbook entry.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To switch the equipment off.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Cargo tank temperature and pressure gauges and reliquefaction plant instruments should be calibrated..
options: preferably at intervals not exceeding 30 months.
at intervals not exceeding 12 months.
whenever a false reading is suspected.
at the Master's discretion.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: preferably at intervals not exceeding 30 months.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Shore cargo hard arms are commonly known as..
options: chicksans.
hose strings.
cargo lines.
manifold lines.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: chicksans.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why are main radio transmitter aerials grounded during cargo operations?
options: To prevent a potential ignition source.
Because they are not needed in port.
Because they are not required for communications in port
Because it is written in the Safety Management System (SMS).
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To prevent a potential ignition source.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is meant by the operating envelope when referring to loading arms?
options: It is the maximum amount the vessel can safely range up and down the berth and generally move without damaging the loading arms.
It is the maximum cargo pressure the loading arm can withstand.
It is the vertical reach of the loading arm.
It is the range of cargo temperatures the loading arm can safely withstand.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It is the maximum amount the vessel can safely range up and down the berth and generally move without damaging the loading arms.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: As part of the Safety Management System (SMS), new personnel joining the tanker must be..
options: familiarised with their duties and responsibilities.
informed of their salary.
introduced to the Captain.
given a minimum of 24 hours to recover after travel.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: familiarised with their duties and responsibilities.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Who has overall responsibility for the maintenance of the cargo system?
options: It will depend upon the owner's/manager's work instructions as detailed in the Safety Management System (SMS).
The Chief Engineer.
The Chief Officer.
The Electrical Officer.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: It will depend upon the owner's/manager's work instructions as detailed in the Safety Management System (SMS).

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is it important to keep the cargo manifold area clear of obstructions?
options: So as not to interfere with the automatic release of a cargo hardarm.
So ship and shore staff can work easily.
Simply to keep the space tidy and ship shape.
For easy access in case of a pollution incident.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: So as not to interfere with the automatic release of a cargo hardarm.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: When would you exceed the maximum pressure ratings of the cargo system?
options: Never. All pressure ratings must be adhered to.
When circumstances dictated a departure from safe operating procedures.
When you think it is safe, according to your own personal experience exceeding pressures on other occasions.
Whenever instructed to do so by the head office.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Never. All pressure ratings must be adhered to.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Offshore manifold gauges need not be fitted?
options: False
True
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: False

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you expect to find the cargo pump performance curves?
options: Adjacent to the cargo / pump control console.
In the Chief Officer's office.
In the engine control room (ECR).
At the top of the pumproom.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Adjacent to the cargo / pump control console.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Where would you expect cargo pump emergency stops to be located?
options: The cargo control room (CCR), the pumproom and the cargo manifold.
On the poop.
In the wheel-house.
In the Master's cabin.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The cargo control room (CCR), the pumproom and the cargo manifold.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: Why is it important to regularly check offshore manifold gauges during a cargo transfer?
options: To check for manifold valve leakage.
To check for pressure in the cargo system.
To comply with the terminal requirements.
To comply with the MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet).
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: To check for manifold valve leakage.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What is a schematic drawing?
options: A drawing in the form of a diagram and not to scale.
An exact technical drawing.
An approximate drawing.
The general arrangement plan.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: A drawing in the form of a diagram and not to scale.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: On a combination carrier, where would the audible bilge alarm sound from a void space forward of the collision bulkhead?
options: The navigation bridge.
The CCR (cargo control room).
On deck close to an accommodation entrance.
No alarm. It would just checked daily by soundings.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The navigation bridge.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What material should manifold reducers be made of?
options: Steel.
Cast iron.
GRP (glass reinforced plastic).
None of these answers.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Steel.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What precaution must be taken when removing a blank flange?
options: Ensuring that the section between the blank flange and last valve does not contain oil under pressure.
Ensuring that the pressure gauge is fitted correctly.
Ensuring that the cock on the pressure gauge is closed.
Ensuring that the correct spanner size is used to remove the bolts.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: Ensuring that the section between the blank flange and last valve does not contain oil under pressure.

CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.question: What must be monitored before entering the pumproom during cargo operations?
options: The hydrocarbon gases and the oxygen content.
The amount of bilge water.
The mechanical ventilation.
The rescue harness.
CD7051 — TOTS 1C-Familiarisation prior C.answer: The hydrocarbon gases and the oxygen content.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Who has the responsibility to ensure the correct health hazard information is passed to the vessel?
options: The supplier of the cargo.
The ship broker.
The ship owner.
MARPOL inspectors.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The supplier of the cargo.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is cargo ingestion?
options: Cargo being swallowed.
Cargo vapours being inhaled.
Cargo having contact with the skin.
Cargo having contact with the eyes.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: Cargo being swallowed.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the common name for a Personal Escape Set?
options: EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device).
ELSA set.
Self Contained Breathing Apparatus.
A resuscitator.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device).

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the minimum air duration for an EEBD?
options: 10 minutes.
15 minutes.
It depends on the type of tanker.
As per the vessels Safety Management System.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: 10 minutes.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the inspection criteria for breathing apparatus on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: A monthly inspection by a responsible officer and annual inspection and testing at an approved facility.
A weekly inspection by the 3rd officer.
The Chief Engineer inspects all the apparatus monthly.
It should be inspected by a class surveyor annually.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A monthly inspection by a responsible officer and annual inspection and testing at an approved facility.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Where would you find information on the cargo to be loaded relating to health hazards?
options: The MSDS (Material Safety data Sheets).
The World Health organisation.
The Ship Captain's Medical Guide.
SOLAS consolidated edition.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The MSDS (Material Safety data Sheets).

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: The cargo being loaded is described as having highly toxic vapour. What must be worn on the cargo deck?
options: Breathing apparatus.
A dust mask.
Rubber gloves.
A face shield.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: Breathing apparatus.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the lifeline and belt that form part of the safety equipment on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: The line and belt must be fireproof and resistant to the cargo being carried.
They must always be orange in colour.
The length of the lifeline must be at least double the tankers moulded depth.
The equipment must be inspected at least annually.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The line and belt must be fireproof and resistant to the cargo being carried.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: When wearing the EEBD how do you support the air bottle?
options: With a strap around the neck supported on the chest
You carry it under your arm.
You strap it to your back.
You put the air bottle into your chemical suit pocket.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: With a strap around the neck supported on the chest

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the important feature of the goggles on a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances?
options: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.
They must be lightweight.
They must have 2 headbands for extra safety.
Nothing in particular, chipping goggles are adequate
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: They must be tight fitting and splash proof.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: According to the IBC code where should in use protective equipment be stowed?
options: In special lockers in easy accessible places.
In the accommodation.
At the top of the pumproom.
At the forecastle head.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: In special lockers in easy accessible places.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: How does the IBC code describe coveralls?
options: They should be made of material resistant to chemical attack.
They should be made of pure cotton.
They must be nylon.
They can be made of any material but must have long sleeves.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: They should be made of material resistant to chemical attack.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What can be worn in addition to or instead of goggles?
options: A face shield.
A smoke helmet.
Breathing apparatus.
An escape set.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A face shield.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: How does one usually separate two different cargo products?
options: A two valve segregation.
Insert spade blanks.
A tank valve and a crossover.
A one valve segregation is sufficient.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A two valve segregation.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is the "pumping clause"?
options: It's the maximum time to discharge the entire cargo or a minimum average pressure at the discharge manifold.
It's the maximum time the cargo pumps can be running.
It's the maximum number of cargo pumps that can be operated at one time.
None of these answers are correct.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: It's the maximum time to discharge the entire cargo or a minimum average pressure at the discharge manifold.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: On a tanker carrying Noxious Liquid Substances, what is the minimum number of protective equipment sets that must be carried?
options: At least three.
Two.
One, provided it's the one that's required by SOLAS.
It can vary as it depends upon the toxicity of the cargo.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: At least three.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: You are concerned about the toxicity of the cargo stated in the voyage orders. What is toxicity?
options: The degree to which a substance or mixture of substances can harm humans or animals.
The amount of alcohol in the blood stream due to toxicity of the cargo.
A gas below its critical temperature.
The name given to a gas sample.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The degree to which a substance or mixture of substances can harm humans or animals.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: The charter party includes information on STS transfer. What is meant by STS transfer?
options: Ship To Ship.
Suitable Tank System.
Suitable Tanker Stability.
Safe Tanker System.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: Ship To Ship.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: Voyage orders instruct you to dose the cargo with an Anti-static additive. What is an Anti-static additive?
options: It's a substance added to a petroleum product to raise its electrical conductivity to a safe level.
It's a substance that enables safer ullaging.
It assists in stabilising the cargo temperature.
It reduces static electricity when tank cleaning with portable machines and hoses.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: It's a substance added to a petroleum product to raise its electrical conductivity to a safe level.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is deadfreight?
options: The sum payable to the owner when the charterer has failed to load a full and complete cargo.
The amount of cargo not shipped on the vessel.
The amount of cargo which is described as FOB (Free on Board).
When the charterer is bankrupt it's the freight claimed by the owner.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: The sum payable to the owner when the charterer has failed to load a full and complete cargo.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What is a charter party?
options: A charter party is the contract between the owner of a vessel and the charterer for the use of a vessel.
A group of ship brokers.
A non-binding agreement between any two parties.
Renting a vessel for an event.
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: A charter party is the contract between the owner of a vessel and the charterer for the use of a vessel.

CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.question: What action would the master take if he thought the proposed cargo was not suitable for his vessel?
options: He would confirm the contents of the charter party and then immediately inform his owners/managers and the charterers.
He would inform the charter broker.
He would inform his owners.
He would inform the QI (Qualified Individual).
CD7052 — TOTS 1C-Cargo Information, Prec.answer: He would confirm the contents of the charter party and then immediately inform his owners/managers and the charterers.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action would you take if, during manoeuvring operations the main engine oil mist detector alarm was activated, the engine automatically slows down and the alarm condition clears?
options: Advise the Master and prepare to stop the engine as soon as it is practical for the manoeuvring operations.
Advise the Master and stop the engine immediately to inspect the crankcase.
Advise the Master and continue with slow speed operation, until the completion of manoeuvring.
Advise the Master of the alarm activation and continue with the normal engine operations.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Advise the Master and prepare to stop the engine as soon as it is practical for the manoeuvring operations.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What minimum starting air pressure is normally required to start a main engine?
options: 12 bars.
10 bars.
15 bars.
17 bars.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: 12 bars.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: During manoeuvring what condition would you expect to consistently apply to the starting air system?
options: The starting air pressure should be kept at the maximum possible level at all times.
The bridge should be informed of the status of the starting air capacity on a regular basis.
Only one air compressor should be run at all times and the second one kept on stand-by.
At least two air compressors should be running at all times.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: The starting air pressure should be kept at the maximum possible level at all times.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: When, during manoeuvring, would you expect to changeover from heavy oil to diesel oil on a vessel where the two fuels are utilised?
options: Prior to manoeuvring.
At a suitable time during manoeuvring.
Just before shutting down allowing time to flush through the fuel system.
It is optional dependent on whether overhaul work will be carried out on the engine.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Prior to manoeuvring.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the maximum allowed sulphur content in "Low Sulphur Fuel"?
What affects the distribution of electrical load between electric generators in parallel?
options: Changing individual prime mover revolutions.
Adjusting individual generator voltage.
Adjusting individual excitation current.
Removal of consumer load demand.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Changing individual prime mover revolutions.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: If one unit of the main engine is out of order due to a fracture in the liner, what action should be taken with respect to the scavenge air supply to the unit before manoeuvring?
options: The scavenge air should be isolated from the unit.
No action needs to be taken with respect to the scavenge air.
The exhaust valve should be adjusted to remain open during the full cycle to prevent build up of air pressure.
The scavenge air should be increased to improve cylinder cooling.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: The scavenge air should be isolated from the unit.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the normally accepted method for testing automatic start-up of stand-by equipment?
options: By manually stopping the in service unit.
By running both units simultaneously.
By checking that the standby unit switch is correctly set.
By doing a black-out simulation.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: By manually stopping the in service unit.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: In what configuration should the starting air system bottles be set prior to arrival manoeuvring?
options: All air bottles should be fully charged with one online and one on stand-by.
All air compressors should be switched to MANUAL mode.
All air bottles should be charged and fully open.
All air-operated deck equipment should be isolated.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: All air bottles should be fully charged with one online and one on stand-by.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action should be carried out when one fuel pump becomes defective during manoeuvring?
options: The fuel pump should be hung up, the inlet valve shut and the bridge informed of the problem.
The main engine should be stopped immediately and the bridge informed of the problem.
The main engine's revolution should be increased to recover the loss of power on one cylinder.
The main engine's revolution should be decreased to avoid overloading other cylinders.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: The fuel pump should be hung up, the inlet valve shut and the bridge informed of the problem.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is one of the first actions that should be carried out during manoeuvring if one or more of the main engine's turbochargers is defective?
options: Check that all auxiliary electric-powered blowers are switched on and operating correctly.
The main engine should be stopped and shore assistance should be called.
The main engine's revolutions should be reduced.
The main engine's revolution should be increased for more power.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Check that all auxiliary electric-powered blowers are switched on and operating correctly.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action should be carried out if an electrical black-out occurs in the engine room during manoeuvring?
options: After the emergency diesel generator starts, run only minimum machinery for safe manoeuvring.
Inform the bridge of the situation and try to restart the diesel generators.
Wait for the emergency diesel generator to start and evacuate the engine room immediately.
Give assistance to the Electrician and try to bring back the electrical power as soon as possible.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: After the emergency diesel generator starts, run only minimum machinery for safe manoeuvring.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action should be taken if the main engine's fresh water cooling pressure drops during manoeuvring?
options: Reduce the main engine revolutions.
Ensure both cooling water pumps are running.
Stop the main engine immediately.
No action is required because the main engine load is low.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Reduce the main engine revolutions.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Who should be present in the engine room during manoeuvring besides duty personnel?
options: A Senior Engineer.
All Engine Staff.
All Engine Ratings.
The Electrician and the Fitter.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: A Senior Engineer.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Why is water not suitable for extinguishing main engine scavenge fires?
options: It will flash off and the fire may develop into a hydrogen fire.
It will cool the space too quickly and cause the liner to crack.
It will leak into the crankcase space and contaminate the lubricating oil.
It will cause the liner, piston rod and scraper box parts to rust.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: It will flash off and the fire may develop into a hydrogen fire.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action would you take if the main engine lubricating oil pressure dropped suddenly during manoeuvring ?
options: Request permission from the bridge to stop the main engine as soon as possible and warn them that it may stop automatically.
The main engine's revolutions should be reduced.
The main engine revolutions should be increased to compensate.
The main engine should be kept running while waiting for the stand-by oil pump to start.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Request permission from the bridge to stop the main engine as soon as possible and warn them that it may stop automatically.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: If, during manoeuvring, you find that a fire had broken out in the purifier room what action should you take after raising the alarm and advising the bridge of the situation?
options: Try to extinguish the fire using portable fire fighting equipment.
Evacuate all non-required personnel from the engine room.
Call the designated person ashore for help.
Call a vessel in the vicinity for help.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Try to extinguish the fire using portable fire fighting equipment.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What condition should stand-by equipment be in prior to arrival / departure manoeuvring?
options: All stand-by equipment should be operable / available and in standby condition.
All stand-by equipment should be switched ON and running.
All stand-by equipment should be switched OFF.
All stand-by equipment should be running but not delivering its intended service.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: All stand-by equipment should be operable / available and in standby condition.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the main purpose of the "Arrival / Departure Checklist"?
options: To confirm that all systems necessary for manoeuvring are in working order.
To ensure personnel changes on board are documented.
To provide Company data required by the office.
To be used as a teaching aid to junior ranks.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: To confirm that all systems necessary for manoeuvring are in working order.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action should be carried out if the CO2 alarm is raised in the engine room?
options: All personnel should be evacuated from the engine room immediately.
The Master should be informed immediately of the alarm.
It should be re-checked to make sure it is not a false alarm.
All running equipment should be stopped first and then all personnel should leave the engine room.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: All personnel should be evacuated from the engine room immediately.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Lubricating oil pressure drops if its temperature rises.
options: True
False
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: True

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Which extinguishing media is no longer acceptable for fitting onboard vessels?
options: Halon.
Water mist.
Low expansion foam.
Carbon Dioxide (CO2).
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Halon.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: As per SOLAS requirements, where should the quick close fuel valves' release cabinets be located?
options: Outside the engine room.
Inside the engine room.
Near the engine control room.
On the navigation bridge.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Outside the engine room.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: If the main engine remote control from the bridge and from the engine control room is defective, what should be done?
options: Transfer should be made to main engine local control.
Transfer should be made to main engine deck control.
Transfer should be made to main engine control from the emergency switchboard.
Transfer should be made to main engine control from the emergency steering gear.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Transfer should be made to main engine local control.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the purpose of a steering gear "Creep Test"?
options: To check the condition of the steering gear hydraulic system seals and valves.
To check if the steering gear autopilot is in good order.
To check if the steering gear non-follow up control system is in good order.
To check that the steering gear does not fall back from the hard-over position.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: To check the condition of the steering gear hydraulic system seals and valves.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What activities related to arrival manoeuvring does the International Safety Management Code (ISM) require to be logged in the Engine Log Book?
options: All pre-arrival checks and tests carried out.
All tests carried out as per arrival check lists.
All function tests carried out on the main propulsion system.
All function tests carried out on communications (Bridge / Engine Room).
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: All pre-arrival checks and tests carried out.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Which regulations cover the discharge of NOx and SOx?
options: MARPOL
SOLAS
ISGOTT
APPS
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: MARPOL

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: If a fire has broken out in the purifier room during manoeuvring, which media should be used as a last resort?
options: Seawater.
Powder.
Foam.
Carbon Dioxide (CO2).
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Seawater.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What does MARPOL regulate in the marine industry?
options: Prevention of Marine Pollution.
Marine Police.
Maritime Protocol of Loading.
Means and Rules governing Repatriation of Leavers.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Prevention of Marine Pollution.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Would you expect the Control Room to be manned during manoeuvring in an UMS classed vessel?
options: Yes.
No manning is required due to UMS conditions.
No manning is required even if no UMS conditions apply.
Yes, as required by the Master.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Yes.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Which of the following tests would NOT normally be carried out as part of a pre-arrival standby routine?
options: The testing of the fuel system quick-closing valves.
The testing of main engine starting ahead and astern.
Testing communications between the bridge and engine room.
The testing of the steering gear.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: The testing of the fuel system quick-closing valves.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Is there a requirement to increase Main Engine Cylinder Lubrication during manoeuvring?
options: No, unless special circumstances apply.
Yes, as manoeuvring is considered a special circumstance.
Yes, as per the lubrication oil company requirements.
No, as per MARPOL requirements.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: No, unless special circumstances apply.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What action should be carried out FIRST if a fire has broken out in the engine room during manoeuvring?
options: Ensure the fire alarm is raised.
Stop the main engine by pushing the emergency stop button.
Call the bridge and ask for assistance.
Call the Emergency Party.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Ensure the fire alarm is raised.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Would you expect the Engine Room itself to have personnel engaged in watchkeeping duties during manoeuvring?
options: Yes.
No, due to Company requirements.
No, due to safety requirements.
Yes, as required by the Master.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Yes.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What should be done if the remote control of the steering system from the bridge becomes defective during manoeuvring?
options: Change over to local control and engage one person for steering.
Stop all operations immediately.
Call tugboats for assistance and proceed with manoeuvring.
Stop manoeuvring until the remote control has been repaired.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Change over to local control and engage one person for steering.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the usual acceptable time for the steering rudder to swing from "hard to port" to "hard to starboard"?
options: 28 seconds.
18 seconds.
38 seconds.
48 seconds.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: 28 seconds.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: Does SOLAS legislation exist stating how many steering gear hydraulic pump units are directly connected to the emergency switchboard?
options: Yes, according to SOLAS legislation there should be a minimum of one pump.
According to SOLAS legislation all the pumps should be connected.
SOLAS do not have the power to legislate on this requirement.
No such requirement exists.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Yes, according to SOLAS legislation there should be a minimum of one pump.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: What is the first action you should take if the main engine oil mist detector alarm sounds?
options: Slow down the main engine immediately and inform the bridge of the problem.
Inform the bridge and re-check the main engine's bearing temperatures.
Check if the alarm is genuine before initiating any action.
Call the Technical Superintendent for help immediately.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Slow down the main engine immediately and inform the bridge of the problem.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: How many persons minimum, would you expect to be on duty in the Engine Room during manoeuvring?
options: One senior and one junior engineer.
All senior engineers and one junior.
The Chief Engineer and one junior engineer.
One Senior and all junior engineers.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: One senior and one junior engineer.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: In the event of a main engine scavenge fire, which of the following options is the best course of action to take immediately?
options: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.
Speed up the engine in an effort to blow the fire out.
Stop the engine and keep it in one position until the fire is out.
Start the auxiliary blowers.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Reduce main engine rpm to a minimum.

CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.question: While on Main Engine stand-by during a river passage towards a port, you get a high exhaust temperature alarm on one main engine cylinder. What would you do?
options: Call the bridge and advise the Master of the problem.
Stop the main engine.
Acknowledge the alarm and watch to see if the temperature increases.
Acknowledge the alarm until you get into port.
CD7053 — TOTS 1C-Engine room operations.answer: Call the bridge and advise the Master of the problem.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: Duty engineers are NOT allowed to create their own personal standing orders for watchkeeping ratings.
options: True.
False.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: True.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How do duty engineers acknowledge the Chief Engineer's standing orders and orders in the Engine Order Book?
options: By signature.
By verbal verification.
Acknowledgement is not required.
By telephone confirmation to the Chief Engineer.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: By signature.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How should the engine watch be kept at anchorage?
options: The vessel is on stand-by for manoeuvring.
The vessel is in port.
The vessel is in navigation.
No watch is required.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The vessel is on stand-by for manoeuvring.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: In port, the engine watch depends on..
options: cargo operations.
crew change operations.
ship supply operations.
crew shore leave.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: cargo operations.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: When the engine watch is changing over from manned to unmanned (UMS) mode, who should be informed?
options: The bridge.
The Chief Engineer.
The Master.
All crew.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The bridge.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What should be done by the watchkeeping engineer if the relieving engineer is not ready for watch hand-over?
options: He should continue with the watch and inform the Chief Engineer.
He should leave the engine room and inform the Chief Engineer.
He should leave the engine room and inform the Master.
He should continue with the watch.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: He should continue with the watch and inform the Chief Engineer.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: When is the Engine Order Book filled in?
options: Whenever the Chief Engineer has additional orders.
From time to time.
Only in port.
When ordered by the Master.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Whenever the Chief Engineer has additional orders.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How many times per day is a regular equipment check to be carried out when the vessel is underway?
options: Once per watch.
Twice a day.
Each hour.
When ordered by the Chief Engineer.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Once per watch.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: While in port, all repairs on the main engine can be carried out without permission from local authorities.
options: False.
True.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: False.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: If the vessel has unmanned machinery space, what precautions should you take before entering, when on UMS mode?
options: Inform the bridge watch keeper
Inform the Chief Engineer.
Inform the 2nd Engineer.
Inform the master.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Inform the bridge watch keeper

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is a dead man alarm?
options: A switch which should be operated at regular intervals which, if not activated, will give an alarm on the bridge.
An Alarm that is activated when an injured crew member is discovered.
A direct link alarm to the office in the event of an emergency.
Terminology for an alarm which is malfunctioning or out of order.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: A switch which should be operated at regular intervals which, if not activated, will give an alarm on the bridge.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is the basic rule for good watchkeeping?
options: Regular visual checks.
To have a good engine rating as a watchkeeper.
To keep the engine room clean at all times.
To have good lighting in the engine room.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Regular visual checks.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: When the engine watch is changing over from manned to unmanned (UMS) mode, which of the following equipment must be switched on?
options: The Engineer call alarm.
Another diesel generator.
The second steering gear pump.
The stand -by cooling pump.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The Engineer call alarm.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is the purpose of the Engineers Call system and when should this be activated?
options: In case of any emergency situation requiring the support of all Engine room staff.
During Fuel Oil and Lub Oil Bunker operations when extra assistance is required.
The Engineers call is used in the mornings to ensure all engine staff are present in the E/R.
When the duty officer is changing rotation, all engine officers are to be present for handover.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: In case of any emergency situation requiring the support of all Engine room staff.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How do the watch keepers ensure various equipment is maintained regularly?
options: A work list is produced from the planned maintenance system & the running hours sheet is followed.
Equipment to be maintained will be identified on a daily basis by the Duty officer.
Through morning meetings and delegation of the 2nd engineer.
The Classification society issues a listing for each vessel of machinery to be overhauled / maintained, and time frames for doing such work.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: A work list is produced from the planned maintenance system & the running hours sheet is followed.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What should be done if any problem to the propulsion power or steering gear occurs during the watch?
options: Immediately inform the Officer of the Watch on the bridge.
Immediately call for help.
Call the Master immediately.
Call the Chief Engineer immediately.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Immediately inform the Officer of the Watch on the bridge.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: If a Rating is part of an engine watch, who is he directly responsible to?
options: To the Duty Engineer.
To the Chief Engineer.
To the Second Engineer.
To the Master.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: To the Duty Engineer.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How do you ensure the various equipment is maintained regularly?
options: By following a work list produced from the planned maintenance system.
The equipment to be maintained will be identified on a daily basis by the Duty officer.
Through morning meetings and delegation of the 2nd engineer.
The Classification Society issues a listing of machinery to be overhauled/maintained, and time frames for doing such work.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: By following a work list produced from the planned maintenance system.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What temperature should HFO be maintained at when passing through the purifier?
options: At a temperature calculated according to the density of the fuel being purified.
It should be maintained at 101 to 103 degree C.
It should be maintained as close to 99 degree C as possible.
It should be maintained at 90 to 95 degree C.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: At a temperature calculated according to the density of the fuel being purified.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: During night-time under-unmanned operations, which procedure for engine entry should be followed?
options: The bridge must be informed of the entry.
Entry is prohibited.
Entry is allowed only with the Chief Engineer's permission.
Entry is allowed only if two people enter together.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The bridge must be informed of the entry.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How frequently should the various auto control devices be tested for correct operation?
options: At regular intervals as laid down in the vessel's planned maintenance system.
All auto control devices are checked during dry docking, and certification is issued.
Auto control devices operate automatically, and therefore do not require intervention.
When stand-by equipment is changed over, the auto control devices indicate any errors, via an alarm.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: At regular intervals as laid down in the vessel's planned maintenance system.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What would rapid fluctuation of the main engine cooling water pressure indicate?
options: The possibility of a cracked cylinder liner or cylinder cover.
Problems with the cooling water temperature control valves.
A problem with the cooling water circulating pump impeller.
Speed fluctuation of the cooling water pump due to a motor problem.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The possibility of a cracked cylinder liner or cylinder cover.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: Where should all important requirements and activities carried out during a watch be written or recorded?
options: In the Engine Log Book.
In the Engine Activities Notebook.
In the Engine Maintenance Log.
On the blackboard in the cargo control room.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: In the Engine Log Book.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: Who is the Duty Engineer directly responsible to?
options: To the Chief Engineer.
To the Master.
To the Company.
To the Superintendent.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: To the Chief Engineer.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What temperature should lubricating oil be maintained at when passing through the purifier?
options: It should be maintained at 90 to 93 degree C.
At a temperature calculated according to the viscosity of the oil being purified.
It should be maintained at 75 to 80 degree C.
It should be maintained at 60 to 65 degree C.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: It should be maintained at 90 to 93 degree C.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How do you ensure the various indicating instruments are reading correctly?
options: By calibrating the equipment for their accuracy.
They are changed during planned maintenance.
By double checking, via portable equipment.
If they are not reading correctly, an alarm will sound and the machinery will not operate.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: By calibrating the equipment for their accuracy.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How do the watch keepers ensure various equipment is working correctly?
options: By regular performance monitoring of each piece of equipment.
By completing planned maintenance in accordance to maintenance schedules.
Via daily log book readings (pressure / temp / etc).
If equipment is defective, the alarm panel will indicate that accordingly.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: By regular performance monitoring of each piece of equipment.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: If an alarm sounds and you are on duty during a UMS period what are the first actions you should take?
options: Cancel the alarm and investigate the cause.
Advise the Chief Engineer that it is necessary to return to full watchkeeping routine.
Call the Bridge to inform them of an alarm state.
Cancel the alarm and reduce the speed of the Main Engine.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Cancel the alarm and investigate the cause.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: In normal circumstances, which parameters on steam boilers are the most important?
options: The water level and steam pressure.
The water temperature and the steam pressure.
The water pressure and the steam temperature.
The water level and the steam temperature.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The water level and steam pressure.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is the diesel oil service tank sludge cock used for?
options: To drain any water out of the tank.
To draw off a sample for analysis.
To draw off clean oil for cleaning equipment.
For draining the tank for cleaning.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: To drain any water out of the tank.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: How are the conditions of the cooling water, boiler water and lube oil maintained?
options: By regular testing and treatment.
By shore side service technicians on a quarterly basis.
By maintaining the correct liquid levels.
By top up of the water level and purification of lub oils.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: By regular testing and treatment.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The watchkeeper must call the Bridge every 20 minutes to advise them if no "dead man" alarm is fitted?
Ear defenders must not be used in the ER as it is essential to hear all noises.
It is expected that the maintenance of equipment will be carried out when on UMS.
When an alarm sounds, no watchkeeper must enter the engine room under UMS until they have advised the Bridge.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The watchkeeper must call the Bridge every 20 minutes to advise them if no "dead man" alarm is fitted?

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: Crankcase Lub oil consumption of a slow speed main engine should be monitored to confirm that it is in line with the makers specific consumption..
options: to verify that oil is not being lost due to leakage or worn scraper boxes.
to ensure that leakage does not contaminate the bilge spaces.
so that the need for regular topping up of the crankcase is not required.
to ensure that there is no air entrainment in the system oil due to the crankcase level running low.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: to verify that oil is not being lost due to leakage or worn scraper boxes.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is the normal temperature for the deep frozen meat and fish chambers?
options: Minus 18˚ Celsius (-18˚C).
Minus 12˚ Celsius (-12˚C).
Minus 8˚ Celsius (-8˚C).
Minus 4˚ Celsius (-4˚C).
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Minus 18˚ Celsius (-18˚C).

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: What is the usual required preheating temperature for 380 cSt (centistokes) of heavy fuel (HFO)?
What will happen if the "dead man alarm" is not reset on time?
options: The general alarm will sound.
The engineer call alarm will sound.
The Chief Engineer will be notified of the alarm.
The Master will be notified of the alarm.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: The general alarm will sound.

CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.question: During cargo operations, on a vessel with steam turbine driven cargo pumps, the condenser salinity alarm sounds intermittently but resets automatically. What action should you take?
options: Test the chloride level in the boiler to check if it is rising.
Ignore the alarm as it is obviously an intermittent fault.
Slow down the turbine to reduce the load on the condenser.
Check the sea water pressure to the condenser to check that it is not too high.
CD7054 — TOTS 1C-Watchkeeping in the Eng.answer: Test the chloride level in the boiler to check if it is rising.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: During discharge, problems with the inert gas plant result in the production of clean inert gas being reduced by 50%. What do you do?
options: Advise the Chief Officer so that he can reduce the discharge rate in line with the reduction of the gas supply.
Adjust the boiler controls to increase the fuel and reduce the air in an attempt to reduce the oxygen content of the gas.
Allow the discharge to continue as the oxygen content in the tanks may not rise significantly during the remaining discharge period.
Shut down the discharge until the inert gas system problem is resolved.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: Advise the Chief Officer so that he can reduce the discharge rate in line with the reduction of the gas supply.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: What is the cause if, on a two stage main air compressor the discharge pressure is low and the 1st stage discharge temperature is higher than normal?
options: The 2nd stage suction valve is defective.
The 1st stage discharge valve is defective.
The 2nd stage piston rings are damaged.
The 2nd stage discharge valve is defective.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: The 2nd stage suction valve is defective.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: What would cause the reduction in viscosity and flash point in the lubricating oil of an auxiliary engine operated on marine gas oil?
options: Fuel leakage into the crankcase.
The wrong grade of lubricant being added to the crankcase.
A build up of combustion products in the lubricating oil.
The lubricating oil is at an operating temperature that is too high.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: Fuel leakage into the crankcase.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: On a tanker with 3 centrifugal cargo pumps, but with discharge reduced to 2 pumps due to shore restrictions you note that the idle pump is running backwards. What would you suspect as being the main problem?
options: The idle cargo pump non-return valve is not closing properly.
The Pumpman has set the valve incorrectly allowing the running pumps to drive the idle pump.
The Pumpman has not closed the idle pump suction and discharge valves.
The non-return valve on one of the running pumps is defective and causing it to drive the idle pump..
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: The idle cargo pump non-return valve is not closing properly.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: A heat exchanger where two liquids flow in opposite directions is called..
options: counter-flow.
parallel flow.
opposite flow.
horizontal flow.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: counter-flow.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: An electrical driven ballast pump will not start because one of the main fuses has blown. Which of the following would you check, prior to trying to restart the pump motor?
options: The motor and pump rotation.
The insulation of the motor windings.
The electrical power supply.
The control system fuses.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: The motor and pump rotation.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: When do you expect to have to change from low to high SW suction?
options: When the ship is entering an area where there will be restricted under keel clearance.
When the ship loads a full cargo and is at maximum draught.
When the ship is in heavy weather.
When the ship is entering a canal.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: When the ship is entering an area where there will be restricted under keel clearance.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: What is meant by hunting in a control system?
options: The system being controlled does not settle on the set point.
The system being controlled does not reach the set point and remains below the set point.
The system being controlled overshoots the set point and remains above the set point.
The system being controlled reaches the set point but then falls back and remains offset.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: The system being controlled does not settle on the set point.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: The cause of an abnormally high condenser pressure within a refrigeration system would be..
options: incondensable gases in the refrigerant.
a low cooling water flow through the condenser.
a defective thermal expansion valve.
an above normal level of refrigerant in the condenser.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: incondensable gases in the refrigerant.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: A ship's air conditioning system is normally designed to give..
options: six to eight changes of air per hour.
two to three changes of air per hour.
twelve to sixteen changes of air per hour.
ten to twelve changes of air per hour.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: six to eight changes of air per hour.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: In plate type coolers you would normally expect the plates to be made of..
options: titanium.
silver.
stainless steel.
nickel brass.
CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.answer: titanium.

CD7055 — TOTS 1C-Operation, monitoring,.question: On a tanker, when on voyage with a heated cargo, the hotwell is found to be overheating due to steam returning from the cargo heating coils. What should you do?
